The framework learns a single curator that adapts to executor behavior via an online behavioral profile of recent execution patterns.

entry.title: Language as the Interface: Foundation-Model Contrastive Learning Links Transcriptomes and Electrophysiology

author.name: Junbo Shen, Jinying Gao, Bo Lei

entry.summary: LangPatch uses paired Patch-seq data to align pretrained GenePT transcriptomic representations with electrophysiological phenotypes via a shared frozen text encoder, embedding gene descriptions and verbalized electrophysiology profiles in a common language-based space. Contrastive learning with adapter modules connects the modalities across mouse data. This is a step toward multimodal foundation models for neuroscience.

entry.title: FedLAFP: Low-Rank Aggregation Meets Full-Rank Personalization in Federated Fine-Tuning

author.name: Mengjun Yi, Huaian Gu, Yinghao Ai, Furao Shen, Jian Zhao

entry.summary: FedLAFP is a role-aware federated fine-tuning framework that couples a globally aggregated LoRA branch for shared knowledge with a client-private RandLoRA branch capable of full-rank personalization. It argues that shared and private adaptation have distinct structural requirements that prior personalized methods conflate under one low-rank structure. The design targets statistical heterogeneity across clients without sharing raw data.

entry.title: Foundations of Proactive Agents: Principles, Technical Layers, and Proactivity-Gym

author.name: Jio Oh, Seunghyun Do, Young-Jun Lee, Steven Euijong Whang, Dongyeop Kang

entry.summary: Proposes foundations for designing and evaluating proactive LLM agents around three principles (Task Capability, Temporal Allocation, Trust), organized into a five-dimension design space, and introduces Proactivity-Gym as an associated evaluation environment. Emphasizes that even correct proactive work can impose review costs and undermine trust.

entry.title: Mubric: Mutation Testing-Guided Rubric Generation for LLM Evaluation

author.name: Jiayuxuan Yang, Jie M. Zhang, Yiling Lou, Zhenpeng Chen

entry.summary: Adapts mutation testing from software engineering to LLM evaluation: Mubric mines common defects from real response pairs, injects them into high-quality responses, and keeps rubric criteria only when scoring detects the injected defect. This yields rubrics that reliably capture task-specific quality requirements.

entry.title: Routing Should Pay for Itself: Sparse Supervision for Economical LLM Routing

author.name: Guannan Lai, Gelin Bian, Hao-Xuan Ma, Jun-Peng Jiang, Long Chen, Jian-Dong Liu, Zhi-Hao Tan, Han-Jia Ye

entry.summary: Highlights that LLM routing research ignores the upfront supervision cost of collecting query-model quality feedback, and shows routing quality saturates well before dense feedback is gathered. SaveRouter selectively collects sparse supervision so that routing savings actually exceed the data-collection expenditure.

entry.title: Beyond a single latent space: a dual-latent world model for long-horizon planning

author.name: Delin Zhao, Zhengrong Yue, Shaobin Zhuang, Junlin He, Xiaoyu Chen, Zikang Wang, Yuxin Liu, Limin Wang, Yali Wang

entry.summary: Dual-WM separates local execution and long-range planning into distinct latent state representations and dynamics models, with a low-level action-conditioned model and a high-level model planning with learned macro-actions. A weighted-rollout representation-learning scheme (LoRe) supervises self-generated predictions at both levels, motivated by an analysis of recursive error propagation.

entry.title: Adam under Generalized Smoothness with Second-Moment-Type Stochastic Gradients

author.name: Ruinan Jin, Difei Cheng, Ling Chen, Jun Luo, Hao Zhou, Youzhi Zhang

entry.summary: This theory paper proves that Adam converges on generalized smooth objectives using only second-moment information on stochastic gradients, removing strong tail assumptions like almost-sure boundedness or sub-Gaussianity. It resolves an open question posed by Li et al. (2023) by extending the Adam self-normalization framework.

entry.title: Probability is Not Enough: Exploring and Counting Divergent Tokens for Reasoning Uncertainty Quantification in LLMs

author.name: Feiyang Li, Shengjing Liu, Qi Zhan, Sijie Cheng, Weiqing Wang, Hongwen Chen, Yuxuan Yang, Wen Wang, Yile Wang, Hui Huang

entry.summary: Finds that selected token probabilities are an opaque and fragile confidence signal for chain-of-thought reasoning, since coarse substitutes can also improve calibration. The paper introduces Divergent Token Confidence, which estimates answer confidence by counting decoding positions where two models strongly disagree, yielding a more robust uncertainty signal.

entry.title: Binarization Flattens the Score Space

author.name: Jacob Cole

entry.summary: This theoretical paper analyzes LLM-judge rewards collapsed to pass/fail verdicts, showing that binarization leaves a policy free to apply affine stretches of the underlying score scale without changing any reported verdict - an unobservable degree of freedom that can hide reward hacking. Under a joint-Gaussian model, adding a third grade with a second threshold removes this ambiguity.

entry.title: $\tau$-Multilingual: Benchmarking Voice Agents Across Languages

author.name: Soham Ray, Edgard dos Santos Paiva, Ruben Valenzuela, Karthik Narasimhan, Keshav Dhandhania, Victor Barres

entry.summary: tau-Multilingual extends a voice-agent benchmark to Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, Hindi, Korean, and Mandarin with native-speaker review across 4,500 full-duplex calls and five voice configurations. It finds Spanish, Portuguese, and Hindi within 3.2 points of English on task completion while Korean and Mandarin drop by 14.7 and 8.4 points, with distinct failure modes; Grok leads task completion but scores lowest on generation quality.

entry.title: Mara Chain: Rethinking Failure as a Stepping Stone for AI System Auto-Evolution

author.name: Yubin Lyu, Fu Li, Jiawei Fei, Yang Zhao, Weixing Mei, Yinan Wu

entry.summary: Mara Chain is a refinement procedure for auto-optimizing deployed AI system artifacts (prompts, skills, harnesses, code) that retains and iteratively refines rejected candidate configurations instead of discarding them, using accumulated failure evidence to guide future proposals. This avoids repeatedly revisiting the same failure modes in propose-evaluate-select loops.

entry.title: One Geometry, Different Outcomes: Readout-Dependent Effects of the Modality Gap in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Aditya Sharma, Divya Saxena

entry.summary: This paper unifies previously divergent findings about the modality gap in contrastive vision-language models by showing the image-text mean separation is approximately rank-one, with a single dominant direction capturing 94.4-99.9% of squared norm separation across CLIP and SigLIP encoders. A decomposition of the similarity score explains why reducing the gap helps zero-shot classification while removing gap structure can degrade image-text retrieval. The effects depend on the task's readout mechanism.

entry.title: Population Fidelity: Evaluating Population Representativeness in LLMs

author.name: Neemias B. da Silva, Martin Lukk, Ali Sutani, Abhishek Moturu, Harris Yang, Daniel Silver, Matt Ratto, Thiago H. Silva

entry.summary: The paper introduces Population Fidelity, a framework for evaluating whether LLM-generated survey responses represent human populations across three dimensions: group-level accuracy, between-group variation, and the structure of that variation. It reproduces a prior machine-bias study and demonstrates how the framework diagnoses where LLM simulations compress or misrepresent subgroups.

entry.title: Audience-Bound Persistent Memory: Authorization Across the Memory Lifecycle

author.name: Sibo Liu

entry.summary: This single-author paper formalizes authorization for persistent memory in personal language agents, ensuring facts learned in one audience context are not surfaced to another. Memory items carry audience provenance, derived items inherit intersected audiences, and access fails closed to public-only when viewer identity is unresolved. It is an early, principled take on a safety problem that will grow as agents gain long-lived memory.

entry.title: Channel-Dependent State Space Model for Multivariate Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Yu-Cheng Wu, Fan-Keng Sun, Li-Chun Lu, Duane S. Boning

entry.summary: Chameleon is a channel-dependent state space model for multivariate time series forecasting that enables fine-grained, data-dependent cross-variable interactions while scaling linearly with the number of variables. It connects selective SSMs with the Kalman filter, using the missing measurement update as a mechanism for cross-channel information flow.

entry.title: Text2Sim: Agentic Physics-Based Simulation Generation with Distilled Expertise

author.name: Xiaoyu Xiong, Tsun-Hsuan Wang, Yi-Ling Qiao, Tao Du, Minchen Li

entry.summary: Text2Sim is an agentic pipeline built on the Genesis simulator that converts text-only requests into executable, editable physical simulations, using a hierarchical structure of a Planner, specialized Writers, asset-generation tools, and an independent Critic. Compact Debug Cards distilled from graphics demonstrations provide role-specific physical guidance for execution-based repair. It is evaluated on 42 held-out prompts across rigid, articulated, and deformable objects.

entry.title: Beyond Conditional Independence: Root Cause Analysis with Deep Causal Models

author.name: Md Musfiqur Rahman, Kenneth Lee, Ziwei Jiang, Padmaja Jonnalagedda, Ruocheng Guo, Murat Kocaoglu

entry.summary: This paper relaxes strong assumptions in root cause analysis by modeling systems as causal models where anomalies correspond to changes in structural functions, handling latent confounders that break conditional-independence-based methods. It establishes a connection to deep causal models to exploit distributional constraints beyond unconfoundedness. This advances principled RCA for real-world systems like cloud infrastructure where hidden confounding is common.

entry.title: Salt++: Context-Aligned Post-Training for Few-Step Streaming Multimodal Generation

author.name: Xingtong Ge, Yutong Wang, Lunjie Zhu, Haitao Lin, Fangyu Lin, Yushi Huang, Xin Zhang, Yi Zhang, Yu Liu, Jun Zhang

entry.summary: Salt++ is a two-stage post-training framework for few-step streaming audio-video generation, combining Causal Self-Flow with context-aligned autoregressive Distribution Matching Distillation. It fixes two context-mismatch problems: teacher forcing supervising contextual representations only indirectly, and bidirectional score models clashing with causal generation contexts in DMD. This enables efficient streaming multimodal generation.

entry.title: Beam Search as Test-Time Self-Distillation via Counterfactual Contexts

author.name: Su Ee Tan, Xiaotong Ji, Rasul Tutunov, Haitham Bou-Ammar, Matthieu Zimmer

entry.summary: This paper extends Self-Distillation Fine-Tuning to inference time, extracting a steering signal from counterfactual contexts (templates priming excellent versus poor reasoning) without parameter updates, reward models, or training data. The pointwise mutual information from SDFT is used at decoding time to guide beam search. This offers training-free capability steering at generation time.

entry.title: Beyond Compression: Diagnosing How Post-Training Changes Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Hongyang Li, Yiming Zhu, Xiao Li, Caesar Wu, Said Mammar, Pascal Bouvry

entry.summary: This paper uses diagnostic probes (cross-surface pass@K over paraphrases, numerical isomorphisms, translations, plus consistency measures) to determine what post-training actually changes in mathematical reasoning, beyond endpoint pass@1. It compares off-policy distillation trajectories, released Qwen3 distillation endpoints, and a DeepSeek-Math GRPO endpoint. Gains are decomposed into newly reachable solutions, cheaper sampling, surface robustness, or memorization.

entry.title: Simultaneous Neural Optimal Transport

author.name: Milena Gazdieva, Kirill Sokolov, Jiawei Chen, Evgeny Burnaev, Alexander Korotin

entry.summary: The paper formalizes the simultaneous optimal transport problem: learning a single shared transport map that carries multiple source distributions to a common target while minimizing average transport cost. This addresses cases like multi-degradation image restoration where naive pooling leaves individual sources misaligned. A neural formulation with theoretical and empirical support is proposed.

entry.title: Dr. OPD: Learning What to Follow for Optimal On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models

author.name: Zhenyu Wang, Tianze Wang, Linjun Zhang, Yifan Hu

entry.summary: Dr. OPD reformulates on-policy distillation as a bilevel optimization in which token-level teacher supervision weights are learned to maximize student performance, recognizing that some teacher signals correct critical reasoning errors while others are uninformative. This matters because on-policy distillation is an increasingly popular cheap route to strong small LLMs, and selective supervision is a principled improvement.

entry.title: MaD-RL: Matching Distributions for Calibrating LLMs with Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Sourabh Kulkarni, Ksheeraj Sai Vepuri, Basar Demir, Jason Bohrer, Emily Shen, Jianfa Chen, Nan Jiang, Ankit Jain, Harihar Subramanyam, Mannat Singh, Chirag Nagpal

entry.summary: MaD-RL proposes an RL-based distribution matching framework for LLM post-training that controls the distribution of a latent categorical attribute of outputs toward a target distribution, beyond maximizing expected per-output reward. It extends dominant recipes like GRPO and demonstrates applications in synthetic data generation, fairness constraint satisfaction, and policy exploration.

entry.title: Does Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture Pretraining Help Time Series Forecasting?

author.name: Yutong Feng, Bowen Liao, See Kiong Ng, Yuxuan Liang

entry.summary: This paper conducts the most extensive cross-architecture evaluation of JEPA self-supervised pretraining for time series, testing one JEPA instantiation across nine backbones and eleven temporal and spatio-temporal benchmarks. It clarifies whether JEPA pretraining is a reliable improvement or heavily dependent on the downstream model. The findings help resolve mixed evidence in the literature about this increasingly popular paradigm.

entry.title: DOHF: Online Diffusion Fine-tuning with Doob's $h$-transform Guidance

author.name: Zhengyi Guo, Jiayuan Sheng, Wenpin Tang

entry.summary: DOHF turns Doob's h-transform into a practical online fine-tuning algorithm for diffusion models, assigning optimality weights to generated samples, estimating local correction terms under the current rollout policy, and distilling them into the generative model. It accommodates black-box and non-differentiable rewards and unifies DiffusionNFT-style updates and classifier-free guidance under one h-transform theory. Useful where desirable outcomes are rare or reward estimates are costly.

entry.title: Representation Learning for Exact Preimages

author.name: Konstantin Hess, Stefan Feuerriegel

entry.summary: The paper addresses the inverse problem of characterizing and optimizing over the preimage of a neural predictor: the full set of inputs meeting a given target performance or safety level. It introduces TRIO, a framework for tractable representations supporting preimage learning and inverse optimization, navigating the trade-off between expressive forward prediction, preimage accuracy, and optimization tractability.

entry.title: On the Capability and Limitation of Hard Prompt

author.name: Lijia Yu, Shuaitong Liu, Gaojie Jin, Xinyu Li, Xiao-Shan Gao

entry.summary: This paper provides the first computational complexity theory for hard (discrete) prompts, proving that deciding whether a hard prompt exists for a transformer to solve a downstream task is NP-complete and finding an optimal prompt is NP-hard. It further makes substantial progress on core theoretical questions about the expressivity and limits of hard prompting of LLMs.

entry.title: Write Back the $\Delta$: Revisiting the Same Tokens with Fresh Representations

author.name: Wencheng Ye, Anning Hu, Xiangdong Zhang, Tianyi Wang, Yikang Li, Hengyu Jin, Bing Li, Junchi Yan

entry.summary: Proposes inference-time feedback for transformers that writes the depth increment (Delta) — newly accumulated computation between two layers — back to earlier layers, rather than full residual states or predefined directions. The approach enables instance-level adaptive computation with better composability and scalability than re-executing depth.

entry.title: Fast and Precise Learned Charged-Particle Trajectory Regression at the Large Hadron Collider

author.name: Jonathan Renusch, Benjamin Huth, Daniel Murnane, Eleni Xochelli, Do\u{g}a Elitez, Paul Gessinger-Befurt, Andreas Stefl, Jeremy Couthures, Andreas Salzburger, Lukas Heinrich, Michael Kagan, Markus Elsing

entry.summary: This work treats charged-particle trajectory fitting at the LHC as a sequence-modeling task, using a bidirectional architecture to match the roughly one-in-100,000 precision of classical Kalman-filter-based fits while being faster. The classical methods rely on detailed detector geometry modeling and precise numerical integration, so a learned approach reaching comparable precision is notable. Collaboration with CERN-affiliated authors lends domain credibility.

entry.title: SoFT: Soft Targets for Generalizable LLM Fine-Tuning

author.name: Huihao Jing, Wenbin Hu, Shaojin Chen, Haochen Shi, Zhongwei Xie, Guijia Zhang, Yuxuan Liu, Haoyu Huang, Haoran Li, Yangqiu Song

entry.summary: SoFT studies multi-teacher, multi-domain distillation into a single student LLM and proposes soft-target fine-tuning that sets a minimum target probability to balance learning teacher behaviors with retaining base-model capabilities. Experiments reveal trade-offs between in-distribution learning and out-of-distribution generalization across SFT methods, motivating explicit control of this balance. It matters for practical LLM fine-tuning pipelines that merge diverse capabilities.

entry.title: The GUI Is Not the State: Diagnosing State Aliasing in GUI World Models

author.name: Dongsheng Liu, Chao Jin, Wenkui Yang, Hejin Wang, Junwei Yang, Zeren Zhang, Ziwei Chen, Huaibo Huang, Jie Cao, Ran He

entry.summary: This paper identifies state aliasing in GUI world models, where identical visible interfaces can correspond to different valid futures because transition-relevant environment state is unobserved, undermining agent planning and simulation. The authors introduce StateAliasBench to isolate such ambiguities and propose lightweight predictive-state recovery that augments frozen GUI world models with structured state inferred from history. This matters for building reliable GUI agents.

entry.title: Permutation-Equivariant Flow Matching for Alignment-Free Neural Weight Generation

author.name: Arkadi Piven, Yam Eitan, Guy Bar-Shalom, Fabrizio Frasca, Daniel Cremers, Thomas Dag\`es, Ron Kimmel, Haggai Maron

entry.summary: This work uses a permutation-equivariant graph meta network to parameterize a flow-matching velocity field for generating neural network weight vectors, learning directly from independently trained networks without alignment or a shared base model. It addresses the permutation symmetry challenge in learned weight-space generative models.

entry.title: The Geometry of Logic: Stratification Induces Semantic Structure and Robust Reasoning

author.name: Cristina V. Lopes, Yuangang Li, Justin Tian Jin Chen, Alberto Krone-Martins, Iris Ma, Md Rakib Hossain Misu

entry.summary: The paper introduces STRAT, an architectural modification that partitions the Transformer residual stream into orthogonal Data and Type subspaces with type-based attention and gating, testing whether separating values from their types improves generalizable logical reasoning. Controlled experiments examine learnability and robustness of the induced mechanisms.

entry.title: What Should Data Teach? Moving Bottlenecks Across Circuit, Store, and Use

author.name: Yixiao Chen, Ke Cheng, Jiangtao Guan, Shuo Huang, Yue Liu, Jun Zhang, Yuhong Liu, Jie Jiang

entry.summary: Taking a circuit view of language model training, the paper identifies three bottlenecks — forming a computation, making its content available, and selecting among routes — and proposes a diagnosis-to-data principle for curriculum and data selection that localizes missing operations and orders prerequisites. Experiments include formation-sensitive selection retaining validation advantage through 100B tokens.

entry.title: The limits of exactness: On the failure of automatic differentiation in physics-informed machine learning

author.name: Ameya D. Jagtap

entry.summary: This position-style paper argues that automatic differentiation, despite machine-precision exactness, can produce derivatives that are mathematically correct but physically wrong for physics-informed machine learning, since AD lacks awareness of physical structure such as conservation, directionality, and thermodynamic consistency. It surveys failure modes across computational science and engineering.

entry.title: CFLoRA: Federated Fine-tuning of LLMs with Complementary Factors for Error-free Aggregation

author.name: Yanan Ma, Qiyuan Chen, Zihan Fang, Xianhao Chen, Yuguang Fang

entry.summary: CFLoRA addresses the structural mismatch in federated LoRA averaging — averaging LoRA factors separately does not equal averaging their products — by partitioning latent LoRA channels into two complementary sets each round, ensuring compatibility. It enables simultaneous factor updates without aggregation errors or expanded communication ranks, unlike freezing or alternating schemes.

entry.title: AG-CoT: Verified Algorithmic Traces for LLM Program Synthesis on Clifford Circuits

author.name: Lu Wei, Yufeng Wang, Chenfeng Cao, Lu Pang, Haibin Ling

entry.summary: The paper targets verified scientific code generation for Clifford circuit synthesis, where an exact classical verifier checks generated OpenQASM circuits against compact stabilizer-generator targets. Supervising models with verifier-checked Aaronson-Gottesman chain-of-thought traces and continuing training on accepted generations multiplies greedy-decode state-equivalence accuracy across 3B and 7B model families.

entry.title: The Price of Locality: Why Forward-Forward Underperforms Backpropagation?

author.name: Zhaoxian Wu, Haichuan Liu, Tianyi Chen

entry.summary: This paper theoretically diagnoses why the Forward-Forward algorithm underperforms backpropagation, identifying two failure modes: an optimization floor caused by inter-layer representation drift under concurrent local updates, and a geometric collapse of layer representations. The authors prove FFA loss satisfies a Polyak-Lojasiewicz inequality per layer but each layer optimizes against a moving input distribution.

entry.title: When to Evict, Not What to Keep: Draft-Guided Eviction for Training-Free KV-Cache Compression

author.name: Haeyong Kang, Chang D. Yoo

entry.summary: The paper argues that existing training-free KV-cache compression methods fail because they evict tokens before the decode-time queries that matter exist, demonstrating two failure modes (compensation and selection). It proposes Draft-Guided Eviction, which defers eviction until after a drafted answer trajectory identifies which tokens future queries will use.

entry.title: FoldAttention: Declared-Reference Softmax for Fast Decode and Deterministic Backward

author.name: Sriman Achanta

entry.summary: FoldAttention reformulates softmax attention with a fixed additive reference chosen before scanning the KV cache, exploiting shift invariance so each weight is final when computed. This enables contributions to add across disjoint key ranges, promising faster autoregressive decoding and deterministic backward passes.

entry.title: MA-JEPA: Joint-Embedding World Models for Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Brandon Gary Kaplowitz, Osaze James Obahor, Christian Schroeder de Witt

entry.summary: MA-JEPA brings joint-embedding predictive representations to multi-agent RL, replacing observation reconstruction with target representation prediction in a stochastic world model. It supports centralized training with decentralized execution using a categorical latent state and causal Transformer trained with action-conditioned dynamics objectives.

entry.title: Pretraining Transformers with Quantized Softmax in Attention

author.name: Shangzhen Zhu, Muyan Hu, Tomasz Kozlowski

entry.summary: This companion paper studies K-interval attention, which approximates the exponential with grid values, during pretraining rather than inference, deriving backward rules including calibration derivatives. It compares grid calibration, interpolation versus rounding, and straight-through surrogate placement under matched training conditions.

entry.title: Reachability is not enough: Diagnosing long-range behavior in GNNs

author.name: Filippo Maria Bianchi

entry.summary: This work presents a diagnostic framework measuring how strongly inputs at each graph distance influence GNN predictions, separating architectural, approximation, training, and numerical limitations of long-range reasoning. It shows finite implementations of mathematically long-range models may still rely mostly on nearby inputs, and explains why equivalent filters differ in learnability and stability. This sharpens the debate on whether GNNs truly use distant information.

entry.title: PI-NOMT: Physics-Informed Neural Optimal Mass Transport for Brain Fluid Dynamics

author.name: Mehmet Emin Acar, Vahit Bugra Yesilkaynak, Helene Benveniste, Gozde Unal

entry.summary: Formulates recovery of hidden transport mechanisms from sparse DCE-MRI brain tracer imaging as physics-informed latent-state inference, representing density, velocity, and source as continuous neural fields within a neural optimal mass transport framework. The transport field itself is the primary inference target rather than an auxiliary variable, aiming to uncover unobserved brain fluid dynamics.

entry.title: When Is an SAE Feature Interpretable? A Validation Ladder for EEG Foundation Models

author.name: Yucong Cao, Chenqi Li, Tingting Zhu

entry.summary: The paper shows that apparent interpretability of sparse-autoencoder features in EEG foundation models can be confounded: alpha-band removal changes latent firing 7.3x more than a sham notch, but after normalizing by removed spectral energy the effect largely disappears. It proposes a validation ladder across 27 settings to distinguish genuine feature meaning from trivial signal-energy artifacts.

entry.title: Transfer Calibrated Prediction Powered Inference

author.name: Aditya T. Vadlamani, Jae Ho Chang, Srinivasan Parthasarathy, Subhadeep Paul

entry.summary: TC-PPI extends prediction-powered inference to settings where the AI predictor was pre-trained on a different source domain, adapting it to the target using gold-standard samples via cross-fitting with methods like LoRA or fine-tuning. The jointly tuned estimator maintains unbiasedness while matching or beating classical and PPI baselines in efficiency.

entry.title: Commutator Memory: Sparse, Path-Local Reading and Steering in Language Models

author.name: John Sweeney

entry.summary: This single-author paper asks whether data-order dependence in SGD training leaves a parametric memory trace, showing that the weight difference between two training orders is, to leading order, eta-squared times a curvature-based commutator term. The identified component is localized in output space, causally modulates the loss gap between orders, and can reveal which training order produced a model.

entry.title: LRC-JEPA: Disentangling Dynamics and Residual Context for Efficient World Models

author.name: Luzhe Huang, Lei Chu, Jingyi Liang, Yuhuan Zhao

entry.summary: LRC-JEPA is a lightweight world model that disentangles action-conditioned dynamics from predictable visual context by routing information into a compact predictive latent used for planning and residual-context embeddings used for reconstruction. A differentiable residual control mechanism prevents dynamics information from leaking into the context channel, improving planning as scenes grow complex.

entry.title: PhysioTRACE: Provenance-Aware Stress Tests for Physiological Foundation Models

author.name: Ayana Mussabayeva, Anuar Aimoldin, Olivier Oullier, Xue Liu, Kun Zhang

entry.summary: PhysioTRACE is a four-axis behavioral audit framework (Recover, Stress, Intervene, Verify) for physiological foundation models that tests whether models rely on acquisition provenance, such as recording conditions, as a shortcut for diagnosis. It distinguishes what a probe can decode from what a task head actually uses, certifying provenance removal against matched random projections. This addresses shortcut learning in medical foundation models where recording-site artifacts can masquerade as diagnostic signal.

entry.title: M3OS: A Monte Carlo Graph Search-Orchestrated Multi-Agent LLM System for Evidence-Traced Molecular Optimization

author.name: Junjie Wang, Yaowei Jin, Ruohui Tang, Guonan Cui, Haojie Wang, Penglei Wang, Dingyan Wang, Duo An, Shuangjia Zheng, Qian Shi

entry.summary: M3OS is a multi-agent LLM system for small-molecule optimization that decouples molecular-design reasoning from optimization-state management via Monte Carlo graph search. A persistent graph links evaluated candidates, parent-child transformations, and evaluation evidence, with rewards and visit statistics guiding LLM-assisted parent selection and tool-driven candidate generation. This tackles the problem of LLMs losing track of optimization history stored only in conversation context.

entry.title: PMOPD: Task Ordering, Cycling, and Parameter-Update Subspace Protection in Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Youzhi Liu, Ruobing Zheng, Boyuan Tong, Tianqi Li, Pingqi Li, Hanbo Bi, Yi Yuan, Jingdong Chen

entry.summary: This work studies multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) for frontier LLM post-training and the capability seesaw problem where improving one domain suppresses another. It observes that parameter updates from different tasks concentrate in distinct low-dimensional subspaces and proposes subspace protection plus task ordering/cycling strategies to mitigate interference.

entry.title: QuantForge: Discovering Residual Decompositions for MXFP4 Post-Training Quantization

author.name: Qiulin Shang, Zhoutong Wu, Jie Hu, Kun Yuan

entry.summary: QuantForge is an LLM-driven program-evolution system for discovering quantization designs under strict MXFP4 W4A4 post-training quantization, recording competing explanations of how coordinate transforms affect block-encoding errors and residuals, selecting discriminating control experiments, and verifying successor code implements conclusions. This residual compilation approach makes the search self-explaining.

entry.title: A Unifying Framework of Concept-based Explainable AI with Completeness Guarantees

author.name: Vojt\v{e}ch K\r{u}r, Adam Kuku\v{c}ka, Tom\'a\v{s} Br\'azdil, V\'it Musil

entry.summary: This paper provides a common mathematical framework for concept-based explainable AI methods, viewing concept discovery as a concept autoencoder over a trained model's latent space, where reconstruction error measures concept completeness. It enables shared analysis of heterogeneous explanation approaches and comes with completeness guarantees. This is a valuable theoretical contribution to interpretability.

entry.title: Teach to Learn: Hint Annealing for Self-improving LLM Reasoning

author.name: Zile Wang, Zijian Li, Haodong Wang, Jian Liu, Qianli Liu, Lucas Muli, Blaze Chen, Song Guo

entry.summary: The paper identifies hinted reward shift in GRPO training, where trajectories generated with auxiliary hints concentrate policy updates and limit hint-free improvement, and proposes hint annealing to recover learning signal on difficult queries without the shift. This improves self-improving reasoning loops where difficult queries yield only incorrect rollouts.

entry.title: FlexiWorld: Learning and Planning via Flexible Action Chunks Across Multiple Time Scales

author.name: Shidu Ren, Qilin Gu, Zhenghao Ni, Junhan Sun, Jiaqi Wang, Damien Scieur, Yunze Liu

entry.summary: FlexiWorld is a JEPA-based world model combining mixed-span goal supervision with variable-length action chunks to improve long-horizon control and planning. It jointly trains a world model, a causal action encoder, and an autoregressive actor, with Student Forcing to reduce exposure bias.

entry.title: AIM-ZO: Activation-Informed Subspace Maintenance for Zeroth-Order LLM Fine-Tuning

author.name: Yue Xie, Zhi Zheng, Yunpeng Ba, Xuyang Wu, Xialiang Tong, Zhichao Lu, Tao Zhong, Zhenkun Wang

entry.summary: AIM-ZO improves zeroth-order fine-tuning of billion-parameter LLMs by maintaining a high-quality activation-informed low-dimensional perturbation subspace, avoiding wasted forward evaluations on weakly informative directions. The method dynamically maintains subspace quality where static or overly compressed subspaces miss useful update directions.

entry.title: Multi-Attractor GNNs: Set-Valued Expressivity Beyond Unique Equilibria

author.name: Jialin Liu

entry.summary: Shows that recurrent and equilibrium GNNs with multiple equilibria can represent set-valued equivariant maps, so different initializations converge to different valid solutions for combinatorial problems with symmetric solution sets. Provides constructions of globally Lipschitz, permutation-equivariant dynamics converging to valid solutions under regularity assumptions.

entry.title: Fiona: Accelerating FHE Inference with Packing-Aware Ternary Weights

author.name: Yiteng Peng, Zhibo Liu, Dongwei Xiao, Shuai Wang

entry.summary: Presents FIONA, an offline optimizer for fully homomorphic encryption inference that ternarizes weight groups in a packing-aware manner, replacing expensive plaintext-ciphertext multiplications with additions while preserving accuracy. Targets the observation that naive ternarization under packed execution yields little benefit or degrades accuracy.

entry.title: Provable Benefits of Regularization: Fast Rates for Adversarial Imitation Learning

author.name: Hanbin Zhou, Shangzhe Li, Alexander Braverman, Weitong Zhang

entry.summary: This theory paper establishes finite-sample fast rates for adversarial imitation learning with joint reward and policy regularization in finite-horizon MDPs with general function approximation. The model-free Dually Regularized AIL algorithm combines KL policy regularization with a quadratic reward penalty, formally explaining why regularization is essential in empirically successful methods like GAIL.

entry.title: The Temporal Tug-of-War: Visualizing and Detecting RAG Conflicts in Diffusion Models via Trajectory Variance

author.name: Sravan Karthick T, Pranav Darshan, Pranav A, Minal Moharir, Ivan P. Yamshchikov

entry.summary: The paper identifies a failure mode in retrieval-augmented discrete diffusion language models: when retrieved context contradicts parametric knowledge, the denoising process becomes a battleground between competing knowledge sources. It introduces the Trajectory Variance Score (TVS), a lightweight, interpretable measure computed from as few as two parallel denoising runs that detects such conflicts. This contributes to understanding and monitoring RAG reliability in the emerging diffusion-LM paradigm.

entry.title: Communication between Frozen Large Language Models via Prompt Optimization in a Referential Game

author.name: Vivek Anand, Muthu Chandrasekaran, Shiva Chaitanya

entry.summary: Two frozen LLMs from different providers with different tokenizers play a referential game where one describes an object in a short fixed-alphabet message and the other identifies it, with isolated prompt optimizers rewriting each agent's prompts from scored interactions. Optimized prompts develop a shared code that generalizes to held-out objects above a no-codebook baseline, even without a memory window.

entry.title: FOCUS: Fixed-Confidence Online Causal Learning Using Sequential Adaptive Interventions

author.name: Haijie Xu, Chen Zhang

entry.summary: This paper studies fully online causal discovery with no historical data, where a learner adaptively selects interventions to recover a causal DAG and edge weights under linear-Gaussian structural equations. The authors prove an instance-dependent lower bound and propose FOCUS, which allocates interventions via an online max-min game and achieves provably correct recovery with expected stopping time matching the lower bound.

entry.title: Prefill-Free Cross-Family KV Cache Transfer for Heterogeneous Multi-Agent LLMs

author.name: Vincent-Daniel Yun, Woosang Lim, Haneul Yoo, Sungjoo Yoo, Murali Annavaram, Sai Praneeth Karimireddy

entry.summary: HeteroFold enables prefill-free KV cache transfer between different LLM families in multi-agent systems, handling tokenization, depth, and representation mismatches while keeping both sender and receiver frozen. Across six transfer directions it eliminates redundant prefill of shared context, saving compute in heterogeneous multi-agent pipelines.

entry.title: When Does Dense Retrieval Need Asymmetric Geometry? A Bias-Variance Theory of Shared and Dual Projections

author.name: Maojun Sun, Yancheng Yuan, Jian Huang, Ruijian Han

entry.summary: The paper develops a bias-variance theory for choosing between shared and dual query-document projections in dense retrieval, deriving the exact approximation gap and proving a local Gaussian boundary where dual projections have lower risk exactly when squared directional signal exceeds the estimation cost of extra degrees of freedom. This motivates CARS, a Cross-fitted Asymmetry Risk Selector that estimates reproducible directional signal from training pairs. It gives practitioners a principled tool for a common architectural decision underlying RAG and semantic search.

entry.title: REFINE: A Resilient Evolution Framework for Intelligent Enterprise Alert Triage in Security Operations Centers

author.name: Huimin Chen, Quan Long, Yanhao Wang

entry.summary: REFINE is an LLM-agent framework for enterprise security alert triage that encodes analyst expertise as structured skills, continuously adapts from analyst disposition feedback, and enforces recall = 1.0 as a hard constraint while maximizing auto-closure of false positives. It also identifies judgment blind spots by combining alert distributions with model error boundaries, and is evaluated on four real industrial datasets. It targets a genuine operational pain point in SOCs where LLM agents struggle to track evolving organization-specific standards.

entry.title: Schur-Neural KF: Learned Schur-Consistent Corrections to the Extended Kalman Filter

author.name: Min Kim, Lianghao Cao, Soon-Jo Chung, Andrew M. Stuart

entry.summary: SN-KF learns corrections to the extended Kalman filter while provably preserving the EKF's probabilistic conditioning interpretation, using a Schur-complement parametrization that guarantees positive semidefinite predictive covariance. The authors prove the filter's uncertainty never increases after measurement updates and rule out arbitrarily large corrections.

entry.title: SAGE: Semantic Audio Generative Encoder

author.name: Francesco Brigante, Luca Cerovaz, Davide Marincione, Giorgio Strano, Luca Zhou, Emanuele Rodol\`a, Michele Mancusi

entry.summary: SAGE is a compact 105M-parameter audio variational autoencoder that shapes its latent space by distilling embeddings from a pretrained audio-text model, trained only on public music. It matches the listening-test quality of an autoencoder 8x larger and 4x slower while running at the inference cost of Stable Audio Open, improving the reconstruction/semantics/speed trade-off.

entry.title: Counterfactual Self-Evolving Agents for Evidence-Grounded Reasoning

author.name: Xing Han, Yuxin Wang, Chen Chen, Wei Dai, Gautham Krishna Gudur, Shijun Li, Hsing-Huan Chung, Gregory D. Hager, Joydeep Ghosh, Paul Pu Liang, Suchi Saria

entry.summary: Introduces counterfactual self-evolution for self-play proposer-solver setups on evidence-identifiable tasks: a trained Proposer generates targeted counterfactual evidence edits with causal explanations, enabling verified task generation. The method is supported by a handcrafted expert-verified counterfactual instruction-tuning dataset.

entry.title: Dynamic Manipulation with World-Action Models via Counterfactual Planning

author.name: Sunwoo Park, Wonbin Lee, Seonghyun Jin, Youngmin Kim, Jangho Park, Jong Chul Ye

entry.summary: The paper identifies target-response collapse in world-action models trained on static demonstrations: policies become biased toward continuing their learned behavior and stop responding to moved targets. Its Dynamic Predictive Planning framework decouples plan-generation context from execution state and uses the model's predictive rollouts to decide when to intervene, formulating dynamic manipulation as counterfactual planning. This improves robot manipulation of moving targets with models trained on static data.

entry.title: Geometry-Adaptive Mechanisms for Private Synthetic Data

author.name: Raoof Zare Moayedi, Amir R. Asadi, Mohammad Hossein Yassaee, Gholamali Aminian

entry.summary: For differentially private synthetic data on the d-dimensional unit cube, existing pure-epsilon mechanisms suffer a curse-of-dimensionality Wasserstein error rate of order (epsilon n)^(-1/d). The paper introduces a multiscale packing-growth dimension k that captures the geometric complexity of the data's support and proposes Adaptive Pruned-PMM, which adapts to lower-dimensional structure to beat worst-case rates when data lie on or near a low-dimensional set. This yields stronger utility guarantees for private data release in realistic geometries.

entry.title: RAISE: Reinforcing Access Control Policy Synthesis in LLMs via Symbolic Evaluation

author.name: Yingming Zhou, Adarsh Vatsa, William Eiers

entry.summary: RAISE trains LLMs to synthesize formally verifiable Cedar access-control policies using CedarInstruct, a 5,800-scenario dataset with verified target policies, via verified SFT followed by reinforcement learning from symbolic verification signals. It shows frontier LLMs often violate intended authorization semantics and that verification-in-the-loop training improves them.

entry.title: Greenpixie's AI Token Methodology: Assessing the Energy, Water and CO2-eq Impact of AI Tokens for Open and Closed Weight Models

author.name: Joshua Horswill, Ross Hunter, Matt Clifford, James Hall

entry.summary: This paper presents a methodology for estimating per-token energy, water, and CO2-equivalent costs of LLM inference, separating prefill from decode tokens. It measures GPU energy empirically for open-weight models, estimates non-GPU server energy from inference wall time, fits Bayesian linear regression across model size and deployment configuration, and bins proprietary frontier models into size buckets using naming and performance priors. This fills an important transparency gap in AI environmental accounting.

entry.title: Same Winners, Different Success Rates: Evaluating How LLM Agents Recover from Failures

author.name: Dong Xu, Zhangfan Yang, Jiantao Wu, Shipeng Zhang, Zexuan Zhu, Jiangqiang Li, Jun Zhang, Junkai Ji

entry.summary: The paper shows that set agreement, the standard ordinal metric for checkpoint-based agent recovery benchmarks, can mask near-zero recovery success because failing actions tie at zero reward and produce identical tied sets. The authors formalize this via a set-path symmetry result and propose evaluation that reflects absolute performance levels.

entry.title: When Does Structured Knowledge Help Neural Theorem Proving?

author.name: Sareh Nabi, Roland Vogl, Marzieh Nabi

entry.summary: MathAgent builds a semantic knowledge graph (MathKG) over Mathlib, connecting 364 theorems and definitions with 9,434 typed semantic edges extracted via LLM-based relation extraction, and uses it to augment LLM theorem provers for Lean 4. A controlled ablation across four augmentation modes investigates when structured mathematical knowledge actually helps proving. The work probes the implicit semantic layer mathematicians use for analogy and generalization.

entry.title: Physics-Attested Federated Learning: Securing Collaborative Anomaly Detection in Critical Water Infrastructure

author.name: Jeff Nijsse, Shu Su, Benjamin Oholeguy, Sreenivas Sremath Tirumala

entry.summary: The paper introduces an admission gate for federated learning in cyber-physical systems that verifies updates against automatically mined physical invariants such as conservation laws, rather than relying only on update-space defenses. Evaluated on SWaT, WADI, and BATADAL testbeds across seven aggregation rules, it defends intrusion-detection models against data poisoning from fabricated telemetry. This bridges federated learning security with domain physics.

entry.title: When Text Matters: Design Principles for Visual Token Pruning in Vision-Language Model

author.name: Minchan Kang, Kyeonghye Park, Seoyoung Cho, Daeshik Kim, Yucheol Cho

entry.summary: The authors derive design principles for visual token pruning in large vision-language models, finding that applying textual guidance too early limits identification of answer-relevant regions, while text-to-visual attention is most informative at intermediate decoder depths. This motivates a training-free method that stages vision-guided pruning early and text-guided selection later. It reduces compute while preserving task-relevant visual information.

entry.title: Continuous Variational Synthesis

author.name: Alan N. Amin, Mattia G. Gollub, Andrei Slabodkin, Elizabeth B. Wood, Eli N. Weinstein

entry.summary: This work trains variational synthesis models, which control chemical reactions to manufacture designed DNA sequences, entirely in continuous space using gradient descent, then discretizes via post-training quantization to satisfy synthesis constraints. This avoids the difficult discrete optimization imposed by chemical hardware limits while achieving stringent reward criteria with diverse designs. The approach adapts quantization ideas from deep learning to biological design.

entry.title: Scaffold Then Internalize: Representation Injection for Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Han Fu, Jiacheng Chen, Baoquan Zhao, Weidong Chen, Wei Liu, Qing Li, Xudong Mao

entry.summary: This paper introduces REPI, a training framework for diffusion transformers that reverses the direction of REPA-style representation alignment: instead of projecting diffusion representations into an encoder space, it injects encoder representations into the denoising process. Projected representations act as a temporary scaffold that the diffusion model progressively internalizes. This offers a complementary route to faster diffusion transformer training.

entry.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Multi-Turn Image Editing

author.name: Liangbing Zhao, Le Zhuo, Mohamed Elhoseiny

entry.summary: MT-OPSD addresses rapid degradation of instruction-based image editing models under recursive multi-turn editing, attributing the failure to a train-test mismatch where models trained on clean sources must condition on their own imperfect outputs. The framework trains on self-generated conditioning states with editing supervision from a clean-conditioned teacher, requiring no multi-turn annotations, and introduces the LME-Bench evaluation. This matters for making iterative editing practical.

entry.title: ScopeIF: Improving Scope-Aware Precise Instruction-Following in Large Language Models via Graded Reward Modeling

author.name: Bosi Wen, Yilin Niu, Xiaoying Ning, Ying Zhang, Hongning Wang, Minlie Huang

entry.summary: ScopeIF is a training framework for precise instruction-following where constraints apply to specific response segments rather than the whole output. It introduces a schema factorizing constraints into decoupled dimensions, builds more diverse training data, and applies graded rather than binary per-constraint rewards.

entry.title: ExpVoyager: Direct Experience Navigation for Dynamic Agent Skill Synthesis

author.name: Kwangwook Seo, Dongha Lee

entry.summary: ExpVoyager reframes agent skill synthesis as dynamic navigation over raw experience rather than premature abstraction into fixed procedural knowledge. Existing approaches compress past experience before downstream demands are known, risking discarding critical knowledge and retaining irrelevant details. The method defers skill construction until runtime demands are clearer, supporting self-evolving LLM agents.

entry.title: How Far Do Persona Effects Generalize in Language Models?

author.name: Yufan Zhou, Yuxuan Liu, Enze Ma, Lyumanshan Ye, Zhongqi Yue, Robin De Croon, Yucheng Jin, Katrien Verbert, Zhao Wang

entry.summary: This study tests whether persona prompt effects are predictable and portable across models, tasks, and attributes, covering 57 attributes, three behavioral domains, and seven pairs of open 7-9B checkpoints. It finds persona effects can be predictable without being portable: borrowed gains from other model-pairs underperform shared scaling, with separate attribute and task components needed, most robustly in OLMo-3. This cautions against assuming persona-effect findings transfer across models.

entry.title: Turning Speech Language Models into Multilingual Listeners

author.name: Tol\'{u}lop\'{e} \`{O}g\'{u}nr\`{e}m\'{i}, Dan Jurafsky, Chris Manning, Ahmet \"Ust\"un, Martijn Bartelds

entry.summary: The authors present MULTISPEECHQA, a synthetic but human-verified dataset of 9,200 hours and 10.8 million spoken QA pairs across 23 typologically diverse languages, plus a benchmark for evaluating speech language models. They find a cascading ASR-LLM system outperforms open-weight SLMs though not closed ones. This directly addresses the scarcity of multilingual speech instruction data limiting access for millions of speakers.

entry.title: Does Learning to Predict the World Help Agents Act? Auditing World-Model Post-Training

author.name: Xinyu Che, Hang Yan, Yanchen Liu, Haochen Liu, Ruifeng Li, Anran Shi, Heng Wang, Jun Liu

entry.summary: The authors audit whether performance gains from world-model post-training of agents actually come from learning to predict the environment by replacing true next-observation targets with in-distribution mismatched ones. This control-based methodology can attribute gains to prediction itself versus generic optimization effects. It provides a valuable critical check on an increasingly popular training paradigm for agents.

entry.title: ManiEdit: Sequential Unstructured Knowledge Editing for Language Models from a Manifold Perspective

author.name: Rui Liu, Chenheng Zhang, Haoxuan Li, Zhouchen Lin

entry.summary: Reframes sequential knowledge editing of unstructured long-form knowledge as a localized displacement of an edit sub-manifold within the global knowledge manifold, addressing edit forgetting and general-capability degradation. The method identifies representative anchor edit points while preserving the rest of the manifold. It addresses a real gap, since most editing methods are designed for atomic structured facts.

entry.title: Faithful Activation Verbalization: Reducing Hallucinations in LLM Representation Interpretation

author.name: Haiyan Zhao, Zirui Hei, Wei Shi, Huiqi Deng, Na Zou, Mengnan Du

entry.summary: This work tackles hallucination in activation verbalization methods that decode LLM hidden states into natural language. AVPO uses a two-stage pipeline, reconstructing source text from an activation and validating it with a frozen QA model, then optimizes the inverter with DPO using rewards for semantic recoverability and lexical fidelity.

entry.title: CRISP: Cultural Reward Modeling for Implicit Situated Propriety

author.name: Zekun Yuan, Yangfan Ye, Baohang Li, Shuaibo Zhao, Zekun Zhou, Ziming Li, Qichen Hong, Kun Chen, Xiaocheng Feng

entry.summary: CRISP-RM is a culturally situated reward model that scores open-ended social responses for cultural appropriateness, paired with Norm Grounding Supervision during policy optimization to improve sensitivity to relevant cultural norms. The work targets implicit situated propriety in open-ended generation, beyond predefined-answer cultural knowledge benchmarks.

entry.title: When Words Fall Short: Iterative Synergy Between Verbalized Reasoning and Hidden Features for LLM Confidence Estimation

author.name: Yekun Xu, Ante Wang, Jingyi Ren, Xuanyi Chen, Weizhi Ma, Yang Liu

entry.summary: Challenging the view that verbalized confidence beats dedicated estimators, the authors show internal representations contain richer confidence signals, then propose IPoET, a framework iteratively combining verbalized reasoning traces with internal features for confidence estimation. This improves trustworthy LLM deployment via better calibrated uncertainty.

entry.title: Beyond Token Alignment: Event Completion for Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Jiacheng Liu, Jingwei Song, Qituan Zhang, Siheng Chen, Linfeng Zhang

entry.summary: Studies on-policy distillation between models with different tokenizers, where a teacher token may span multiple student tokens and the teacher specifies only the required byte-level completion, not how probability should split among valid continuations. Introduces Event-Set Completion to handle this ambiguity in constructing prediction targets.

entry.title: OpenWhistle: A Large-Scale Longitudinal Dataset and Benchmark of Bottlenose Dolphin Vocalizations

author.name: Faadil Mustun, Chiara Semenzin, Roberto Dessi, Pablo Robin Guerrero, Pierre Orhan, Alexis Emanuelli, Emanuele Rossi, Yair Lakretz, Gonzalo de Polavieja, German Sumbre

entry.summary: Releases OpenWhistle, the largest public dolphin vocalization dataset: about 180,000 whistles (114 hours) recorded over five years from a stable pod of five individuals in a semi-natural environment, with standardized benchmarks. It addresses the species-shallow, bird-centric bias of existing bioacoustics corpora.

entry.title: Decide, Don't Generate: Competitive Dimensional ABSA with Jev's Typed Decisions

author.name: Yiqun Zhang, Peidong Wang, Zihan Wang, Shi Feng

entry.summary: Shows that aspect-based sentiment analysis can be competitive without text generation by decomposing SemEval-2026 tasks into typed decisions made by a frozen model with rubric scores and yes/no judgments, with only 488 fitted coefficients on CPU. It achieves the lowest aggregate error in valence-arousal regression and beats fine-tuned Llama-3.3-70B and GPT-OSS-120B baselines on extraction tasks.

entry.title: MS-GLA: Multi-Scale Gated Linear Attention for Addressing Representational Bottlenecks via Multi-Temporal Resolution

author.name: Prasoon Dev, Anirudh Sankar, Vasudeva Varma

entry.summary: MS-GLA addresses a representational bottleneck in Gated Linear Attention transformers, where fixed-capacity memory matrices operate at a single temporal resolution and must encode both local syntax and long-range semantics. The proposed architecture distributes attention heads across multiple temporal resolutions, letting coarser heads specialize in long-range dependencies while finer heads retain local sensitivity. This is a targeted architectural refinement for efficient sequence modeling.

entry.title: On Evaluating and Improving Conversational Agents in Production

author.name: Kasra Hosseini, Wen-Sen Cheng, Marco-Andrea Buchmann, Emir Mulabegovic, Weiwei Cheng

entry.summary: This paper presents an evaluation framework for a large-scale, multi-agent production shopping assistant, tackling three obstacles: non-replayability of logged conversations, stochasticity of both system and environment, and the opacity of aggregate quality scores. The framework isolates behavioral causes of quality changes for reported issues. It offers rare, valuable insight into real production LLM-system evaluation practice.

entry.title: Retrieved but Not Delivered: Multimodal Memory Delivery for Long-Term Agents

author.name: Yuhang Jiang, Qingwei Liao, Kaize Yin, Xingling Liu, Luca Cuomo, Silvio Bacci

entry.summary: This paper identifies a previously unisolated stage in multimodal agent memory pipelines, delivery, namely what form retrieved memory reaches the model. With retrieved evidence fixed, delivering original pixels instead of withholding them raises accuracy by 13.87 points on an 8B backbone, versus only 2.31 points from perfecting retrieval, and the delivery term dominates across three MemLens backbones. The proposed DeliverMem method shows that delivery, not retrieval, may be the larger bottleneck for multimodal long-term agents.

entry.title: Adaptive Consistency Graph for Long-Horizon Agents

author.name: Jiecong Wang, Hao Peng, Zhanyi Wang

entry.summary: Proposes ACG, a persistent graph that incrementally organizes execution evidence and provenance, then builds temporary requirement-centered views per decision under a bounded context budget to prevent drift in long-horizon agent tasks. It augments rather than replaces the base agent's planner and executor.

entry.title: Semantic Prefix Oracles for LLM Decoding: Contracts and Differential Validation

author.name: Paul Kronlund-Drouault

entry.summary: The paper introduces semantic grammar specifications, a declarative formalism attaching semantic constraints (scope, typing, declaration effects) to a context-free surface executed during Earley descent, with safe pruning that rejects only unrepairable prefixes. It provides formal contracts including dead-end freedom plus sufficient conditions, validated differentially.

entry.title: Persistence Forcing: Exploiting Feature Specialization in Pixel-Space Diffusion

author.name: Chong Wang, Zixuan Fu, Shiqi Huang, Siyuan Yang, Hao Cheng, Bihan Wen

entry.summary: This paper introduces heterogeneous refinement in pixel-space diffusion Transformers, assigning different feature groups distinct refinement budgets across depth. This induces an ordered feature specialization where sparsely refined features encode global structure and heavily refined features specialize in local texture and detail. The approach exploits the multi-granularity organization of natural images to improve efficiency and quality of pixel-space diffusion generation.

entry.title: Towards Scalable Context-Aware Single-Cell Spatial Transcriptomics Prediction from Histology Images

author.name: Zijun Gao, Chunbin Gu, Jinxi Xiang, Xiangde Luo, Pheng-Ann Heng

entry.summary: This work extends gene-expression prediction from H&E histology images to single-cell resolution, addressing the scale mismatch where pathology foundation models mix multiple cells in patch-level representations while per-cell cropping distorts morphology and removes context. The proposed context-aware approach balances pretrained-encoder capacity with per-cell fidelity, overcoming limitations of both naive foundation-model application and segmentation-only pipelines. Single-cell resolution preserves cellular heterogeneity that spot-level aggregation obscures.

entry.title: Learning via Self-Consistency for Diffusion-based Video Reasoning

author.name: Zhenghao Ni, Weimin Qiu, Meng Tang

entry.summary: This work shows that diffusion-based video generation models exhibit zero-shot visual reasoning capabilities that can be improved with self-consistency, analogous to chain-of-thought self-consistency in LLMs. The authors introduce a training-free test-time scaling method that samples multiple video generations and aggregates extracted paths, locations, or masks into consensus predictions. It matters because it offers a cheap way to improve the reliability of video models on deterministic downstream vision tasks.

entry.title: Sparse cubical complexes for efficient topology-preservation in image data

author.name: Alexander H. Berger, Marco Fontana, Daniel Rueckert, Johannes C. Paetzold, Laurin Lux, Ulrich Bauer

entry.summary: This paper argues that the runtime cost of persistent homology in image applications is dominated by processing topologically unimportant information, and proposes sparse cubical filtrations that reduce PH computation cost by up to 100x on real datasets while closely approximating results. This makes topology-preserving objectives feasible for segmentation.

entry.title: SAM Meets VLM: Parameter-Decoupled Full-Parameter Training for Unified Medical Reasoning and Segmentation

author.name: Xuyang Cao, Enyou Liu, Jun Zhao, Zhuoyun Liu, Jintao Fei, Leo

entry.summary: This paper proposes a parameter-decoupled training framework that unifies medical VLM reasoning with SAM-style pixel-level segmentation, treating a special hidden state as a semantic-to-spatial prompt for the mask decoder. The decoupling resolves conflicts between image-level reasoning and pixel-level segmentation requirements on the shared representation space.

entry.title: Anatomy-Aware Prediction of Bronchoscopic Accessibility from 3D CT

author.name: Linkai Peng, Cuiling Sun, Bin Wang, Jamie Rowell, Catherine Gao, Oyku Ikizgul, Eminenur Sentasci, Andrea Bejar, Halil Ertugrul Aktas, Gorkem Durak, Momen Wahidi, Christopher Kapp, Ulas Bagci

entry.summary: The paper formalizes bronchoscopy accessibility prediction as a supervised learning task and presents the first end-to-end framework for it, using an Anatomy-Aware Mixture-of-Experts model with dedicated CT, lobe, and path-geometry experts. It also curates the first clinical dataset of 438 cases with pre-operative annotations.

entry.title: Attention-Scoped Guidance: Training-Free Spatial Control for Image Editing

author.name: Zeyan Li, Wei Zhou, Hadi Amirpour, Minghao Zou, Panqi Yang, Jianfeng Xu

entry.summary: Attention-Scoped Guidance (ASG) is a training-free sampler wrapper for instruction-guided image editing that makes dual classifier-free guidance weights spatial, reading a soft support map from the instruction attention already computed by the editor. It strengthens image anchoring in edited regions and weakens text guidance elsewhere, with no training, external masks, or extra network evaluations, showing gains on MagicBrush and PIE-Bench.

entry.title: VoxelSage: Tool-Augmented 3D CT Analysis and Simulator-Shielded Sequential Resection Planning for Liver Tumors

author.name: Binghong Qian, Xuanhe Liu, Yifan Xing, Wenjie Deng, Jian Wu, Haochao Ying

entry.summary: VoxelSage is a multimodal system for 3D CT liver-tumor analysis and preoperative resection planning with a dual-port architecture that separates language-model orchestration from image computation, keeping physical measurements out of the LLM and in deterministic code. It integrates visualization, segmentation-based measurement, evidence return, and simulator-shielded sequential planning of resections.

entry.title: ReCaVSR: One-Step Streaming Diffusion Video Super-Resolution with Recycled Latents and Learned Cache Routing

author.name: Xijun Wang, Xin Li, Suhang Yao, Zirui Lang, Bingchen Li, Zhibo Chen

entry.summary: ReCaVSR is a one-step diffusion framework for real-time streaming video super-resolution built on Wan2.2, combining learned layer-wise KV-cache routing with recycled super-resolution latents that carry local temporal context. This reduces the historical context each new frame needs, enabling low-latency generative fidelity for online video.

entry.title: VISTA: Internalizing Collective Visual Experience via On-Policy Distillation for Active Multimodal Agents

author.name: Zheng Jiang, Houde Qian, Yiming Chen, Ling Li, Chaoyang Li, Yueqi Li, Yuxuan Liu, Lifeng Sun

entry.summary: VISTA improves active multimodal agents by turning visual observations from same-input RL rollouts into shared supervision through collective visual experience distillation, plus a heterogeneity-aware policy improvement step that reinforces successful trajectories. This makes better use of complementary discoveries that outcome-based group advantages discard.

entry.title: PowerSim: Differentiable Physics Simulation and Rendering with Power Diagrams

author.name: Trong-Tung Nguyen, Anand Bhattad

entry.summary: PowerSim couples PowerFoam's power-diagram-based 3D scene representation directly to Material Point Method simulation, exploiting the alignment between primitive properties and MPM quantities so simulated motion drives geometry and appearance without an intermediate representation. Applications include interactive scene simulation, material field recovery, and more. It brings differentiable dynamics to a compact 3D representation.

entry.title: One-Step Next-Latent Prediction Is Not a World Model

author.name: Shitong Wang, Zhongang Cai, Yuzhou Hong

entry.summary: This paper argues formally that one-step next-latent prediction (as in LeNEPA) does not yield a world model, since a fitted conditional mean is a transition kernel only in special cases: for linear-Gaussian latents, open-loop squared error at horizon K grows with K even after an exact one-step fit, and composing nonlinear mean maps is not the multistep solution. It provides a sharp theoretical critique of conflating one-step regression objectives with rollout-capable world models. This is a timely caution for the world-model literature.

entry.title: Pow3R-SLAM: Real-Time RGB-D SLAM with 3D Reconstruction Priors

author.name: Christopher Kolios, Ishaan Mehta, Sasa Janjic, Yeganeh Bahoo, Sajad Saeedi

entry.summary: Pow3R-SLAM extends MASt3R-SLAM-style two-view 3D reconstruction priors to RGB-D SLAM by using depth as a prior on network predictions rather than as geometry to fuse, yielding better-conditioned pointmaps and inferring missing depths. Evaluated on TUM, 7-Scenes, and Replica, it runs 1.6x faster in wall time than MASt3R-SLAM with improved accuracy. This makes learning-based SLAM more practical in real time.

entry.title: Scouting the Dynamics Gap: Test-Time Policy Adaptation via Action-Outcome Feedback

author.name: Yishu Li, Liyuan Geng, Xinyi Mao, Amber Li, David Held

entry.summary: SCOUT is a dynamics-aware meta-learning framework enabling manipulation policies to rapidly adapt at deployment by revising internal beliefs about environment dynamics. It couples an action-prediction policy with a forward dynamics model through a shared belief latent space, exploiting rich geometric feedback from physical interaction rather than sparse scalar rewards.

entry.title: Learning Expressive and Compositional Motion Representation via Spectral Skills

author.name: Feiyang Wu, Chenxiao Gao, Chen Yang, Ye Zhao, Bo Dai, Anqi Wu

entry.summary: The paper introduces spectral skills, a latent command interface between hierarchical planners and controllers for humanoid robots, learned via predictive representation learning rather than input reconstruction. Spectral skills compactly encode short motion segments and support composition of new behaviors, demonstrated on a 29-DoF humanoid where the controller conditioned on these latents improves execution fidelity.

entry.title: WayFinder: Hierarchical Visual-Language-Action for Zero-Shot Waypoint Generation and Low-Level Kinematic Control

author.name: Timothy K Johnsen, Marco Levorato

entry.summary: WayFinder is a hierarchical VLA framework that decouples high-level waypoint generation by an offboard multimodal LLM from lightweight onboard real-time kinematic control, avoiding costly per-robot fine-tuning. The closed-loop, asynchronous design targets reliable real-world deployment of VLA models on arbitrary embodiments. Its significance lies in addressing the two main bottlenecks of VLA deployment: unreliable execution and prohibitive fine-tuning cost.

entry.title: Can Representation Learning Decouple from Loss Minimization? Polar Updates Have an Answer

author.name: Akash Kumar

entry.summary: Studies matrix Muon optimization near the edge of stability, showing period-2 loss oscillations where mean loss plateaus yet weights keep moving and learned features continue aligning with the teacher subspace. Provides explicit cycle and alignment formulas for linear teacher-student settings and plateau/decay bounds for a mean-field ReLU model.

entry.title: Scalable Diffusion SBI for Compositional Inference under Simulator Misspecification

author.name: Vincent D. Zaballa, Elliot E. Hui

entry.summary: Develops sampling and fine-tuning methods for diffusion-based simulation-based inference in design-conditional settings with many heterogeneous observations, hierarchical latents, and simulator misspecification. Contributions include a continuous-time diffusion coefficient for compositional score inference and Hierarchical Blockwise Diffusion Sampling using a single pretrained model with a learned misspecification corrector.

entry.title: The effects of an “algorithmic monoculture” depend on the details

author.name: Adam Zewe | MIT News

entry.summary: MIT researchers systematically evaluated major objections to algorithmic monoculture — the concern that identical algorithms across an industry create systematic exclusion, as when a candidate rejected by one firm's resume screener is rejected by all. They find many objections fail or are not decisive in all forms, and mathematically prove that monoculture instead tends to create informational echo chambers that hinder exploration. The work nuances the dominant harms narrative with formal analysis.

entry.title: More Programs or More Rolls? Separating Coverage from Specialization in LLM Harnesses

author.name: Ziyang Xu, Haitian Zhong, Hao Zhou, Hao Qin, Chenhan Jin, Te Qi, Shengze Xu, Tieyong Zeng

entry.summary: This study disentangles whether gains from automatically generated LLM harnesses come from genuine task specialization or merely from repeated execution coverage, using controlled comparisons including byte-identical baseline copies. Findings show identical programs yield substantial repeat-averaged oracle headroom, and generated programs mainly expose persistent weaknesses rather than true specialization.

entry.title: An Empirical Study and Assessment of EU AI Act Compliance Checkers

author.name: Zhen Tao, Alize Kahraman, Shidong Pan, Zhenchang Xing, Chiara Ullstein, Jens Grossklags, Chunyang Chen

entry.summary: This paper empirically evaluates automated EU AI Act compliance checkers (AIACCs), tools intended to help developers and smaller organizations translate legal obligations into engineering practices. The study assesses how well these tools cover security, privacy, transparency, robustness, and data governance requirements. It matters because it provides the first systematic quality assessment of a rapidly growing tool category at the intersection of AI governance and engineering.

entry.title: Can AI Scientists Change Their Minds? Prior-Evidence Conflict in Synthetic Universes

author.name: Kargi Chauhan

entry.summary: This paper introduces Synthetic Universes, a benchmark pairing canonical famous physical worlds with matched twisted twins governed by nearby noncanonical mechanisms, testing whether AI scientists truly infer laws from evidence or merely recognize priors. In an interim 20-twin-trial analysis, 8 trials pass predictive verification while only 5 recover the generating mechanism, with dissociation in both directions. The work measures belief updating under prior-evidence conflict.

entry.title: ARC-KV: Amortizing Anchor Search for Reconstruction-Based KV Cache Compaction

author.name: Zheyu Shen, Guanhua Wang, Dezhan Tu, Mengchi Zhang, Yanjia Li, Adnan Aziz, Chunqiang Tang, Ang Li

entry.summary: ARC-KV accelerates reconstruction-based KV cache compaction by learning a reusable anchor-selection policy across contexts while retaining context-specific reconstruction, amortizing the iterative anchor search that dominates attention-matching costs. This targets long-context inference where KV caches grow linearly with sequence length.

entry.title: SimpleEvol: An Agent-Loop Framework for LLM-Driven Automated Heuristic Design with Minimal Human Priors

author.name: Jianghan Zhu, Cong Zhang, Rongjie Zhu, Chi Zhang, Zhiguang Cao

entry.summary: Argues that current automated heuristic design frameworks misuse LLMs as narrow fixed components within hand-engineered evolutionary loops, violating the bitter lesson principle. SimpleEvol instead places the LLM at the center of a minimal agent-loop framework with few human priors, letting stronger LLM capabilities translate directly into better heuristic design.

entry.title: KV-Kaizen: Learning Context-Adaptive Cache Compression Choices

author.name: Joao Monteiro, Louis B\'ethune, Anastasiia Filippova, Sonia Laguna, David Grangier, Marco Cuturi

entry.summary: Proposes learning a selector that produces per-layer KV cache configurations under an overall compression budget, avoiding the riskiness of token eviction. The selector operates along axes including sharing one cache across layers, giving context-adaptive compression choices that mitigate the memory-bound decoding bottleneck of long-context LLMs.

entry.title: Retrieval-Augmented Skill Optimization via Cross-Harness Adaptation

author.name: Jaewon Chu, Ji Soo Lee, Jihwan Park, Dohwan Ko, Jeehye Na, Seunghun Lee, Taehoon Lee, Minseo Yoon, Minseok Joo, Yunyang Xiong, Hyunwoo J. Kim

entry.summary: This paper proposes RASO (Retrieval-Augmented Skill Optimization), a framework that improves agent skills — reusable natural-language task guides — by retrieving and adapting relevant skills from a large public corpus rather than relying solely on costly agent rollouts. By treating the accumulated ecosystem of publicly shared skills as prior knowledge and adapting them across different harnesses, RASO aims to make skill optimization cheaper and more effective. The work is significant because it shifts skill optimization from a from-scratch, trial-and-error process toward leveraging community-scale prior knowledge, echoing the retrieval-augmentation trend at the skill level.

entry.title: Constructing Challenging Browser-Use Tasks by Controlled Environment Interventions

author.name: Xunjian Yin, Tianchen Guan, Jinao Wang, Weili Cao, Daisy Xinlei Lin, Royce Cheng-Yue, Keagan Long, Kyle Wong, Bhuwan Dhingra, Xiangjun Wang, Shuyan Zhou

entry.summary: BreakingWeb makes browser-agent task difficulty programmable by pairing solvable base tasks with deterministic, detectable, recoverable interventions at different layers of the web stack, preserving the user instruction and success criterion. This enables controlled study of what actually makes tasks hard and cheap refreshing of benchmarks as agents improve.

entry.title: Draft in Parallel, Condition Through Depth: Adjacent Causal Injection for Speculative Decoding

author.name: Haohui Zhang, Keyu Chen, Haocheng Sun, Weibo Gu, Ruizhi Qiao, Xing Sun, Bo Jiang

entry.summary: The paper proposes DSpine, a speculative decoding drafter that injects causal conditioning at every layer of the backbone via gated adjacent injection, rather than deferring conditional decoding to a lightweight post-backbone module. Built on analysis showing early positions form recoverable predictions in shallow layers, this improves acceptance of consistent draft continuations for faster inference.

entry.title: AdaKerNet: Neural Kernel Decoding for Task-Adaptive Prediction with Multimodal Large Models

author.name: Konstantinos D. Polyzos, Eleni Oikonomou, Tara Javidi

entry.summary: AdaKerNet is a learnable task-adaptive neural kernel decoder that adapts frozen multimodal foundation models to downstream tasks without accessing or fine-tuning model parameters. It works solely on frozen representations, making it applicable to closed-source models and low-supervision settings. This addresses a practical limitation of both fine-tuning and neural decoders under limited data.

entry.title: FocusVTC: Efficient and High-Performance Visual Text Compression with Adaptive Resolution

author.name: FangZhi Zhong, Xuerui Qiu, Yuqi Pan, Ya Liu, Shaowei Gu, Bo Xu, Guoqi Li

entry.summary: FocusVTC improves visual text compression, which reduces LLM input length by rendering text as images, by combining compressed low-DPI global views with selective high-resolution region enhancement to break the token-versus-legibility trade-off of fixed-resolution rendering. It includes a 29.4K-example Reasoning-Evidence Localization CoT dataset linking reasoning traces to relevant regions. The method preserves general multimodal capabilities while cutting context costs.

entry.title: NesTok: Nested Self-Aligned 1D Tokenizer for Autoregressive Image Generation

author.name: Jiawei Zhang, Shuhao Liu, Rong Huang, Yuancheng Li, Zhihui Li, Xiaojun Chang, Changlin Li

entry.summary: NesTok improves 1D variable-length visual tokenizers, which let autoregressive image generators trade off quality versus compute using a single tokenizer. Its cross-length training jointly optimizes reconstruction across token lengths, with full-length sequences guiding shorter ones, addressing capacity underuse in nested-dropout approaches. This improves the efficiency-quality frontier for AR image generation.

entry.title: AeroManip-VLA: Scalable Vision-Language-Action Learning for Aerial Manipulation with RL-Generated Demonstrations

author.name: Rui Huang, Yanlin Mu, Lidong Li, Yucong Wang, Zichen Yan, Lin Zhao

entry.summary: AeroManip-VLA presents a scalable benchmark for aerial manipulation with vision-language-action models, using RL-generated demonstrations to overcome the cost and difficulty of collecting data on physical aerial platforms. It addresses challenges unique to aerial manipulation: tight flight-manipulation coupling, changing observations, and safety-critical contact. This extends the VLA paradigm to a domain ground robots cannot reach.

entry.title: MotionInsight: Diagnosing Object Motion Deficiencies in Generated Videos

author.name: Jiahao Zhan, Yongrui Ma, Qunliang Xing, Xuanyu Zhang, Jingqi Tong, Junlin Li, Li zhang, Shijie Zhao, Tianfan Xue

entry.summary: The paper introduces VidMotion, a diagnostic dataset of 6,879 videos with designated moving objects and fine-grained annotations of dimension-wise scores and failure causes, plus MotionInsight, an evaluator for object-centric motion fidelity. It assesses object consistency, motion continuity, and physical plausibility, shifting evaluation from implicit RGB-frame observation to explicit motion-space analysis. This fills a gap left by aesthetics- and alignment-focused video quality metrics.

entry.title: A Comprehensive View of Fairness through Distributional Stability

author.name: Gayane Taturyan, Charlotte Laclau, Stephan Cl\'emencon

entry.summary: The paper reframes fairness as distributional stability: a predictor is fair if its predictions remain stable under perturbations that modify the composition of protected groups. Classical fairness notions emerge as stability against specific perturbations, with unfairness gaps expressed as Lipschitz constants of a prediction-rate functional. This yields uniform guarantees over demographic compositions without knowing the deployment distribution.
