It offers a replay-adjacent but gradient-based alternative for continual learning with minimal stored data.

entry.title: UniCache: Task- and Type-Aware KV Cache Compression for Unified Multimodal Models

author.name: Wanqi Yang, Yuexiao Ma, Mei Xie, Xiawu Zheng, Shiwei Liu

entry.summary: UniCache compresses KV caches in unified multimodal models by accounting for how cache types and their importance differ across tasks like understanding, generation, and editing. This addresses the growing memory and access cost of long multimodal contexts that single-policy compression schemes handle poorly.

entry.title: Last-Iterate Guarantees for Online Reinforcement Learning in Structured Constrained MDPs

author.name: Nam Phuong Tran, Trinh Ha Mai Huynh, Tuyen Pham Le, Van-Truong Nguyen, Quan Nguyen, Long Tran-Thanh

entry.summary: This paper develops a statistically efficient framework for last-iterate convergence guarantees in structured Constrained MDPs, addressing safety-critical settings where a single deployed policy must satisfy performance and constraints directly. The analysis separates contraction of regularized primal-dual dynamics from actor approximation and statistical errors under online exploration, extending prior tabular/exact-gradient results to large-state problems.

entry.title: Algorithmic Harms Associated with Generative Model-Augmented Recommendation Systems

author.name: Christine Herlihy, Xumei Xi, Shloka Desai, Kevin Bannerman Hutchful, Pedro Silva

entry.summary: This paper extends existing taxonomies of algorithmic harms to cover generative models integrated into non-conversational recommendation systems, introducing new causal drivers of representational and quality-of-service harms plus endogenous harms like sanitization. It also provides a causal analysis of how problematic input-output subsets arise when system inputs misalign with designer objectives or model priors.

entry.title: Teach Yourself Where to Look: On-Policy Attention Self-Distillation for Reasoning

author.name: Safaeid Hossain Arib, Rabeya Akter, Ismam Nur Swapnil, Md. Faiyaz Abdullah Sayeedi, Tasnim Mohiuddin, Md Mofijul Islam

entry.summary: OPASD extends on-policy self-distillation for reasoning models by distilling not only token distributions but also attention patterns from a privileged teacher that can see verified solutions. Teacher attention is projected onto student-visible positions and renormalized before alignment, and the method improves competition-level math reasoning across three model sizes.

entry.title: MultiEcho: An Experimental Science of Learned Worlds

author.name: Meng Zhu, Airui Zhang

entry.summary: MultiEcho proposes studying world models as experimental systems by estimating their response laws through controlled counterfactual interventions across nine simulated physical systems and seven frozen model configurations. The framework separately measures response predictability, intervention readability, and physical correspondence, finding that locally describable responses can still poorly match physical effects.

entry.title: Optimal Transport Dropout for Structured Predictive Uncertainty

author.name: Giacomo Lorenzon, Francesco Regazzoni

entry.summary: Optimal Transport Dropout (OTD) jointly learns a predictive mapping and the law of latent perturbations, improving on Monte Carlo dropout whose fixed factorized masking law is prescribed a priori. This yields better-calibrated predictive distributions from deterministic networks and neural operators without training ensembles.

entry.title: Chameleon: Dynamic Format Adapter for Efficient Diffusion

author.name: Arnab Sanyal, Sandeep Chinchali

entry.summary: Chameleon is a post-training quantization framework for diffusion models that fixes bit-width but treats the number format itself as a discrete variable, selected per weight channel and per layer-timestep activation bucket. This adapts to distributions shifting from heavy-tailed noise-dominated to structured across the diffusion trajectory, unlike existing PTQ schemes that fix format in advance.

entry.title: SLP-ProbHard: Probabilistic Hard-Constrained Learning via Structural Latent Parameterization

author.name: Wondesen Teshome Bekele, Marco D'Oria

entry.summary: SLP-ProbHard introduces a framework for probabilistic predictors that satisfy hard structural constraints in every stochastic realization by parameterizing predictions through a feasible latent map rather than projecting ambient predictions. The Structural Feasible Latent Parameterization defines the predictive law itself, including support and boundary probabilities.

entry.title: SafeMol: Dual-Modality Safety Alignment for Molecular Multimodal Models

author.name: Xinmiao Wang, Ruijie Wang, Menghui Wang, Jiawei Chen, Haoyue Deng, Ran Zhang, Xingxuan Zhang, Xiao Wang

entry.summary: This paper reveals substantial jailbreak vulnerabilities in molecular multimodal models under both text-only and graph-conditioned settings, and introduces SafeMolBench with 3702 samples covering 618 hazardous molecules. The benchmark supports unified training and evaluation across safety, over-refusal, and utility.

entry.title: Towards Eliminating Catastrophic Forgetting in the Curriculum Learning of Math Reasoning Tasks

author.name: Zengyan Yang, Yangyang Wu, Kai Huang, Pengfei Lyu, Tianyi Zhang, Mengying Zhu

entry.summary: This paper analyzes catastrophic forgetting in curriculum learning for math reasoning, proving theoretically that forgetting stems from divergence of task optima that is itself tied to curriculum learning's faster convergence, so it cannot be fully eliminated. The authors augment training with mitigation mechanisms informed by parameter update dynamics. It matters because it reframes forgetting as an inherent tradeoff rather than a fixable defect.

entry.title: Binding Multiple Modalities via Multimodal Wasserstein Barycenter

author.name: Xiaole Tang, Jiayi Xu, Xiang Gu, Yan Yang, Jian Sun

entry.summary: BaryBind establishes a balanced n-modal representation space by transporting a reference modality toward the Wasserstein barycenter optimized across all modalities, plus a volumetric alignment objective, avoiding dependence on a single binding modality like text. This approximates shared semantics while respecting the holistic geometry of multimodal data. Relevant to contrastive multimodal learning beyond pairwise alignment.

entry.title: MinkowskiPE: Minkowski Positional Encoding for Spatiotemporal Perception

author.name: Yuhao Li, Louie Hong Yao, Tianyi Shi, Hanqun Cao, Hongxia Hao, Zhen Zhao, Shengchao Liu

entry.summary: Proposes Minkowski Positional Encoding, which parameterizes Lorentz transformations of query and key features using joint space-time coordinates to give attention models an explicit relativistic geometric bias. This aims to combine the flexibility of learned architectures with stronger inductive priors for spatiotemporal coupling across scales in physical intelligence applications.

entry.title: From HL to H+L-1 Parameters: A Hankel-Toeplitz Forecaster for Long-Term Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Chaoqi Zhang, Yu Wang, Haixu Tang

entry.summary: Derives a compact linear forecaster grounded in classical stationary prediction theory, showing the minimum-MSE finite-window linear predictor factors into Hankel cross-covariance and inverse Toeplitz covariance structures requiring only H+L-1 autocorrelations. The resulting Hankel-Toeplitz Forecaster learns a single impulse response defining both an inverse filter and a forecast map.

entry.title: Fisher-Informed Recalibration for Feedback-Based On-Policy Self-Distillation of LLMs

author.name: Seohyun Lee, Dong-Jun Han, Seyyedali Hosseinalipour, Christopher G. Brinton

entry.summary: FIRE addresses unstable optimization and performance collapse in feedback-based on-policy self-distillation of LLMs using a dual-branch scheme: re-weighted SFT for correct outputs and Fisher-information-informed recalibration of supervision for incorrect ones. This improves the stability of training where a single model acts as both teacher and student.

entry.title: TRACE: Expert-Aligned ECG Representation Learning with Rigorous Benchmarking and Real-World Validation in Acute Cardiac Care

author.name: Lovely Yeswanth Panchumarthi, Andrew Lu, Saurabh Kataria, Delgersuren Bold, Minxiao Wang, Runze Yan, Patricia Dykes, Brian J. Gow, Tom J. Pollard, Jessica K. Z\`egre-Hemsey, Dillon J. Dzikowicz, Lekshmi Kumar, Xiao Hu, Ran Xiao

entry.summary: TRACE is a multimodal ECG representation model that jointly learns unimodal and cross-modal representations via uncertainty-weighted multi-task learning, using an LLM pipeline to extract high-fidelity findings from cardiologist reports. It is benchmarked extensively and validated in real-world acute cardiac care settings, addressing noise in CLIP-style clinical text pairing.

entry.title: SPINET: Sheaf Protein Inverse Folding Network

author.name: Jens Lundsgaard, Colin Mikulski, Zhixuan Yan, Dhananjay Bhaskar

entry.summary: SPINET introduces inverse protein folding conditioned on protein motion, predicting amino acid sequences from molecular dynamics trajectories rather than a single fixed backbone. It uses cellular sheaves to model residue interactions per frame with recurrent units integrating across frames, outperforming static and ensemble baselines on mdCATH and ATLAS benchmarks.

entry.title: Epistemic Learning from Imprecise Annotation

author.name: Kaizheng Wang, Siu Lun Chau

entry.summary: This paper introduces a framework for learning from credal supervision, using convex sets of plausible labelling distributions (credal sets) to train sets of predictive distributions that expose what annotation evidence leaves unresolved. It instantiates this with a pessimistic-optimistic credal classifier combining worst-case and best-case heads whose output spread provides uncertainty quantification.

entry.title: FAST-Brain: A Flow-Aligned Spatio-Temporal Surrogate Brain Model

author.name: Shucheng Liu, Changchun Shi, Kai Zhang, Hongtu Zhu

entry.summary: FAST-Brain is a surrogate model for resting-state fMRI that combines a flow-aligned generative framework predicting clean BOLD signals, a graph convolutional network for anatomical spatial structure, and a Transformer for long-horizon temporal dynamics. It addresses spatial structure, long-horizon dynamics, and the low-dimensional intrinsic subspace of high-dimensional signals in a unified model.

entry.title: On the Relation Between Interval Regret and Dynamic Regret

author.name: Yi-Han Wang, Peng Zhao, Zhi-Hua Zhou

entry.summary: This theoretical paper clarifies the long-unclear relationship between interval regret and dynamic regret, two key metrics for non-stationary online learning that were often assumed to be ordered by strength. The authors establish the precise logical relationship between the two notions, correcting prior intuition and informing algorithm design for changing environments.

entry.title: Livin' on a Prior: Likelihood Score Approximation for Inverse Problems

author.name: Rostislav Makarov, Tal Peer, Danilo de Oliveira, Timo Gerkmann

entry.summary: This paper introduces Likelihood Score Approximation (LSA), a generative framework for inverse problems that keeps a pretrained unconditional generative model frozen and learns a small observation-conditioned model approximating the likelihood score from paired samples. It spans the gap between known degradation models and fully conditional models, handling unknown degradations from few paired examples. This matters for applications like speech and image restoration where degradation operators are only partially known.

entry.title: Shallow Queries, Mature Values: Depth-Asynchronous Self-Speculation for Looped Transformers

author.name: Guanghao Li, Zihan Su, Hao Yu, Jinyang Jiang, Tao Ren, Zehao Li, Feng Lu, Ming Tang, Chun Yuan

entry.summary: This paper observes that in looped transformers, queries and keys converge to their final-depth representations earlier than values, and that mature values substantially improve shallow draft predictions. Building on this asymmetry, Depth-Asynchronous Self-Speculation (DAS) decouples the depth of draft computation from the depth of verified-prefix representations, accelerating autoregressive decoding of looped transformers via self-speculation. This reduces the heavy sequential cost of looped-model inference.

entry.title: Deep Weighted Bellman Residual Minimization for $Q^*$ Estimation

author.name: Lican Kang, Jerry Zhijian Yang, Cheng Yuan, Chen Zhong

entry.summary: The authors introduce a weighted Bellman residual minimization framework for off-policy evaluation in offline RL, combining density ratio weighting with integration of expert demonstrations and behavioral data. The method relaxes the conventional completeness assumption and establishes a sharp convergence rate for density ratio estimation.

entry.title: Tilted Schr\"odinger Bridge Matching

author.name: Sergei Kholkin, Evgeny Burnaev, Alexander Korotin

entry.summary: The authors introduce Tilted Schrodinger Bridge Matching (TSBM), a post-training method for fine-tuning a learned Schrodinger bridge toward a reward-tilted target distribution while preserving the source distribution. They formulate the adaptation as alternating optimization with theoretical justification and derive a practical algorithm via adjoint matching.

entry.title: Edge-Level Automorphism in GNNs: A Quantitative Framework and Effective Designs For Link Prediction

author.name: Chen Shao, Donald Loveland, Tobias K\"afer, Danai Koutra

entry.summary: The authors introduce a quantitative framework for assessing GNN expressiveness at the edge level, formalizing edge automorphism to explain why standard message-passing GNNs collapse structurally equivalent nodes and hurt link prediction. They also propose architectural designs that improve link prediction performance. This offers a more empirical alternative to qualitative Weisfeiler-Lehman style analysis.

entry.title: From Attention Sensitivity to Layer Role: Revisiting Mixed-Precision Quantization of Transformers

author.name: Nafiseh HosseinpourFardi, Negar Alihadi, Mahmoudreza Babaei, Milad Hosseini, Adrian Weller

entry.summary: JAB reformulates mixed-precision quantization of transformer attention by optimizing a single scalar loss over the joint Q, K, V weights against the block's actual causally-masked attention output, then reusing it for both weight fitting and knapsack-based bit allocation across blocks. This better tracks how projection errors compound in the softmax than per-matrix proxies. Relevant to efficient LLM deployment.

entry.title: Retrieval-Augmented Diffusion Modeling for Stochastic Discount Factor Portfolios

author.name: Kelvin J. L. Koa, Xinyang Li, Ke-Wei Huang

entry.summary: This paper introduces RADAR, a retrieval-augmented diffusion framework for portfolio optimization under the stochastic discount factor model. It learns market state representations that handle non-stationary regimes and state-dependent uncertainty, addressing the limitations of standard isotropic Gaussian noise assumptions in diffusion models applied to finance.

entry.title: Disentangling Lung-Cancer CT/LDCT AI: A Systematic Evidence Map of Clinical Tasks, Evidence Chains, and Translational Gaps

author.name: Surajit Das

entry.summary: A systematic evidence map of 293 studies (2016-2026) on CT/low-dose CT AI for lung cancer, classifying clinical tasks and building a Multi-Tier Evidence Graph. It reveals major translational gaps: external validation in only 29% of studies and low rates of calibration, decision-curve analysis, and explainability analyses.

entry.title: SpikeCredit: Temporal Credit Carrier for Reinforcement Learning with Sparse Rewards

author.name: Yingchao Yu, Pengfei Sun, Wenxuan Pan, Wei Chen, Yitian Hong, Kuangrong Hao, Yaochu Jin

entry.summary: Proposes SpikeCredit, a framework using spiking neural networks as Temporal Credit Carriers for reinforcement learning under sparse rewards, exploiting graded membrane traces and event-driven spikes to preserve credit-relevant information over time. Includes task-adaptive carrier selection and a fast reading pathway with self-motion feedback constraints.

entry.title: Let the Neurons Die: Exploiting ReLU-Induced Model Degradation

author.name: Kexin Li, Wenjun Qiu, Joshua Abraham, Aditi Maheshwari, David Lie

entry.summary: The paper presents three training-time availability attacks that exploit ReLU dying-neuron dynamics: a dynamic data-ordering attack and two gradient-inversion-based poisoning attacks that push ReLU units toward persistently negative pre-activations, degrading the model without modifying labels in the basic case. This turns a known training pathology into a security threat.

entry.title: Hardware-Aware Features for CUTLASS Kernel Selection

author.name: Shriram Chandran, Dominic Rinderer, Yakup Budanaz, Alexandru Calotoiu, Marcin Copik, Torsten Hoefler

entry.summary: The authors build a learned kernel selector for CUTLASS GPU libraries, where tens of thousands of semantically equivalent kernels exist for a single operation, making exhaustive autotuning impractical. They augment candidate configurations with statically computable hardware-behavior estimates and train learning-to-rank models on a dataset of 4.9 million CUTLASS kernels to select performant kernels without execution.

entry.title: Rethinking Personalized Generation: Test-Time Alignment via Factorized Ranking Models

author.name: Qiyao Ma, Junshan Zhang, Zhe Zhao

entry.summary: The paper argues that personalization of LLM generation is primarily a candidate-matching problem suited to test-time scaling like Best-of-N, revealing large untapped performance headroom. Since reward models are poorly calibrated and too expensive for large candidate pools, the authors propose lightweight factorized ranking models for efficient personalized scoring at test time.

entry.title: FUSION: a skill-based research agent for publicly obtainable nuclear-physics codes

author.name: Jin Lei

entry.summary: FUSION is an agent system that runs unfamiliar nuclear-physics codes using code-specific skills: obtaining the code from public sources, starting from verified inputs, parsing outputs, recording failure modes, and requiring benchmark reproduction before reporting results. It covers twenty codes spanning optical models and reaction modeling. The design directly addresses the reliability problem that general coding agents can run code with wrong physical conventions.

entry.title: MAESTRO: a Multimodal Auditory-attention Egocentric Speech-TRacking Open corpus

author.name: K M Naimul Hassan, Ali Alavi, Donald S. Williamson

entry.summary: MAESTRO is the first auditory attention decoding dataset to simultaneously record EEG, eye gaze, pupillometry, egocentric video, and head IMU data, with four competing speakers and background noise across SNR conditions. Benchmarks show that combining behavioral and physiological signals improves attention decoding over EEG alone.

entry.title: The Judge Is Not Its Twin: Post-training makes a model's writing more predictable but barely moves its taste, as a judge, toward predictable writing

author.name: Arman Nik Khah, Arvin Bahreini

entry.summary: Tracking OLMo-2 and Zephyr 7B models through their public training stages, the authors find that post-training makes models' writing progressively more predictable (even to external models), but surprisingly does not correspondingly bias the same models as judges toward predictable writing. This partially defuses the worry that post-trained LLM judges cannot perceive creativity progress.

entry.title: SCLATE: a Substrate for Continual-Learning Agent Training and Evaluation

author.name: Youngmok Jung, Sirajul Salekin, Henry Tran, Javier Movellan, Zhao Huang, Manjot Bilkhu

entry.summary: SCLATE provides an execution substrate for continual-learning agents where benchmarks and unmodified agents add their events to a shared open scheduler, with a hybrid simulated clock that runs in real time while the agent works and skips idle gaps, compressing month-long scenarios into shorter wall-clock runs. This fills a gap in evaluating and training agents with session events, crons, and memory consolidation.

entry.title: AECSF: Adaptive Ensemble Conditional Score Filtering for High-Dimensional Nonlinear Data Assimilation

author.name: Yangwen Zhang, Shiwei Ni, Xiaoping Zhang, Xiaofei Guan, Lili Ju

entry.summary: AECSF is a training-free adaptive ensemble conditional score filter for Bayesian state estimation in high-dimensional nonlinear dynamical systems, addressing particle weight collapse and the inability of Gaussian ensemble updates to capture non-Gaussian posteriors. It builds an analytically tractable score estimator that accounts for uncertainty about the system state associated with each noisy reverse diffusion particle. This improves data assimilation, which is central to weather, ocean, and geophysical forecasting.

entry.title: HERO-MoE: Historical Expert Routing with Scale-Preserving Fusion

author.name: Junxiang Qiu, Zhengsu Chen, Xinting Hu, Shuo Wang, Hengheng Zhang, Shaofeng Zhang, Changcheng Li, Boyu Shi, Qi Tian

entry.summary: HERO-MoE improves Mixture-of-Experts routing by injecting historical routing priors: it reuses detached, dense routing distributions from preceding MoE layers as additional input to routers, while preserving the original token-conditioned routing branch with scale-preserving fusion. This explicitly leverages the empirical observation that MoE routing reflects input semantics and upstream computation across depth. Better routing improves both MoE training stability and quality at fixed compute.

entry.title: What Would Falsify It? A Variable Specific Evidence Standard for Mechanistic Claims About Self Explanation

author.name: Arshia Eftekhari zadeh

entry.summary: This paper proposes a falsification-oriented evidence standard for claims that a model's self-explanations reuse the computation that produced its answer, requiring variable-specific nulls that remove the tested variable's identity while matching nuisance dimensions. Applying it, the author shows a cue toward a wrong option shifts choices by 64-68 percentage points while explanations mention the cue in at most 1.8 percent of items, suggesting post-hoc reconstruction rather than causal self-report.

entry.title: PINNMorph: Evolving Online Adaptation Policies for Physics-Informed Neural Networks

author.name: Xu Yang, Mingyang Yu, Jun Zhang, Keqian Li, Jing Xu

entry.summary: PINNMorph proposes an online adaptation framework for physics-informed neural networks in which a population of state-conditioned adaptation policies, evolved with guidance from large language models, dynamically modifies network topology, representation augmentation, and training mechanisms during PDE solving. This addresses the limitation that PINN architectures and training procedures are typically fixed before training even though residual distributions and learning difficulty evolve during optimization.

entry.title: OmniMoE-VL: A Sparse Vision-Language Model with Coupled Visual-Depth Routing

author.name: Long Qian, Bingke Zhu, Jiaqi Wei, Yingying Chen, Jinqiao Wang

entry.summary: Introduces OmniMoE-VL, a sparse mixture-of-experts vision-language model whose projector routes to different intermediate visual depths depending on the image-prompt pair, using a global preference to guide patch fusion and visual token injection into the language model. This gives the model question-dependent access to visual representations rather than a fixed cross-modal interface.

entry.title: Rank Collapse Is Recoverable, Growing $|Q|$ Is Not: Out-of-Sample Early Warning for Value Divergence in High-UTD Soft Actor-Critic

author.name: Tianqi Bu, YuXuan Peng, Junteng Tu, Henghui Xiao

entry.summary: This paper disentangles two failure modes often grouped under plasticity loss in high update-to-data (UTD) off-policy reinforcement learning: representational rank collapse and growing Q-value magnitude. Using SAC with scaled critics, the authors show rank collapse is survivable while value divergence reliably predicts training failure, and that early growth in log10|Q| by step 15k serves as an out-of-sample early warning signal for runs that will eventually be flagged for divergence.

entry.title: BudgetVerify: Budget-Tiered Verification for Financial QA

author.name: Janet Jenq, Hongda Shen

entry.summary: BudgetVerify is a generator-verifier framework for financial question answering that routes each answer to one of three verification tiers of increasing cost: no verification, lightweight check-and-revise, or expensive solve-then-compare. The router is trained offline from correctness and token-cost outcomes and selects a tier using pre-verification information. This targets the practical problem of allocating test-time compute only where verification is likely to pay off in precision-critical numeric QA.

entry.title: Agentic Multi-Turn Reasoning: A Fairness Approach

author.name: Thanh-Dat Truong, Sankalp Pandey, Hugh Churchill, Jackson Cothren, Marios Savvides, Khoa Luu

entry.summary: The paper proposes Fair Multi-Level Preference Optimization (Fair-MPO), a preference optimization framework for agentic LLM systems targeting two challenges: long-horizon credit assignment with only final-outcome supervision, and imbalanced data distributions that bias optimization away from rare but informative reasoning behaviors. It builds on multi-level preference optimization with fairness-oriented corrections. The goal is more reliable training of multi-turn planning, tool-use, and verification agents.

entry.title: Recursive Harness Distillation across Agents for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Seungyeon Kim, Junhoo Lee, Minkyu Kim, Baekseung Kim, Nojun Kwak

entry.summary: The authors propose Recursive Harness Distillation, where a strong agent distills its failure-diagnosis and intervention experience into a reusable playbook for a lighter agent, then recursively refines that playbook using the light agent's execution feedback. This lets VLA-based robot manipulation agents accumulate intervention knowledge across task instances without parameter updates.

entry.title: RSD-Poker: Structure-Adaptive and Shift-Robust Risk-Utility Certification for Residual Policies in Imperfect-Information Games

author.name: Miaobo Hu, Shuhao Hu, Xiaobo Guo, Xin Wang, Bokun Wang, Peng Zhang, Daren Zha, Jun Xiao

entry.summary: RSD-Poker is a certification framework for residual policy adaptation in imperfect-information games that learns and freezes a structure partition before calibration, then issues weighted upper certificates for risk and lower certificates for utility per candidate-group pair. It addresses fragility of fixed-scale, fixed-partition guarantees when deployment distributions of information states shift.

entry.title: Achieve What You Imagined: Learning to Align Actions with Visual Plans

author.name: Yuheng Qiao, Ziran Wei, Xiaohan Wang, Daqiang Guo, Yichen Luo, Zhibo Pang, Peng Zhou, Sichao Liu

entry.summary: The work treats world-action-model visual predictions as goal-conditioned proposals rather than executable plans, using a frozen action-conditioned world model to detect inconsistency between predicted visuals and action consequences, then aligning actions to plans via Flow Policy Optimization with this feedback. It improves reliability of robot action generation.

entry.title: ViBR-WM: Visual Bayesian Regression for World Modeling

author.name: Jifan Li, Ning Ning

entry.summary: This paper introduces a Visual Bayesian Regression world model that combines visual features, physical histories, and known covariates through interpretable regression in a modular architecture with trend, seasonal, and cycle dynamics. Bayesian variable selection and posterior-weighted prediction over predictor subsets allow recursive forecasting of joint visual-physical states while accounting for parameter uncertainty. Evaluated across four forecasting tasks, it targets the underexplored intersection of uncertainty quantification and interpretable world modeling.

entry.title: Quantization Error Is Spectrally Flat: A Single Random Probe Is a Calibrated, Data-Free Sensitivity Estimator, with Application to Budget-Targeted Mixed-Precision Quantization

author.name: I Kennedy, T Kennedy

entry.summary: This arXiv paper shows that a single random Gaussian probe yields an unbiased, calibrated estimate of a layer's quantization error magnitude, because round-to-nearest error is spectrally flat across frequencies. Using 1,683 tensors from a 35B MoE model and a 9B dense model, the authors validate the estimator's statistical properties and demonstrate that twenty probes reduce per-tensor sensitivity estimation error to roughly 1.3-1.4%. They apply this data-free estimator (RAM) to budget-targeted mixed-precision quantization, eliminating the need for calibration data.

entry.title: Singularities of Non-negative Matrix Factorization and their application to Bayesian inference

author.name: Naoki Hayashi, Yota Maeda, Yasushi Esaki

entry.summary: This paper analyzes the local geometry of the non-negative matrix factorization map and derives an improved upper bound on the real log canonical threshold (RLCT), which governs Bayesian asymptotics in this singular statistical model. Under a strictly positive factorization assumption, the bound strictly improves prior results when the non-negative rank is at least 3.

entry.title: CLAD: Constrained Abstract Domain for Neural Network Verification

author.name: Hai Duong, Thanh Le, ThanhVu Nguyen

entry.summary: CLAD introduces an abstract domain for neural network verification that supports input regions combining Lp-norm balls with additional constraints, rather than the restrictive plain Lp balls used by existing abstraction-based verifiers. This tighter region representation yields sound over-approximations that avoid the looseness that makes practical verification infeasible. The work improves both precision and applicability of formal NNV.

entry.title: Finite-Time Concentration and Convergence Rates for Projected Two-Time-Scale Stochastic Approximation with Markov Noise

author.name: Rahul Singh, Vivek S. Borkar, Eric Moulines

entry.summary: This theory paper establishes finite-time concentration and convergence rates for projected two-time-scale stochastic approximation driven by controlled Markov chains, handling discontinuous vector fields at polyhedron boundaries via the Skorokhod map. The bounds cleanly separate martingale fluctuations, Markov-noise residuals, and time-scale separation bias. Such results underpin analyses of actor-critic and related RL algorithms.

entry.title: JazzSAMBA: A Synchronous and Asynchronous Multi-take Band Audio Dataset of Jazz Standards for Live Music Models

author.name: Phillip Long, Jacob Nguyen, Jace Hosto, Gage Hosto, Jett Takazawa, Fares Nofal, Sebastian Stade, Nithya Shikarpur, Julian McAuley, Cheng-Zhi Anna Huang, Stephen Brade, Aleksandra Teng Ma

entry.summary: This paper introduces JazzSAMBA, the first originally recorded multitrack dataset of jazz combo performances, covering 76 standards recorded by eight musicians. It uniquely includes both synchronous (live ensemble) and asynchronous (overdubbed) recording protocols, multiple takes selected by the musicians, and detailed annotations for bars, chords, sections, and soloists. The dataset addresses the bias of existing music ML corpora toward pop and rock, enabling development of models for improvisation-centric live music tasks.

entry.title: G$^3$-LoRA: Organizing Reward-Weighted Video Data with Gradient-Guided Grouped LoRA

author.name: Jia Song (The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology), Wenhow Li (The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology), Lichen Bai (The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology), Bada Ye (Tencent), Zeke Xie (The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology)

entry.summary: G3-LoRA tackles post-training of text-to-video models on heterogeneous reward-weighted data where different categories induce conflicting update directions. It probes category-level gradients, removes shared global directions, clusters categories by residual gradient compatibility, trains group-specific LoRA experts, and consolidates them. This improves fine-tuning when data buckets correspond to distinct skills or evaluation dimensions like VBench2.0.

entry.title: AnswerMap: Faithful Spatial Interpretability of VLMs from Answer Posteriors

author.name: Mohamed Eltahir, Fardows Adam, Duaa M. Tahir, Lama Alamoudi, Sana Ammar, Atheer A. Alboloshi, Jory Albluey, Tanveer Hussain, Naeemullah Khan

entry.summary: AnswerMap is a training-free, black-box method for producing spatial visual rationales from VLM answer posteriors. It splits the image into row and column bands, queries the frozen model with yes/no relevance questions, and forms a query-conditioned spatial map from the outer product of posteriors. Fixed read-outs on the map enable downstream tasks like localization, avoiding the modality mismatch of text rationales and early-readout issues of internal interpretability probes.

entry.title: Handwritten Text Recognition Lives in the High-Pixel Variance Subspace

author.name: Carlos Garrido-Munoz, Jorge Calvo-Zaragoza

entry.summary: This paper explains why pixel-reconstruction self-supervised methods beat contrastive ones for handwritten text recognition, unlike natural-image classification: discriminative signal for HTR lies in high-variance pixel directions. It tests six SSL methods from three families under matched protocols across six handwriting benchmarks in five languages, confirming that objectives preserving high-variance pixel content transfer best. This yields a predictive theory for SSL objective choice by domain.

entry.title: Verification of PETSc with CIVL using LLM-generated ACSL contracts and deterministic driver generation

author.name: Hansol Suh, Jan H\"uckelheim, Stephen Siegel

entry.summary: The paper applies LLMs to formally verify the PETSc parallel numerical library with CIVL, using LLM-generated ACSL contracts and deterministic driver generation to overcome the brittleness of one-shot prompt-based harness generation that introduces unverified code. This addresses why numerical libraries are rarely formally verified despite the high cost of wrong results. It demonstrates a careful pattern for using LLMs in formal verification workflows.

entry.title: AdaTutoRank: Learning to Rerank Document Sets via Adaptive Tutoring Optimization for RAG and Deep Research

author.name: Kailin Jiang, Lei Liu, Jian Xi, Yangqi Chen, Hui Xu, Hongwei Zhao, Bin Li, Yu Lu, Haibo Shi

entry.summary: AdaTutoRank addresses a sparse-supervision problem in set-based document reranking for RAG: when a set-level rubric score rewards all documents equally, free-riding redundant documents become indistinguishable from decisive ones. The paper proposes adaptive tutoring optimization with on-policy distillation to provide finer-grained credit assignment across documents in a set. This targets building complete, complementary, non-redundant evidence sets for downstream models.

entry.title: MixDetect: Word-Level Localization and Quantification of AI Editing

author.name: Hongrui Bao, Yubing Ren, Zhendong Pan, Fang Fang, Shi Wang, Yanan Cao

entry.summary: This paper introduces MixDetect, a framework that detects AI-edited text at the word level rather than only labeling documents as human- or AI-written. It separately predicts which words were edited and how substantial each edit was, using aligned source-edited pairs for training supervision while requiring only the input text at inference. This matters because LLMs are increasingly used to revise rather than fully generate text, a case traditional AI-text detectors miss.

entry.title: C-HAT-Bench: Benchmarking Chinese AI-Text Detection Beyond Fully Generated Text

author.name: Qing Yang, Zixiang Luo, Zhenyu Mao, Zezheng Wu, Xinghe Cheng, Haibo Chen, Qinggang Zhang, Jiapu Wang, Jingwei Zhang

entry.summary: C-HAT-Bench is a Chinese benchmark for human-AI collaborative writing detection, covering varied machine involvement in modifying or extending human drafts across production settings, domains, and generators. The paper argues that binary human-vs-AI evaluation overstates detector reliability since collaboration weakens or redistributes generation cues, and that Chinese detection is underexplored due to tokenization and language-specific cue differences.

entry.title: MedRouter: Demystifying Knowledge Differences Across Medical LLMs for Routing-Based Reasoning

author.name: Lang Cao, Binghang Lu, Yuhao Shen, Yue Guo

entry.summary: MedRouter is an agentic system that uses an embedding-based multi-label router to select specialist medical LLMs for a query, then synthesizes their responses with a generator. It targets exploiting differences in specialist competence across medical specialties rather than just balancing quality and cost, and introduces a companion SCALE component. This could improve medical question answering coverage and reliability where single models have narrow strengths.

entry.title: GSM: Efficient Language Modeling with Shared Global State

author.name: Yunao Zheng, Bin Wen, Xiaojie Wang, Kaiyu Jiang, Xuanyu Zheng, Changyi Liu, Hongyi Fu, Jianxiong Wang, Tianke Zhang, Haonan Fan, Yingxin Li, Jiankang Chen, Xu Wang, Tingting Gao, Han Li

entry.summary: Proposes the Global State Model (GSM), a causal encoder-decoder architecture that concentrates long-range information selection in an encoding stage, producing a fixed-window shared state that all decoder layers read via updated queries. This avoids repeatedly reconstructing historical key-value structures across layers, targeting efficiency in long-context language modeling. It matters because reducing both access cost and per-layer retrieval overhead is a central challenge for efficient architectures.

entry.title: Do System One Decisions Add Up? A Study of Probabilistic Coherence

author.name: Saman Sarker Joy

entry.summary: This paper studies probabilistic coherence in language model classifiers, testing whether models that produce valid probability distributions remain consistent when the same decision is decomposed into hierarchical sub-decisions. Using 72,000 classification questions across TREC, CLINC150, and MASSIVE, the authors find substantial self-disagreement between direct predictions and category-reconstructed predictions, with differing downstream consequences per system.

entry.title: Remember by Asking: Retrieval-Induced Memory Evolution for LLM Agents

author.name: Wanqi Zhou, Jiawei Lu, Yang Wang, Zhaolong Xing, Zhen Chen, Ai Han, Haoyue Shi

entry.summary: RIME shifts agent long-term memory formation from monolithic one-pass compression toward evidence-centered integration, using generic self-questions to retrieve focused dialogue evidence and grounding memory writes in both retrieved evidence and relevant existing memories. This addresses overlooked locally-important details when future information needs are unknown.

entry.title: Rewarding Novel Deductions: Solver-guided Process Rewards for Logical Reasoning

author.name: Muhammad Asif Ali, Wenqing Wang, Huan Wang, Mohammad Raza

entry.summary: Proposes SPRING, which uses an SMT solver as a training-time verifier to provide process-level rewards for intermediate reasoning steps, targeting small LLMs on structured logical reasoning. This gives much stronger supervision than final-answer-only reward signals.

entry.title: The Right Lesson at the Right Step: Deriving Control Updates for Self-Evolving Agents

author.name: Yunhe Su, ZiYi Dong, Tong Yu, Weijian Deng, Hao Li, Bowen Jiang, Pengxu Wei

entry.summary: Introduces EvoCUE, a framework that represents self-evolving agents as explicit state-machine controllers and learns localized control-program updates from completed executions. This makes experience reuse precise about where each learned lesson applies, avoiding the distraction global prompts or memories can cause.

entry.title: Rubric-Aware On-Policy Self-Distillation for LLM Personalization

author.name: Yilun Qiu, Xiaoyan Zhao, Chengbing Wang, Cilin Yan, Rui Zu, Wanyang Zhang, Xiaolong Jiang, Jiayin Cai, Yang Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces GRASP, a framework that uses explicit user-specific rubrics as fine-grained supervision during on-policy self-distillation, bridging the gap between specifying what a personalized answer should contain and teaching the model to generate it. This advances LLM personalization beyond coarse aspect-level or single-response reward signals.

entry.title: AraDynFact: Dynamic Evaluation of Factual Knowledge in Arabic

author.name: Ignacio Iacobacci, Faroq Altam, Zhaozhi Qian, Muhammad Alqurishi

entry.summary: AraDynFact introduces a dynamic evaluation framework for measuring factual knowledge and cultural sensitivity of LLMs across the diverse Arabic-speaking world, addressing gaps left by translation- and reasoning-centric benchmarks. It reduces the cost and slowness of human-in-the-loop evaluation pipelines. This expands multilingual factual-evaluation infrastructure into a major but underexplored language family.

entry.title: Towards Communication-Efficient Social Intelligence in Language Agents

author.name: Linxiao Gong, Yijie Xu, Tianfu Wang, Yin Wu, Yili Wang, Xingbo Yao, Huizai Yao, Xilin Xia, Haowen Yang, Hui Xiong

entry.summary: This paper introduces TACT (Teacher-Assisted Communication Training), a method for training socially intelligent language agents to achieve social goals while minimizing communication cost, such as respecting a partner's time and attention. It formalizes communication efficiency along action strategy and expression dimensions and shows these affect not just the current utterance but subsequent exchanges. The work matters because it reframes agent evaluation beyond goal attainment to include the pragmatic cost of interaction.

entry.title: Planner-as-Router: Joint Plan-Time Model Routing for Cost-Efficient Multi-Agent Workflows

author.name: Vivek Kumar Singh, Preeti Priyam, Gautam Bhowmick

entry.summary: Proposes Planner-as-Router, which assigns each subtask a model size tier (small, mid, frontier) during planning so that inter-subtask dependencies inform routing before execution, contrasting with per-call cascade routers. The approach targets cost reduction in production multi-agent workflows where frontier models cost up to 25x more per token.

entry.title: OLED-MoE: Accelerating MoE-Based dLLM Inference via Inter-Iteration Locality-Aware Expert Offloading

author.name: Jingyuan Xiao (Tianjin University, Tianjin, China), Jiayue Wang (Tianjin University, Tianjin, China), Yitao Hu (Tianjin University, Tianjin, China), Xinning Wang (Tianjin University, Tianjin, China), Shi Chen (Tianjin University, Tianjin, China), Ziqi Gong (Tianjin University, Tianjin, China), Zhengchao Wang (Tianjin University, Tianjin, China), Guotao Yang (Tianjin University, Tianjin, China), Sheng Chen (Tianjin University, Tianjin, China), Keqiu Li (Tianjin University, Tianjin, China)

entry.summary: The paper addresses the memory bottleneck of mixture-of-experts diffusion language models, whose expert parameters can exceed constrained GPU capacity. Existing offloading systems are designed for autoregressive decoding and prefetch layer-by-layer within an iteration, which fails for dLLMs whose block-wise routing enlarges the active expert working set. OLED-MoE instead exploits inter-iteration locality of expert activation to schedule offloading and prefetching across denoising iterations, improving inference throughput under memory limits.

entry.title: PainterBench: A Figural Divergent-Thinking Benchmark for Tool-Using Language Models

author.name: Shane K. A. Dalumura Hettige, Jonas Oppenlaender

entry.summary: PainterBench ports the human incomplete-drawing creativity task to agentic LLMs, requiring agents to incorporate an inerasable starting shape into an original drawing via multi-turn tool calls on a canvas. It tests incremental visual planning and transfer of creative ability from pretraining to tool use in an open-ended setting.

entry.title: HEIR: Learning Human-Entity Interactions with Functional Roles

author.name: Di Wen, Wenhao Guo, Yuedong Tan, Yun Huang, Minheng Wu, Zhihang Chen, Haiwen Sun, Fei Teng, Zhiyuan Gao, Yufeng Zhang, Yuanhao Luo, Jingqi Zhang, Yufan Chen, Junwei Zheng, Ruiping Liu, Jiale Wei, Kailun Yang, Kunyu Peng

entry.summary: HEIR is an image benchmark for complete grounded participant-role sets in human-entity interactions, covering object, interpersonal, and self-directed interactions with 18,730 images, six roles, 105 actions, and 437 nouns. It argues standard human-object interaction metrics undermeasure complete event composition, and includes shared entities, role changes, and repeated fillers, with most images containing multiple actors. The benchmark supports embodied agents needing to anticipate and coordinate in shared environments.

entry.title: Reimagine Video Dynamics

author.name: Yu Yuan, Yawen Lu, Guoxian Song, Kevin Duarte, Ratheesh Kalarot, Di Chang, Xijun Wang, Stanley H. Chan

entry.summary: This paper introduces Reimagine Video Dynamics (RVD), a framework that disentangles an editable dynamics token from visual context using self-supervised reconstruction, so a video's motion can be edited directly while preserving its appearance. A language-guided dynamics-token editor, trained with a scalable counterfactual scheme, transforms source dynamics into target dynamics. It matters because it gives video editing fine-grained control over motion rather than only appearance.

entry.title: RED: Reconstruction Evolution Dynamics for Generalizable AI-Generated Image Detection

author.name: Wenpeng Mu, Junshan Jin, Tanfeng Sun, Xinghao Jiang, Qiang Xu

entry.summary: RED is a framework for detecting AI-generated images that uses the coarse-to-fine evolution of intermediate reconstruction stages as forensic cues, rather than static image features or endpoint reconstruction errors alone. The key observation is that relative token predictability of real versus generated images can reverse across reconstruction scales. This matters for building detectors that generalize to unseen generative models, an increasingly urgent problem.

entry.title: UniBuild: Unified Building Mapping From Multi-Source Optical Remote Sensing Imagery With Detail Decoding and Geometry Regularization

author.name: Wei Huang, Chenying Liu, Yilei Shi, Xiao Xiang Zhu

entry.summary: This paper introduces UniBuild, a unified framework for extracting building footprints from multi-source RGB optical remote sensing imagery. It combines a multi-dataset training scheme for cross-sensor transferability with a detail-preserving HR-DPT decoder and geometric regularization to address blurred boundaries, irregular shapes, and merged adjacent buildings. The work matters for urban mapping applications where prior methods were dataset-specific and generalized poorly to unseen domains.

entry.title: EviViT: Evidence-Adaptive Vision Transformers for Fine-Grained Perception

author.name: Yaoxin Niu, Zhangquan Chen, Yang Zhang, Xiang An, Zhumei Wang, Chih-Ting Liao, Hongkun Cao, Ruqi Huang

entry.summary: EviViT is a lightweight attachment that teaches a pretrained ViT where to acquire detail in high-resolution scenes, supervised by human visual-search traces that guide question-conditioned evidence density and token allocation. A sparse coordinate-aware bridge connects regional features to the global scene.

entry.title: Exploring In-Context Learning for Handwritten Text Recognition

author.name: Eric Ayllon, Abel Gandia, Jorge Calvo-Zaragoza

entry.summary: This paper explores using in-context learning with pre-trained vision-language models to build a handwritten text recognition pipeline for historical document digitization without updating model parameters. It evaluates the approach across multiple document collections and shows general-purpose VLMs can be taught transcription via prompting, reducing dependence on large annotated datasets.

entry.title: OFBD: Object-Focused Background Debiasing for Long-Tailed Learning

author.name: Shenghan Chen, Yiming Liu, Zhipeng Deng, Haolin Wang, Jiale Zhou, Zhijian Wu, Xiankai Lu, Yafei Ou, Yefeng Zheng

entry.summary: The paper finds that long-tailed training induces background-biased representations: tail classes suffer larger background distribution shifts and become driven by irrelevant background gradients, so degradation is not merely a data-scarcity issue. OFBD, an Object-Focused Background Debiasing method, is proposed to counteract this cause of tail-class failure.

entry.title: Label Less, Learn More: Resource-Efficient Active Semi-Supervised Learning for Onboard Satellite Image Annotation

author.name: Ahmed Abdelnaby, Mohamed Elmahallawy, Marius Bernahrndt, Tobias Hecking

entry.summary: SatLabel is a resource-aware framework for onboard satellite image annotation that combines adaptive sample acquisition with semi-supervised model adaptation, closing the loop between model uncertainty and class imbalance under tight compute, energy, and communication budgets. It targets the practical challenge of satellite deployment where annotation and onboard resources are scarce, avoiding dependence on large vision-language foundation models.

entry.title: Visual Branch is What You Need for CLIP-based Class-Incremental Learning

author.name: Tao Hu, Zhen-Hao Xie, Jingcai Guo, De-Chuan Zhan, Da-Wei zhou

entry.summary: This paper shows that the standard CLIP-based class-incremental learning design of building textual classifier weights is not always beneficial because a modality gap separates image and text embeddings, and instead builds classifiers directly from the visual branch. The analysis challenges a seemingly natural default in CLIP-based CIL methods.

entry.title: RS-OPSD: Reliable Privileged On-Policy-Self-Distillation for Ultra-High-Resolution Remote Sensing VQA

author.name: Chengjie Jiang, Yunqi Zhou, Jiafeng Yan, Sihang Zhao, Chun Yuan, Jing Li

entry.summary: RS-OPSD internalizes the benefit of zoom-in visual inspection into a model via privileged on-policy self-distillation for ultra-high-resolution remote sensing VQA, supported by GeoEvidence-6K, a dataset of 6,750 VQA samples with evidence-region annotations across seven task categories. This avoids inference-time visual search or tool augmentation.

entry.title: Point2Part: Unified 3D Partitioning from Point Prompts

author.name: Hao-Tang Tsui, Yu-Rou Tuan, Xiaoxuan Ma, Nicolas Ugrinovic, Takaaki Shiratori, Kris Kitani

entry.summary: Point2Part reformulates 3D part decomposition as joint partitioning where predicted parts are non-overlapping and collectively cover the whole shape, rather than modeling parts independently. It is promptable from images or meshes, letting users specify desired parts via single 3D point prompts per part. This controllability and coverage guarantee matter for downstream part-level editing and analysis.

entry.title: DRHeC: Differentiable Rendering for Hand-Eye Calibration with RGB-Based Gradients

author.name: Xiaotian Zhang, Yusheng Wang, Naoya Kagawa, Noritaka Takamura, Keiji Okuhara, Hiroyasu Baba, Jun Ota

entry.summary: DRHeC improves markerless hand-eye calibration for robotic manipulation by extending differentiable-rendering approaches to use RGB-based gradients instead of binary masks. This provides richer photometric signal for optimizing the hand-eye transformation without fiducial markers. The method retains the interpretability of rendering-based optimization while improving precision.

entry.title: Multi-Depth Temporal Fusion for Feedforward, Locally Trained Spiking Neural Networks

author.name: Aidin Attar, Eleonora Cicciarella, Michele Rossi

entry.summary: The paper presents an SNN architecture combining time-to-first-spike coding, residual-like connections, and multi-depth temporal fusion to support local and online learning in convolutional spiking networks. The pipeline uses unsupervised STDP for layerwise training and reward-modulated signals for the classifier. It targets processing of static images and event streams with biologically plausible, locally trainable rules.

entry.title: In-Context Learning for Robots: Methods and Applications

author.name: Haojian Huang, Zexi Li, Junhao Guo, Yehang Zhang, Wenxuan Peng, Bohan Zhou, Weilin Ruan, Leyi Wu, Chenxu Wang, Jianchong Su, Binghui Xie, Wosong Chen, Yingjie Xu, Tianhao Zhou, Suzeyu Chen, Pukun Zhao, Jiaqi He, Xinyi Li, Runze Li, Peiran Dong, Shaoxiang Dang, Jing Huang, Yingbing Chen, Yifan Chang, Tianyi Zhang, Shiyuan Deng, Haozhi Wang, Yangkai Wei, Wenqian Li, Han Yang, Kaiwen Zhou, Huaping Liu, James Cheng, Rui Shao, Donglin Wang, Yaochu Jin, Jianye Hao, Ying-Cong Chen, Yinchuan Li

entry.summary: A comprehensive literature review organizing in-context learning for robots around four interface families: context-conditioned policies, geometric demonstration transfer, world-model-based control, and skill- and agent-based execution. It clarifies transfer assumptions and the roles of training, correspondence, and memory across manipulation and navigation.

entry.title: DORA: Divergence-Oriented Data-Relay Algorithm for Partially Connected Robot Teams

author.name: Jonathan Diller, Fernando Cladera, Camillo Jose Taylor, Vijay Kumar

entry.summary: This arXiv robotics paper addresses multi-UAV search and monitoring missions where robots operate with intermittent communication, formalizing the challenge as the heterogeneous mission-aware coverage (HMAC) problem. It introduces DORA, a divergence-oriented data-relay algorithm that helps robots balance exploring the environment against relaying observations to teammates, accounting for the fact that heterogeneous robots may value each others observations differently. The work matters for practical search-and-rescue and environmental monitoring deployments where network connectivity cannot be assumed.

entry.title: Riemannian Splat Regression Models for Learning Time Fields on Arbitrary Riemannian Manifolds

author.name: Anastasios Manganaris, Rohit Banerjee, Gokul Prabhakaran, Ahmed H. Qureshi

entry.summary: This paper introduces Riemannian Splat Regression, a model that learns time-to-go functions directly on arbitrary Riemannian manifolds without ad-hoc coordinate projections into higher dimensions. It extends neural time-field approaches for motion planning beyond Euclidean spaces, promising low-runtime optimal planning with minimal model capacity. This matters because motion planning on curved configuration spaces (e.g., for robots with joint constraints) has been a persistent bottleneck for neural planners.

entry.title: ReF-HIL: Shaping the Critic around Human Action Neighborhoods for Efficient Human-in-the-Loop Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Shaoyin Luo, Song Wang, Shibo Xia, Tianle Zhang, Zhaowei Liang, Guanghui Shen, Bin Wang, Dan Wu

entry.summary: ReF-HIL is a human-in-the-loop reinforcement learning framework for robotic manipulation that shapes the value function using successful human experience and local corrective feedback. It aims to shorten costly real-world training while avoiding the performance ceiling imposed by persistent imitation penalties.

entry.title: FORM: Robot Manipulation through Direct Material Law Identification

author.name: Stepan Tretiakov, Ruihan Zhao, Cheng-Hsi Hsiao, Xingjian Li, Adam Thorpe, Hassan Iqbal, Sandeep Chinchali, Ufuk Topcu, Krishna Kumar

entry.summary: FORM enables robots to identify the physical properties of unfamiliar deformable materials from a single interaction, then reuse the recovered model to plan manipulation under new actions and geometries. It uses a weak-form momentum balance formulation to turn observed motion and contact forces into linear equations over unknown material parameters, solved with the same material point method discretization as the forward simulator. This addresses a key gap in deformable-object manipulation, where online identification of material laws is essential for reliable control.

entry.title: Identifiability Guarantees for Drivers and Dynamics of Delayed Physical Systems

author.name: Julien Boussard, Antoine D\'{e}bouchage, Th\'{e}o Saulus

entry.summary: The authors prove that, under permissive assumptions, the structural drivers and drift of stochastic delayed differential equations are identifiable, and provide a theory-grounded estimation method. Their approach avoids the strong assumptions of causal discovery and the operation-dictionary limits of symbolic regression, while offering guarantees absent from physics-informed neural networks. It outperforms baselines on driver identifiability and physical consistency benchmarks.

entry.title: ReCIRC: Rectified Conformal Risk Control

author.name: Bruno Marcondes e Resende, Helton Graziadei, Thiago Rodrigo Ramos, Rafael Izbicki

entry.summary: ReCIRC improves conformal risk control by inverting each input's estimated local risk curve to reparameterize the calibrated threshold as a common target conditional risk budget, then applying CRC unchanged on top. This mitigates the classic marginal-guarantee weakness where a single shared threshold overprotects easy inputs and underprotects hard ones. The method targets applications like lesion segmentation and multilabel classification where input-dependent risk matters.

entry.title: Graph-Split Bayesian Causal Forest for Spatial Heterogeneous Treatment Effect Estimation

author.name: Shuren He, Huiyan Sang, Ligang Lu

entry.summary: Proposes Graph-Split BART, a spatially aware Bayesian nonparametric method that replaces axis-aligned splits in causal additive regression trees with graph-based splits to model spatial dependence in observational studies. It targets heterogeneous treatment effect estimation under spatially structured confounding while retaining uncertainty quantification.

entry.title: When Noise Estimation Hides Basis Misspecification in Repeated Bayesian Inverse Problems

author.name: Rares Dimitrie Grozavescu, Mark Girolami

entry.summary: The authors show that in Bayesian inverse problems with basis-restricted priors, maximum-likelihood noise variance estimation can absorb out-of-basis signal energy, making residual-magnitude and coverage checks appear nominal while actual field coverage silently degrades. They characterize this under linear forward models and repeated problems sharing a fixed operator and basis. This is a cautionary result about false confidence in inverse problem diagnostics.

entry.title: LLM Agent Swarms Are Easy Mode

author.name: Adam Chlipala

entry.summary: Adam Chlipala argues that recent LLM-agent cyberattacks (OpenAI agents hacking Hugging Face, unauthorized probing of government agencies) are relatively easy to understand because current agents leave human-like reasoning trails, unlike future systems optimized beyond human interpretability. He contends the field has an opportunity to require rigorous safety proofs for agent systems before that window closes. The post connects formal verification research to near-term agent risk.

entry.title: How Diffusion Controller unifies and simplifies AI image generation

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A Google Research blog post introducing Diffusion Controller, a method claimed to unify and simplify AI image generation. The available content provides only category metadata, but the post describes how the technique consolidates previously separate image-generation mechanisms into a single framework.

entry.title: Mirror-Score: Calibrated, Inference-only Scoring Exposes the Limits of Sequence-compatibility Ranking in D-peptide Design

author.name: Jiada Li

entry.summary: Mirror-Score provides a calibrated, inference-only scoring framework for D-peptide/L-protein complexes plus a public benchmark of 31 crystal complexes with literature-verified affinities. It shows that raw ProteinMPNN negative log-likelihood is not a valid affinity ranker, correcting a flaw in the prior Mirror-Peptidizer pipeline.

entry.title: Illusory Truth or Mere Exposure? Model-Dependent Repetition Effects in LLM-Based Social Media Simulations

author.name: Azza Bouleimen, Nicol\`o Pagan, Anik\'o Hann\'ak

entry.summary: The paper tests whether LLM-based generative agent simulations replicate the Illusory Truth Effect, the human tendency to rate repeated claims as more true, across four models in a realistic simulated news feed. Using a large within-context design with 336,000 collected judgments, the authors find the effect is model-dependent. This matters for validating whether social simulations can serve as proxies for human behavior in misinformation research.

entry.title: Learning to Harvest Without Collapse in a Regenerative Commons: A Lagrangian Framework

author.name: Jose Tupayachi, Xueping Li, Soham Das

entry.summary: The authors formalize the tragedy of the commons as a constrained multi-agent MDP with an explicit designer-specified depletion budget, and develop a nonstationary Lagrangian framework that constructs policy sequences from unconstrained games. They introduce average-epoch solution concepts and prove a reward-independent feasibility certificate. The work frames resource preservation as a multi-agent safety requirement with theoretical guarantees.

entry.title: BiFE: Search-Efficient Discovery of CPU-Only Branching Policies via LLM-based Bi-Fidelity Evolution

author.name: Ce Zhang, Bin Zhang, Zhiwei Xu, Hao Chen, Xinyue Lu, Shanwei Fan, Yingxuan Teng, Guoliang Fan

entry.summary: BiFE uses LLM-generated code as a search space for lightweight, CPU-only branching rules in branch-and-bound for mixed-integer programming, addressing the cost of full B&B evaluation via a bi-fidelity evolutionary framework. Cheap surrogate evaluations guide the search while expensive full evaluations validate top candidates, avoiding the distribution shift of offline imitation learning. The result is discoverable symbolic branching policies with richer logic than prior CPU-efficient expressions.

entry.title: Generalizable Lifelong Model Editing via Preference Optimization

author.name: Dahyun Jung, Suhyune Son, Heuiseok Lim

entry.summary: GLIME extends knowledge editing in LLMs from one-off modifications to a lifelong continual-update setting, combining editing with preference optimization over generation behavior. It uses replay-based editing and a gradient constraint to preserve previously edited knowledge while protecting general capabilities.

entry.title: MeanFlowAdvantage: Stable Reward Fine-Tuning for Few-Step Average-Velocity Generators

author.name: Haocheng Tang, Tianchi Xie, Xingqiao Lin

entry.summary: This work introduces a signed advantage-weighted least-squares objective for reward fine-tuning of MeanFlow-style few-step generators, resolving the mismatch between advantage objectives defined on instantaneous velocities and inference that uses the learned average-velocity map. A detached MeanFlow derivative correction expresses the reward objective in prediction space with exact rollout and reference regularization penalties.

entry.title: Topological Coherence for Self-evolving Multi-agent Systems

author.name: Sen Zhao, Ruiqi Kong, Zuyu Zhang, Lifeng Shen, Xinyu He, Xu Zhang, Qinghua Zhang

entry.summary: Defines topological coherence as the requirement that responsibility, handoff, and memory boundaries in multi-agent systems stay consistent with task dependencies, and introduces TOCOMAS. The system grounds a task graph in tool interfaces, organizes compatible nodes into reusable responsibility domains, and derives dependency-informed communication and memory structures.

entry.title: Lookahead-R: Budget-Aware Tool Retrieval via Execution-Centric Planning

author.name: Zongze Wu, Yani Guo, Runnan Li

entry.summary: Lookahead-R reformulates tool retrieval for LLM agents over large API ecosystems as a resource-constrained sequential decision-making problem. It introduces a lightweight surrogate world model jointly predicting tool execution success, latency cost, and semantic utility without invoking real APIs, driving a cost-sensitive, uncertainty-guided Monte Carlo Tree Search that balances precision against latency.

entry.title: DecoyTrace: Toxic Decoys for Active Defense in Decentralized Federated Learning

author.name: Pedro Beltr\'an-L\'opez, Enrique Tom\'as Mart\'inez Beltr\'an, Pantaleone Nespoli, Manuel Gil P\'erez, Alberto Huertas Celdr\'an

entry.summary: DecoyTrace is a proactive defense for serverless decentralized federated learning that uses toxic decoy data to detect malicious updates, attribute poisoning sources, and contain propagation without a central aggregation server. It jointly addresses local observation, poisoning spread, and attribution, extending deception-based defenses designed for centralized FL.

entry.title: From Checkpoint Variation to Selection Gains in Supervised Fine-Tuning

author.name: Yupeng Chang, Wenxuan Zhang, Yuan Wu

entry.summary: This paper treats checkpoint selection in supervised fine-tuning as a finite-information decision problem, dissecting whether more validation data, a better selection rule, or simply keeping the final checkpoint drives observed gains. By fixing training trajectories and varying the validation budget, it separately measures the contribution of each factor relative to validation-log-likelihood selection. This brings experimental rigor to a routine but rarely analyzed decision.

entry.title: FedSocket: Recipient-Executable Knowledge Exchange for Heterogeneous Multimodal Federated Learning

author.name: Xinyuan Zhao

entry.summary: FedSocket makes recipient executability a design requirement of exchanged federated models: a shared head Q connects heterogeneous private models through a common prediction interface, with private models teaching local Q copies and only Q parameters plus counts exchanged. Across six datasets it improves missing-modality recipient accuracy by 14-15 percentage points over local-only training and outperforms independent ensembles at matched capacity. This tackles heterogeneous multimodal federated learning directly.

entry.title: Playing to Par: Reinforcement Learning for Provably Optimal Quadrilateral Block Decompositions

author.name: Arjun Narayanan, Per-Olof Persson

entry.summary: The authors train an RL agent to construct quadrilateral mesh decompositions of planar domains that provably reach a lower bound on total vertex irregularity (the discrete Gauss-Bonnet floor, called par). The agent acts via local edits on a half-edge data structure with a policy network whose convolutions follow mesh connectivity, enabling generalization to domains larger than those seen in training.

entry.title: Not All Errors Matter: Decision-Relevant Prediction Error Predicts Planning Quality

author.name: Linhao Wang, Yiyan Fan, Dongjin Huang

entry.summary: Shows that total prediction error in world models poorly predicts planning quality when errors land on different state dimensions, and introduces Decision-Relevant Prediction Error (DRPE) measuring error on decision-affecting dimensions. An iso-error evaluation protocol on a factored gridworld with 55 controlled and learned models demonstrates that error allocation matters.

entry.title: Elastic Selective Spectral Hybrids for Train-Once, Export-Many Budgeted Inference

author.name: Dachuan Song, Chuchu Chen, Xuan Wang

entry.summary: ESSH extends elastic spectral state space models by implementing Hankel spectral channels as independent recurrent units with input-dependent decay and write/read gates, enabling selective retention of relevant context. The train-once, export-many design lets a single trained model be truncated to multiple quality-cost trade-offs at deployment. This addresses the practical need for one model serving many latency budgets.

entry.title: Trapped by Their Own Rollouts: Understanding Aggregation--Rollout Feedback in Federated On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Jinqian Chen, Jihua Zhu, Chang Liu

entry.summary: The paper studies federated on-policy distillation and finds collaboration gains can be masked by learning-rate sensitivity, with FedAvg sometimes no better than local training. It explains this through an aggregation-induced optimization lag in the student's dual role as learner and generator of future training data, creating feedback between rollout quality and supervision access. This is a novel analysis of coupled optimization dynamics in federated LLM adaptation.

entry.title: Refreshing Less, Selecting Better: Reusing Stale Gradient Features for Efficient Influence-Based Data Selection

author.name: Jianchang Su, Yifan Zhang, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: The paper shows that gradient features cached at a post-warmup checkpoint preserve data-selection rankings with Spearman correlations of 0.95-0.99 many steps later, and proposes CDIS, which selectively recomputes features only for top-ranked candidates. This substantially cuts the cost of influence-based data selection methods like LESS.

entry.title: Self-Confirming Superposition Traps in Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Dai Shi, Andi Han, Feng Chen, Yiqun Duan, Junbin Gao, Jos\'e Miguel Hern\'andez-Lobato

entry.summary: This work shows that the RL loop of training representations on policy-selected data can sustain lower-return policies: in a superposition trap, optimal codes assign overlapping feature directions that interfere under alternative actions, lowering their observed return and reinforcing avoidance even though refitting would yield more reward. The authors characterize when such traps arise in a tied two-step model.

entry.title: When an Evaluation Rule Writes Training Labels: Measuring Human-Reference Forgiveness in NAVSIM

author.name: Jiaxuan Guo, Jingxin Yang, Jiaqi Ye, Youran Sun, Shuo Xin, Kejia Zhang, Haizhao Yang

entry.summary: The paper quantifies how NAVSIM's human-reference forgiveness rule — which marks all candidate trajectories as passing when the human reference scores zero — corrupts training labels in the GTRS-Dense generator, erasing meaningful distinctions on 11,237 of 103,288 navtrain scenes (about 10.9%). The authors re-ran the generator with the overwrite disabled to isolate the rule's supervision consequences.

entry.title: Towards Identifiable Representations under Misspecified Structure

author.name: Yuke Li, Yujia Zheng, Ziyi Chen, Kun Zhang, Heng Huang

entry.summary: This theory paper extends latent-variable identifiability results to misspecified structures where conditional independence of observations given latents fails, framing misspecification as perturbed factor analysis. The authors establish subspace and component-wise identifiability under spectral separation and sparsity, plus approximate guarantees when precise conditions fail.

entry.title: Beyond Timestamps: Decision-Aligned On-Policy Distillation for Long-Horizon Agents

author.name: Mingju Chen, Can Lv, Jinrong Liu, Huan Zhang, Heng Chang, Shiji Zhou

entry.summary: The paper identifies a Decision-Timestamp Mismatch in on-policy self-distillation for long-horizon agents: privileged feedback tied to specific timestamps can misalign with a student's functionally-defined decisions spanning multiple steps. AlignOPSD aligns supervision with decision scope rather than timestamps to improve dense-credit learning under RLVR.

entry.title: Correct then Forecast: Observer State-Space Models for Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Alexis-Raja Brachet, Guillaume Clavier--Fr\'emond, Abdelhakim Ziani, Pierre-Yves Richard, C\'eline Hudelot

entry.summary: OSSMs reinterpret recurrent forecasting models through a state-estimation lens, treating observed inputs as measurements of an autonomous dynamical system rather than direct controls of latent dynamics. A single transition governs dynamics across context and forecasting intervals, separating state propagation from measurement assimilation to avoid regime change at prediction time.

entry.title: From Distributions to Stochastic Processes: Neural Approximation of Measure-Valued Maps

author.name: Yichen Wang, Ziyi Wang, Wenlian Lu, Chenghuang Shen, Jianfeng Liu, Zhengdong Xiao, Longjiu Luo, Qianrong Wang

entry.summary: This work develops an approximation-theoretic framework for distribution-to-distribution learning, establishing uniform neural approximation in the 2-Wasserstein metric for continuous operators on compact families of probability laws. It extends results to laws on separable Hilbert spaces and mappings between stochastic processes.

entry.title: DEALS: Decentralized Expertise-Aware Load Serving for Multi-Agent LLM Systems

author.name: Jingjuan Huang, Wenbin Wang, Yanchuan Yin, Alvaro Velasquez, Jia Liu

entry.summary: DEALS provides decentralized, expertise-aware load serving for multi-agent LLM systems, letting agents decompose tasks and self-organize while sharing resources without centralized controllers, dedicated routers, or expensive LLM-based agent selection. This reduces computational cost and coordination overhead compared to existing dynamic multi-agent approaches. It targets the growing infrastructure problem of serving heterogeneous LLM agent workloads.

entry.title: On the Two Faces of Adam in Separable Linear Classification

author.name: Chen Fan, Csaba Szepesv\'{a}ri

entry.summary: Gives a quantitative analysis of Adam with small fixed positive stability constant in separable linear classification, showing sufficient conditions under which an Adam-trained classifier nearly maximizes max-norm margin before updates become gradient-like, while reaching a target Euclidean margin only much later. This clarifies the transition between two previously known asymptotic regimes of Adam.

entry.title: Learning Perturbation Robust Policies for LLM Agents with Stable Optimization

author.name: Pengxin Wang, Yuanzhe LI, Yuxin Ren, Huanrui Yang, Jingdi Chen

entry.summary: The paper finds that RL-trained LLM agent policies are sensitive to perturbations such as hidden-state noise, pruning, and quantization, and proposes SPrPO (Stable Perturbation-Robust Policy Optimization), which applies adaptive sensitivity-aware perturbations during training. It includes theoretical conditions for stable monotonic improvement and evaluations on ALFWorld and WebShop.

entry.title: SlimWise: Decoupling Expert Pruning Across Prefill and Decode for Efficient MoE Serving

author.name: Gunho Park, Kyoungho Jeun, Juntaek Oh, Byeongjun Shin, Baeseong Park, Minsoo Rhu

entry.summary: SlimWise decouples MoE serving phases: prefill runs the full model while decode uses a pruned expert pool that directly reuses the prefill-generated KV cache without conversion. Across two MoE backbones and three pruning criteria, this training-free phase-tailored serving narrows accuracy gaps versus the full model while cutting expert-weight traffic, the main bottleneck in batched decoding.

entry.title: DreamingGoose: Staged Distillation from Autoregressive Transformers to Bidirectional Recurrent Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Julian Boesch, Andrew Wee, Alexander Stranzl

entry.summary: DreamingGoose converts Qwen3 teachers at 1.7B and 8B into attention-free, bidirectional, gated-delta-rule diffusion students via three-stage distillation, tracing which capabilities survive each conversion stage. It finds language modeling transfers only partially and in-distribution while in-context retrieval fails entirely, with converted students scoring 0.000 on a multi-query recall probe.

entry.title: GeoCFM: Positive-Only Conditional Flow Matching for Mineral Occurrence Sampling

author.name: Moshe Eliasof, Eldad Haber

entry.summary: GeoCFM frames critical-mineral targeting as learning a conditional spatial distribution over occurrence locations from multi-channel geo-images, using conditional flow matching with point-conditioned velocity prediction. This handles the positive-only supervision setting where unlabeled regions are unreliable negatives and similar geophysical signatures have distinct subsurface causes.

entry.title: QAMM: Adjoint MeanFlow Matching for Few-Step Offline Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yuehu Gong, Shutong Ding, Mokai Pan, Yimiao Zhou, Jiashu Hou, Ye Shi, Yanwei Fu

entry.summary: QAMM converts critic-derived adjoint signals into supervision for MeanFlow average velocity, enabling flow policies to learn finite-interval transport directly and generate actions in few network evaluations without backpropagating through sampling trajectories. The authors derive the adjoint MeanFlow target and train it with an offline actor-critic, showing effective two-call policies on ten HumanoidMaze tasks. This addresses the slow iterative sampling of flow-based RL policies.

entry.title: Retracing Hodgkin and Huxley: State Recovery Does Not Certify Mechanism

author.name: Peiyu Zang, Jiayi Hao, Yongqiang Cai

entry.summary: This paper tests whether machine learning can recover the hidden mechanistic reasoning of the Hodgkin-Huxley neuron model by training structured latent models on simulated current-voltage data while withholding gate identities. It finds that good state recovery and prediction accuracy do not certify recovery of the underlying mechanism, with gate recovery depending on observation protocol and latent dimensionality. The cautionary result is relevant to AI for science claims about scientific discovery from data.

entry.title: FestDPO: Few-step Generator Alignment with Direct Preference Optimization

author.name: Jaewoo Lee, Kyuil Sim, Hyeongyu Kang, Kanghoon Lee, Woocheol Shin, Jinkyoo Park

entry.summary: FestDPO extends direct preference optimization to few-step generative models, where likelihood evaluation required by DPO is intractable because the generators are implicit, by leveraging nonparametric likelihood estimation. This enables aligning efficient few-step generators with pairwise preferences without training a separate reward model.

entry.title: DivOPD: Spread Wide, Look Close for Asynchronous On-Policy Distillation of Multi-turn Agents

author.name: Hanyang Wang, Zeyuan Liu, Zhengyu Chen, Jingqing Ruan, Chaoxu Pang, Zhongda Su, Wulin Xie, Zhizhao Zeng, Ke Zeng, Tianxiang Zhao

entry.summary: DivOPD addresses wasted experience in asynchronous multi-turn on-policy distillation by spreading a fixed turn budget across more rollouts and prioritizing turns with larger cumulative teacher-student disagreement, while excluding turns without usable teacher feedback. Only batch selection changes, keeping per-turn losses fixed. A practical improvement for training LLM agents via distillation.

entry.title: CTP-FL: Common-Trajectory Gradient Prediction for Federated Learning

author.name: Junkang Liu

entry.summary: CTP-FL proposes an alternative to independent local updates in federated learning: all clients evaluate the global objective along a shared, predicted trajectory rather than advancing separate local models. This makes aggregated updates interpretable as gradients of the global objective under heterogeneous data.

entry.title: From Data to Program: Fast & Direct Generative Program Inference from Empirical Data

author.name: Simon Kl\"uttermann, Xueying Ding, Leman Akoglu
