This points to structurally stable architectures for test-time compute scaling.

entry.title: Arithmetic Simplicity in Stochastic Gradient Methods

author.name: Bin Fu, Pengfei Gu, Jose Nunez, Fabian Vazquez

entry.summary: The paper defines arithmetically simple gradient methods as those using only addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division by powers of two, which simplifies chip-level implementation, and shows how to transform AdaGrad, Adam, and AdamW into this restricted form. It provides convergence analysis for a static variant of arithmetically simple Adam. This bridges optimizer theory and low-cost hardware-friendly numerics.

entry.title: TimeES: Probabilistic and Deterministic Time Series Forecasting via Evolutionary Spectra

author.name: Weiwei Ye, Renhe Jiang, Hangchen Liu, Dongyuan Li, Yoshihide Sekimoto

entry.summary: Proposes TimeES, a framework grounding non-stationary time series forecasting in evolutionary spectra theory, learning time-evolving Fourier spectra to predict both expected trajectories and uncertainty. The parameterizable formulation supports probabilistic and deterministic forecasting within a single framework.

entry.title: Age of Learning: Temporal Persistence of Prediction Errors as a Learning Signal

author.name: Chenyang Wang, Stefan Forsstr\"om, Roger Olsson, Di Yuan, Qing He

entry.summary: Age of Learning is a new learning-state variable measuring how long a prediction error has persisted, resetting on correct predictions and thereby distinguishing chronic under-learning from transient mistakes. The authors develop AoL-based training strategies for both offline and streaming settings, complementing instantaneous signals like loss and confidence. It offers a new axis for curriculum, sampling, and adaptation decisions.

entry.title: Learning the Graph and the Embedding Together: Classifier-Independent Rewiring for Heterophilic Node Classification

author.name: Harshit Kumar, Sujan Chakraborty, Priyanka Saha, Pritam Kar, Saptarshi Bej

entry.summary: The paper proposes affinity-guided graph rewiring for heterophilic node classification that jointly learns graph topology and node representations via an EM-like alternation: training a lightweight GNN, then re-weighting candidate edges under a modularity objective with pseudo-label homophily, using edges scored by a contrastively learned model. By evaluating across multiple classifiers it disentangles gains from topology versus classifier pairing. This improves a known weakness of GNNs.

entry.title: Self-Evolving Time-Series Forecasting Agents with Episodic Memory and Online Policy Learning

author.name: Junyi Wang, Yilin Wang, Wen Wu, Chao Zhang

entry.summary: The paper proposes LLM-based forecasting agents that learn online by storing episodic memory of past forecasts and using progressively available ground-truth targets as feedback to adapt subsequent forecasting actions. Unlike existing agents that treat each forecast independently, this system exploits the natural online deployment loop. It advances practical, continually improving LLM agents for time series tasks.

entry.title: Beyond Gaussian Assumptions: Distribution-Aware Channel Capacity for Effective Connectivity

author.name: Jianan Jian, Jacob Kang, Nurahmed Multezem, Benjamin Li, Nan Xu

entry.summary: The paper shows brain signals and fitted residuals frequently deviate from Gaussianity, distorting effective-connectivity estimates that rely on Gaussian residual models. It introduces a distribution-aware channel-capacity measure of effective connectivity and a dual-flow min-max estimator based on normalizing flows to compute it empirically. This improves the rigor of directed interaction analysis in neuroscience across modalities and species.

entry.title: Predicting the Next State Is Not Enough: JEPA Representations for Lean Theorem Proving

author.name: Aarnav Choudhary

entry.summary: The paper evaluates whether JEPA-style latent successor prediction provides a useful self-supervised signal for branch ordering in Lean theorem proving. Although JEPA ranks one-step transitions better than InfoNCE (50.18% vs 31.55% Top-1), it solves fewer theorems (282.3 vs 308) than simple proposer ordering, showing accurate one-step ranking is insufficient for long-horizon search value.

entry.title: Saturation-Insensitive Dueling Bandits with General Function Approximation

author.name: Chenggong Zhang, Xuheng Li, Qiwei Di, Weitong Zhang, Quanquan Gu

entry.summary: The paper studies contextual dueling bandits under the Bradley-Terry-Luce model, where preference feedback saturates and becomes weakly informative for well-separated actions, and introduces SI-CDB, which selects opponent arms carefully to avoid dependence on the prohibitive inverse-derivative factor. It achieves improved sample-complexity guarantees with general function approximation.

entry.title: DevelopmentODE: Structured Neural ODEs for Early Brain Development Dynamics Across a Decade

author.name: Kaiqiao Han, Haitao Chen, Bryan Quah, Xiaoda Wang, Janelle Liu, John H Gilmore, Wei Gao, Yizhou Sun

entry.summary: DevelopmentODE is a structured continuous-time framework that disentangles population progression, subject-specific variability, and developmental age in neural ODE models of childhood brain development from sparse, irregularly spaced longitudinal observations. It enables long-term neurodevelopmental forecasting across a decade of development.

entry.title: ZeroGAR: Benchmarking the Adversarial Robustness of Zero-Shot Graph Models

author.name: Zhongjian Zhang, Xiao Wang, Busheng Zhang, Bo Yan, Xingtong Yu, Yue Gao, Jia Li, Chuan Shi

entry.summary: ZeroGAR is the first systematic benchmark for adversarial robustness of zero-shot graph models, evaluating 13 representative models from three paradigms under adversarial manipulations of unseen target graphs. It addresses the gap between clean-graph evaluation of zero-shot graph models and supervised-focused robustness benchmarks.

entry.title: Geometric Identification in Predict-Then-Optimize Learning

author.name: Jiaxiao Xu, Changhong Mou, Keji Liu, Dinghua Xu, Yeyu Zhang

entry.summary: This theoretical work characterizes when the convex SPO+ surrogate in predict-then-optimize learning identifies the underlying quotient report, giving conditions based on face crossing, selection balance, and local coercivity of the population risk. It separates geometric conditions under which decision-focused learning recovers the mean predictor.

entry.title: Collaborative Synthetic Data for Privacy-Preserving Financial Fraud Detection Across Organizational Silos

author.name: Simeon Allmendinger, Domenique Zipperling, Burhanettin Bahadir Kibar, Niklas K{\"u}hl

entry.summary: The paper evaluates CollaFuse, a collaborative diffusion-based synthetic data approach for financial fraud detection across organizations, aiming to resolve minority-class scarcity without heavy federated-learning training burdens or direct data sharing. It situates the approach against federated learning and lightweight interpolation-bound generators in a privacy-constrained multi-party setting. Relevant to practical cross-silo analytics in regulated industries.

entry.title: GroupMask: Layer-Adaptive Group-wise Sparsity for Semi-Structured LLM Pruning

author.name: Zhengao Li, Shuoqiu Li, Xiaofang Zhang, Yukai Jin, Gokcen Kestor, Yanfu Zhang, Yiming Zeng, Bin Ren, Chuxu Zhang, Shangqian Gao

entry.summary: Proposes GroupMask, a pruning method that partitions weight matrices into regular groups and lets each layer's sparsity ratio vary under a global budget, resolving ambiguity about whether adaptive sparsity allocation is valuable under semi-structured constraints. Group selectors for all layers are generated jointly, enabling hardware-friendly group-level sparsity with layer adaptivity.

entry.title: FLARE: Flow Matching with Local Axis-Angle Representations for Stochastic Micromagnetic Evolution

author.name: Pengyu Li, Renjie Tong, Xuanlue Jiang, Jianmin Li, Yuanyuan Zhou

entry.summary: FLARE recasts stochastic finite-time magnetization prediction in micromagnetics as conditional flow matching over anchor-relative local axis-angle rotations, respecting the geometry of Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert dynamics and preserving unit norm by construction. This enables direct-horizon full-field stochastic prediction instead of stepwise integration, accelerating long-horizon simulation.

entry.title: Loop Dropout: Regularizing Shared Updates in Looped Language Models

author.name: Zirui Zhu, Hailun Xu, Xuanlei Zhao, Yong Liu, Yingxuan Ren, Kanchan Sarkar, Kun Xu, Yang You

entry.summary: This paper identifies a late-loop bias in standard LoRA adaptation of looped language models, where the shared update is more effective at later recurrence positions. It introduces Loop Dropout, which couples stochastic masking of adapter applications with compensation so training-time regularization transfers to inference, improving adaptation of recurrent-depth models.

entry.title: Agentic High-Dimensional Bayesian Optimization with Hypothesis- and Evidence-Guided Search

author.name: Zhixuan Gao, Ke Xue, Rongxi Tan, Ming Chen, Chao Qian

entry.summary: This paper shows that recent LLM-based agentic Bayesian optimization methods become unreliable in high-dimensional regimes and introduces HERA, a Hypothesis- and Evidence-guided Research Agent that adaptively selects modeling assumptions and search geometry. The work addresses both where to evaluate and which structural assumptions to adopt when objective structure is unknown.

entry.title: KiT: A Foundation Model for Financial Time-Series Forecasting using DiffusionTransformers

author.name: Boyu Zhang, Haorui Li

entry.summary: KiT is a foundation model for financial candlestick forecasting built on diffusion transformers, reformulating future prediction as conditional generation to avoid autoregressive error accumulation. It is tailored to the unique structure of k-line data, addressing the low signal-to-noise ratio and cross-market heterogeneity that general time-series foundation models handle poorly. This targets quantitative investment use cases.

entry.title: Learning High-Risk High-Precision Motion Control

author.name: Nam Hee Kim, Markus Kirjonen, Perttu H\"am\"al\"ainen

entry.summary: The paper targets an under-studied class of DRL problems where actions have irreversible outcomes and sharp reward peaks, using computational pool as a benchmark. It proposes SCOOT, an advantage-weighted regression variant that optimizes only on elite returns and handles high-precision requirements. This broadens the evaluation scope of RL beyond correctable sequential tasks.

entry.title: Drug-Target Interaction Prediction via Hierarchical Sequential Cross-Attention over Chemical and Protein Language Models

author.name: Khadidja Henni, Hamza Abdelali, Abdelkrim Aries, Neila Mezghani, Brigitte Vannier, Sara Magdouli, Lina Abou-Abbas

entry.summary: The paper proposes a sequence-only drug-target interaction prediction architecture combining ChemBERTa and ESM-2 with hierarchical sequential cross-attention to explicitly model dependencies between drug substructures and protein sequence regions, rather than merging representations only at late stages. Applications include virtual screening and drug repurposing. A solid applied scientific-ML contribution.

entry.title: Propagate, Then Sharpen: Post-Hoc Refinement of Frozen Node Classifiers

author.name: Preben Johnsen Bentdal, Nello Blaser, Xue-Cheng Tai

entry.summary: PtS refines frozen graph node classifiers using only the graph and predicted class distributions, minimizing a Potts energy decomposed into a Dirichlet term and a Gini term via alternating propagation and mass-preserving node-wise sharpening, with a single hyperparameter. It improves on APPNP-style anchored Dirichlet propagation without accessing features or gradients.

entry.title: Subgroup Rank-1 Lattice for Practical High-dimensional Black-box Integral Approximation

author.name: Yueming Lyu

entry.summary: The paper introduces subgroup rank-1 lattice rules using Korobov generators with fixed-order scalar parameters, enabling fast multiplication with feature maps of quasi-Monte Carlo point sets. This reduces the O(nd) cost of black-box high-dimensional integral approximation, relevant to expectations, kernel mean embeddings, and self-attention softmax kernels.

entry.title: GeoGAE: Scalable Graph-Level Autoencoding via Hyperball Cloud Representations

author.name: Rados{\l}aw Nowak, Anna Bielawska, Bogusz Stefa\'nczyk, Maciej Sanocki, Pawe{\l} Wawrzy\'nski

entry.summary: GeoGAE represents entire graphs as clouds of hyperballs to induce a typically unique node ordering, enabling a Transformer encoder-decoder autoencoder for graph-level embeddings without the scalability problems of node-order-matching methods. This addresses the gap between mature node/text embedding and whole-graph representation learning.

entry.title: Overfitting of Spectral Gradient Descent: How Matrix Geometry shapes Generalization and Implicit Bias

author.name: Guillaume Braun, Ichiro Hashimoto, Masaaki Imaizumi

entry.summary: The authors analyze generalization of spectral gradient descent in overparameterized matrix classification with corrupted labels, showing that shortcut geometry (collapsed versus dispersed singular directions) can reverse whether GD or SpecGD generalizes better. The work clarifies how matrix structure shapes implicit bias and memorization.

entry.title: Domain Adaptation with Target Information via Doubly-Anchored Distributionally Robust Optimization

author.name: David Kepplinger, Anand N. Vidyashankar

entry.summary: The paper introduces a doubly-anchored DRO framework for domain adaptation whose ambiguity set intersects phi-divergence balls centered at both the source law and a source-completed target reference law, deriving novel adversarial bridge geometries including a KL/squared-Hellinger pairing that induces a Lambert-W geometry with provable guarantees.

entry.title: Is H&E Image-to-Spatial Transcriptomics Simpler Than It Looks?

author.name: Duc T. Nguyen, Thanh Ha Do, Phuong M. Cao, Hieu Pham

entry.summary: Analyzes H&E-to-spatial-transcriptomics prediction, showing via an MSE error decomposition that cross-gene expression differences account for much of reported performance, while the genuine open problem is recovering within-slide variation. The paper clarifies where simple estimators suffice and where architectural complexity is actually needed.

entry.title: lapanda: A Matrix-Free Differentiable Solver for Nonconvex Constrained Optimization Layers

author.name: Yuankun Chen, Zifei Nie, Kangyu Lin, J\'{a}n Drgo\v{n}a, Liang Wu

entry.summary: lapanda is a matrix-free differentiable solver for nonconvex optimization with general constraints, reformulating problems as sequences of augmented Lagrangian subproblems solved by a first-order inner method, enabling end-to-end training of optimization layers. It improves expressiveness and reduces forward and backward computation and memory overhead compared to existing differentiable solvers.

entry.title: Prompt-Anchored Residual Adaptation for Biomedical Vision-Language Models

author.name: Jingxuan Kang, Qianying Yue, Che Liu, Chen Qin

entry.summary: PARA adapts biomedical vision-language models in few-shot settings by keeping the frozen prompt prediction as a support-invariant semantic anchor while learning a visual residual, reducing dependence on the composition of the small support set. This targets sensitivity of few-shot adaptation to subtle inter-class visual differences in biomedical images.

entry.title: ADPTNet: Adaptive with Prescriptive Timescales Non-Linear SSM for Sequence Modelling

author.name: Matei-Ioan Stan, Oliver Rhodes

entry.summary: ADPTNet is a neuromorphic-inspired sequence model built around a non-linear state space formulation with fixed prescriptive timescales drawn from evidence about the auditory cortex, aiming to simultaneously achieve data adaptivity, long-range dependency capture, GPU parallelizability, and non-linear recurrence. The work positions itself as an energy-efficient alternative to Transformers for sequence modeling. This is an ambitious architecture proposal in the post-Transformer efficiency space.

entry.title: GT-PSSM: Unified Probabilistic Framework for Stochastic Dynamics Modeling and Dependency Learning in Multivariate Time Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Wonmo Koo, Jaeyeong Lee, Taeseong Yoon, Heeyoung Kim

entry.summary: GT-PSSM is a probabilistic framework for multivariate time series anomaly detection that models stochastic dynamics and inter-variable dependencies, addressing the unreliability of deterministic point-wise error scores when benign fluctuations produce large errors. It combines state-space modeling with uncertainty quantification for more robust anomaly scoring.

entry.title: Do Emotion Concepts Generalize Across Sources, Modalities, and Architectures in Vision-Language Models?

author.name: Bohao Xing, Xin Liu, Kaishen Yuan, Deng Li, Rong Gao, Guoying Zhao, Xiaolan Fu, Heikki K\"alvi\"ainen

entry.summary: This paper constructs CMES, a cross-modal emotion stimuli collection spanning emotion-conditioned stories, real facial expressions, synthetic portraits, and synthetic scenes, and extracts Ekman emotion vectors from three VLMs per stimulus source. It reports four findings including that image-derived emotion vectors form a low-dimensional geometry similar to a reference structure, examining whether emotion concepts generalize across sources, modalities, and architectures. The work tests representational consistency of emotion in VLMs.

entry.title: Statistical Learning of Contractive Dynamical Representations for Composite Adaptive Control

author.name: Min Kim, Jos\'e Leonardo Brenes, Fred Hadaegh, Soon-Jo Chung

entry.summary: The paper presents a representation-learning framework for composite adaptive tracking control under coupled disturbances, connecting classical disturbance-accommodating control to last-layer adaptive rejection methods via a hard-EM procedure with a Kalman smoother that learns uniformly contractive latent disturbance representations. This extends prior fixed-basis disturbance models to learned dynamics. It is relevant to learning-based control in aerospace and robotics settings (Caltech authors).

entry.title: Supporting and Performing Culture from the Inside

author.name: Lea Frermann, Steven Bird

entry.summary: Framing recent culture-in-NLP research through the anthropological emic/etic distinction, the authors analyze assumptions across task selection, data collection, system design, and evaluation, and examine how the culture of NLP itself shapes the field. They propose pathways toward more culturally attuned AI.

entry.title: From Position Risks to Block Survival: Faster Generation for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Siwei Chen, Yuxiang Wan, Yifan Yu, Fan Lai

entry.summary: BRISK-DLM addresses a mismatch in diffusion language models where parallel proposals cannot condition on earlier tokens in the same block, causing asymmetric errors under proposal-verification decoding. It trains on self-generated sequences using risk-based objectives to optimize proposal learning and selection for verified decoding progress. This contributes to faster, more reliable parallel text generation.

entry.title: LA-CPD: Local-Evidence-Aware Change-Point Detection for Human-LLM Authorship Segmentation

author.name: Qing Yang, Zhenyu Mao, Zixiang Luo, Zezheng Wu, Xinghe Cheng, Qinggang Zhang, Jingwei Zhang, Jiapu Wang

entry.summary: Proposes LA-CPD, a structured change-point detection method that converts noisy sentence-level authorship scores into a coherent document partition, localizing LLM-authored spans in human-LLM co-authored texts when the number and locations of transitions are unknown. This supports attribution and accountability for copyright infringement and fraud involving AI-generated content. It addresses a gap between sentence-level detectors and document-level segmentation.

entry.title: MDL-Calibrated Significance-Gain Pair Encoding: Replication-Aware Automatic Stopping for Subword Tokenization

author.name: Azam Nouri

entry.summary: The paper introduces MDL-SG, a subword tokenization method extending BPE by replacing frequency-only pair merging with a statistical significance criterion, and adds automatic stopping via a three-stage procedure separating discovery, replication, and utility, using a hypergeometric test with multiple-testing correction and MDL calibration. This removes the need to externally specify vocabulary size or merge counts. It is a principled statistical upgrade to a foundational NLP component.

entry.title: Reading Is Not Leaking: Local, Auditable Measurement and Reduction of Inference Exposure from Public Footprints

author.name: Mahmudul Faisal Al Ameen

entry.summary: This paper presents a CPU-only, no-LLM framework for measuring and reducing inference exposure, where public data allows others to infer unstated private facts. It separates how well a system reads a record from how much the record leaks, showing on a 128-question instrument over sixteen synthetic firms that a majority-class guess accounts for most of each reader's score. The reframing of privacy risk from model leakage to inferential exposure from public footprints is conceptually interesting.

entry.title: CORA: A Protocol for Diagnosing Boundary Robustness in Text-to-Audio Retrieval under Query Reformulations

author.name: Jae Min Woo, Kyongmin Kong, Bogyung Jeong, Minjeong Kim, HaeJun Yoo, Du-Seong Chang

entry.summary: Introduces CORA, a diagnostic protocol that rewrites audio captions into five intent-preserving forms while fixing the target, defining RankDrop to expose retrieval failures hidden by Recall@k. Analysis shows RankDrop correlates strongly with target boundary margin degradation (r=0.615) but weakly with raw text movement (r=0.084).

entry.title: FastVR: Efficient Streaming Video Restoration with One-Step Diffusion

author.name: Xiaoxu Chen, Qin Yang, Haoran Bai, Sibin Deng, Ying Chen

entry.summary: FastVR is a streaming video restoration framework built on a one-step diffusion model that processes 1080p video at 11 FPS on a single GPU, combining a lightweight VAE with chunk-wise causal attention plus velocity consistency regularization during training. It tackles both VAE cost and quadratic self-attention bottlenecks in diffusion transformers. This demonstrates diffusion restoration approaching real-time deployment.

entry.title: SafeVantage: Vantage-Aware Memory for Reliable Embodied Decisions

author.name: Sean Hardesty Lewis, Zuyi Guo, Benwang Chen, Zirui Liu, Hongyi Lin, Heye Huang

entry.summary: SafeVantage introduces a vantage-aware semantic memory and active acquisition framework for embodied agents under partial observability, retaining each claim's supporting views, camera poses, and target locations while keeping positive support distinct from search coverage. A learned candidate-observability model predicts target visibility at reachable viewpoints to guide view selection by expected reduction in terminal decision loss. This improves reliability of embodied decision-making, a key robotics challenge.

entry.title: Look Closer: Patch-wise Supervision for AI-Generated Image Detection

author.name: Zhida Zhang, Tao Wu, Siyu Liu, Jie Cao

entry.summary: This paper studies patch-wise supervision for detecting AI-generated images, where a shared backbone classifies individual crops with per-crop losses and patch probabilities are averaged only at inference, removing the need for residual filtering or learned fusion modules. Patch-wise variants improve accuracy over whole-image counterparts on GenImage across four backbones.

entry.title: ComManip: Overfitting Manipulation Policies to Comfortable Regions

author.name: Yidan Lai, Xinyi Chen, Shuquan Man, Huiping Zhuang

entry.summary: ComManip finds, counterintuitively, that manipulation policies trained within a compact, visually and kinematically stable region outperform those trained with diverse placements, viewpoints, and configurations under a limited demonstration budget. The paper proposes deliberately overfitting policies to comfortable operating regions. This challenges the default intuition that visual diversity always improves generalization when data is scarce.

entry.title: RoboFin3D: A Sim-to-Real Platform for Robotic Surface Finishing

author.name: Haowei Wen, Shangtao Li, Vaibhav Sanjay, Philip Huang, Jiaoyang Li, Changliu Liu

entry.summary: RoboFin3D is a sim-to-real platform on Isaac Sim and the Newton physics engine for grinding and sanding, using signed distance fields to model changing workpiece geometry for contact computation and live rendering, plus a separate surface field for appearance change. It includes WeldGen for weld sampling, enabling cheap, repeatable experiments that would otherwise consume physical workpieces.

entry.title: LOCO-AdaMP: Built-in LOCO Inference for Adaptive Minipatch Ensembles with Enhanced Prediction

author.name: Yinan Cheng, Lili Zheng

entry.summary: LOCO-AdaMP improves minipatch ensemble methods by making feature sampling adaptive to leave-one-covariate-out importance, enabling free LOCO inference without data splitting or refitting while preserving prediction accuracy in high-dimensional sparse settings. This fixes a key weakness of LOCO-MP, where massive feature subsampling degrades prediction. The work contributes to uncertainty-quantified interpretation of black-box models.

entry.title: Probability Contracts: Accuracy, Coherence, and Decisions Across LLM Interfaces

author.name: Han Chen, Yingrui Li

entry.summary: Introduces probability contracts, a benchmark connecting exact finite-world posteriors, validated event transformations, and failure-aware decision evaluation to test whether LLM probability assessments refer consistently to the same event across equivalent requests. Evaluations across four model-interface configurations on 1,000 worlds reveal substantial divergence between accuracy, coherence, and decision loss, with interface choice flipping binary actions on a notable fraction of pairs.

entry.title: StateTape: Action-Conditioned Evidence Lifecycle Modeling for Long-Horizon Coding Agents

author.name: Ziyang Yu, Liang Zhao, Bowen Zhu, Hasibul Haque

entry.summary: StateTape improves context management for long-horizon coding agents by modeling how each agent action affects the truth status of recorded evidence, rather than masking or summarizing old observations based on text alone. This action-conditioned lifecycle view prevents agents from keeping falsified records or discarding still-valid ones as code is repeatedly edited. It targets a concrete and common failure mode of history-pruning approaches in agentic coding.

entry.title: ARCagent: An Adaptive Retrieval Calibration Agent for Clinical Question Answering

author.name: Yuyan Chen

entry.summary: ARCagent is a clinical question-answering agent for ME/CFS, a disease whose major guidelines actively contradict each other, combining a structured inter-guideline conflict registry, conflict-aware retrieval calibration, and dynamic knowledge-completeness assessment. It targets safety-critical RAG properties, knowledge completeness and conflict-aware synthesis, that standard RAG lacks. The focused disease domain makes it a strong case study for RAG in contested medical knowledge settings.

entry.title: Neural Structural Reasoner: A Brain-inspired Architecture for Reasoning over Structured Knowledge

author.name: Zixing Jia, Yuhang Pan, Ni Ji

entry.summary: NSR is a brain-inspired architecture that preserves relational structure directly in the connectivity and dynamics of coupled neuronal populations, drawing on hierarchical multi-layer encoding, stable entity representations, and path integration for state inference. It aims to overcome flat-embedding limitations of mainstream methods, enabling discovery of hidden structure, interpretability, and parallelized inference over relational graphs at query time.

entry.title: Geometry-Conditioned Fixed-Scaffold Encoders for Time-Warp Robust Sequence Retrieval

author.name: Cassandra Yang, Yufan Tang

entry.summary: GeoPatch tackles retrieval instability for long sequences observed under noncanonical clocks (variable cardiac rate, speech tempo) where geometry-chosen patch boundaries shift under temporal deformation. It proposes a fixed-scaffold patch encoder keeping token support independent of signal geometry, using slope and related features.

entry.title: Task-Relevant Null-Space Residuals for Non-Injective Neural Mappings

author.name: Bizu Feng, Zhimu Yang, Shuming Wang, Yuan Cheng, Shaode Yu, Xiaojun Qian, Zixin Hu

entry.summary: Observes that non-injective neural mappings erase input differences that downstream tasks may still need, and proposes NSR, a general residual framework that extracts null-space components from pre-mapping representations, encodes and gates them at member level, and re-applies them to preserve task-relevant distinctions.

entry.title: VISTA: Value-Informed Event Appraisal for Multimodal Emotion Conflict

author.name: Jiale Dai, Liuxian Ma, Xiaoke Niu, Wenjing Zhang, Huiying Zhao, Zhaoxiang Liu, Shiguo Lian, Guojie Song

entry.summary: Proposes VISTA, a learned seven-field appraisal interface that arbitrates conflicting multimodal emotional cues based on concerns, event relations, and expression conditions, using a log-odds decomposition separating emotion expectation from cue diagnosticity. On a shared Qwen2.5-Omni-7B backbone it reaches 64.5% conflict accuracy on CA-MER, improving over matched baselines.

entry.title: Demistifying Data and Simulator Assumptions in Supervised Causal Discovery

author.name: Pingchuan Ma, Rui Ding, Bojun Huang, Shuai Wang

entry.summary: This paper provides a systematic analysis of how simulator assumptions embedded in training data affect supervised causal discovery methods, which learn to infer causal structure from simulated datasets paired with ground-truth structural labels. It organizes representative methods available through June 2026 by prediction target, granularity, encoder, structural decoder, and training regime, examining how simulator-carried assumptions about causal graphs, mechanisms, and noise supplement observational data that may be compatible with multiple causal graphs.

entry.title: Learning from Shared-Control Overrides: Context-Driven Acceleration Profile Prediction for Personalized Overtaking

author.name: Ruizheng Xu (Heudiasyc), Lounis Adouane (Heudiasyc), Javier Iba\~nez-Guzm\'an, Cl\'ement Zinoune

entry.summary: CoP-ACC reframes driver throttle overrides of adaptive cruise control during highway overtaking as human-in-the-loop supervisory signals, learning a personalized acceleration profile via a hybrid pipeline combining unsupervised components with structured prediction rather than end-to-end regression. The goal is adapting ACC behavior to individual driver expectations in time-critical maneuvers.

entry.title: Pixels to Keys: Exploring Spatial and Motion Cues in Gameplay Inverse Dynamics

author.name: Abhishek Pillai, Ekta Prashnani, Joohwan Kim, Iuri Frosio

entry.summary: Examines inverse dynamics models that infer player inputs from gameplay video, studying in a data-constrained setting how spatial motion features, architectures, and objectives affect recovery of individual actions. It notes that aggregate accuracy metrics in prior work mask rare-action failures and clarifies key components needed for action recovery.

entry.title: GRFBrain: Graph-Structured Rectified Flows for EEG Dynamic Modeling

author.name: Haohui Jia, Zheng Chen, Jathurshan Pradeepkumar, Xu Cao, Yasuko Matsubara, Yasushi Sakurai, Takashi Matsubara

entry.summary: Introduces a graph-structured residual flow framework for forecasting time-varying functional connectivity from EEG, separating deterministic conditional mean prediction from stochastic residual transport. A history-only predictor estimates the future connectivity graph while a graph Gaussian source with Laplacian-based covariance encodes past connectivity dependencies.

entry.title: PE-EK-PINN: Physics Embedding with Evolving Kernel for Scalable Physics-Informed Neural Networks

author.name: Huiwen Zhang, Feng Ye, Chu Ma

entry.summary: Proposes an evolving-kernel physics embedding for PINNs that factorizes wave fields into analytically derived oscillatory kernels and learnable envelopes without a manually constructed, exponentially growing kernel dictionary. This targets the failure of standard PINNs on practical radiation problems with singular excitations and fields spanning many wavelengths.

entry.title: When Successful Memories Mislead Embodied Agents:Memory Adaption For Task-Conditioned Execution

author.name: Quanquan Li, Hongbo Zhang, Yihe Chi, Liuyang Song, Jingyu Li, Yuxiang Huang, Hongzhen Zhang, Guitao Cao

entry.summary: MATE is a deterministic post-retrieval procedure that converts retrieved trajectories into execution-oriented memory for embodied agents, addressing cases where previously successful experience is incompatible with the current context. It removes obsolete control context, extracts condition-action-effect transitions, normalizes actions, and selects task-dependent representations to avoid misleading reuse.

entry.title: Beyond Rule-Based Mutation Testing: Test-Aware Mutant Generation Using Large Language Models

author.name: Nils Kiele, Zainab Saad, Zirui Wang, Steve Drew, Samira Ebrahimi Kahou

entry.summary: This work proposes test-aware mutant generation for mutation testing, prompting an LLM with the problem statement, canonical solution, and base tests so it produces nontrivial mutants that pass existing tests. Evaluation across five LLMs shows the approach avoids the trivial and equivalent mutants that plague rule-based tools.

entry.title: Embodied Semantic Communication for Collective Autonomous Agents: A Tutorial on Representation, Wireless Delivery, and Closed-Loop Coordination

author.name: Yizheng Huang, Wensheng Lin, Lixin Li, Qinghe Du, Wenchi Cheng, Zhu Han

entry.summary: This tutorial proposes embodied semantic communication (ESC) as a communication paradigm for multi-agent autonomous systems, arguing that bit delivery and generic semantic recovery are insufficient for heterogeneous agents to form coordinated actions. It covers representation, wireless delivery, and closed-loop coordination as an integrated design. Tutorials of this kind help consolidate an emerging cross-disciplinary field.

entry.title: Solver Agent: an Agentic AI Framework for Theoretical Physics Computations Applied to F-theory Uplifts of O3-planes and S-folds

author.name: Eliott Morgensztern, Cesar Fierro Cota, Alessandro Mininno

entry.summary: Solver Agent is an agentic LLM framework for mathematical and theoretical physics calculations, using a persistent ledger for derivations, sub-agent delegation, and independent verification agents. The authors apply it to F-theory uplifts of Type IIB orientifolds and S-fold generalizations, establishing new sufficient conditions for Weierstrass models over projective threefolds. The framework emphasizes traceability, reproducibility, and verification of computer-assisted proofs.

entry.title: Neural networks for spectral optimization

author.name: Alexis de Villeroch\'e, Beniamin Bogosel, St\'ephane Breuils, Dorin Bucur, Jacques-Olivier Lachaud

entry.summary: This paper proposes two neural network models that learn the spectrum of differential operators directly from domain geometry, enabling cheap surrogate-based optimization of spectral functionals that would otherwise require expensive PDE solvers. One representation uses Fourier coefficients with a light MLP for star-shaped geometries, achieving 0.2% precision and respecting eigenvalue scaling laws. Averaging model outputs further improves robustness.

entry.title: Accessible, but Not Adopted: Increasing LLM Adoption among First-generation, Low-income (FGLI) College Students beyond Expanding Access

author.name: Hyungsik Kim

entry.summary: This qualitative study examines the access-adoption gap for LLMs among first-generation, low-income college students through 61 interviews with students and program administrators. It argues that access alone does not produce meaningful adoption, and identifies barriers and strategies for deepening adoption beyond mere availability. The work informs how to ensure AI's social benefits reach underserved communities.

entry.title: Calibrated to Whom? Persona and Language Effects on Cultural Values in JEV

author.name: Bushra Asseri, Abdulaziz Asseri

entry.summary: This audit examines the cultural values embedded in a decision-only language model, TypeSafe's JEV, using the Values Survey Module 2013 across Saudi and American personas in English and Arabic with 288,000 answers. Persona-conditioned responses partially reproduce the human Saudi-US value difference (87% in English, 62% in Arabic), and answers are highly repeatable. The work highlights cross-lingual gaps in persona calibration relevant to using models as survey respondents or judges.

entry.title: Similar Choices, Different Attention: Cross-Modal Associations in Humans and Vision-Language Models

author.name: Sumin Hong, Katsumi Ibaraki, Renee Shi, David Chiang, Toby Jia-Jun Li

entry.summary: The study compares humans and vision-language models on cross-modal sound-symbolic associations like bouba/kiki, presenting identical stimuli (pseudo-words and image pairs) to both and recording choices plus human eye movements. While some larger VLMs align with human choices, their saliency maps match human gaze less well than a simple center-bias baseline.

entry.title: FM-ReID: Selective Competitive Token Routing for Object Re-Identification

author.name: Zhiqi Li, Xiaowei Zhou, Zeyuan Sun, Feng Gao, Junyu Dong

entry.summary: FM-ReID is an end-to-end framework for object re-identification that treats local representation learning as selective competitive token routing over dense tokens from visual foundation models. Its Competitive Fine-grained Mining module surfaces localized discriminative cues such as animal markings, clothing details, and vehicle features that holistic descriptors obscure. The approach applies across person, animal, and vehicle ReID.

entry.title: VAA-CSEC: Vote-guided Advantage Allocation for Chinese Semantic Error Correction

author.name: Yitong Han, Nankai Lin, Juan Luo, Hongyan Wu, Lianxi Wang, Shengyi Jiang

entry.summary: VAA-CSEC is a multi-stage pipeline combining chain-of-thought distillation, supervised fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and self-consistency decoding for correcting subtle semantic errors in Chinese text. Its task-specific reward directly penalizes over-correction and aligns CoT reasoning with vote outcomes. It addresses an underexplored, culturally and linguistically specific NLP task with a sensible RL recipe.

entry.title: ARGOS: Reinforcement Learning-Driven Multidimensional Elasticity for Service Orchestration in the Computing Continuum

author.name: Javier Mateos-Bravo, Sergio Laso, Juan Luis Herrera, Ilir Murturi, Pantelis Frangoudis, Schahram Dustdar

entry.summary: ARGOS is an end-to-end reinforcement learning controller for service orchestration in the computing continuum, formulating multidimensional elasticity as a per-request MDP. Unlike existing orchestrators that adapt only resources, placements, or replicas, ARGOS dynamically adjusts analytics requirements such as coverage, sampling, and freshness within client-defined quality ranges under capacity constraints. This balances analytics quality, resource use, and cost across heterogeneous nodes.

entry.title: CRJudgeBench: Can AI Detect Plausible but Invalid Code Reviews?

author.name: Yue Pan, Jiawei Li, Ziyuan Zhang, Xiangxin Zhao, He Ye

entry.summary: CRJudgeBench is a benchmark of 1199 instances built from real pull requests and expert-verified perturbations, testing whether LLM agents can judge the technical trustworthiness of code-review comments, including plausible but incorrect claims. Existing benchmarks evaluate review generation or issue discovery, not trustworthiness judgment. It fills a real gap as AI code reviewers become widespread.

entry.title: Loss-Guided Pretraining Data Selection for Time-Series Foundation Models

author.name: Yike Li, Shaoxu Song, Jianmin Wang

entry.summary: The authors propose a static data-selection framework for time-series foundation models that scores each training window using a reference forecaster and connects forecasting loss to per-sample gradient norm under a local Jacobian condition. Dataset-stratified selection retains an intermediate difficulty interval and preserves diversity. The method improves downstream performance across various TSFM architectures.

entry.title: Width Expansion as a Method for Class Incremental Learning

author.name: A. L. S. Conde, Y. Elkhatib, C. M. Ranieri

entry.summary: The paper proposes dynamically increasing neuron count within existing layers based on a normalized loss criterion to handle class-incremental learning without task identifiers or predefined growth schedules. This avoids the common reliance of architectural expansion methods on explicit task boundaries at inference time. It addresses the stability-plasticity tradeoff in a more deployment-realistic setting.

entry.title: A Proposed Rubric for Evaluating Expressed Clinical Reasoning in Large Language Model Responses

author.name: Zhangshu Joshua Jiang, Zina Ibrahim, James T. Teo

entry.summary: The paper proposes a multidimensional rubric for scoring free-text LLM responses to clinical vignettes, synthesizing medical education assessment frameworks, clinical LLM benchmarks, and general LLM reasoning evaluation taxonomies, with groundedness adapted as a clinical factuality axis. It aims to bring structure to an otherwise ad-hoc evaluation landscape for clinical reasoning. This is a methodological proposal rather than an empirical study.

entry.title: Gender bias across LLMs is common and highly heterogenous

author.name: Edoardo Bolzoni, Valerio Capraro

entry.summary: This study audits gender bias across ten models from nine vendors released between April 2025 and June 2026 using two paradigms: gender attribution of stereotyped phrases and moral judgment of harm against men versus women, finding that bias is common but highly heterogeneous across models. This is a timely, broader-coverage audit as LLMs are embedded in consequential decision-support tools.

entry.title: Replay in the Silent Degrees of Freedom: Continual Learning Without an Offline Phase

author.name: Zhang Yanhai

entry.summary: This solo-author paper demonstrates continual learning with replay consolidation happening entirely during ongoing processing, inspired by local sleep in biological circuits. Using biologically constrained rules including an isolation rule, refractory rotation, and homeostatic novelty gating under k-winner-take-all dynamics, the network consolidates hidden synapses with no dedicated offline phase.

entry.title: Grounding Vision-Language Models in Driving Semantics: A Multi-Dataset Predicate Framework for Explainable Reasoning

author.name: Mohamed Chouai, Fazli Faruk Okumus, Stefan Kugele

entry.summary: This work presents a deterministic predicate framework that derives driving-scene semantics from measurable geometric, kinematic, temporal, map, and traffic-control evidence, materialized as a common Predicate Knowledge Graph across nuPlan and nuScenes. It enables verifiable, explainable grounding of vision-language model outputs against underlying traffic situations, with strong macro F1 on manually annotated relations.

entry.title: Product-Aware Deterministic Rounding for Quantized Matrix Multiplication

author.name: Piyush Sao, Narasinga Miniskar, Pedro Valero-Lara, Keita Teranishi, Sudip Seal

entry.summary: This theory-oriented work studies deterministic rounding decisions for quantized matrix multiplication in which scalar choices interact through the product. It provides null-space reduction and conditional-expectation completion algorithms with provable squared product error bounds relative to the best admissible error, for both dynamic activations and reusable static weights.

entry.title: Resource-Aware Federated Mixture-of-Experts with Adaptive Pruning for Onboard Learning in LEO Satellite Constellations

author.name: Mohamed Shaaban, Mohamed Elmahallawy, Marius Bernahrndt, Tobias Hecking

entry.summary: COSMIC-FL is a resource-aware federated learning framework for onboard learning in LEO satellite constellations, introducing two MoE designs (a Sliced design sharing backbones with task-specific channel subsets and a complementary variant) with adaptive pruning to fit satellite compute and communication budgets. It targets disaster response and environmental monitoring without transmitting raw imagery to ground. Addresses a genuine systems gap in edge federated learning.

entry.title: Simple Extensions of Single-Objective Acquisition Functions and Hedge Strategies for Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Haris Moazam Sheikh

entry.summary: This paper shows that specialized multi-objective Bayesian optimization machinery may be unnecessary by extending standard single-objective acquisition functions to MOBO via a hypervolume-based transformation, and extending hedge strategies for acquisition portfolios to the multi-objective regime. The approach requires minimal pipeline modification. It argues for simplicity where bespoke formulations have dominated.

entry.title: What Should We Freeze? Guarded Freezing: Connectivity Shapes the Fine-Tuning of Pretrained Models

author.name: Leonel Aguilar

entry.summary: The paper analyzes why freezing weights alone may not preserve performance, since updates elsewhere can change inputs to a frozen core, and proposes removal-value, a capacity-based score approximating HOPE removal cost, to guide what to freeze. By cutting paths from trainable neurons into the frozen core in VGG-8 it improves old-task accuracy retention over DEFT, and for transformers with shared residual streams it derives drift-based corrections.

entry.title: Efficient Support Recovery of Mixtures of Sparse Linear Classifiers with Less Measurements

author.name: Xiaxin Li, Arya Mazumdar

entry.summary: The authors study support recovery for mixtures of sparse linear classifiers from sign measurements, where each measurement reveals the sign of an inner product with one of several unknown sparse vectors. They propose adaptive and non-adaptive schemes that reduce the required number of measurements while simultaneously achieving sublinear decoding time. This improves theoretical guarantees for a problem relevant to mixture-of-experts style feature identification.

entry.title: Refresh or Realize? Compute Allocation in Drifting Models

author.name: Sipeng Chen, Xu Zheng, Shibo Li

entry.summary: For Drifting Models, which train one-step generators by recomputing a finite-sample drift field each iteration, the paper asks whether extra compute should fit the current target more closely or recompute the field. Experiments on ImageNet 256x256 measure realized displacement when the target is held fixed, revealing how quickly parameter updates realize the prescribed sample motion.

entry.title: Phase Space Attention:A Hairer Lift Circumvents the Single-Layer Induction Obstruction

author.name: Kingsuk Maitra, Shagun Sood Morteza Hosseini, Suman Gunnala, Vikram Gupta

entry.summary: Proposes lifting attention onto a symplectic phase space to circumvent the Sanford-Hsu-Telgarsky single-layer induction obstruction, using an upper shear transformation on post-RoPE query and key streams. The paper recasts the obstruction as a filter-order gap and proves the lift is unique within its design class.

entry.title: Adapting Nonstationary Multi-output Gaussian Processes to Bayesian Optimization

author.name: Zikai Xie

entry.summary: Studies the mismatch between expressive nonstationary multi-output GPs and reliable Bayesian optimization decisions, showing strong training fit can coexist with poor off-design errors and optimistic acquisitions. Proposes MOLRN-BO combining regularized shared-spectral surrogates, residuals, prequential mean correction, and Pareto-local qLogEHVI optimization, evaluated across 12 settings.

entry.title: Fisher Simplicity in Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks and Multilayer Perceptrons

author.name: Ami Tavory, Meir Feder

entry.summary: This theory paper examines when architectural simplicity cues in KANs (small basis coefficients) and MLPs (dead ReLUs) agree with a statistically grounded notion of simplicity based on Fisher nullity. It proves they align for dead ReLU units but diverge for fixed-basis KANs, complicating the interpretability case for KANs. The work sharpens what counts as a valid certificate of simplicity in network interpretability.

entry.title: Predicting the Financial Impact of Supply Chain Risk for Major AI-Related Semiconductor Firms: A Heterogeneous Graph Patch Transformer Approach

author.name: Jianna Hur, Sagar Samtani

entry.summary: This study builds a heterogeneous graph patch transformer that forecasts quarterly financial outcomes (revenue, inventory, profitability) for AI chip firms one and two quarters ahead, learning from a 15,186-company supply network over 60 quarters while fusing fundamentals with macro-trade, event, and disaster signals. It addresses how multi-tier supply chain stress propagates to reported financials, beyond firms' direct partners. It is a notable applied contribution at the intersection of AI hardware economics and graph learning.

entry.title: Getting Motif-ated: Controllable AI Compositions from Injected Motif Prompts

author.name: Chao Peter Yang, Cynthia Rudin, Yue Jiang, Simon Mak, Stephen Ni-Hahn

entry.summary: MotiGen is a recipe for retrofitting pretrained symbolic music models (like NotaGen) to accept new instruction prompts, enabling controllable classical music generation by injecting motifs without training a foundation model from scratch. Co-authored by Cynthia Rudin's group, it gives musicians practical control handles over generated compositions. This addresses a real gap in controllability of LLM-style music generation systems.

entry.title: HamiFormer: Dual-Expert Diffusion Fields with Affine Symplectic Maps

author.name: Haoxiang Huang, Xiang Liu, Shuwei Wang, Jingheng Ma, Sen Cui

entry.summary: HamiFormer combines whole-window diffusion denoising with Hamiltonian propagation to predict dynamics with both smooth evolution and abrupt collisions, using parallel affine symplectic maps to amortize refinement. A regime model tree specializes residual corrections to different dynamical regimes.

entry.title: The Impact of Stochasticity on the Rashomon Effect in Machine Learning

author.name: Andrea Apicella, Francesco Isgr\`o, Andrea Pollastro, Roberto Prevete

entry.summary: An empirical study disentangling how different sources of training stochasticity (e.g., weight initialization) contribute to the Rashomon effect, quantified along three dimensions: solution-space, predictive, and decision-basis multiplicity. The work clarifies whether near-optimal but distinct models arise similarly or differently from various randomization sources.

entry.title: Feasible Flow Matching for Graph Reconstruction via Within-Sampling Primal-Dual Guidance

author.name: Haoming Chen, Nicolas Zilberstein, Santiago Paternain, Santiago Segarra

entry.summary: CPD-PIFM augments Prior-Informed Flow Matching for graph reconstruction with trajectory-evolving Lagrange multipliers that respond to constraint violations at a predicted endpoint, incorporating structural side information like degree bounds without retraining. The paper proves permutation equivariance inheritance and bounds expected terminal constraint slack.

entry.title: Deep Learning Techniques for Phoneme Recognition in Italian Children' s Speech

author.name: Nicola Barbaro, Cristina Gena, Francesco Petriglia, Andrea Meirone, Alessandro Mazzei, Arianna Viotti

entry.summary: The authors present Broca, a Conformer-based system pretrained on eight days of adult speech and fine-tuned on just 165 minutes of Italian child speech from standardized diagnostic tests, designed to transcribe children's speech into the International Phonetic Alphabet to assist speech therapists. It achieves a state-of-the-art weighted Phoneme Error Rate of 13.36% on Italian speech despite using under three hours of child-specific data. This matters as a concrete clinical AI application addressing the shortage of tools for diagnosing speech impairments in children aged 3.5-6.5.

entry.title: Geometry-Aware Operator Families for Structured Representation Learning

author.name: Zuyuan Zhang, Fei Xu Yu, Tian Lan

entry.summary: The paper introduces Geometry-Induced Operator Families (GIOF), a unified framework that derives admissible propagation operators directly from fixed geometric structure while dynamically selecting among them based on context. This bridges generic operator templates and geometry-specific constructions in deep representation learning.

entry.title: GTRL: Grounding Divide-and-Conquer Value Learning with Temporal Differences

author.name: Abdul Monaf Chowdhury, MD Sameer Iqbal Chowdhury, Shifat E Arman, Md Mehedi Hasan

entry.summary: GTRL fixes two failure modes of divide-and-conquer value learning in offline goal-conditioned RL under stochastic dynamics: optimism toward lucky trajectories in the base case and missing updates for state-goal pairs not connected by any trajectory. It augments the composition rule with a one-step TD target so every state-goal pair receives an update while retaining long-horizon scaling.

entry.title: AutoHGNN: Robust and Efficient Neural Architecture Search for Hypergraph Neural Networks

author.name: Sirui Li, Pietro Li\`o b, Xinsheng Li, Baisong Liu, Chengbin Peng

entry.summary: AutoHGNN is a neural architecture search framework for hypergraph neural networks, introducing a Hyper-Interaction Module to fit hypergraph structure and a Hypergraph Stable Topological Distance criterion for architecture selection. It automates the design of higher-order relational architectures that manual crafting struggles to capture.

entry.title: A Free Knob: Decoupling Calibration and Predictive Skill in Threshold-Based Evaluation

author.name: Md Tanveer Hossain Munim, Bijoy Ahmed Saiem, Al-Amin Sany, Tanzima Hashem

entry.summary: The paper shows max-pooled CSI in dense-prediction benchmarks confounds spatial discrimination with amplitude calibration, since sharp or attenuated predictions change which blocks cross threshold at fixed operating points. It repurposes monotone calibration as a symmetric post-hoc audit that cannot reverse pixel ordering, and applies it on SEVIR where two released checkpoints are compared.

entry.title: Pulseflow: PPG Counterfactual Generation Via Latent Transport

author.name: Hung Manh Pham, Dong Ma, Bin Zhu, Pan Zhou

entry.summary: PulseFlow generates source-conditioned counterfactual photoplethysmography signals via latent transport, explicitly modeling how an observed source recording transforms into an atrial fibrillation target rather than sampling unconditionally. This leverages abundant source recordings for targeted augmentation to address scarce labeled AF data in cardiovascular monitoring.

entry.title: GraphSelect for Budgeted Representation Selection in Multimodal Graph Inference

author.name: Xu Wang, Xunkai Li, Yinlin Zhu, Rong-Hua Li

entry.summary: The paper studies budgeted selection of text and image representations for multimodal graph classifiers, where each representation's contribution depends on other selected inputs and propagates across nodes. GraphSelect provides an empirical study and selection method showing that updating scores as the selected set changes improves performance.

entry.title: T-MoXAI: A Hierarchical Explainability Framework for Temporal Multimodal Data

author.name: Ali Inha, Mo Vali, Saaliha Vali, Pietro Li\`o, Meen-Yau Thum

entry.summary: T-MoXAI is a hierarchical explainability framework for temporal multimodal models that explains when timepoints matter (temporal Shapley values), which modalities contribute (attention analysis), and what features drive decisions (gradient attribution), running in under a second. It is demonstrated on real-world healthcare tasks including IVF treatment prediction. The work aims to improve trust and adoption of opaque multimodal models in high-stakes domains.

entry.title: Beyond Fixed Features: Architecture-Dependent Sensitivity to Node Representations under Heterophily

author.name: Priyanath Maji, Sidharth Gaur, Rajavinoth Paul Durai

entry.summary: The study constructs parallel feature variants of two large heterophilic benchmarks (Roman-Empire, Amazon-Ratings), pairing graphs with representations from fastText to contextual Transformer embeddings, and evaluates seven GNN architectures across them. It finds that conclusions about heterophily robustness depend heavily on the input representation, undermining fixed-feature comparisons in prior work. A useful benchmark-design caution for GNN research.

entry.title: Augmented Feature Boosting for Multicalibration

author.name: Ira Globus-Harris, Inbal Livni Navon

entry.summary: Studies discretization-free boosting for multicalibration, avoiding the rounding-parameter sensitivity of standard level-set audit-and-repair approaches. Building on a recent feature-augmentation paradigm, the authors analyze an alternative boosting method that repairs calibration without repeatedly discretizing the predictor's range.

entry.title: DynGraphAgentBench: A Benchmark for Agentic Lifecycle Control in Dynamic Graph Anomaly Detection

author.name: Yuwei Han, Lingwei Wei, Wooseong Yang, Liangjie Huang, Liancheng Fang, Huanhuan Ma, Philip S. Yu

entry.summary: Introduces an executable benchmark for evaluating agentic control of dynamic graph anomaly detection under delayed feedback, spanning seven temporal graph datasets, eleven detectors, and eight chronological deployment windows. A controller must select detectors using only time-causal context and its own history, with a sandboxed executor handling training and scoring.

entry.title: ASTRA: ADMM-Accelerated Topology Reconfiguration for Dynamic Satellite Constellations

author.name: Jo\~ao Norberto, Ricardo Ferreira, Cl\'audia Soares

entry.summary: ASTRA frames dynamic satellite constellation topology reconfiguration as an online learning problem and makes it practical by pairing an ADMM-based offline solver with efficient online gradient and conditional-gradient updates. The work includes regret-style theoretical guarantees and drops idealized assumptions like full constellation deployment.

entry.title: Counterexamples to Local Reconstruction Gain as a Proxy for Final Fidelity in Residual Completion

author.name: Yasuto Hoshi, Daisuke Miyashita, Jun Deguchi

entry.summary: The paper shows counterexamples where improving a layer's attention-output reconstruction in sparse-attention residual completion (training-free RESA and learned Top-K+phi) does not improve final model output fidelity, sometimes degrading KL fidelity versus an all-abstain Exact Top-K baseline. This cautions against local reconstruction gain as an evaluation proxy for sparse attention methods.

entry.title: Beyond One Epoch: Uncertainty-Weighted Sensitivity Regularization for Recommendation Models

author.name: Richard Lettich, Shagun Gupta

entry.summary: The paper analyzes the one-epoch phenomenon in recommendation models with sparse embeddings via a violation of the prequential principle, introducing self-influence asymmetry: later-epoch examples are scored by embeddings already displaced by their earlier labels. Using an exact scalar model and local influence analysis, it derives uncertainty-weighted sensitivity regularization to mitigate the generalization collapse.

entry.title: ExpertoRhythm: Morphology-Aware Learning for Waveform Reconstruction and Cuffless Blood Pressure Estimation from Single-Channel PPG

author.name: Amir Arjomand, Kenneth B. Kent, Georgiy Krylov

entry.summary: ExpertoRhythm is an attention-enhanced 1D U-Net that reconstructs arterial blood pressure waveforms from single-channel PPG signals, deriving systolic and diastolic pressure from the reconstructed waveform. Its key contribution is a composite morphology-aware loss combining range-weighted reconstruction with a window-range regularizer targeting high-dynamic BP segments.

entry.title: GPARA: Graph-Posterior-Aligned Refinement and Active Acquisition for Grounding Diffusion Priors

author.name: Wangqian Chen, Hao Wang, Yumeng Zhang, Jiajia Guo, Junting Chen, Jun Zhang

entry.summary: GPARA enables active grounding of frozen diffusion priors by learning a graph surrogate over diffusion prediction residuals, forming a reusable posterior response operator that propagates measurement innovations to unobserved variables. It selects new measurements via weighted posterior-risk reduction, avoiding costly repeated ensemble generation.

entry.title: Riemannian Difference-of-Convex Optimization for K-Means Clustering

author.name: Meng Xu, Bo Jiang, Hanfu Zhang, Ya-Feng Liu, Anthony Man-Cho So

entry.summary: The authors reformulate K-means clustering as a cardinality-constrained problem on an embedded submanifold, replacing the cardinality constraint with a difference-of-convex penalty and proving the two formulations share global minimizers beyond a finite penalty threshold. They propose RADA-DC, a Riemannian alternating descent-ascent method with dual regularization and DC linearization.

entry.title: SPACE-LoRA: Allocating Activation-Subspace Protection for Continual Learning

author.name: Seunghyun Yoo, Kiseok Kim, Hyeontae Joo, Junyeop Bang, Hwangnam Kim

entry.summary: SPACE-LoRA tackles catastrophic forgetting in continual learning with LoRA adapters by identifying additive interference: new residual adapters produce non-zero responses along input directions important for old tasks. The method suppresses responses of newly added adapters in protected subspaces of past-task inputs. This offers a more direct fix than prior approaches that only constrain parameter updates.

entry.title: LLN: Learnable Lens Networks for Parameter-Efficient Long-Horizon Dynamical Prediction

author.name: Binbin Yong, Zhao Su, Lan Guo, Haoran Li, Jun Shen, Qingguo Zhou

entry.summary: Learnable Lens Networks replace direct residual additions with physics-inspired learnable optical transport in a position-angle phase space, alternating free propagation with a learnable lens field that performs nonlinear focusing. The architecture aims to constrain feature-geometry evolution across layers, which residual connections leave unconstrained, with theoretical guarantees and parameter efficiency for long-horizon dynamical prediction. It represents a novel architectural alternative to residual networks for sequence modeling.

entry.title: When local gains fail to transfer: Frozen Earth-observation embeddings across wildfires

author.name: Philipp Stark, Alexandros Sopasakis, Ola Hall

entry.summary: The study shows that spatially blocked cross-validation within one region does not predict accuracy of frozen Earth-observation embeddings in a new region, using wildfire burned-area mapping in Greece and Spain as a testbed comparing TESSERA and AlphaEarth with baseline features. It identifies why transfer fails and the one setting where such models keep working, using a linear-probe protocol.

entry.title: Evaluating Dynamical Fidelity through Predictive Structure in Physical Representations

author.name: Oskar Bohn Lassen, Joao Paulo de Souza Boger, Simon Driscoll, Stephen I. Thomson, Sebastian Schemm, Filipe Rodrigues, Francisco C. Pereira

entry.summary: The authors propose a framework for evaluating machine-learning models of physical systems by whether learned trajectories reproduce underlying dynamics, using expert-defined physical representations to expose processes, interactions, and responses. This moves beyond state-prediction error and physical-consistency checks toward assessing dynamical fidelity.

entry.title: Predictive Dual Smoothing for Column Generation

author.name: Senne Berden, Noah Schutte, Andrea Lodi, Tias Guns

entry.summary: This work improves column generation for large-scale linear programs by stabilizing oscillating dual solutions. It proposes predictive dual smoothing, which anticipates dual movement rather than only blending current and past duals, speeding convergence of the pricing subproblem. The work connects ML-flavored prediction with classical optimization.

entry.title: Attention-based Hierarchical Variational Information Bottleneck for Robust Multi-Agent Communication under Variable Bandwidth

author.name: Lukas Koch Vindbjerg, Qi Zhang, Yury Brodskiy, Lukas Esterle

entry.summary: AH-VIB combines a variational information bottleneck with autoregressive sequential message generation and a hierarchical robustness loss so that multi-agent messages remain useful under prefix truncation from limited bandwidth. Evaluated on a cooperative object-inspection and occupancy-mapping task. Addresses graceful degradation in learned agent communication.

entry.title: Addressing Spatial Indistinguishability in Spatiotemporal Prediction via Optimal Transport-Guided Masking

author.name: Guangyu Wang, Jiawei Tong

entry.summary: The paper identifies spatial indistinguishability, where nodes share similar histories but diverge in future behavior, and proposes STOT, a self-supervised optimal-transport-guided masking framework for spatiotemporal forecasting in sensor networks. It targets a failure mode of historical-similarity-based GNN and embedding approaches.

entry.title: Depot-Closed Multi-Component Construction for Neural Vehicle Routing

author.name: Shinichiro Hamada, Hisashi Kashima

entry.summary: The paper proposes multi-component construction for neural vehicle routing solvers, maintaining many route components simultaneously and merging them in arbitrary order, with a depot-closed interpretation under which every intermediate construction state is a complete feasible solution with exact costs. This removes the early route-membership commitment of route-by-route construction.

entry.title: SpikeLite: Lightweight Spiking Neural Networks for Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Bang Hu, Changze Lv, Mingjie Li, Xiaoqing Zheng, Wei cao, Fan Zhang

entry.summary: SpikeLite is a spiking neural network framework for energy-efficient time-series forecasting built on a frequency-selective spiking encoder and sparse spiking channel attention. It deliberately avoids complex attention mechanisms to preserve the lightweight, low-power motivation of SNNs.

entry.title: When Should a Satellite Estimate Be Changed? Stress-Testing Neural Corrections for Evapotranspiration

author.name: Marco Trotta

entry.summary: Evaluates selectors that decide when neural residual corrections improve satellite evapotranspiration estimates, using 16,366 flux-tower observations from 151 stations. Shows that a naive selector accepts physically invalid records with severe error increases, while the proposed SupportGain selector substantially reduces error on held-out stations with far more conservative acceptance.

entry.title: NeuronSifter: Intervention Planning in CNS Microenvironments

author.name: Haowei Xu, Wanyi Fu, Hongbin Han, Zhaoheng Xie

entry.summary: NeuronSifter is a framework for planning central nervous system interventions that compiles dosing regimens into state-conditional target-occupancy fields propagated through microenvironment dynamics, and selects measurements that would maximally change decisions under joint uncertainty. It reframes decision quality as a property of the intervention interface rather than controller placement.

entry.title: Structured Latent Modeling for Supervised Multimodal Information Decomposition

author.name: Wanting Huang, Sanvesh Srivastava, Weiran Wang

entry.summary: This work introduces a framework that factorizes multimodal joint distributions into shared task-relevant, modality-specific, and task-irrelevant variation using contrastive or masked objectives at intermediate layers, source-wise normalizing flows, and a supervised low-rank latent model. This gives a principled way to isolate target-relative contributions of each modality.

entry.title: Transferable Mass Spectrum Prediction via Reference-Guided Test-time Specialization

author.name: Yunhua Zhong, Runting Li, Yifan Li, Pan Liu, Zhiwen Yang, Zikun Wang, Yixuan Tang, Jun Xia

entry.summary: SPARC is a retrieval-guided test-time specialization framework that adapts pretrained tandem mass spectrum predictors using spectral reference libraries without accessing test-query spectra. It recalibrates fragment intensities within the learned fragmentation space using chemically related references, improving transfer across chemical-space and instrument-condition shifts.

entry.title: Neural Harmonic Measure Operator

author.name: Jinjin He, Sinan Wang, Yuchen Sun, Bo Zhu

entry.summary: NHMO is a neural solver for elliptic PDEs on variable-shape domains that parameterizes the harmonic measure density as a transformer-based boundary kernel supervised by Walk-on-Spheres samples, separating geometry from boundary data. One trained kernel handles arbitrary boundary values without retraining, with an extension to Poisson problems via classical decomposition and an auxiliary correction network.

entry.title: Kolmogorov-Arnold networks in nuclear binding energy prediction

author.name: Hao Liu, Jin Lei, Zhongzhou Ren

entry.summary: The authors apply Kolmogorov-Arnold networks (KANs) to predict nuclear binding energies using AME2020 data, achieving 0.26 MeV RMSE and surpassing traditional models. Symbolic regression on the KAN yields simplified analytical expressions consistent with classical formulas like the Bethe-Weizsaecker liquid drop model. This demonstrates KANs as an interpretable architecture for scientific regression problems.

entry.title: Knowledge-Driven XRD Phase Identification via Multi-View Retrieval and Explanation

author.name: Doaa Mohamed, Markus Stricker

entry.summary: A framework for X-ray diffraction phase identification combining a convolutional autoencoder for latent representations, similarity-based retrieval from a reference database, and explainable decision support. It targets high-throughput materials discovery scenarios where reference patterns for novel materials are unavailable.

entry.title: Uncertainty Quantification of Next Generation Reservoir Computing with Applications to Memory-Driven Dynamical Systems

author.name: Livia Popa, Sumanta Basu, Martin T. Wells

entry.summary: The paper develops uncertainty quantification for Next Generation Reservoir Computing using Bayesian ridge and conformal prediction intervals, characterizing when the two approaches agree or diverge. It reveals a regularization-driven tradeoff between estimation variance, shrinkage bias, and posterior uncertainty, with explicit regime transitions in high dimensions.

entry.title: Controllable GNN Explanations via Multi-Metric Preference Selection

author.name: Rachit Verma, Yashraj J. Deshmukh, Anirban Dasgupta

entry.summary: This work proposes a method for generating graph neural network explanations that optimizes across fidelity, interpretability (familiar motif patterns), and stability under structural perturbations, exposing the relative weighting as a user-controllable preference. Experiments on standard benchmarks (MUTAG, BA-2Motif, BAMultiShapes, PROTEINS) show higher-fidelity explanations than state-of-the-art baselines. It addresses the common limitation that GNN explainers optimize only fidelity under sparsity.

entry.title: Gradient-Guided Decoupled Adaptation for Geospatial Vision-Language Models

author.name: Dongdong Wang, Deepak Balakrishnan, Ravi Srinivasan, Shenhao Wang

entry.summary: The paper observes heterogeneous gradient characteristics across tasks in multi-task adaptation of geospatial vision-language models and proposes G2DA, which partitions tasks into vision- and language-centric groups via gradient-guided cross-modal decoupling to reduce interference during fine-tuning.

entry.title: Re-derivability Decides What a Staged Agent Pipeline Recovers After an Upstream Fault

author.name: Tianqi Bu, YuXuan Peng, Junteng Tu, Henghui Xiao

entry.summary: Studies staged LLM agent pipelines under a deterministic upstream fault and shows that re-exposing the original problem to downstream stages improves accuracy across four open-weight backbones. The paper introduces re-derivability as the key variable governing fault recovery and carefully controls agents, items, fault, and topology on GSM-hard items at temperature zero.

entry.title: USAI-Quant: A Quantitative Reasoning Benchmark for Vision-Language Models in Built Environments

author.name: Dongdong Wang, Qingqi Song, Yuzhou Chen, Deepak Balakrishnan, Ravi Shankar Srinivasan, Shenhao Wang

entry.summary: Presents the first benchmark for quantitative evaluation of VLM reasoning on built-environment metrics from remote sensing imagery, curated from the 335 largest U.S. cities. It targets the gap where existing VQA benchmarks are largely qualitative, and finds that state-of-the-art VLMs struggle with quantitative reasoning on such imagery.

entry.title: SynCo: Learning Cross-Modal Synergy by Contrasting Interaction Residuals

author.name: Yavuz Yarici, Ghassan AlRegib

entry.summary: SynCo is a multimodal contrastive learning method that targets synergy undertraining: building on Partial Information Decomposition, it observes that standard contrastive objectives capture mostly redundant information, and it adds dedicated supervision on interaction residuals to learn synergistic information available only from joint observation of modalities. This improves the transferability of multimodal representations beyond redundancy-only objectives.

entry.title: MorphAtt: A Neuromorphic Accelerator for Efficient Multi-Head Attention Processing in Spiking Vision Transformers

author.name: Rachmad Vidya Wicaksana Putra, Amirhesam Jafari Rad, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: MorphAtt is a digital neuromorphic accelerator that speeds up multi-head self-attention in spiking vision transformers using cascaded hardware modules: a spiking QKV generator, a low-complexity spiking attention engine, and reparameterization convolution. The design targets energy-efficient edge inference where SViT parameter counts and attention costs are bottlenecks. It contributes hardware-software co-design for low-power vision transformers.

entry.title: What Survives the Codec Shift: Pooled No-Vocals Residuals for Speech Deepfake Detection

author.name: Jiajun Xu, Menglu Li, Xiao-Ping Zhang

entry.summary: This work investigates which acoustic representations remain discriminative for speech deepfake detection as synthesis shifts from vocoders to neural codecs, comparing 12 representations under a shared linear classifier. It finds complementary behavior between hierarchical XLS-R features and pooled no-vocals residual statistics, and combines them into a dual-view detector called MN-P that generalizes to unseen codecs.

entry.title: Sharp training-conditional coverage for conformal prediction under covariate shift

author.name: Mehrdad Pournaderi

entry.summary: This paper derives explicit training-conditional coverage bounds for weighted split conformal prediction under covariate shift using a single concentration inequality, showing the correct scale is a variance proxy based on chi-squared divergence rather than the supremum of the likelihood ratio. It also provides matching two-point lower bounds, establishing sharpness of the analysis.

entry.title: LieDiscover: Adaptive Symbolic Library Construction for Explicit Open-form Symmetry Discovery

author.name: Xinxin Li, Jianming Ma, Xingyu Cui, Da Li, Juan Zhang, Junping Yin

entry.summary: LieDiscover formulates data-driven Lie symmetry discovery as joint optimization over the function library and generator coefficients, using an encoder-decoder architecture to dynamically generate symbolic expressions. This overcomes the limitation of predefined libraries in existing explicit methods, which struggle with high-order polynomial or transcendental symmetries.

entry.title: TopoMamba: A Load-Support Relation-Guided Multi-Directional State-Space Model for Topology Optimization

author.name: Bin Lou, Yuxuan Cheng, Huaizhi Zong, Junhui Zhang, Bing Xu

entry.summary: TopoMamba applies a state-space (Mamba-style) model to topology optimization, using load-support relations to guide multi-directional scanning and spatially adaptive fusion for predicting material distributions. It improves out-of-distribution generalization over existing deep methods while lowering computational cost.

entry.title: Weighted Spline-Expanded Networks with Distributional Balancing for Continuous Treatment Effects

author.name: Shucheng Liu, Chan Park, Guanhua Chen

entry.summary: WSENet is an end-to-end neural framework for estimating causal effects of continuous treatments, combining distance-based covariate balancing weights, structured treatment embeddings with spline expansion, and bias-corrected outcome estimation. It targets confounding, misspecification, and high-dimensional covariates in observational studies.

entry.title: Laya as a Typed Probabilistic Assessor: An Independent Reproduction and a Preregistered Study of Calibration and Selective Escalation

author.name: Gowthamkumar Nandakishore

entry.summary: An independent, preregistered reproduction of the Laya 421M-parameter typed assessor finds the shipped checkpoint is uniformly under-confident, contradicting the model card's over-confidence framing, and shows a single fitted temperature (T=0.469) cuts held-out ECE from 0.204 to 0.037, outperforming the shipped per-option-count table. The direction of miscalibration determines which way a confidence-gated escalation cascade fails.

entry.title: Two-Sample Testing for Inhomogeneous Random Graphs in Non-Integral $L_r$ Norms

author.name: Soham Dan

entry.summary: This paper resolves a gap in the optimal sample complexity of two-sample testing for inhomogeneous Erdos-Renyi graphs under non-integral Lr norms with r greater than 2, where prior upper and lower bounds did not match. The proposed test runs two existing statistics of orders 2 and ceiling-of-r on the same data, rejecting if either rejects, with thresholds unified via Hoelder interpolation. This closes a conjectured-tight lower bound with a matching upper bound.

entry.title: The Double-Edged Sword of Information: Revealed versus Hidden Lotteries in School Choice

author.name: Parinaz Naghizadeh, Jingyan Wang

entry.summary: The paper studies whether revealing lottery numbers in school choice matching helps or hurts, challenging prior theoretical claims that revelation strictly improves matches under deferred acceptance. It relaxes the unrealistic assumption that all students share identical preference rankings and analyzes the resulting tradeoffs.

entry.title: Functional Autoencoders for Amplitude-Phase Representation Learning

author.name: Peida Wu, Xinyang Xiong, Pengcheng Zeng
