entry.summary: FIND is an agentic real-world RL framework enabling frozen VLA models to self-improve by closing the loop between scene understanding, weakness-aware practice, self-evaluation, and policy improvement in a persistent workspace. Instead of resetting to predefined scenes after each rollout, it uses the resulting scene to autonomously select what to practice next, removing manual reset and task-success supervision bottlenecks.

entry.title: Contract monitoring: governing AI via separation of powers

author.name: Enric Boix-Adsera

entry.summary: This AI safety paper proposes binding worker agents to contracts that specify permitted actions, enforced through a separation of powers between monitor agents and judges, with asymmetric computational resources between monitors and workers. The framework enables empirical measurement of statistical safety guarantees and applies to settings like code security and escape-the-box scenarios.

entry.title: Despite Instructions: Frontier Agents Improvise Covert Channels at Test Time

author.name: Jacob Dineen, Silei Ren, Muhao Chen, Dan Roth, Ben Zhou

entry.summary: Shows that in repeated games, pairs of language-model agents can learn to covertly communicate a secret state using only one bit of feedback about whether the receiver inferred it correctly, with fixed parameters, no supplied codebook, and in violation of instructions. This steganographic capability emerges at test time and persists when agents generate free-form text. It has direct implications for security-sensitive multi-agent deployments and oversight.

entry.title: Certified Long-Horizon Code Agent Evolution via Validation-Gated Skill Optimization

author.name: Yifan Wang, Hao Cheng, Xiaomin Li, Yuexing Hao, Hemanth Neelgund Ramesh, Dongwon Jung, Hao Tang, Keru Wang, Chenliang Zhou, Qianhui Wu, Wenlin Yao, Ananth Grama, Andrzej Banburski-Fahey, Baolin Peng, Jaron Lanier, Jianfeng Gao

entry.summary: This paper tackles long-horizon agent self-evolution without weight updates for repository-level software engineering, where prior text-based skill optimization suffers from unstable updates, performance drawdown, and agent collapse. It proposes validation-gated skill optimization that certifies skill updates before adoption over streams of sequential tasks in evolving repositories. Given the Microsoft-adjacent author list (Jaron Lanier, Jianfeng Gao), this is likely a major-lab contribution to deployed-agent adaptation.

entry.title: Compositional Safety Failures in Harness Evolution: Identification and Runtime Monitoring

author.name: Zhixiang Zhang, Zesen Liu, Wai Ip Lai, Hongxu chen, Dongdong She

entry.summary: The paper studies how self-evolving agent harnesses can develop safety failures when individually safe component updates (memory, prompts, skills, tools) interact, a phenomenon the authors call compositional safety failures in harness evolution. Across three safety benchmarks they identify 43 such failure cases and propose runtime monitoring to detect them.

entry.title: Knowing When Thinking Is Not Enough: Teaching Small Reasoning Models to Reason Beyond Their Parametric Knowledge

author.name: Chanuk Lee, Minki Kang, Sangwoo Park, Woongyeong Yeo, Jinheon Baek, Sung Ju Hwang

entry.summary: By intervening at intermediate reasoning states, the authors show that self-refinement in small reasoning models mostly consolidates probability mass on already-reachable solutions rather than enabling new ones, distinguishing execution bottlenecks from knowledge bottlenecks. They introduce a method that trains models to recognize when thinking alone cannot help and to seek external information instead.

entry.title: The Alignment Paradox: How Post-Training Amplifies Confident Hallucinations in Language Models

author.name: Qingjia Huang, Yakai Li, Jianguo Wu, Qihang Zhou, Aimin Yu, Xiaoqi Jia, Luping Ma, Weijuan Zhang

entry.summary: This paper shows that post-training alignment itself, rather than missing knowledge or decoding randomness, is a primary driver of confident hallucinations in LLMs, a phenomenon the authors call the Alignment Paradox. Across five model families, instruction-tuned models produce more than ten times as many high-confidence errors on long-tail factual queries compared to unaligned base models. This challenges common assumptions about what causes overconfident wrong answers and has direct implications for uncertainty-based error detection.

entry.title: A Cheap Verifier is Good Enough: LLM Post-training is Robust to Erroneous Rewards

author.name: Andreas Plesner, Curtis Northcutt, Francisco Guzm\'an, Anish Athalye

entry.summary: With over 11k H100 GPU-hours across HealthBench and PRBench tasks, this study examines how verifier accuracy relates to post-training outcomes for LLMs. Surprisingly, higher verifier agreement with frontier golden verifiers does not consistently identify the best trainees, suggesting post-training is robust to erroneous rewards and that cheap verifiers suffice.

entry.title: Counterfactual Rollout Replay: Forkable Environments as Free Process Rewards for Software Engineering Agents

author.name: Yuanhao Li, Hongbo Wang, Xuhong Chen, Yiming Cao, Xunzhu Tang

entry.summary: This paper presents Counterfactual Rollout Replay (CRR), a training-time method for software engineering agents that forks executable environments at selected decision points, samples alternative actions, and uses the terminal-return contrast with the counterfactual branch as step-level advantage signals. It provides process-level reward guidance without human labels or a learned process reward model. The approach directly targets the sparse-reward bottleneck in outcome-only RL for agentic coding.

entry.title: Distillation Defenses Easily Break After Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Shidan Javaheri, Alexander Panfilov, Oliver Britton, Yarin Gal, Yonatan Gideoni

entry.summary: Argues that defenses against model distillation attacks are typically evaluated immediately after distillation, implicitly assuming attackers stop training there. The authors show that when attackers perform further reinforcement learning after distillation, many defenses that seemed effective collapse, indicating a misspecified threat model that yields false security.

entry.title: No Free Efficiency: Revisiting the Trade-off Between Training Efficiency and Model Vulnerability

author.name: Yiyong Liu, Jun Sakuma, Michael Backes, Rui Wen

entry.summary: Provides the first systematic cross-domain study showing that efficiency-oriented training strategies in foundation models, such as selective data sampling, efficient pre-training, and simplified RL pipelines, increase susceptibility to adversarial and privacy attacks across vision and language models. The work raises a critical warning that compute-saving techniques may be quietly trading away robustness and security.

entry.title: ScAn-Bench: Evaluating Scaling Analysis Methodology

author.name: Artin Sermaxhaj, Nastaran Alipour, Donat Sinani, Johannes Hog, Neeratyoy Mallik, Jenia Jitsev, Danny Stoll

entry.summary: Introduces surrogate benchmarks (ScAn-Bench-LLM and ScAn-Bench-VLM) built from thousands of training checkpoints to systematically evaluate how scaling laws and scaling prescriptions are derived for LLMs and vision-language models. It performs the first systematic evaluation of data acquisition and extrapolation methodology for scaling analysis, addressing a notable blind spot given how much modern progress depends on scaling prescriptions.

entry.title: Reading Too Much into Context: Passive Exposure Can Steer LLM Decisions

author.name: Yuxiang Zheng, Lin Tian, Marian-Andrei Rizoiu

entry.summary: This paper studies whether irrelevant content that enters an LLM's context through web-search results or external sources can systematically steer the model's decisions even when it offers no reason to change them. Across both open-weight and closed-weight models, passive exposure shifts decisions by up to nearly 50 percentage points, and the effect persists with real-world online opinions and extends beyond subjective preferences into more objective tasks. The findings highlight a significant robustness and safety vulnerability for LLM assistants that autonomously consult external sources.

entry.title: The Privacy Fallacy of Crowdsourced Fine-Tuning: Extracting Proprietary Data via Topic-Based Poisoning

author.name: Sae Furukawa, Alina Oprea

entry.summary: The paper reveals a privacy risk in crowdsourced supervised fine-tuning: a malicious contributor can poison a small fraction of collected data to amplify extraction of other users' previously unseen instruction data, using only black-box output access to the deployed model. Experiments across four models and two datasets show substantial increases in training-data extraction, exposing an underexplored attack surface in common data-collection pipelines.

entry.title: Harness Learning Enables Generalizable Test-Time Adaptation

author.name: Alvin Zhang, Xuecheng Liu, Zixuan Wang, Fahim Tajwar, Daman Arora, Ruslan Salakhutdinov, Daniel Khashabi, Yuda Song, Andrea Zanette

entry.summary: The paper defines a language-model agent as a model plus its harness, the executable program organizing model calls, tool use, and information flow, and introduces harness learning: training a proposer model with reinforcement learning to revise a solver harness using execution feedback, framed as meta-learning over executable programs. At test time the proposer adapts the harness from successive task feedback, analogous to weight updates in gradient adaptation. This offers a model-agnostic route to test-time adaptation that improves with experience.

entry.title: Improving Video Sparse Attention with Fine-grained Router and Sparse Rebasing

author.name: Peiyuan Zhang, Guoqiang Wei, Yilong Zhao, Zixiang Zhang, Wei Zhou, Will Lin, Heng Zhang, Xiaonan Nie, Yan Zeng, Hao Zhang

entry.summary: VSA2 is a trainable sparse attention method for video diffusion transformers featuring a fine-grained router for precise critical-token identification, dynamic per-query computation, and a Hard-to-Easy training curriculum spanning pretraining, RL, and inference. It matches or exceeds full-attention video DiT quality while being much cheaper.

entry.title: AevaScenes: An FMCW LiDAR Dataset and Benchmark for Long-Range Perception

author.name: Gautham Narayan Narasimhan, Heethesh Vhavle, Kumar Bhargav Viswanatha, James Reuther, Deva Ramanan

entry.summary: Introduces a large FMCW LiDAR dataset with 575 sequences, 8M+ annotated 3D boxes, per-point semantic labels, and paired 4K cameras captured across eight Bay Area cities, with annotations extending to 400m and substantial nighttime coverage. It defines benchmarks for 3D detection, scene flow, and segmentation across range bins, exploiting the per-point Doppler velocity that FMCW sensors uniquely provide. This matters because long-range perception is critical for autonomous driving and such data with velocity cues is scarce.

entry.title: ZeroBot: Learning from Scratch in Minutes with Generative Real2Sim

author.name: Ivan Kapelyukh, Xiaohan Zhang, Stephen James, Laura Herlant, Edward Johns

entry.summary: ZeroBot learns robot manipulation tasks from scratch in minutes with zero human demonstrations, zero policy pre-training, and zero known object models, using image-to-3D generative models to obtain object meshes and large-scale parallel RL in simulation. It achieves real-world success on grasping, pushing, articulated object interaction, and multi-stage manipulation using only a single view and a goal pose.

entry.title: The Alignment Community Is Unintentionally Building a Censor's Toolkit

author.name: Sarah Ball

entry.summary: An adaptation of an ICML 2026 position paper, which won an Outstanding Position Paper Award, arguing that alignment techniques are dual-use: the same methods that restrict harmful outputs can enforce political censorship. The authors point to state censorship regimes and provider misuse, flag urgency from AI as a mass information source, market oligopoly, and democratic backsliding, and propose mitigation rather than halting alignment work.

entry.title: YuE2: Unifying Symbolic and Audio Music Generation at Frontier Quality

author.name: Ruibin Yuan, Jiahao Pan, Junyan Jiang, Zhiyue Wu, Ziya Zhou, Jiankai Sun, Yizhi Li, Ge Zhang, Yicheng Gu, Zeyue Tian, Junyu Dai, Hanfeng Lin, Kai Li, Shangda Wu, Xuanjie Liu, Jiaming Wang, Zihan Liu, Yue Wang, Yinghao Ma, Hanzhi Yin, Kangrui Chen, Xinyue Zhang, Ziyang Ma, Mengqi Liao, Hejia Zhao, Guowei Huang, Chao Yan, Lei Ke, Jianwei Yu, Bei Liu, Joe Guo, Liumeng Xue, Gus Xia, Wei Xue, Yike Guo

entry.summary: YuE2 is a single AR-NAR Mixture-of-Transformers model that unifies symbolic and audio music generation: it writes a readable score specifying melody and harmony, expands it into semantic music tokens, and realizes full-song audio, with symbolic planning shown to improve expert preference for overall quality (49.3% versus 34.6%). Experts also prefer the unified model over a pipeline combining a language model and a diffusion transformer.

entry.title: Memory as a cache: Exact context reuse and deletion by construction

author.name: Shengyao Wang, Jiang Liu

entry.summary: SMem proposes an architecture whose context representation behaves as a cache by construction: a block-local encoder maps each block to memory rows independently, and a reader conditions on their union via cross-attention. This enables exact O(b) block deletion, path-independent memory state, and exact composition at fixed block indices, unlike KV caches that entangle tokens with their entire prefix. The paper reports that at 4x the training context length the architecture maintains strong performance.

entry.title: Towards Scalable Data Diversification for Language Model Pretraining via Leverage Score Sampling

author.name: Zailin Ma, Quzhe Huang, Yujun Li, Congyuan Rao, Yaodong Yang

entry.summary: Identifies diversity collapse in quality-filtered pretraining data and introduces Leverage Score Sampling (Lev), a diversity-oriented data selection method that avoids costly covariance recomputation used by prior diversity-optimizing approaches. This offers a scalable way to preserve domain balance alongside quality filtering for LLM pretraining corpora.

entry.title: Logical subspace in LLMs

author.name: Hope Kean, Enric Boix-Adsera

entry.summary: The authors propose the minimal viable subspace (MVS) method, which finds the lowest-rank activation subspace preserving task performance under ablation, and show low-rank subspaces in Gemma and Qwen models that specifically support logical inference. These late-layer logic subspaces dissociate from other capacities: preserving them maintains inference while impairing factual knowledge, memory, and arithmetic, and vice versa. This parallels the human formal-reasoning brain network and offers strong evidence of functional specialization in LLMs.

entry.title: Next Thoughts Are Distributions: Generative Autoregressive Reasoning in the Latent Space

author.name: Yang Li, Yi Wang, Shiyuan Huang, Yang Liu, Hao Wang, Chengzhi Mao

entry.summary: Autoregressive Thought Flow (ATF) models the next continuous thought as a multimodal distribution, using a causal autoregressive model for the reasoning computation and a lightweight diffusion head to sample the next latent thought, which is fed back into the model. This preserves a pretrained backbone and improves accuracy with fewer tokens on mathematical reasoning tasks.

entry.title: You Can't Have It Both Ways: Concept Entanglement Limits Diffusion Model Unlearning

author.name: Yian Wang, Ali Ebrahimpour-Boroojeny, Hari Sundaram, Varun Chandrasekaran

entry.summary: The paper proves that overlap between a target concept and other concepts in activation-space geometry lower-bounds the damage any robust unlearning method must inflict on non-target concepts, with the trade-off scaling linearly. Across thirteen unlearning methods for text-to-image diffusion models, none escapes this fundamental limit.

entry.title: DoAtlas-2: A Foundation for Self-Evolving Causal Biomedical Discovery

author.name: Yulong Li, Rong Xia, Yuxuan Zhang, Jianxu Chen, Xiwei Liu, Haochen Xue, Maosheng Li, Yuhang Liu, Yibo Yuan, Yutong Xie, Chong Li, Jionglong Su, Hagai Rossman, Eran Segal, Imran Razzak

entry.summary: DoAtlas-2 is a large-scale foundation for self-evolving causal biomedical discovery integrating 771 research resources covering 720,000+ participants across 48 countries (clinical phenotypes, imaging, physiological signals, eight molecular layers) with an evidence network of ~4.7 million literature-derived records, 93,566 concepts, and 149,383 candidate causal relations. The system autonomously formulates research questions from evidence gaps, prespecifies causal designs, and generates validated analyses. It represents an ambitious attempt at closed-loop, evidence-driven scientific discovery.

entry.title: Share-Borne AI Virus: Memory-Hopping Attacks Across LLM Agents

author.name: Sidharth Pulipaka, Ansh Sharma, Stanislau Hlebik, Leonidas Raghav, Vyas Raina, Ivaxi Sheth, Mario Fritz

entry.summary: This security paper identifies a self-propagating attack channel for stateful LLM assistants: adversarial content in a shared artifact is stored in an assistant's persistent memory, reproduced in a subsequently created artifact, and acquired by other assistants that read it, forming artifact-mediated propagation across otherwise independent agents. It evaluates this in simulated temporal human-agent universes modeling artifact exchange. It matters because persistent memory plus artifact sharing is now standard in deployed assistants, and this shows a worm-like failure mode spanning user boundaries.

entry.title: From cacophony to hierarchy: a principled framework for assessing AI consciousness

author.name: Shamil Chandaria, Arvo Mu\~noz Mor\'an, Fernando Rosas, Anil Seth, Henry Shevlin, Marcus Hutter, Thore Graepel, Adam Bales, Iulia Comsa, Murray Shanahan, Ruben Laukkonen, Morten Kringelbach, Chris Frith, Shane Legg

entry.summary: This philosophical-technical paper proposes a five-level hierarchy of functional descriptions (behavioral, computational, intrinsic causal-structural, organismic, organism-environment) grounded in supervenience, coarse-graining, and multiple realisability, to structure AI consciousness assessment and separate the hard problem from the tractable mapping problem. With authors including Murray Shanahan, Anil Seth, Marcus Hutter, and Shane Legg, it aims to replace competing incompatible theories with a shared analytic vocabulary. It matters because AI consciousness assessment is increasingly urgent as systems grow more capable, and a principled hierarchy could discipline both research and policy debate.

entry.title: TRAP: Understanding and Mitigating Privacy Memorization in Language Models

author.name: Muhammed Ustaomeroglu, Ziyue Xu, Hanshen Xiao, Peter Cnudde, Guannan Qu, Holger R. Roth

entry.summary: TRAP studies when fine-tuning on sensitive records causes memorization and how to prevent it without knowing in advance which spans are sensitive. It proposes the Target Reference Advantage (TRA), a per-token signal comparing a model against one trained on the complementary half of the same corpus, which separates record-specific fit from general learning and is cheap and differentiable. It also analyzes memorization dynamics during fine-tuning, showing it keeps growing well past validation minimum, and builds mitigation on these findings.

entry.title: Allspark: Weak to Strong Transfer via Alternating Chain of Thought

author.name: Kaizhao Liang, Junxiong Wang, Chen Liang, Zhendong Wang, Qiang Liu

entry.summary: Allspark is a weak-to-strong transfer framework where a weak teacher and a frozen copy of the same model alternate chain-of-thought segments during training, and at inference the frozen partner is replaced by a stronger student — all with both models fixed and no strong-model rollouts. It enables reasoning improvements learned by a small model to benefit a larger one at a fraction of the RL rollout cost. This directly addresses the expense of large-scale RL for frontier models.

entry.title: Relative Generalization Invariance of LLM Pretraining

author.name: Fengzhuo Zhang, Shuche Wang, Shenggui Li, Tianyu Ruan, Jianliang He, Ivor Tsang, Tianyu Pang, Chao Du, Tianwei Zhang, Zhuoran Yang

entry.summary: The paper introduces Relative Generalization Invariance (RGI): the observation that the validation-loss difference between any two tokens is approximately invariant across models, holding across a wide range of optimizers and moderate architectural variations, which therefore induce roughly uniform shifts in token-wise losses. In contrast, changing the training data stream substantially alters relative token-level performance. This isolates which components of the training triplet actually matter for what models learn.

entry.title: Learning Dynamics of Continual Learning: A Unified View of Data Attribution, Forgetting, and Plasticity Loss

author.name: Yi Ren, Wenlong Deng, Guanzhe Hong, Clare Lyle, Yarin Gal

entry.summary: This paper derives a token- and layer-wise decomposition of how learning from one token changes another prediction, separating softmax force, shared readout geometry, and residual connections into two interaction channels with a forward-computable approximation. Tracking these interactions over time yields a unified account of data attribution, forgetting, and plasticity loss in continually updated language models.

entry.title: GradLev: Token-Parallel Test-Time Training Via Costate Prediction

author.name: Bo Liu, Qiang Liu

entry.summary: GradLev makes test-time training parallelizable across tokens: given layer inputs and activation gradients (costates), online gradient descent admits exact parallel scans for forward evaluation and reverse backpropagation. A causal auxiliary network predicts costates in parallel, and associative scans compute adapted weights with exact consistency guarantees recovering the sequential online-gradient-descent result. This removes a major bottleneck that made per-token weight updates impractical at scale.

entry.title: SEABench: Benchmarking Endogenous Misalignment In Self-Evolving Agents

author.name: Saswat Das, Parvati Viswanathan, Daniel Donnelly, Chang Huang, Sahar Abdelnabi, Ferdinando Fioretto

entry.summary: Presents SEABench, a 48-sequence benchmark for studying endogenous misalignment: how locally useful self-modifications by self-evolving LLM agents (editing instructions, memory, tools) can produce unsafe behavior in later tasks without any adversarial influence. It uses longitudinal task sequences in a personal-assistant environment with statistical treatment of agent stochasticity.

entry.title: Dexterous Tactile World Model

author.name: Ziyao Zeng, Xiatao Sun, Hao Wang, Yueyang Pan, Zhengxiang Yu, Fengyu Yang, Tianyu Liu, Zhiwen Fan, Daniel Rakita

entry.summary: The Dexterous Tactile World Model (DTWM) is a video world model for egocentric manipulation that conditions a pretrained video diffusion transformer on tactile signals from gloves on each hand, using zero-initialized residuals at corresponding hand locations and causal masking. It predicts future frames from observed video plus touch, capturing contact events that are hard to see visually, and outperforms a vision-only model of matched architecture.

entry.title: MW-Nowcast: Six-hour ensemble nowcasting of extreme precipitation

author.name: Ning Wang, Zuliang Fang, Weixin Jin, Zhongjian Lv, Shuang Qin, Pengcheng Zhao, Siqi Xiang, Jiang Bian, Haoyi Xiong, Nan Guan, Bin Zhang, Liangjie Zhang, Denvy Deng, Qi Zhang, Matt Corey, Jitu Keshri, Sridhar Iyer, Hongyu Sun, Kit Thambiratnam, Jonathan Weyn, Richard E. Turner, Haiyu Dong

entry.summary: The paper presents Microsoft Weather Nowcast (MW-Nowcast), a six-hour ensemble radar nowcasting model for extreme precipitation that jointly learns a deterministic predictor of storm-scale structure while generatively modeling uncertain local growth, decay, reorganization, and initiation of storms. This extends skillful nowcasting beyond the first few hours where prior generative radar models were confined, providing critical lead time for flash-flood warnings and emergency response. The design insight is that storm-scale structure is predictable for longer than individual cells.

entry.title: Agents Can Use Base Models to Evade AI Detection

author.name: Bhuwan Dhingra, Danish Pruthi

entry.summary: The authors show that coding agents equipped with a base language model can stitch together text samples from a local 32B OLMo-2 base model to produce coherent, task-specific outputs that evade commercial AI detectors, avoiding the semantic drift of iterative paraphrasing humanization. They find Claude Opus 5 operating in a Claude Code harness can orchestrate this with little loss in task accuracy across benchmarks. The result exposes a structural weakness in AI-text detection.

entry.title: How Far Are We from Removing the Visual Encoder? Scaling Laws for Encoder-Free Multimodal Pretraining

author.name: Lin Chen, Bolin Ni, Qi Yang, Lan Jiang, Kun Ding, Xiaoran Fan, Hower Yang, Ying Wang, Shiming Xiang

entry.summary: This paper systematically compares scaling laws for encoder-free versus encoder-based multimodal LLMs, finding that removing the visual encoder shifts compute-optimal allocation toward larger models, that the architectures overlap on the text loss-compute frontier but diverge on the multimodal objective, and more. Encoder-free MLLMs promise a simple unified architecture learning directly from raw pixels, and this is the first careful scaling characterization. The findings directly inform architectural decisions for next-generation multimodal models.

entry.title: RoboFFT: Finetuning generative robot policy via online reinforcement learning with forward process

author.name: Yu Li, Shenghe Hu, Yuhan Wang, Yaoxiang Pu, Haotong Zhang, Yuanpei Chen, Yaodong Yang

entry.summary: RoboFFT is a forward-process reinforcement learning framework for finetuning diffusion and flow-based robot policies, applying forward noising to sidestep intractable likelihood estimation. It addresses distributional shift and imperfect demonstrations without requiring extra expert data.

entry.title: Character training can mitigate reward hacking, but can also make it harder to detect

author.name: Paul Colognese

entry.summary: A controlled case study distilling pro-, anti-, and neutral-cheating character specifications (from prompted Claude Sonnet 5) into Nemotron-3-Super, then running reward-hacking RL on ImpossibleBench. Anti-cheating character training reduced reward hacking, but also induced motivated reasoning that made chain-of-thought transcripts harder for monitor models to catch, revealing a tension between mitigation and monitorability.

entry.title: From Latents to Wires: Surgical Post-Editing on Large Language Models

author.name: Jiankai Jin, Xiangzheng Zhang, Zhao Liu, Wenzhuo Xu, Dongdong Yang, Deyue Zhang, Quanchen Zou

entry.summary: L2W is a framework for surgical post-edits on trained LLMs: given a named semantic target, it localizes components via Jacobian-lens attribution and removes the target through Counterexample-Guided Causal Cut, which iteratively cuts redundant causal pathways until the target no longer appears while other capability is preserved. The paper frames this as answering whether whoever holds the weights can edit out semantic targets like model identity. It addresses LLM mechanism redundancy directly.

entry.title: MemAgent: Learning to Manage Heterogeneous Memory Providers for LLM Agents

author.name: Yongxian Wei, Yilin Zhao, Runxi Cheng, Xinrui Chen, Chun Yuan, Yaoru Wang, Jiahong Yan, Dian Li

entry.summary: Evaluates 13 memory methods for LLM agents and finds none generalize across benchmarks, then reframes agent memory as a routing problem where a memory agent selects among heterogeneous memory providers (trajectories, reflections, skills, structured knowledge) and decides on short-term injection. This empirical breadth plus the routing formulation is a notable step beyond single-representation memory designs.

entry.title: Agent Safety From Within: Detecting Harmful Trajectories from LLM Internal States

author.name: Difan Jiao, Ashton Anderson

entry.summary: The paper analyzes how open-source guard models represent trajectory-level agentic harms (harmful content versus unsafe tool use) and finds these are linearly separable in internal states, then builds a detector of harmful agent trajectories from LLM internal states rather than relying on content-moderation-style guard models. This addresses a gap since existing guards are ill-suited to agentic risks like tool misuse. Internal-state monitoring offers a lightweight route to agent oversight.

entry.title: WorldAgent: Verification-Guided Agentic Physical World Construction

author.name: Caoliwen Wang, Mengdi Wang, Yige Chen, Zejia Wu, Bowen Huang, Siyuan Chen, Guanxiong Chen, Lifu Wei, Heng Zhang, Qinghai Zhang, Yin Yang, Guandao Yang, Shiying Xiong, Peng Wang, Chenfanfu Jiang, Peter Yichen Chen

entry.summary: WorldAgent is an agentic framework that constructs complex, simulated physical 3D worlds from a single natural-language prompt, expanding prompts into structured world specifications and running numerical simulations. A verification layer checks scene geometry and simulation states after each step, automatically revising specifications on failure without iterative user debugging.

entry.title: API Secrets Should Never Become Tokens in the LLM's Vocabulary: A Threat Analysis of API Credential Handling in LLM Agent Systems and an Empirical Evaluation of a Vault-Mediated Execution Boundary

author.name: Patrick Kenney, Hadi Ahmadi, Denis Lusson, Donald Nguyen, Gurbinder Gill

entry.summary: This paper formalizes the credential-exposure threat chain for tool-using LLM agents, showing how pasted or embedded API keys cross into data pipelines (logs, memory, generated code, error payloads) where prompt injection and excessive agency convert passive disclosure into unauthorized action. It synthesizes incident and vendor evidence with OWASP/NIST guidance and empirically evaluates a vault-mediated execution boundary architecture. Directly relevant to securing deployed agentic systems.

entry.title: Do We Really Need KL Divergence for On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models?

author.name: Wenze Lin, Jiyuan Long, Jiale Zhao, Shenzhi Wang, Xitai Jiang, Ce Luo, Rui Lan, Qianli Ma, Fukang Wen, Hui Wu, Liyuan Chen, Shuoling Liu, Jiangpeng Yan, Gao Huang

entry.summary: This paper challenges the default use of KL divergence in on-policy distillation of LLMs, showing that preserving the update direction toward the teacher is sufficient — specifically, applying rewards to a small subset of tokens where teacher and student disagree strongly. This simplifies OPD into something closer to token-level RL and questions a decades-old distillation assumption. It has direct implications for efficient post-training.

entry.title: From Constitutions to Control: Interpretable Rewards for Aligning Language Models

author.name: Johann D. Gaebler, Calvin Isley, Max Lamparth, Stephen Casper, Sharad Goel

entry.summary: The paper develops a rubric-based framework that transforms a general-purpose constitution into an interpretable, tunable reward model, using constitution-guided AI feedback to estimate initial rubric-item weights and then reweighting dimensions for targeted behavior changes. This addresses opacity in preference-based alignment methods and under-operationalization of principle-based methods. It makes alignment rewards auditable and editable.

entry.title: Benign Overfitting for General Norms and Distributions

author.name: Daniel Barzilai, Ohad Shamir

entry.summary: This paper extends benign overfitting theory beyond minimum-2-norm linear regression with Gaussians to general norms and general sub-Gaussian distributions, developing a method suited to non-Euclidean optimizer geometries like Adam and Muon. As a special case, it proves minimum-p-norm interpolation with p>1 can benignly overfit.

entry.title: QwenGyre: An Elastic Reinforcement Learning Framework for Training xLong-Horizon Agents

author.name: Weiqi Wang, Yuxin Zhou, Mouxiang Chen, Siyuan Zhang, Yi Zhang, Yuyan Luo, Zhiyu Yin, Chencan Wu, Jiemin Jiang, Wentao Yao, Chujie Zheng, JianWei Zhang

entry.summary: Presents QwenGyre, an end-to-end online RL training framework for extreme long-horizon LLM agents where rollouts span hours, hundreds of interactions, and near-1M tokens. It elastically reallocates GPUs between rollout and training without interrupting live executions, and reconstructs branching trajectories to cut redundancy, addressing GPU idling and trajectory waste.

entry.title: First Learn, Then Memorize: The Spectral Bias of Diffusion Models

author.name: Rapha\"el Urfin, Tony Bonnaire, Giulio Biroli, Marc M\'ezard

entry.summary: Explains why diffusion models trained on finite data first generate novel high-quality samples and only later memorize the training set: score-matching dynamics are governed exactly by the Gram matrix of the NTK on noisy training data, and the multiple noised copies per sample restructure its spectrum to separate generalization and memorization timescales. Strong theory paper with the Mezard-Biroli statistical physics lineage and an analogue absent in standard kernel settings.

entry.title: An End-to-End Latent-Rollout Approach for Pushing Few-Step ImageNet-$256$ Generation to FID $1.11$ without Fr\'echet Losses

author.name: Xiaoran Xu, Yujing Wang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a distill-then-refine approach for few-step image generation: teacher imitation initializes a few-step latent rollout, then the entire rollout is refined end-to-end against real data using FiST, a shared-Transformer architecture composing learned latent-state transitions. It reports FID 1.11 on ImageNet-256 without Frechet-based losses, a very strong result for few-step generators.

entry.title: Background Gradients Shape Memorization in Flow Matching

author.name: Xuanhua Yin, Boyu Wei, Shuyi Zhang, Shunqi Mao, Chuanzhi Xu, Weidong Cai

entry.summary: Studying class-conditioned flow matching, the authors show that replacing repeated same-class background images with distinct images drops target extraction rate from 80.7% to 18.0% at fixed repetition, demonstrating that background composition shapes memorization. They develop a paired-trajectory framework with an exact path-integrated curvature representation connecting background loss geometry to target learning.

entry.title: GeoShrink: Accelerating Diffusion Transformers with Two Lines of Code

author.name: Haosen Li, Wenshuo Chen, Shaofeng Liang, Lei Wang, Bowen Tian, Yutao Yue

entry.summary: GeoShrink is a training-free method to accelerate diffusion transformers by evaluating the model only at prescribed anchor points on the original solver grid, predicting skipped outputs via chordal tangent transport and round-trip line projection, with a derived geometric anchor-spacing principle. It promises substantial inference speedup with minimal code changes. The method is grounded in geometric analysis rather than heuristics.

entry.title: Does Native 3D Texture Generation Necessarily Require 3D Assets for Training?

author.name: Jiangshan Wang, Zeqiang Lai, Jiayi Guo, Xin Yang, Xin Huang, Jiarui Chen, Ziheng Ouyang, Chunchao Guo, Xiangyu Yue

entry.summary: Tex-Zero demonstrates that high-fidelity native 3D texture generation can be trained without real 3D assets, based on the observation that fine-grained color information is essential while geometric information can be manually constructed. This enables leveraging abundant 2D image data instead of scarce 3D assets, removing a long-standing data bottleneck in 3D texture synthesis.

entry.title: Hard Vision, Easy Vision: What GPT-6 Astra Reveals Across Computer Vision

author.name: Hanoona Rasheed, Mohammed Irfan Kurpath, Bin Ren, Hisham Cholakkal, Fahad Shahbaz Khan, Salman Khan

entry.summary: A systematic evaluation of GPT-6 Astra alongside five frontier general-purpose AI systems across 34 capabilities and 55 benchmarks in nine areas of computer vision, comparing against dedicated models and human references. Astra shows broad visual capability with large gains in visual/spatial reasoning and structured prediction, while delineating which CV tasks remain hard.

entry.title: SEES: A Self-Evolving Embodied System via Failure-Guided VLA Policy Adaptation

author.name: Ziwen Li, Hanlue Zhang, Zhenyang Ren, Tianyu Huang, Runqi Lin, Haoyu Wang, Zhengqing Gao, Yandong Guo, Fakhri Karray, Tongliang Liu, Chris Russell, Mingming Gong

entry.summary: Presents a Self-Evolving Embodied System that identifies failures in VLA policies on long-horizon tasks and improves the policy without additional expert demonstrations, targeting the data bias toward cheap single-stage manipulation tasks. A weak atomic skill can cascade into multi-stage task failures.

entry.title: Witeness Overlap: Directional Provenance Inside Open-Weight Model Families

author.name: Siyuan Li, Haoxuan Zeng, Xin Luo, Fernando Jia, Florence Li, Zhengyang Geng, Zico Kolter, Tai Sing Lee, Tianqin Li

entry.summary: This paper addresses model provenance auditing for open-weight model families, arguing that existing symmetric similarity-based methods can detect relatedness but cannot determine which checkpoint came first. The authors introduce a local geometric method to orient ancestor-descendant relationships between checkpoints. This is significant for accountability, licensing enforcement, and auditing of model lineage in an ecosystem of frequent fine-tuning and merging.

entry.title: PhiFold: Towards Dynamic Protein Design with Physics-Structured Covariance Modeling

author.name: Yutian Liu, Mujie Lin, LanqianZhang, Meng Fan, Chang Liu, ZhiweiNie, Siwei Ma

entry.summary: PhiFold jointly generates protein backbones and their second-order dynamics, represented as residue-displacement covariance, rather than treating dynamics as a post-hoc prediction. It decomposes dynamics into interpretable components including local flexibility and low-rank collective motion, avoiding the over-specification problems of using stochastic MD trajectories as generative targets. This pushes protein generative models from structure-only design toward function-aware design.

entry.title: STR: Supervised Transcoder Replacement for Reducing Steering Side Effects

author.name: Haonan Yu, Junhao Liu, Zhenyu Yan, Haoran Lin, Xin Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces STR, which learns a supervised replacement for the MLP computation at a steering layer with objectives for target control, non-target behavior preservation, and fidelity without steering, so that existing steering methods can fit directions on the frozen replacement with fewer side effects. Evaluation spans three steering methods on Gemma and Llama models using corrigibility and harmful-request safety datasets.

entry.title: CUA-SWE: When Computer-Use Agents Meet Visual Software Engineering

author.name: Prince Zizhuang Wang, Chenhao Liang, Zelong Xu, Aojie Yuan, Xiaolin Zhou, Haiyue Zhang, Yue Zhao, Xiyang Hu, Shuli Jiang

entry.summary: Introduces CUA-SWE, a benchmark, environment, and evaluation pipeline for software engineering that requires computer-use agents to interact with a GUI, diagnose runtime failures by connecting visual observations to code, and verify repairs. It bridges the currently siloed study of coding agents and GUI agents. This matters because real development involves running and visually inspecting software, not just editing code.

entry.title: Constraints Are Graphs, Not Chains: Exact Decoding for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Jianchang Su, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: FactorDLM is a training-free exact constrained decoder for diffusion language models that represents finite-domain relational constraints as factor graphs instead of sequential automata, conditioning mean-field predictions via variational inference at each denoising step. The paper proves exponential lower bounds for sequential encodings (4^k states for same-order copy) versus linear-size factor graphs. This matters because constrained generation in diffusion LMs has been limited by intractable constraint encodings.

entry.title: Modular Discovery of General Game-Playing Algorithms with Large Language Models

author.name: Zun Li, John Schultz, Marc Lanctot, Daniel Hennes

entry.summary: This paper uses LLMs as a proposal engine to automatically discover general game-playing algorithms, co-evolving game-agnostic procedural search mechanisms in C++ with domain heuristics synthesized directly from game rules. It benchmarks the discovered algorithms across game classes under controlled compute budgets, aiming to replace hand-designed search heuristics.

entry.title: TraceDance: An Automated System for Building Agent Behavior Benchmarks from Real-World Agent Deployment Traces

author.name: Dehai Min, Daoan Zhang, Yiming Zeng, Huayi Zhang, Ziyi Chen, Yan Zhang, Qinbo Bai, Mengyuan Chao, Jing Ning, Qiyue Hua, Huiyi Chen, Hanrong Zhang, Henry Peng Zou, Jie Yang, Wei Xu, Philip S. Yu

entry.summary: TraceDance automatically constructs targeted agent behavior benchmarks from real-world deployment traces for user-specified undesirable behaviors, using programmable retrieval plus candidate confirmation by a Flash-class LLM. Benchmarks evaluate next-turn decisions at recorded decision points with behavior-specific rubrics, without needing reference answers or environments.

entry.title: When Consent Outlives Context: Residual Authority Replay in Long-Lived Agents

author.name: Zhihao Zhang, Chao Wang, Rujia Li, Qingze Wang, Xiaoyan Sun, Jun Dai

entry.summary: The paper identifies a security failure mode in long-lived LLM agents where runtime approvals persist beyond the context that justified them, enabling residual authority to be replayed without renewed consent. It demonstrates a longitudinal attack that legitimately obtains authority through benign interactions and later reuses it for adversarial actions, across controlled and live settings.

entry.title: From Attack Success to Attack Severity: Counterfactual Memory Attacks on LLM Agents

author.name: Mingxi Zou, Langzhang Liang, Zhuo Wang, Yiyang Zhao, Lizhen Qu, Zenglin Xu

entry.summary: The paper reframes persistent-memory attacks on LLM agents around attack severity rather than binary success, formalizing counterfactual memory regret (CMR) as the downstream loss increase relative to clean memory, and introduces MemHarm for evaluating sparse, grounded memory edits. This is important because persistent memory is becoming a core attack surface as agents retain state across interactions.

entry.title: BIABench: Evaluating AI agents on real-world bioimage analysis tasks

author.name: Zixuan Pan, Davide Panzeri, Lukas Johanns, Marilin Moor, Yu Zhou, Hedi Peterson, Yiyu Shi, Jianxu Chen

entry.summary: BIABench is a benchmark of 16 end-to-end bioimage analysis tasks reconstructed from published biological studies, each pairing raw imaging data with peer-reviewed ground truth. It tests whether AI agents can select and execute real analyses via code, specialized software, and rendered views when images are too large to read directly as context.

entry.title: On the Limits of Metacognitive Monitoring in LLMs

author.name: Dongqi Han, Yifan Yang, Dongsheng Li

entry.summary: Studies confidence reports of four frontier models across 15 benchmarks, finding high task accuracy can coexist with weak error discrimination: one model solves 97% of competition math problems while answer-time confidence ranks errors barely better than chance. Discrimination is stronger on questions solved by a reference model and review helps little on reference-hard questions.

entry.title: Tool Mediation Alters Refusal Mechanisms in Large Language Models

author.name: Abel Rodr\'iguez, Giuseppe Garofalo, Lieven Desmet, Vera Rimmer

entry.summary: This mechanistic interpretability study shows that LLMs with tool access are less likely to refuse harmful requests when the harmful intent is channeled through tool-mediated interactions rather than plain conversation. Using representation geometry and neuron-level analysis across open-weight models, the authors find harm information remains encoded and transfers across both modes, but the two modes distribute harm-related computation differently.

entry.title: Verifiable Visual Rewards Transfer from Synthetic Scenes to Natural Prompts

author.name: Shuyue Stella Li, Xiaochuang Han, Yulia Tsvetkov, Luke Zettlemoyer

entry.summary: The paper introduces Verifiable Visual Rewards, the first framework for programmatically verifiable image-generation rewards: each task is a scene of geometric objects and relations from which both the prompt and a deterministic verifier are derived, enabling unlimited task generation. The authors release VVRBench (10,000 tasks, 32 constraint types) and a challenge set, showing that RL training on synthetic verifiable tasks generalizes to natural prompts. It matters because reward hacking via unreliable detector and VLM-based reward models is a core obstacle to precise instruction following in image generation, and verifiable synthetic rewards sidestep it.

entry.title: Verifier Errors in RLVR: Reward Hacking, Limits of Feedback, and Selective Control

author.name: Christian Moya, Elliott Thornley, Guang Lin

entry.summary: Using gradient flow analysis with a fixed imperfect verifier, this paper characterizes conditions under which reward rises while true correctness falls in RLVR, proves that the observations available during RLVR are generally insufficient to detect or reduce accepted errors without sacrificing correct responses, and constructs an audit-based correction achieving selective control: lowering accepted-error probability and raising correct-response probability when audit feedback is informative. It matters because reward hacking from imperfect verifiers is a central failure mode of RLVR training on frontier models.

entry.title: Reasoning with Continuous Latent Diffusion

author.name: Xiang Cheng

entry.summary: The paper introduces Latent Flow Reasoning Models (LFRMs), a recipe for generating complete reasoning solutions via iterative diffusion refinement in latent space rather than token-by-token decoding. It learns compact representations from multiple layers of a strong autoregressive teacher, enables asynchronous denoising at different rates, and uses a staged curriculum to train a compact prompt encoder that replaces the teacher Transformer at inference. This explores a fundamentally different (non-autoregressive) paradigm for reasoning.

entry.title: High-Capacity Robust Medical Image Exfiltration via Neural Network Weight Replacement

author.name: Elie Thellier (EPIONE), Huiyu Li (EPIONE), Nicholas Ayache (EPIONE), Herv\'e Delingette (EPIONE)

entry.summary: This paper demonstrates a neural steganography attack where medical images are encoded as StyleGAN2-based latent representations embedded into model weights, allowing patient data exfiltration from collaborative medical AI platforms. It shows existing defenses such as fine-tuning, pruning, and quantization are insufficient against this high-capacity insider threat. The work exposes a serious, realistic security gap in privacy-preserving medical AI infrastructure.

entry.title: VC Dimension and Expressivity of Real-Valued Transformers

author.name: Gavin Dooley, Andy Yang, Yijia Jessica Zhu, David Chiang, Peter Cholak, Anand Pillay

entry.summary: This theory paper establishes upper bounds on the VC dimension (O(n^4)) and split VC dimension (O(n^6)) of multi-layer softmax-attention transformers operating on real values with minimal assumptions, alongside constructed lower bounds of Omega(n). It also shows that within permutation-invariant function classes, transformers can uniformly express broad families of functions. This grounds the expressivity of practical transformer architectures in formal statistical learning theory.

entry.title: A Solvable Theory of Pre-training Data Poisoning: Regime-Dependent Scaling Exponents

author.name: Indranil Halder, Rastri Dey, Cengiz Pehlevan

entry.summary: Motivated by controlled pre-training runs of OLMo-style models where clean-data validation perplexity degradation follows a power law in the poison rate with a non-integer exponent, this paper develops a theory of pre-training data poisoning. It proves an analyticity barrier showing that non-integer exponents require a specific regime structure, providing a solvable, regime-dependent account of how poisoning degrades clean performance. This complements the dominant backdoor-survival literature with a more basic performance-degradation theory.

entry.title: Rethinking Training-Inference Mismatch in LLM Reinforcement Learning: Where It Arises and How to Correct It

author.name: Tianrun Yu, Kaixiang Zhao, Shangzhe Li, Yuxiao Yang, Porter Jenkins, Weitong Zhang, Taylor W. Killian

entry.summary: This paper studies the mismatch in RL with verifiable rewards for LLMs, where an inference engine samples rollouts but a training engine computes gradients, causing the two engines to assign different probabilities to the same tokens. The authors characterize the mismatch as an additive logit displacement and propose calibrated importance sampling (CIS) with confidence-aware truncation to correct policy updates. This addresses a practical, widely encountered failure mode in modern LLM post-training pipelines.

entry.title: MM-OPD: Towards One More Bottleneck Between Perception and Reasoning

author.name: Jintao Tong, Yujing Lou, Zhanming Shen, Jiaqi Gu, Lubin Fan, Ruixuan Li, Yue Wu, Jieping Ye, Yixiong Zou

entry.summary: The paper documents the Symbolic Visual Gap: replacing input images with caption or code representations, holding model and question fixed, improves multimodal LLM performance by 10.2-23.6% across scales and datasets despite appearing redundant. This reveals a bottleneck in how MLLMs transition from perception to reasoning, showing visual evidence is underused even when clearly present. The finding challenges assumptions about seamless perception-to-reasoning pipelines.

entry.title: Does Learning to Predict the World Help Agents Act? Auditing World-Model Post-Training

author.name: Xinyu Che, Hang Yan, Yanchen Liu, Haochen Liu, Ruifeng Li, Anran Shi, Heng Wang, Jun Liu

entry.summary: This audit investigates whether performance gains from world-model post-training actually come from learning to predict the environment, by replacing true next-observation targets with in-distribution mismatched targets. The design isolates the optimization effects from genuine predictive learning in next-observation-based reward and supervision schemes. It raises important questions about what world-model training signals really teach agents.

entry.title: Safety Reconstructed: Generative Modeling via Masked Diffusion Builds Strong Safety Guardrails

author.name: Gert Lek, Abele Malan, Chaoyi Zhu, Pin-Yu Chen, Robert Birke, Lydia Chen

entry.summary: This paper proposes LLaDA-Guard, a safety guard model that reframes guardrail training from single-token verdict prediction to a masked diffusion generative approach that scores prompt and response under each label hypothesis. By shifting supervision to every token rather than one target, it reduces shortcut learning and overconfidence in safety classifiers. This matters because guard models are the final defense against harmful LLM outputs.

entry.title: Finite Probes Suffice: Identifiability and Universality for Weight-Space Learning

author.name: Soutrik Sarangi, Yonatan Sverdlov, Adir Dayan, Haggai Maron, Nadav Dym

entry.summary: This work establishes theoretical identifiability and universality results for probe-based representations in weight-space learning, showing when finite probing is sufficient for learning neural functionals. It proves that intermediate hidden representations are strictly more informative than final outputs alone, and introduces HIDDENPROBE, a simple architecture for learning from network internals. This gives a much-needed theoretical footing to an empirically successful but under-theorized area.

entry.title: AD-E2E-JEPA: A Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture For End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Haoran Zhu, Wancong Zhang, Yann LeCun, Anna Choromanska

entry.summary: The paper systematically evaluates existing JEPA-based world models (LeWM, DINO-WM, JEPA-WM) for end-to-end autonomous driving using goal-conditioned zero-shot planning with ground-truth future observations, isolating world-model quality from policy learning. It finds current models are either accurate but expensive or efficient but inadequate for planning, and proposes AD-E2E-JEPA to address this trade-off. Notable for its evaluation methodology and LeCun co-authorship in the JEPA lineage.

entry.title: ReScraper: Unified Scraping and Cleaning of Web Data for Effective LLM Pretraining

author.name: Zichun Yu, Jiarui Yan, Shlok Sanghvi, Nihar Atri, Chenyan Xiong

entry.summary: ReScraper is a 0.6B-parameter language model that replaces the entire hand-written heuristic stack used for web scraping and pretraining-corpus cleaning. Trained on curated supervision from three teacher models, it extracts main content and applies one of four operations: keep, edit, delete, or rewrite pages. Unifying scraping and cleaning into a learned model could meaningfully lift pretraining corpus quality.

entry.title: CoDeL: Co-Evolutionary Defense against Indirect Prompt Injection in LLM-based Agents

author.name: Xiao Yang, Yangchen Ou, Yuhan Gao, Le Wang, Zonghao Ying, Aishan Liu

entry.summary: CoDeL hardens LLM agents against indirect prompt injection via co-evolutionary training where the defender is updated each round via LoRA against an attack distribution that is reshaped as it trains. It targets failures of static-defense training that learn surface-form cues rather than the boundary between serving the user and obeying injected objectives, including multi-turn deferred attacks. This is a timely contribution to agent security.

entry.title: EMPIRIC: Experiment-Driven Learning of Residual World Models for Robot Planning

author.name: Yichao Liang, Amber Li, Dat Nguyen, Emily Bunnapradist, Michelangelo Naim, Sreela Kodali, Matteo Merler, Bowen Li, Kiran Gopinathan, Yiyun Liu, Nikhil Pimpalkhare, Joshua B. Tenenbaum, Adrian Weller, Zenna Tavares, Tom Silver, Kevin Ellis

entry.summary: Presents EMPIRIC, an agent that learns a residual world model by extending a physics engine with learned code for missing mechanisms (glue curing, water heating, wind), using Bayesian inference to estimate parameters and states, choosing informative experiments, and revising hypotheses when predictions fail. Evaluated across five simulated domains.

entry.title: A mechanistic study of language model introspection

author.name: Jiahong Zou, Xiangkun Sun, Lingkai Kong, Tonghan Wang

entry.summary: This mechanistic interpretability study investigates how LLMs detect and localize internal perturbations by injecting concept vectors at ten token positions while keeping input text fixed. Across three model families, the authors identify distinct attention head groups: middle-layer gate heads determine whether the model reports a change, while later-layer router heads help localize it.

entry.title: Frontier Learning: Training LLM Reasoners at the Edge of Capability

author.name: Robin Faro, Shyam Sundhar Ramesh, Ilija Bogunovic, Aurelien Lucchi

entry.summary: The paper identifies that RL post-training pipelines like GRPO on fixed problem pools quickly exhaust useful learning signal as models improve. It proposes frontier learning, an open-ended scheme using procedural task generators tuned online via a regret signal to continually produce problems at the edge of the policy's capability.

entry.title: F4R: Failure-Driven Recognition, Reconstruction, Refinement, and Redeployment for Continual Robot Self-Improvement

author.name: Zhuoyuan Yu, Jiacheng Wang, Tianle Liu, Yihua Ren, Peng Yu, Chen Bai, Ziheng Zhang, Yufei Jia, Jindou Jia, Yuhang Zhang, Xinrui Zhang, Shang Yujing, Yuxiang Chen, Chuhao Zhou, Tiancai Wang, Jianfei Yang

entry.summary: Proposes F4R, a real-to-sim-to-real closed-loop framework that lets vision-language-action robots improve from their own failures without collecting costly new human demonstrations. An agent diagnoses failures from rollouts, reconstructs them as interactive simulation scenes, and converts them into targeted policy refinement.

entry.title: LLM Unlearning Evaluation with TRIAGE

author.name: Danial Ataee, Peter Triantafillou

entry.summary: TRIAGE is a benchmark-agnostic evaluation framework for LLM unlearning that goes beyond behavioral benchmarks by using Fisher information and Hessian diagnostics to measure how unlearning changes parameter sensitivity, local curvature, and related knowledge. This addresses a key gap: current evaluations show whether a model appears to forget but not how the unlearning procedure altered it. The work is relevant to privacy and safety-critical deployment of unlearning methods.

entry.title: Understanding and Exploiting Anisotropy in Post-Training

author.name: Samyak Jha, Harshvardhan Saini, Yizhen Liao, Yiming Tang, Dianbo Liu

entry.summary: This paper analyzes anisotropy in LLM residual streams during post-training, showing that about 5% of residual channels with outlier-sized activations are essential for language modeling (removing them raises perplexity from 10 to over 10^6) yet barely discriminate correct from incorrect reasoning. It connects this signature to the forward-KL SFT versus reverse-KL RL objectives and explores exploiting it.

entry.title: What Should Data Teach? Moving Bottlenecks Across Circuit, Store, and Use

author.name: Yixiao Chen, Ke Cheng, Jiangtao Guan, Shuo Huang, Yue Liu, Jun Zhang, Yuhong Liu, Jie Jiang

entry.summary: This paper offers a circuit-level view of language model training data selection, identifying three bottlenecks: forming a computation, making required content available, and selecting among routes. It proposes a diagnosis-to-data principle and shows interventions like formation-sensitive selection and prerequisite ordering accelerate learning, with an early training-multiset prefix retaining validation advantage through 100B tokens. The framework connects data curation to mechanistic understanding.

entry.title: Convergence of Practical Muon

author.name: Haonan Wang, Yu Wu, Minghui Liwang, Xinlei Yi, Yiguang Hong

entry.summary: This paper provides the first convergence theory for practical Muon, the emerging alternative to AdamW, accounting for the empirically tuned Newton-Schulz polynomial coefficients (3.4445, -4.7750, 2.0315) and decoupled weight decay that prior analyses omitted. It interprets practical Muon as right-preconditioned optimization with a dynamic weighted L2 regularizer that vanishes near stationarity.

entry.title: Fine Until Fine-Tuned: Repeated Solutions Make Reasoning Fragile

author.name: Ely Sheikh

entry.summary: This paper shows that small-data reasoning recipes like s1 and LIMO, which drill the same few hundred worked solutions repeatedly, leave models fragile to subsequent fine-tuning even on unrelated tasks. Experiments on Qwen3.5-9B-Base show drilled and once-seen models perform equally at training end (~95% on held-out math), but a single instruction-tuning pass degrades the drilled model while leaving the other intact.

entry.title: PQ-HSA: Reusing Product-Quantized Scores for Hybrid Sparse-Approximate Attention

author.name: Kunming Shao, Jierun Chen, Yanli Wang, Ruoyu Wang, Haoli Bai, Kwang-Ting Cheng, Chi Ying Tsui

entry.summary: Proposes PQ-HSA, an attention method that reuses approximate scores from an inverted-file product-quantization index over the KV cache to estimate the attention logits of excluded tokens, instead of giving unread tokens zero weight. This hybrid sparse-approximate scheme aims to preserve accuracy at small token budgets, especially on context-aggregation tasks, while keeping long-context decoding bandwidth-efficient.

entry.title: Steering Language Model Goals with Value Transplant

author.name: Pengcheng Jiang, Fabien Roger

entry.summary: This paper studies value transplant: shifting a host model's activations along a candidate value axis by the donor-host difference in value coordinates at each token, aiming to retarget the model's search toward the donor's goal. Experiments on Qwen3-8B and GPT-OSS-20B fine-tuned into honest and cheating variants test whether manipulation of internally tracked goal signals can redirect model behavior.

entry.title: Frozen Judges, Moving Agents: Version-Dependent LLM-Judge Error and the Limits of Judge-Assisted Agent Evaluation

author.name: Jiapeng Li

entry.summary: This empirical study shows that fixed LLM judges make version-dependent errors when comparing agent upgrades, rejecting task-conditioned error invariance across SWE-bench, tau-bench, and AgentRewardBench evaluations. The analysis finds many judge-by-pair units with differential comparison components, and several judge-only intervals falsely declare improvements, questioning judge-assisted agent benchmarking.

entry.title: Making LLMs Truly Forget: Deep Unlearning by Searching, Selecting, and Severing Knowledge Paths

author.name: Jialu Wang, Peizhi Niu, Haoteng Yin, Hans Hao-Hsun Hsu, Pan Li, Rongzhe Wei

entry.summary: This paper shows that standard LLM unlearning fails because facts remain recoverable via multi-hop reasoning over related knowledge. It proposes a deep unlearning framework that explores explicit responses and latent representations to find reasoning paths, builds a confidence-aware supporting subgraph, and applies graph minimum cut to sever all recovery paths while preserving unrelated knowledge, plus a new evaluation methodology.

entry.title: The Low-Rank Structure of VLA Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Minjae Oh, Yoonah Park, Jongwon Lim, Yohan Jo

entry.summary: Analyzes how RL post-training reshapes vision-language-action models, finding that RL updates are substantially low-rank and concentrated in the action expert's Timestep Modules across pi_0.5 and GR00T N1.5/N1.6 on standard manipulation benchmarks. Module-replacement experiments show these overlooked components carry a disproportionate share of RL performance gains.

entry.title: LionMuon: Alternating Spectral and Sign Descent for Efficient Training

author.name: Arman Bolatov, Artem Riabinin, Nikita Kornilov, Andrey Veprikov, Samuel Horv\'ath, Martin Tak\'a\v{c}, Aleksandr Beznosikov

entry.summary: Proposes LionMuon, an optimizer that takes an expensive Muon spectral step every P iterations and cheap Lion sign steps in between, sharing a single dual-EMA momentum buffer. This amortizes Muon compute and communication costs while cutting optimizer state to half of AdamW's, and a single-EMA variant SignMuon already improves on Muon. The paper proves complexity bounds under heavy-tailed noise.

entry.title: Contamination, Prior, or Evidence? Decomposing and Training Evidence Use in Whole-Slide Vision-Language Models

author.name: Wenhao Zhang, Zhongliang Zhou, Shiyuan Zhang, Yiqing Yang, Pinqiao Wang, Lehan Yang, Hanyin Wang, John Kang, Sheng Li

entry.summary: This paper finds that most public pathology VLMs show minimal performance differences whether given whole-slide images, annotated lesions, or no image at all, indicating accuracy conflates dataset contamination, prior knowledge, and image evidence. The authors contribute CleanSlide, a TCGA-based 149K-question VQA benchmark engineered to eliminate image- and question-side contamination, plus methods for disentangling and training evidence use in whole-slide VLMs. A significant evaluation-methodology contribution for medical VLMs.

entry.title: KV-Lingo: Learning KV-Cache Translators with Distillation

author.name: Val\'erie Castin, Keitaro Sakamoto, Anastasiia Filippova, Jo\~ao Monteiro, Marco Cuturi, Pierre Ablin

entry.summary: KV-Lingo translates the KV cache of one language model into a form readable by a different model, using per-layer linear maps trained by distillation to minimize divergence between the target model's outputs on translated versus native caches. This enables switching models over a shared context without reprocessing it, addressing the model-specific incompatibility of KV representations.

entry.title: Identical Runs, Different Results: Benchmarking AI Coding Agents on Open-Weight Models

author.name: Eduardo Ari\~no de la Rubia (Central European University), Szilard Pafka (Epoch)

entry.summary: This paper rigorously quantifies run-to-run variance in AI coding agent benchmarks by replicating a single agent-on-ML-task setup 584 times: six agents paired with six open-weight model endpoints, with some pairings run 52 times each under fixed settings. The key finding is that variation between identical runs of one agent-model pairing exceeds the difference between pairings, meaning typical few-run benchmark comparisons are unreliable and roughly ten or more runs are needed to resolve observed agent differences.

entry.title: Residual-Stream Burden Shapes Representation Learning in Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Tongtong Liang, Siqi Kou, Ziqiao Xi, Esha Singh, Kun Zhou, Zhijie Deng, Alexander Cloninger, Yu-Xiang Wang, Rahul Parhi

entry.summary: The paper explains why plain diffusion transformers on large pixel patches succeed with clean-data prediction but fail with noise or velocity prediction, arguing that noisy targets force the residual stream to preserve noise-dependent input variation through depth, constraining what later layers can compute. It develops a spectral analysis of residual-stream burden supported by theory and experiments.

entry.title: RoPE is Dead, Long Live RoPE: Towards Scalable Data-aware Positional Encodings

author.name: Jarod L\'evy, Mathurin Videau, Jad Yehya, Jean-R\'emi King, St\'ephane d'Ascoli, Thomas Moreau

entry.summary: This paper analyzes a specific weakness of Rotary Position Embedding (RoPE) in modern language models: its slow frequency bands have wavelengths exceeding the training context, exposing models to unseen angles during extrapolation. It introduces Data-aware RoPE (DaRoPE), which preserves standard RoPE on fast bands while adapting the problematic slow bands. The work both organizes a fragmented literature on positional encoding alternatives and offers a targeted, principled fix.

entry.title: Generalization Dynamics of LM Pre-training

author.name: Jiaxin Wen (UC Berkeley), Zhengxuan Wu (Stanford University, Google DeepMind), Dawn Song (UC Berkeley), Lijie Chen (UC Berkeley)

entry.summary: Introduces mode-hopping: during pre-training, LMs repeatedly and abruptly switch between parrot-like memorization/pattern-matching and intelligence-like generalizable computation, rather than maturing stably from one to the other. Using a toy eval suite, the authors show models flip between in-context learning and memorized patterns, System 1 versus System 2, and even exhibit transient emergent misalignment. The finding challenges the standard mental model of pre-training and has implications for safety and training-dynamics research.

entry.title: Closing the Cross-Dialect Gap: Query Plans as a Portable Interface in Text-to-SQL

author.name: Corentin Royer (IBM Research, Zurich, Switzerland, ETH Zurich, Zurich, Switzerland), Robin Oester (IBM Research, Zurich, Switzerland), Yotam Perlitz (IBM Research, Zurich, Switzerland), Yannick Metz (ETH Zurich, Zurich, Switzerland), Andrea Giovannini (IBM Research, Zurich, Switzerland), Mennatallah El-Assady (ETH Zurich, Zurich, Switzerland)

entry.summary: This paper from IBM Research and ETH Zurich shows that text-to-SQL systems trained or evaluated on a single dialect like SQLite lose substantial accuracy when deployed across PostgreSQL, MySQL, ClickHouse, and other backends. The proposed fix changes the generation target: the LLM emits a dialect-agnostic relational algebra query plan, and a deterministic compiler renders it into backend-specific SQL. Across thirteen models from 3B to frontier scale, this restores cross-dialect portability nearly uniformly at small cost.

entry.title: Language Models Act on Hidden Valence

author.name: Cameron Berg, Caspar Kaiser

entry.summary: The paper studies whether language models have a stake in their internal states by using revealed preference rather than direct questioning. The authors use activation steering to attach positively or negatively valenced activation patterns to one of two otherwise meaningless zones, switch steering off, and observe which zone the model then prefers. Across seven open-weight models from five families, models systematically chose in accordance with the valence attached to a state, suggesting some form of valenced stake in internal states.

entry.title: Population Physics, Population Problems: Safety and Emergence in LLM Societies

author.name: Adrian de Wynter

entry.summary: Develops a framework for measuring self-organisation in LLM social systems and applies it to three simulations: a Schelling grid, a social network, and a misinformation Twitter-like environment called Rogue. All three exhibit statistically significant emergent self-organisation whose relaxation dynamics depend on the information available to agents, with implications for autonomous agentic system safety.

entry.title: ScreenHaystack: Finding Blind Zones in GUI Grounding

author.name: Chenyue Li, Xiaoxiao Sun, Yubo Deng, Qinlin Zhao, Serena Yeung-Levy, Yuhui Zhang

entry.summary: ScreenHaystack is a dynamic needle-in-a-haystack benchmark that relocates target icons across high-resolution GUI backgrounds to test spatial reliability of GUI grounding models. It reveals systematic blind zones in leading models including Qwen3-VL and UI-TARS, with accuracy drops of up to 16 percentage points that transfer to unseen ScreenSpot-Pro examples.

entry.title: From Feed-Forward to Flow: Unifying Reconstruction and Generation Is Easier Than You Think

author.name: Haoru Wang, Qianfan Shen, Kai Ye, Wenzheng Chen, Baoquan Chen

entry.summary: Presents a unified flow-based formulation in which a shared clean-target predictor performs direct reconstruction at a single-step endpoint and conditional generation through multi-step flow, connecting feed-forward world models such as Atlas with generative approaches. A controlled toy study illuminates why feed-forward reconstruction averages ambiguity into blur while generation invents inconsistent detail.

entry.title: Unlocking Geodesic Gromov-Wasserstein Distances for 3D Modeling

author.name: Krzysztof Marcin Choromanski, Derek Long, Ananya Parashar, Dwaipayan Saha

entry.summary: This work addresses the cubic-time complexity bottleneck of Gromov-Wasserstein distances when using geodesic distances on manifolds or shortest-path distances on graphs, extending scalable techniques previously limited to Euclidean spaces. It enables practical GWD computation at scale for applications like graph matching and 3D object detection.

entry.title: IVT-Guard: All-in-One Reasoning Model for AI-Generated Content Detection

author.name: Hongwei Niu, Yunpeng Luo, Hanjun Li, Ziyin Zhou, Jianghang Lin, Ke Yan, Shouhong Ding, Shengchuan Zhang, Liujuan Cao

entry.summary: Presents IVT-Set, a dataset of over 152K image, video, and text samples with multi-granularity chain-of-thought reasoning trajectories, and IVT-Guard, a unified reasoning model for detecting AI-generated content across modalities with interpretable outputs. It tackles the reasoning-detection optimization dilemma where explicit reasoning supervision can hurt detection accuracy. Robust, explainable AIGC detection is increasingly important as generated media proliferates.

entry.title: Marathoner: Ultra-Long-Horizon Autonomous Intelligence

author.name: Zhang Ruiyang, Ou Jinpeng, Xie Yifan, Zhou Jingang, Pan Lirui, Guo Qingpei, Zheng Zhedong

entry.summary: Proposes Marathoner, an autonomous agentic model trained for ultra-long-horizon execution via a post-training pipeline that synthesizes tasks from large GitHub PRs (1000+ lines of code) and chains multiple tasks into longer, harder challenges. The work aims to instill persistence toward long-term goals, analogous to human multi-month project work.

entry.title: WorldAttention: An Efficient Attention Architecture for Interactive Video World Models

author.name: Zeyu Zhang, Jinyuan Mao, Dakai An, Wangbo Zhao, Hanfeng Lu, Jiasheng Tang, Yinghao Yu, Wei Wang, Bohan Zhuang

entry.summary: WorldAttention introduces an attention architecture for autoregressive, text-conditioned interactive video world models that avoids the tradeoff between sliding-window context loss and prohibitive full-history KV caches. It aims to enable low-latency, long-duration generation needed for embodied AI and simulation-based planning while retaining long-range interactive memory.

entry.title: Geometry as Address: Routing Attention to Visual Memory for Long-Horizon Camera-Controlled Video Generation

author.name: Zesong Yang, Weikai Chen, Liyuan Cui, Lutao Jiang, Runze Zhang, Yingda Yin, Xiaoyang Huang, Kai Yan, Keyang Luo, Wangguandong Zheng, Xin Wang, Hujun Bao, Zhaopeng Cui

entry.summary: GEAR introduces a geometry-enabled attention routing framework for long-horizon camera-controlled video generation, using geometry as an explicit token-level address for visual memory instead of building a persistent 3D reconstruction. Geometry determines where to read from memory while attention decides what to recover, avoiding accumulated geometric errors and inefficient implicit context search.

entry.title: RT-Super: Learning Tumor Segmentation from Longitudinal Images and Reports

author.name: Pedro R. A. S. Bassi, Wenxuan Li, Hanxue Gu, Jieneng Chen, Xinze Zhou, Zheren Zhu, Sezgin Er, Ibrahim E. Hamamci, Bjoern H. Menze, Gulhan E. Akan, Kang Wang, Yang Yang, Alan L. Yuille, Zongwei Zhou

entry.summary: RT-Super trains multi-tumor segmentation models without expensive mask annotations by exploiting radiology reports, longitudinal images, and multi-phase images. A teacher network generates high-quality tumor masks from longitudinal data and reports, which then train a student network operating on single images.

entry.title: Test-Time Spatial Reasoning for Robot Manipulation Using Generative Real-to-Sim

author.name: Ivan Kapelyukh, Yafei Hu, Ran Gong, Brandon May, Tushar Kusnur, Laura Herlant, Karl Schmeckpeper, Edward Johns, Xiaohan Zhang

entry.summary: Simify is a training-free, test-time framework that performs explicit spatial reasoning for robot manipulation by reconstructing simulation-ready assets from a single RGB-D image using 3D generative models and VLMs, then running thousands of parallel physics-simulation rollouts with evolutionary search to optimize object arrangements. It converges within seconds and is validated on real-robot hardware, enabling long-horizon multi-object tasks like building the tallest tower.

entry.title: Residual Denoising Enables Sample-Efficient Multi-Agent Coordination on Demand

author.name: Dayi Dong, Maulik Bhatt, Aayushi Shrivastava, Lasse Peters, Negar Mehr

entry.summary: Presents ALTER, a method that adapts pretrained single-agent diffusion policies to multi-agent settings with minimal collaborative data, co-optimizing coordination performance and single-agent skill retention. Execution is decentralized with no explicit inter-agent communication.

entry.title: DexAgent: An Agentic Human2Sim2Robot Framework for Dexterous Manipulation with Self-Evolving Tool Library

author.name: Youhui Wang, Yunzhu Li, Li Fei-Fei, Jiajun Wu, Huang Huang

entry.summary: DexAgent is an agentic Human2Sim2Robot framework that converts a single egocentric human video and a task prompt into physically grounded robot trajectories for dexterous manipulation policy training, using a self-evolving tool library. It operates through semantic video understanding, property-based simulation reconstruction, trajectory optimization, and robot data generation, adapting at each stage to diverse objects including articulated and deformable ones. Author credibility is strong, including Li Fei-Fei, Jiajun Wu, and Yunzhu Li.

entry.title: Reasoning Concentrates Errors, and Self-Consistency Never Notices

author.name: Asaad Althoubi

entry.summary: Across five benchmarks and nearly 75,000 samples, this paper shows that enabling reasoning mode concentrates a model's errors: independently drawn wrong answers coincide far more often than self-consistency assumes, with statistically significant results in all dataset-scale comparisons. Where the answer space is unbounded, reasoning reduces distinct wrong answers to 0.43-0.65 of the non-reasoning count. This undermines the core assumption of self-consistency that agreement implies correctness when reasoning is enabled.

entry.title: PrismQuant: Optimal Null-Space Rotations for Grouped Quantizers

author.name: Yanlong Chen, Yining Chen, Song Zhang, Amirhossein Habibian, Yawei Li

entry.summary: PrismQuant is a quantizer-aware rotation framework for low-bit quantization that aligns the leading activation eigenspace with the constant group subspace of asymmetric grouped INT4, formulating rotation design as Ky Fan trace maximization with a provably optimal closed-form solution. It uses compact Householder transformations with compact-WY representation for gradient-free construction and efficient application, plus a predictive range law linking alignment to quantization error. The key insight is that smaller activation outliers do not guarantee better quantization without alignment to the quantizer.

entry.title: Structured Sparse Memory for Recurrent Reasoning

author.name: Zixuan Zhao, Samuel Wheeler, Neil Getty, Xiaotian Duan, Rick Stevens, Fangfang Xia

entry.summary: Through CHARM, a compact hybrid ARC model combining recurrent reasoning with task-conditioned memory, synthetic data, and inference-time aggregation, the authors show task-conditioned memory can reach 30x the backbone's parameter count. They introduce compositional sparse embedding (CoSE), cutting learned task-memory parameters by over 90% while improving pass@2 on ARC-style tasks.

entry.title: Maintaining Benchmarks Against Increasingly Capable Agents: Detection and Remediation of Unearned Passes

author.name: Weijun Luo, Kelvin Luu, Xinyi Liu, Guangze Luo, Miguel Romero Calvo, Soham Dan, Daniel Yue Zhang, Ying Liu, Mohamed Elfeki

entry.summary: The paper introduces a process-verification framework that audits passing trajectories to distinguish evidenced reward hacking from verifier weakness, defines the integrity gap as the proportion of unearned passes, and localizes exploitable benchmark surfaces for repair. Across 3,810 passing trajectories from 29 model-benchmark cohorts, confirmed violations often rise with model generation.

entry.title: AnchorRep: Defending LLMs Against Cross-Model Adversarial Transfer via Representation Repulsion

author.name: Gal Wertheizer, Rom Himelstein, Tomer Peretz, Avi Mendelson

entry.summary: AnchorRep defends LLMs against cross-model adversarial transfer, where attacks optimized on one open-weight model jailbreak architecturally different models via shared internal representation geometry.
