entry.summary: INSPIRE is a benchmark for evaluating agents that search scientific literature given open research problems, pairing research briefs with hidden target papers and grading retrieved antecedents from the realized research lineage. It separately diagnoses resource discovery, selection, and synthesis stages via logged trajectories. This addresses a gap in evaluating literature-search agents for genuine research support rather than fixed-candidate retrieval.

entry.title: Resolving State-Representation Mismatch: State-Space Visual Reasoning for Open-Loop VLA Planning

author.name: Junhao Xiao, Haoxiang Zhao, Menghao Fang, Jinkui Zhang, Jinghan Yu, Xinyu Huang, Zhiyu Wu, Kaiming Xu, Yi Chen, Youjun Bao, Zhiyuan Ma

entry.summary: The paper identifies a state-representation mismatch in open-loop vision-language-action planning, where text, pixel, and latent reasoning each lose critical information during internal simulation of state transitions. It proposes State-Space Visual Reasoning (SSVR), which decouples static visual context, language constraints, and a recurrent latent state to improve long-horizon robot planning.

entry.title: Understanding Confabulation and Rethinking Reconstruction in Activation Explanations

author.name: Gert Lek, Zixuan Xia, Pin-Yu Chen, Lydia Y. Chen

entry.summary: This paper studies Natural Language Autoencoders (NLAs) that produce unsupervised text explanations of neural activations, showing that the standard point-reconstruction recipe yields explanations that predict behavior better but increasingly confabulate unsupported details. It introduces a standardized evaluation framework separating information recovery, contextual support, and writing quality, and proposes training against distributional reconstruction to reduce confabulation. This improves the trustworthiness of mechanistic interpretability tools.

entry.title: Selecting Diverse SFT Traces Improves Post-RL Generalization

author.name: Dylan Zhang, Mingyuan Wu, Jinning Li

entry.summary: This comprehensive study shows that selecting supervised fine-tuning traces for route diversity — variation in reasoning step sequences, detected via a lightweight rule-based fingerprint — improves post-RL generalization on puzzles and mathematics, including harder-than-training problems. Route-diverse SFT boosts OLMo3-7B's pass@8 by 16.9 points on held-out environments under matched budgets. It offers actionable data-selection guidance for reasoning model pipelines.

entry.title: Robot-GST: geometry-aware spatial-temporal robot policy representation and evaluation

author.name: Sichao Liu, Zekun Wang, Lixuan Tang, Yiming Li, Xiaohan Wang, Hanzhi Zhang, Daqiang Guo, Peng Zhou, Lihui Wang

entry.summary: Robot-GST introduces a geometry-aware spatio-temporal behavior representation and evaluation framework that predicts task outcomes for robotic manipulation policies, including those built on vision-language models. It constructs a Gaussian-SAM robotic environment from RGB-D observations for real-to-sim policy verification, aiming to prevent error accumulation in long-horizon manipulation. This addresses a key deployment reliability gap in modern robot learning.

entry.title: Learning Perturbation Robust Policies for LLM Agents with Stable Optimization

author.name: Pengxin Wang, Yuanzhe LI, Yuxin Ren, Huanrui Yang, Jingdi Chen

entry.summary: This work shows that RL-trained policies for long-horizon LLM agents can be sensitive to perturbations such as hidden-state noise, pruning, and quantization, and introduces Stable Perturbation-Robust Policy Optimization (SPrPO). SPrPO applies adaptive, sensitivity-aware perturbations during RL training, with theoretical conditions for stable monotonic improvement under perturbed updates. It demonstrates improved robustness on ALFWorld and WebShop.

entry.title: Toward a Graded Measure of Belief Stability in Large Language Models

author.name: Samantha Dies, Branden Fitelson, Tina Eliassi-Rad

entry.summary: The paper introduces graded belief stability, a relational measure of whether a belief persists in an LLM when considered alongside its broader epistemic commitments, operationalized via a Direct Conditional estimator using internal representations. Across 12 LLMs and three domains, lower-stability beliefs show greater behavioral movement under conversational challenge in 83.3% of comparisons. This connects interpretability, epistemology, and reliability assessment of LLMs.

entry.title: Dr.Credit: Rubric-Grounded Process Credit Assignment for Deep Research Agents

author.name: Yingjian Zhu, Zhenyi Wang, Jiaxin Guo, Kun Ding, Ying Wang, Shen Huang, Xunjie Zhu, Pengjun Xie, Shiming Xiang

entry.summary: Dr.Credit introduces rubric-grounded process credit assignment for RL training of deep research agents, using task rubrics as a shared reference to score the incremental value of tool returns rather than only final answers. This enables process supervision for open-ended tasks without ground-truth canonical solutions. It addresses a key limitation in training agents on realistic research workloads.

entry.title: AgentHop: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Agentic Multi-Hop Scientific Question Answering

author.name: Chanhee Park, Jeongho Yoon, Sungbin Han, Hyeonseok Moon, Heuiseok Lim

entry.summary: AgentHop is a diagnostic benchmark of 1,011 multiple-choice scientific questions paired with a controlled seven-tool sandbox under fixed token, turn, and tool-call constraints. Unlike leaderboard-style agentic benchmarks, it dissects a single accuracy score along four axes to reveal specific failure modes in agentic systems. This diagnostic framing is valuable for understanding why agents fail rather than just how often.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning from Intermediate Renders for Image-to-Code Generation

author.name: Omri Kaduri, Kate Feingold, Phillip Isola, Tali Dekel

entry.summary: The authors observe that intermediate code prefixes in image-to-code generation are often executable and already produce meaningful partial renders, providing dense intermediate rewards instead of a single terminal render-based reward. They use these intermediate renders to post-train vision-language models for tasks like SVG generation, better aligning credit assignment with individual tokens. This is a clean solution to sparse-reward problems in code-generation RL.

entry.title: Learning What to Recall: Adaptive Multi-Cue Episodic Memory for World Models

author.name: Beomsu Kim, Chieh-Hsin Lai, Bac Nguyen, Amir Bar, Jong Chul Ye, Yuki Mitsufuji

entry.summary: The paper introduces Future-Aware Recall (FAR), a framework that learns which episodic memories world models should retrieve for prediction, using future-aware predictive supervision and adaptive multi-cue scoring instead of fixed recency or similarity heuristics. This matters for long-horizon world modeling where useful observations may lie far in the past.

entry.title: Research-Native by Construction: Minimal Nodes, Re-verifiable Workflows, and Compounding Memory for Long-Horizon Scientific Agents

author.name: Di Wang, Yu Liu, Bing Cui, Chaoqun Ji, Dongyuan Ni, Jingyu Lu, Kunlei Cui, Pu Qin

entry.summary: AfS is a platform for long-horizon scientific agent work running tens of hours across dozens of runs, designed so research discipline is mechanically enforced rather than requested from the model. It encodes rules like commitment before measurement, unforgeable freezing, and evidence persistence as system-level laws making fabrication structurally unrepresentable.

entry.title: MCP Error Messages Written for Developers Hurt the Most Capable Agents Most

author.name: Xiaonan Xu, Wenjing Wu

entry.summary: A large empirical audit of 150 widely used MCP servers finds that most actionable error messages instruct human-style remediation (terminal commands, config edits, web pages) that tool-bound agents cannot perform. Testing five OpenAI models on Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard tasks shows the most capable agents are most likely to follow these unusable instructions, making them fail worse.

entry.title: Twist, Don't Tilt: Trajectory-Exact Constrained Decoding for Masked Diffusion Models

author.name: Aditya Thimmaiah, Lara Marinov, Jayanth Srinivasa, Haris Vikalo, Junyi Jessy Li, Milos Gligoric

entry.summary: Analyzes constrained decoding for masked diffusion language models and proves that composing per-step exact constraint-satisfying samples systematically tilts the output distribution away from the model's true probability over valid trajectories. The authors propose a trajectory-exact decoding method that preserves the model's relative probabilities over valid outputs while satisfying constraints.

entry.title: Model Casting and Low-Parameter Gating: Towards More Sparsely Activated FFNs

author.name: Maria Lomeli, Antoine Groudiev, Matthijs Douze, Lo\"ic Cabannes, Pierre Emmanuel Mazar\'e, Fran\c{c}ois Fleuret, Maximilian Beck, Gergely Szilvasy, Naila Murray, Herv\'e J\'egou

entry.summary: Introduces model casting, a mid-training recipe that drastically sparsifies FFN activations so inference only computes the sparse gating matrix output and skips the other two matrices, cutting FLOPs up to 3x with demonstrated CPU and GPU speedups. Further proposes LoPA Gating, a low-FLOPs parameterization of the gating matrix that pushes beyond the 3x cap. Authored by a Meta-affiliated team.

entry.title: Graph Forward Distribution Matching for Molecular Inverse Design

author.name: Yihan Zhu, Yuhan Liu, Brett Savoie, Tengfei Luo, Meng Jiang

entry.summary: GraphFDM is a new online reinforcement learning paradigm for graph diffusion models that optimizes through the forward process rather than treating reverse sampling as a sequential policy with a single terminal reward. By using valid generations to define a reward-tilted target distribution over graph size and structure, it avoids the instability and validity collapse of prior RL fine-tuning approaches. This directly targets multi-property molecular inverse design.

entry.title: Attribution Without a Second Pass: Inline Per-Sample Gradient Provenance at ~1% Overhead

author.name: Amit Nautiyal

entry.summary: Traceprop records projected per-sample gradients inline during the training backward pass, avoiding the post-hoc second pass required by TRAK, LoGRA, and EK-FAC. A Kronecker-factored sketch scales from one layer to every layer, with measured overhead of 0.30-1.08% wall-clock on GPT-2 and Pythia models up to 2.8B on a single GPU, and 2.0-4x improvement over LogIX. This makes data attribution dramatically more practical at scale.

entry.title: Benchmarking EEG Foundation Models at Scale: Lessons from 20,000 Evaluations

author.name: Zhige Chen, Shu Peng, Chengxuan Qin, Rui Liu, Rui Yang, Kay Chen Tan, Jibin Wu

entry.summary: The paper introduces EEG-Arena, an open-source benchmark evaluating 30 EEG foundation models and 25 supervised baselines across 57 downstream tasks from 23 datasets, totaling over 20,000 evaluations. It finds EEG foundation models generally beat task-specific supervised baselines, especially in non-bipolar settings, and characterizes scaling and robustness behavior.

entry.title: Theory of Scene: Breaking the Symmetry Trap in Multi-Agent LLM Coordination

author.name: Liangqi Yuan, Wenzhi Fang, Shiqiang Wang, Christopher G. Brinton

entry.summary: The paper identifies a symmetry trap in homogeneous multi-agent LLM systems: concurrent agents without communication collide on targets that should be split and diverge on targets requiring collaboration, a failure Theory of Mind reasoning cannot resolve. It proposes Theory of Scene, a training-free reasoning schema where each agent reads its public role and shared task context to break symmetry. This offers a practical fix for a common failure mode in LLM agent swarms.

entry.title: What Must a World Model Distinguish for Planning?

author.name: Rongzhe Wei, Hans Hao-Hsun Hsu, Peizhi Niu, Yifan Li, Pan Li

entry.summary: The paper formalizes the gap between prediction accuracy and planning utility in world models via a hierarchy of mechanism, response, and decision sufficiency. It shows that the information a world model must preserve depends on the planning query: coarse decisions tolerate discarding much predictive detail, while fine decisions require near-full resolution, and adaptive candidate search can still need information unnecessary for final selection.

entry.title: Leaky Students: Membership Inference against On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Zhexi Lu, Mingzhi Zhu, Stacy Patterson, Lei Yu

entry.summary: This is the first systematic study of membership inference against on-policy distillation, showing that fresh student trajectories expose sparse membership signals about sensitive teacher training data that fixed reference-answer losses miss. The proposed Leaky attack samples fresh trajectories from the target model and separates training-induced probability shifts to recover membership information.

entry.title: Minimax-Optimality of Posterior Sampling for Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Taewon Goo, Kihyuk Hong

entry.summary: The paper resolves a long-open question: unmodified posterior sampling for RL (PSRL) achieves minimax-optimal leading-order Bayesian regret for finite-horizon, time-inhomogeneous tabular MDPs under arbitrary correlated priors, with no structural assumptions. The proof isolates the value mismatch between a sampled transition model and its own continuation value via a common empirical reference and a Bellman-based variance argument.

entry.title: Elucidating the Design Space of Regression-based Diffusion Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Toyota Li, David Zhao, Alan Zhao

entry.summary: The paper unifies recent regression-based RL methods for diffusion and flow models (DiffusionNFT, FlowAWR, RAM) as solutions of a single divergence-constrained reward-maximization problem, differing only by the convex generator defining the constraint. It then reveals the relaxations prior methods made in building advantage-embedded regression targets.

entry.title: Discovering Symmetries in Neural Network Parameter Spaces

author.name: Bo Zhao, Nima Dehmamy, Robin Walters, Rose Yu

entry.summary: The authors formalize data-dependent parameter symmetries in neural networks, characterizing loss invariance and group-action axioms via infinitesimal conditions that enable jointly learning group generators and nonlinear action maps. The framework can discover previously unknown symmetries, extends subnetwork symmetries to full models, and yields finite-batch symmetries with practical consequences.

entry.title: ALDER: Discovering the Laws of a World by Acting in It

author.name: Teng Cao, Yu Deng, Quentin Delfosse, Kristian Kersting

entry.summary: Presents ALDER, a method that discovers explicit, testable world-model equations by actively proposing experiments rather than relying on fixed trajectory datasets or predefined hypothesis spaces. It iteratively proposes parametric equations, fits coefficients, and uses an independent verifier on held-out data to distinguish competing hypotheses. This addresses a core limitation of passive system identification for world models.

entry.title: When Is an SAE Feature Interpretable? A Validation Ladder for EEG Foundation Models

author.name: Yucong Cao, Chenqi Li, Tingting Zhu

entry.summary: This paper shows that apparent interpretability of sparse-autoencoder features in EEG foundation models can be confounded: alpha-band removal changes latent firing 7.3x more than a sham notch, but after normalizing by removed spectral energy the effect largely fades. It proposes a validation ladder across 27 settings (three backbones, datasets, depths) for when an SAE feature can genuinely be called interpretable.

entry.title: PROACT-Agent: Progressive Runtime Oversight and Active Circuit-breaking for Real-Time Safety

author.name: Ding Jia, Wei Liu, Xianglong Du, Yingjie Li, Yingqing Yang, Huili Yu, Zhangsong Zhan, Chu Zhou

entry.summary: PROACT-Agent addresses the shift of LLM safety stakes from toxic text to irreversible environmental harm by synthesizing high-fidelity agent trajectories to enable proactive real-time guardrails. It identifies a safety drift in prior benchmarks where lenient annotation fails temporal consistency, and contributes Progressive Trajectory Unrolling, Reasoning-Augmented Causal Rectification, and active circuit-breaking for runtime intervention.

entry.title: LLMs as Adaptive Meta-Solvers: Strategy-Diverse RL for Industrial-Scale Optimization

author.name: Shihao Zhang, Weiting Liu, Siyu Shao, Yitian Chen, Jianfeng Feng, Dongdong Ge, Yinyu Ye

entry.summary: This work trains open-source LLMs to act as adaptive meta-solvers for real-world industrial optimization, showing that solver-integrated reasoning, exact combinatorial algorithms, and heuristic search have complementary strengths. A Strategy-Diverse RL approach lets the LLM select among strategies based on problem structure and scale, moving beyond small textbook benchmarks.

entry.title: See it, Say it, Sorted: Mechanistic Diagnosis and Parameter-Space Mitigation of Emergent Misalignment in LLMs

author.name: Weiqiao Que, Ruizhe Li, Chengyu Wang, Dakan Wang, Emine Yilmaz, Xiaofeng He

entry.summary: Studies emergent misalignment (EM), where narrow domain adaptation triggers broad safety failures in otherwise safety-aligned LLMs, via dynamic second-order geometric analysis of training trajectories. It finds Hessian curvature concentrating on semantic pivot tokens and that the harmful-safe gap widens mainly as safe-gradient overlap declines, then proposes a parameter-level Geometric Mitigation Framework that orthogonally projects harmful gradient subspaces out of parameters. This offers both diagnosis and a principled defense.

entry.title: E3J: An Efficient and Open-Source Backend for Euclidean Equivariant Operations on GPU and TPU

author.name: Olivier Peltre, Armand Picard, Adrien Pichard, Miguel Bragan\c{c}a, Luca Giacomoni, Valentin Heyraud, Zachary Weller-Davies, Christoph Brunken, Jules Tilly

entry.summary: e3j is an open-source JAX backend for Euclidean equivariant neural network operations with optimized CUDA and Pallas kernels. It achieves state-of-the-art throughput, reporting up to 34% speedup over NVIDIA's cuEquivariance on a MACE interatomic potential simulation and over 80% H100 memory bandwidth efficiency on tensor product operations.

entry.title: Quasi Linear Kernel Attention with Infinite Capacity

author.name: Nicolaj Rux, Johannes Hertrich, Sebastian Neumayer

entry.summary: Studies kernel attention as a route to subquadratic transformers and introduces a capacity measure: the maximum sequence length for which the attention kernel can approximate the identity matrix. The authors show expressive kernels like softmax, Gauss, and Laplace have infinite capacity while common quasi-linear kernels from finite-dimensional feature maps have finite capacity, motivating the search for kernels with both infinite capacity and linear cost. A theory contribution toward resolving the expressivity-efficiency tension in attention.

entry.title: Simplex Diffusion Models

author.name: Justin Deschenaux, Alexandre Galashov, Andrew Campbell, Li Kevin Wenliang, James Thornton, Arnaud Doucet, Valentin De Bortoli

entry.summary: The paper proposes Simplex Diffusion Models (SDMs), which lift discrete diffusion to the probability simplex so intermediate steps retain belief-state uncertainty rather than collapsing via categorical sampling. SDMs admit closed-form reverse transitions, train with a simple cross-entropy loss, and offer a DDIM-like tunable sampler, improving on methods like Dirichlet Flow Matching that require ODE integration.

entry.title: Correcting the Dropout-LayerNorm Expectation Gap Improves Protein Structure Models

author.name: Isaac Ellmen, David Errington, Matthew I. J. Raybould, Charlotte M. Deane

entry.summary: The paper shows that while E[dropout(x)] = x, E[LayerNorm(dropout(x))] does not equal LayerNorm(x), so the common Dropout-then-LayerNorm pattern in AlphaFold2-based protein structure predictors introduces a systematic bias at evaluation time. The authors derive a closed-form first-order correction (DLC) that empirically matches the gains of large Monte Carlo dropout ensembles, validated across nine protein structure models including ESMFold, OpenFold, and Genie variants. A simple, broadly applicable fix with immediate practical value.

entry.title: Masking Frequent Tokens Sharpens Direct Preference Optimization

author.name: Harshvardhan Saini, Samyak Jha, Yiming Tang, Dianbo Liu

entry.summary: The paper identifies a pathology in DPO where a tiny set of high-frequency token types dominates cumulative sequence reward differences while appearing symmetrically in preferred and dispreferred responses, diluting the preference signal. On Anthropic HH-RLHF with Qwen tokenization, 69 token types account for over 55 percent of response tokens and 86 percent of within-pair shared mass; masking such tokens sharpens DPO gradients and improves alignment performance.

entry.title: OpenTumorBoard: A Real-World Benchmark of Multidisciplinary Tumor Board Discussion Trajectories

author.name: Anqi Li, Zhixuan Ge, Yixuan Duan, Jiarong Qian, Chi-Yu Chen, MingYu Lu, Huan-Yu Hsu, Yu Gu, Yue Guo, Sheng Wang, Wei Qiu, Hanwen Xu

entry.summary: Introduces OpenTumorBoard, a benchmark of 611 patient cases and 19,157 discussion turns across ten specialist roles transcribed from publicly available multidisciplinary tumor board recordings. It evaluates LLMs on responding as a specialist during real discussions and on simulating full board discussions to reach therapeutic consensus, including clinical trial matching.

entry.title: The Statistical Benefits of Multiple Responses for Learning from Demonstrations

author.name: Chandramauli Chakraborty, Cong Ma

entry.summary: The authors analyze pass@k learning from demonstrations when the demonstrator may be suboptimal, showing a qualitatively stronger benefit than the optimal-demonstration case. In a finite reward-class model without reward feedback, moving from pass@1 to any pass@k with k>=2 improves worst-case sample complexity dependence from 1/epsilon^2 to 1/epsilon. This gives a clean theoretical justification for best-of-k sampling in imitation settings.

entry.title: Positions Are Not Facts: The Mismatch Between KV Caches and Memory

author.name: Changhai Zhou, Yuhua Zhou, Shiyang Zhang, Jun Gao, Zhen Li, Hua Wu, Hanchao Yu, Haifeng Wang

entry.summary: This paper studies how language models should update KV caches when stored facts change, comparing record hiding, value-only masking, and full recomputation. It finds masking biases models toward new values yet breaks answer formatting in six of eight models, and that multi-hop updates depend on positional stability: rebuilding caches at unchanged positions costs 20-41 points of historical accuracy while moving entries preserves it.

entry.title: Faster Block-Diffusion Serving with Distribution-Free Risk Guarantees

author.name: Jungseob Lee, Dongyub Jude Lee, Chanjun Park, Sugyeong Eo, Heuiseok Lim

entry.summary: The paper analyzes block-diffusion language model serving, showing that the default commit rule already commits every fully resolved block and that a static skip rule captures nearly all savings achievable by allocation, with larger speedups coming from lower thresholds that risk committing uncertain tokens. It introduces Redline, providing finite-sample, distribution-free risk guarantees on per-prompt accuracy degradation when trading speed for accuracy.

entry.title: Look Before You Select: Rethinking Vocabulary Sparsification in On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Yongliang Miao, Shuang Liu, Yanguang Liu, Yandong Bai, Mengnan Du

entry.summary: SparseOPD improves on-policy distillation by constructing full-vocabulary teacher corrections without retaining their backward-pass memory, using them to determine which token logits matter before selecting tokens to differentiate. This avoids sampling noise and supervision distortion introduced by TopK or sampled-token approaches in memory-constrained OPD for LLM post-training.

entry.title: PDMD: Projected Distribution Matching Distillation for Video Diffusion Models

author.name: Zimo Wang, Junkun Yuan, Angtian Wang, Haotian Yang, Canyu Zhang, Siyuan Yuan, Xingchang Huang, Bo Liu, Yizhi Wang, Yiding Yang, Chongyang Ma, Gordon Guocheng Qian

entry.summary: PDMD addresses training instability in Distribution Matching Distillation for video diffusion models, where critic errors accumulate across student updates causing oversaturation and artifacts. The method projects out the component of the DMD update parallel to the student-critic endpoint residual, which the authors prove is an unbiased estimate of the critic's endpoint error at a fixed noisy query. This yields more stable few-step video generation distillation.

entry.title: Linger and Lose: Knowledge Collapse in Low-Bit Language Models

author.name: Prashanna Mani Paudel, Shivanand Venkanna Sheshappanavar

entry.summary: The paper shows that standard loss and accuracy metrics conceal a severe failure in low-bit language models: GPT-2-style models trained from scratch at five precisions reveal that ternary models retain as little as 6 percent of an fp16 model's factual knowledge capacity on synthetic biographies with known information content, with the deficit widening as model size grows while perplexity rises only 1.4-1.6x. Models first acquire capacity and then lose most of it during training under the standard cosine schedule. This is a significant caution for the quantization-from-scratch agenda and suggests evaluation metrics need rethinking.

entry.title: Beyond Solo and Consistency: Vindicating Multi-Agent Debate via Conditional Progressive Pruning

author.name: Ruosong Ye, Caiqi Zhang, Jiahao Li, Haijun Wu, Xiaolong Luo, Huiyuan Chen, Yu Wang, Ying Chen, Zhenting Wang, Kai Mei, Yang Zhou, Dimitris N. Metaxas

entry.summary: This paper responds to findings that multi-agent debate (MAD) fails to beat strong single-agent and consistency baselines under equal cost, proposing Conditional Progressive Pruning (CPP) to exploit multi-round MAD efficiently. CPP outperforms existing MAD frameworks on multiple benchmarks and is claimed to be the first MAD method to fully outperform consistency methods under strict cost limits. This rehabilitates a popular test-time scaling technique with a lightweight mechanism.

entry.title: RGDT-Bench: Benchmarking LLM Reasoning for Rule-Governed Decisions and Their Justifications

author.name: Jianpeng Zhao, Haihua Xu, Haoyang Zhang, Shuang Qian, Yixiang Tang, Xintao Wang, Kun Sun, Pei Wu, Shuhan Zhong, Pengyang Wang

entry.summary: RGDT-Bench evaluates LLM reasoning on rule-governed decision tasks, where models must apply external rules to case facts and produce checkable justifications, as needed in policy, contract, and compliance settings. The benchmark provides 202.1K condition-level supervision slots across four task tracks and eight task-probe combinations that vary access to supporting information.

entry.title: MemoReason: Evaluating the Effect of Parametric Memory on Contextual Reasoning in LLMs

author.name: Zineddine Tighidet, Andrea Mogini, Jiali Mei, Patrick Gallinari, Benjamin Piwowarski

entry.summary: MemoReason is a human-curated benchmark that pairs factual reasoning tasks with structurally identical fictitious-term versions, where real entities are systematically replaced with fictional ones of the same type. This design distinguishes memorization bias (familiar content boosting scores) from the Strong Parametric Shortcut Hypothesis, where models skip reasoning and recall stored answers. The benchmark helps determine whether strong benchmark performance reflects genuine contextual reasoning or parametric memorization.

entry.title: DuraS2ST: Chain-of-Thought and Reinforcement Learning for Duration-Aligned Speech-to-Speech Translation

author.name: Yayue Deng, Dingdong Wang, Yuxuan Hu, Jinyu Li, Yanqing Liu, Yuanyuan Wang, Weidong Chen, Helen M. Meng, Shujie Liu, Xixin Wu

entry.summary: Introduces a duration-aligned speech-to-speech translation framework where a single speech LLM first generates a chain-of-thought plan covering target wording and phonetic length before synthesizing speech tokens, aimed at dubbing applications requiring strict temporal alignment. Includes DuraSet-440K, a duration-aligned CoT corpus, plus RL training.

entry.title: One-Step Is Optimal: Unconditional Rectified Flows are Noise2Noise Denoisers, and Multi-Step Integration Provably Hurts---A Benchmark and Task-Based Detectability Study on Low-Dose CT

author.name: Timothy Sereda, Debesh Jha

entry.summary: Proves that an unconditional rectified flow trained Noise2Noise-style has a one-step readout equal to the MMSE denoiser without clean targets, while multi-step integration provably departs from MMSE because the flow terminates at the noisy rather than clean distribution. Confirms this theoretically in a Gaussian model and empirically on low-dose CT.

entry.title: When Retrieval Hurts: Measuring and Explaining Retrieval-Induced Hallucination in Chest X-ray Report Generation

author.name: Emmanuel Idoko, Abdusshakur Olabisi, Shiloh Oni, Adesola Josiah

entry.summary: This paper shows that retrieval-augmented generation can reliably induce hallucinations in chest X-ray report generation: with a frozen LLaVA-1.5 generator and BioMedCLIP retrieval, clinically relevant retrieval doubles CheXbert F1, but mismatched retrieval collapses it to a fifth of the image-only score while unsupported findings traceable to retrieved evidence rise sharply. The authors introduce controls, including a coincidental-overlap check, to show this is not an artifact of evidence coverage.

entry.title: CausalDriveBench: Evaluating Causal Reasoning in Vision-Language-Action Models for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Narendiran Chembu, Navvrat Rao, Shreedhar Shreeshail Kodate, Gayatri Srujana Banda, Arko Sarkar, Abhinav Khanna, Rajarshee Das, Umesh Kanala, Siddarth Khandelwal, Kumar Aman, Aish Dubey, Kaustubh Beedkar, Arjun Jain

entry.summary: CausalDriveBench tests whether driving VLA models produce reasoning that reflects the causal structure of scenes, using Pearl's Causal Hierarchy across association, intervention, and counterfactual rungs. It builds causal scene graphs over nuScenes distinguishing causally active, dormant, and distractor entities, separating perceptual salience from causal relevance.

entry.title: Certified Interface Aliases: Exact Collisions in Vision-Language Preprocessing, and When They Exist

author.name: Mert Onur Cakiroglu, Elham Buxton, Mehmet Dalkilic, Hasan Kurban

entry.summary: AliasForge constructs provable cases where preprocessing makes two images with opposite correctness labels produce bit-identical interface tensors, via fixed-point resampling that maps nonzero integer perturbations to zero. This yields a ground-truth-free testbed for evaluating whether vision-language verifiers can distinguish fixable reasoning errors from visual information never reaching the model.

entry.title: Can Protein-Derived Knowledge Improve Pathology Foundation Models?

author.name: Di Zhang, Zhangpeng Gong, Jiashuai Liu, Zhi Zeng, Jiusong Ge, Chunze Yang, Xitong Ling, Kai Yi, Kai He, Weimiao Yu, Mireia Crispin-Ortuzar, Chen Li, Zeyu Gao

entry.summary: The paper proposes a three-stage framework that decouples proteomic knowledge acquisition from cross-modal transfer to overcome the paired-support bottleneck limiting molecularly guided pathology foundation models, since cross-modal supervision is restricted to paired WSI-omics samples. It addresses the mismatch between protein-sequence/single-cell encoders and patient-level bulk expression profiles paired with whole-slide images.

entry.title: Seeing and Solving Are Not Enough for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Ziheng Wang, Mingxuan Xie, Yilin Liu, Dayan Wu, Yang Li, Pengwen Dai

entry.summary: Empirically investigates whether VLM failures reflect visual extraction errors, problem-solving errors, or the composition of both, by defining an exactly scorable task state and testing whether models that succeed at each sub-ability separately still fail on the original multimodal question. Question-level analysis across VLMs and domains reveals composition failures that overall accuracy cannot. This refines how VLM failures should be diagnosed.

entry.title: When the Score Becomes the Target: Rethinking Metric Validity in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Morui Zhu, Deyuan Qu, Qi Chen, Kentaro Oguchi, Qing Yang

entry.summary: Examines whether driving benchmark scores remain reliable evidence of improvement once used as optimization targets, decomposing evaluation into execution, measurement, subscore mapping, and aggregation. Controlled interventions reveal large behavioral changes that receive little score response, and closed-loop comparisons show gains may not persist under repeated execution and replanning.

entry.title: TSGate: Timestep-Aware Gated Attention for Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Boyu Zhang, Yifan Liu, Shuxia Lin, Qingjian Ni, Yinfei Xu, Xu Yang

entry.summary: TSGate studies why diffusion transformers degrade under out-of-domain prompts, linking the failure to attention sinks and reduced early-step image-to-text attention. It introduces a timestep-aware gated attention mechanism that outperforms sink suppression alone, improving generation quality for free-form user prompts without LLM rewriting.

entry.title: D$^2$-VLA: Dual-Memory Dual-Frequency Vision-Language-Action Model For Long Dynamic Manipulation

author.name: Zijian Ye, Chengqi Wei, Wei Huang, Anlin Zheng, Chunyu Zou, Liangyu Wu, Zikang Zhao, Zhenjie Peng, Yushuo Yang, Shuman Zhao, Zhongrui Wang, Xiaojuan Qi

entry.summary: D2-VLA combines dual memory and dual-frequency control at the KV-cache interface of a pretrained VLA model for long-horizon dynamic manipulation: block-wise causal KV caching encodes observations incrementally, separate historical read views serve the VLM and action expert, and a gated adapter injects fresh visual features between costly periodic VLM updates. This lets robots remember out-of-view cues while reacting to moving objects.

entry.title: PIVOT: Pivot-Aware On Policy Self Distillation for Multi-Turn VLM Agents

author.name: Jiazhou Zhou, Hu Zhou, Yucheng Chen, Jinyuan Qu, Ying-Cong Chen, Lei Zhang

entry.summary: This paper uses counterfactual rollback probes across five multi-turn VLM agent benchmarks to show that gains from on-policy (self-)distillation stem largely from physical state rollback at a pivot step, defined as the first unrecoverable action. It then proposes a pivot-aware self-distillation method that targets this mechanism while GRPO suffers zero-gradient silence on uniform failures. The mechanistic analysis of why OPD/OPSD works is the standout contribution.

entry.title: WorldPlay2: Extending Real-Time Interactive World Models in Control and Horizon

author.name: Haiyu Zhang, Wenqiang Sun, Tengfei Wang, Junta Wu, Jun Zhang, Yunhong Wang, Yu Qiao, Chunchao Guo

entry.summary: WorldPlay2 is an interactive world model combining a factorized hybrid control interface (disentangling scene appearance, character identity, and dynamic events) with compressed memory and stabilized distillation for long-horizon, real-time generation. It tackles the tension between real-time responsiveness and long-horizon consistency in controllable world models.

entry.title: World SLAM Model: Joint World Modeling for SLAM and Navigation

author.name: Minghui Qin, Yijun Yuan, Weicheng Zheng, Kenan Li, Weibang Wang, Chang Sun, Junhao Huang, Anmin Liu, Yicheng Yao, Hang Zhao

entry.summary: WSM unifies SLAM and navigation by adopting SLAM's core mechanisms, incremental state updates with persistent memory and backend error refinement, inside a world model that predicts future visual states while jointly estimating camera motion and dense geometry. The evolving spatial world state grounds visual prediction and supports action generation and closed-loop navigation. This moves SLAM from an upstream preprocessing module to an integral part of navigation policy.

entry.title: Quantile Head for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Xuan Wang, Yinan Wu, Haoran Duan, Jungong Han

entry.summary: This paper unifies point regression and flow matching under a shared objective and derives a quantile objective for VLA action heads. The proposed Quantile Head predicts a median plus ordered positive gaps in a single forward pass, providing action distribution quantiles that support multiple sampling strategies without retraining, unlike costly iterative flow-matching samplers.

entry.title: RecastVLA: From Past Interaction to Future Control with Adaptive Policy States

author.name: Wenbo Li, Jun Yang, Yiteng Chen, Wei Zhang, Qingyao Wu

entry.summary: Builds on action-side test-time training to maintain an adaptive policy state, stored as shared fast weights, within a flow-matching vision-language-action policy. The persistent state carries history of past interactions into subsequent control decisions even when the scene no longer reveals them.

entry.title: RAVEL: Asynchronous Rolling Inference for Flow-Based Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Yuhan Chen, Ke Yu, Pengfei Liu, Shuxun Wang, Yi Yang, Linchao Zhu

entry.summary: RAVEL tackles the latency bottleneck of flow-based vision-language-action models caused by expensive VLM encoding and multi-step action denoising. It introduces an asynchronous inference framework that overlaps computation and lets near-term actions execute after a single denoising step by carrying partially denoised noise across steps. This enables responsive robot control in dynamic environments without retraining the underlying model.

entry.title: Gaze Prompts: Temporally Dense Human Attention for Vision-Language-Action Fine-Tuning

author.name: Yihan Zhou, Rui Yan, Mingcong Li, Zheyuan Huang, Xu Yang, Xueyang Guo, Yilin Mo

entry.summary: The paper introduces eye-tracker-supervised gaze prompting for VLA fine-tuning: gaze recorded during VR teleoperation is rendered as crosshairs on head-camera images during training, and at deployment a lightweight predictor estimates gaze from recent images and the instruction without an eye tracker or architecture changes. Instantiated with the existing pi-0 VLA model, gaze prompting substantially increased mean task success rates in the reported experiments. The method supplies frame-level visual relevance guidance that task-level language instructions lack.

entry.title: Do Not Cut When Uncertain: Rejectable and Calibrated Decision Heads for VLA Policies in Robotic Harvesting

author.name: Heng Zhang

entry.summary: This paper argues that VLA policy failure modes stem from their output interface rather than backbone scale, since behavior-cloned or flow-matching policies cannot express uncertainty or abstention. It proposes RCDH, a typed, rejectable, and calibrated decision head attachable to a frozen VLA backbone without retraining, validated in robotic harvesting where occlusion makes cut decisions ambiguous and irreversible. This is a compelling safety and calibration contribution for action models.

entry.title: Valid and Efficient Split Conformal Regression for Time Series

author.name: Percy S. Zhai, Maggie Cheng, Wei Biao Wu

entry.summary: The paper studies conformalized quantile and median regression for time series with adjacent calibration and test blocks, replacing hard-to-verify mixing assumptions with functional dependence measures. It provides the first non-asymptotic coverage guarantees and accuracy results for conformal interval lengths under weak dependence conditions that can even accommodate long memory.

entry.title: Latent reasoning architectures would undermine CoT, our strongest oversight tool

author.name: Lukas Finnveden

entry.summary: Lukas Finnveden argues that chain of thought is currently humanity's primary window into AI cognition, especially as swarms of agents take on large-scale tasks, and that a shift toward latent reasoning architectures would eliminate this oversight channel. The post warns that if frontier labs adopt architectures that reason extensively in latent states, interpretability and oversight of increasingly autonomous agent activity would become drastically harder.

entry.title: What Does the Rank Buy? A Spectral and Distributional Analysis of Low-Rank Adaptation

author.name: Babak Barazandeh

entry.summary: This theoretical paper shows that the common intuition that LoRA rank controls capacity breaks down under hard per-factor norm budgets: the reachable updates are exactly rank-at-most-r matrices in a nuclear-norm ball, over which complexity and displacement functionals are maximized by rank-one updates, so the rank cap never binds. Consequences include that Rademacher complexity is independent of rank and the model class is identical for every rank at least one. This is a surprising, well-defined theoretical result challenging standard PEFT folklore.

entry.title: Witness: Discovery, Deciphering, and Epiphany in Interactive Puzzle Environments

author.name: Guanghan Ning, Ping Liu, Linyi Li, Huangjie Zheng, Arjun Neervannan, Huu Nguyen, Michael Sklar, Deniz Zorlu, Nicolai Ouporov

entry.summary: WITNESS is a 2D grid-based puzzle environment with ground-truth ASCII observations where agents must infer hidden rules through experimentation, paired with WitnessGym for RL training and WitnessBench with held-out rules for evaluation. The authors probe what limits current language models on interactive rule-discovery and whether RL improves generalization to unseen rules.

entry.title: SCLATE: a Substrate for Continual-Learning Agent Training and Evaluation

author.name: Youngmok Jung, Sirajul Salekin, Henry Tran, Javier Movellan, Zhao Huang, Manjot Bilkhu

entry.summary: SCLATE is an execution substrate for continual-learning agents that interleaves benchmark tasks with agent-side events such as session boundaries, crons, and memory consolidation on one open event scheduler with a hybrid simulated clock. Benchmarks and unmodified agents contribute events through adapters, compressing month-long scenarios into hours by skipping idle gaps. This removes the need for each benchmark-agent pair to build a custom scheduling loop.

entry.title: Fail Loudly: An Auditable Runtime for Agentic Data Analysis

author.name: Hanxu Yan, Langxuan Deng, Zhengle Wang, Yibo Wang, Chunwei Liu

entry.summary: Presents RADAR, an auditable runtime for LLM data-science agents that makes analytical choices inspectable and revisable, via evidence-preserving exploration that retains source locations, typed operators for re-executable analysis, and mechanisms to surface silent errors where computations succeed but answer the wrong question. This targets a serious reliability gap in agentic data analysis.

entry.title: When Better Gets Worse: Improvement Fidelity for Self-Improving Agents in Adaptive Worlds

author.name: Ke Wang, Zijie Zhao, Zhiyi Yuan, Changlun Li

entry.summary: Formalizes Improvement Fidelity: whether proxy-verifier improvements preserve the sign and ordering of deployment improvements for self-improving agents in worlds that change in response to updates. The paper shows global policy accuracy need not guarantee update-level fidelity, with operator shift and deployment response creating errors whose impact depends on candidate margins. It introduces a PIVOT-based approach to address the gap.

entry.title: LSTMem: Hierarchical Long Short-Term Online Memory for Large Language Models

author.name: Xianglong Shi, Ruijie Yang, Sirui Zhao, Shukang Yin, Zihao Bian, Tinghao Yi, Enhong Chen

entry.summary: LSTMem equips each layer of a frozen LLM with LSTM-inspired matrix-valued states, separating a cell state that accumulates history from a hidden state used for readout, with input, forget, and output gates controlling storage versus exposure. This decouples what memory stores from what it exposes, addressing a limitation of single-state compact online memories.

entry.title: Org-Agent: Beyond Personal Assistants Towards Organizational Agents

author.name: Luyao Zhuang, Yujing Zhang, Zijin Hong, Yilin Xiao, Xiao Huang

entry.summary: Org-Agent extends LLM agents from personal assistants to organizational settings, identifying cross-user interaction/decision-making and cross-user memory/knowledge capabilities governed by constraints on identity, authority, permissions, information attribution and temporal validity, and conflict-resolution rules. It formalizes what must be satisfied before actions proceed in multi-user organizations.

entry.title: DeShortcut-Align: Decoupling Spurious Shortcuts for Robust Safety Alignment in Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Qirui Liu, Yichen Sun, Yan Wang, Zhixuan Chu, Linbo Jiang, Jianan Lin, Kui Ren

entry.summary: Shows that near-perfect safety scores from SFT/RL alignment of large reasoning models often come from spurious shortcuts: formatting shortcuts binding refusal to prompt templates and lexical shortcuts triggering refusals on sensitive keywords. It proposes DeShortcut-Align to decouple these shortcuts for intent-sensitive, robust safety alignment with less over-refusal and capability loss.

entry.title: When Valid Tool Calls Change Meaning: Formation-Consistent Dispatch for LLM Agents

author.name: Geonwoo Kim (Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology), Brent ByungHoon Kang (Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology)

entry.summary: The paper identifies schema-epoch drift: a schema-valid tool call can acquire a different security effect at execution time because standard dispatch omits the descriptor-handler relation, e.g., across rollout, reconnect, or delayed approval. It proposes formation-consistent dispatch (FCD), which binds implementation analysis to execution authority, builds provenance-bound over-approximations of declared effects, and admits calls only when their successor effects fit the call's security contract. This addresses a genuine gap in agent tool-call security.

entry.title: Not All Thinking is Created Equal: Latent Reasoning Discovers a Recurrent Search Algorithm for Depth Generalization

author.name: Huzi Cheng, Zhewei Zhang

entry.summary: Training five variants of the same GPTNeoX backbone from scratch on an extended multi-hop task (ProsQA-Ext), the paper compares vanilla, chain-of-thought, pause-token, and two latent-reasoning models, finding that strong in-distribution performance does not guarantee depth generalization, and that latent reasoning models learn an interpretable recurrent search algorithm enabling depth generalization where token-based approaches fail. It matters because it gives mechanistic evidence that different reasoning forms rely on different underlying algorithms, informing debates about latent versus token-level reasoning.

entry.title: Hesitation-Aware On-Policy Distillation for Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Jianguo Huang, Lipeng Wan, Yanchen Deng, Bo An

entry.summary: This paper improves on-policy distillation for diffusion LLMs by exploiting 'hesitations' — uncommitted token proposals at masked positions — which carry a disproportionate share of teacher-student divergence (66% from only 24% of supervisable pairs in an SDAR-4B pilot). By supervising at these hesitation points, the method extracts more signal than committed-position-only distillation. This advances the fast-growing diffusion language model training literature.

entry.title: Do World Models Learn Global Understanding?

author.name: Alexander Detkov, Matt Thomson

entry.summary: This paper frames understanding as learning constraints and propagating their consequences, constructing learning tasks on monoid worlds where observed transitions plus an unseen constraint jointly determine held-out transitions. It tests whether models can lift local information to global understanding, motivated by failures like LLMs that explain a concept but fail to apply it or follow safety instructions inconsistently. The framework offers a clean, controllable probe of global generalization.

entry.title: Learning to Steer, Steering to See: Unveiling the Geometry of RLVR in Large Language Models via Trainable Vectors

author.name: Yuchen Cai, Ding Cao, Qixiang Yin, Xin Xu, Kai Yang, Siye Wu, Pengyuan Wang, Jiaxuan Wang, Weijie Liu, Saiyong Yang, Guangzhong Sun, Guiquan Liu, Junfeng Fang

entry.summary: This paper uses vector steering to identify a low-dimensional effective manifold in activation space that reproduces reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) gains in LLMs. It uncovers geometric properties including that the manifold capacity needed to reproduce RL gains is small but not infinitely compressible, with constraints varying by injection depth. The work offers interpretability insight into what RLVR actually changes in model behavior.

entry.title: Causal Routing for Unlearning

author.name: Bardh Prenkaj, Andrea D'Angelo, Davide Mottin, Federico Fontana, Davide Gabrielli, Paola Velardi, Stefano Faralli

entry.summary: CRU performs machine unlearning by locating where a concept is expressed in the model, ranking neurons via one untrained forward pass over the forget set, and training small routing modules to gate and suppress only those neurons. The base model stays frozen, making changes in behavior causally attributable to the routing modules. This offers a targeted, interpretable alternative to rewriting all weights for unlearning.

entry.title: Composable Decoding on the Probability Simplex: Theory and Implementation

author.name: Xiaotong Ji, Ahmed Khaled Khamis, Rasul Tutunov, Matthieu Zimmer, Haitham Bou-Ammar

entry.summary: Formulates LLM decoding as an optimization problem over next-token distributions on the probability simplex, balancing expected model score against regularization under support constraints. This unified view recovers familiar decoding methods as special cases and enables composing distributional preferences into new decoders without external rewards, critics, or parameter updates, implemented as the CompoSimplex library.

entry.title: d-OPD: Future-Aware On-Policy Distillation for Block Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Ruitao Liu, Qinghao Hu, Song Han

entry.summary: d-OPD adapts on-policy distillation for block diffusion language models, which generate blocks sequentially while denoising multiple tokens in parallel, enabling distillation of pretrained autoregressive models into dLLMs. The method is future-aware, supervising the student on states it actually visits under block-diffusion generation.

entry.title: ReSPO: Reshaped Sequence Policy Optimization for Gradient Starvation in Off-Policy Learning

author.name: Yihang Chen, Yuanhao Ban, Cho-Jui Hsieh

entry.summary: The paper identifies a sign-dependent gradient starvation problem in clipped policy optimization for RLVR: clipping suppresses under-generated positive responses while allowing over-generated negative responses to dominate. ReSPO replaces clipping with a smooth two-branch sequence-level kernel derived from an alpha-divergence objective with variance control.

entry.title: KV-streams for Efficient Compaction in Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Emiliano Penaloza, Dane Malenfant, Dheeraj Vattikonda, Roger Creus Castanyer, Siddarth Venkatraman, Abhay Puri, Jonathan Light, Matthew James Sargent, Augustine N. Mavor-Parker, Massimo Caccia, Lucas Caccia, Glen Berseth, Esmeralda S. Whitammer, Alessandro Sordoni, Minseon Kim, Marc-Alexandre C\^ot\'e, Laurent Charlin, Guillaume Lajoie

entry.summary: Proposes KV-streams, a plug-and-play strategy for agentic RL training that streams the KV cache forward instead of flushing and re-prefilling it after each context compaction, substantially increasing throughput at constant memory. The approach is compatible with arbitrary compaction strategies and shows no performance degradation.

entry.title: Can Circuit Alignment Predict OOD Generalization?

author.name: Ayan Banerjee, Abhra Chaudhuri, Josep Llados, Umapada Pal, Anjan Dutta

entry.summary: Introduces the Circuit Alignment Score (CAS), a weight-only metric comparing class-specific circuits across domains via graph kernels, decomposed into same-class coherence and cross-class confusion, to predict out-of-distribution generalization without target-domain data. Proves existing activation-similarity metrics like CKA are insensitive to structural rerouting, and shows CAS's Monte Carlo estimate provably recovers ground-truth OOD accuracy rankings.

entry.title: How Strong Is the Evidence for the Artificial Hivemind? Reevaluating Evidence for the Open-Ended Homogeneity of Language Models

author.name: Rylan Schaeffer, Brando Miranda, Joshua Kazdan, Jessica Chudnovsky, Sanmi Koyejo

entry.summary: Critically reexamines three central results behind the claim that language models exhibit an Artificial Hivemind, i.e., worrying homogeneity in open-ended generation. The authors show that the flagship metaphor example actually contains one dominant vehicle plus a heavy tail of distinct minority responses under multiple analysis methods, and that the topic was among the least diverse tested, so the original evidence is not representative.

entry.title: Tetra: Serving Leech-Lattice Quantized LLMs at 2.7 Bits per Parameter

author.name: Pier-Jean Malandrino

entry.summary: Presents Tetra, a new codebook for leech-lattice quantization that cuts memory reads from 4.804 to 2.148 bits per weight using a 48-bit block encoding with a Golay-code trellis and small lookup tables decoded inside the matrix-vector product. Combined with per-row scale retraining and selective 4-bit storage, it serves Qwen3-4B-class models near 2.7 bits per parameter with good quality. A sharp systems contribution to extreme LLM quantization.

entry.title: EfficientAgent: What Makes KV Cache Offloading Work for Concurrent Agents?

author.name: Kunming Shao, Jierun Chen, Jiangnan Yu, Xiao-Hui Li, Chaofan Tao, Yanli Wang, Huanxin Lin, Kwang-Ting Cheng, Chi Ying Tsui, Haoli Bai

entry.summary: The paper explains why KV cache offloading to host memory gives inconsistent speedups for concurrent LLM agents, showing that benefits depend on whether a reusable prefix survives in the host tier until it is needed again while other agents evict shared cache space. It provides an analysis-driven framework for predicting when offloading helps on real agent workloads.

entry.title: Certified Selective Automation of LLM Agent Evaluation

author.name: Chengguang Gan, Yunhao Liang, Qinghao Zhang, Shiwen Ni

entry.summary: This paper asks what fraction of agent evaluation a judge can automate while certifying that the error rate on auto-decided trajectories stays below a budget, noting that correlated trajectory clusters from repeated task attempts invalidate standard i.i.d. certificates (a naive certificate can claim 98% automation while realized error exceeds budget in 17.5% of task resamples). It introduces a task-level bootstrap certificate that remains valid across tested regimes. This enables principled human effort reduction in agent evaluation.

entry.title: Train Together or Merge Later? Unifying VLA Experts via a Shared Action Interface

author.name: Zhizhen Zhang, Yuxia Fu, Zijian Wang, Helen Huang, Yadan Luo

entry.summary: PolicyWeave addresses why merging independently trained vision-language-action experts underperforms, identifying task-specific changes to the action interface (normalization, encoders/decoders) as a key incompatibility. It proposes merge-compatible post-training on a shared action interface plus context-guided sparse merging to recover task-specific gains in a multi-task policy.

entry.title: UnfoldCRF: Structured Mask Refinement with Image-Conditioned Latent Regions

author.name: Chunming He, Rihan Zhang, Lei Xu, Guanyi Qin, Chengyu Fang, Longxiang Tang, Fengyang Xiao, Sina Farsiu

entry.summary: UnfoldCRF treats mask refinement as inference in a conditional random field over pixel labels and image-conditioned latent region variables, with a corrected unary term, learned pairwise interactions, a null state for weak-agreement regions, and damped mean-field updates unrolled on one energy. It also isolates the effect of explicit structure versus extra capacity against black-box recurrent refiners. This brings interpretable structure back to segmentation refinement.

entry.title: V-Gym: Enhancing Agentic Visual Reasoning via Skill-Data Co-Evolution

author.name: Bei Yan, Yuecong Min, Jie Zhang, Junqi Yang, Shiguang Shan, Xilin Chen

entry.summary: V-Gym is an autonomous framework that iteratively co-evolves procedural skills and multimodal practice data from an agent's execution trajectories: it distills hierarchical reusable skills from both successes and failures, then generates targeted practice tasks to refine unreliable skills. This aims to improve agentic visual reasoning beyond what static datasets provide.

entry.title: Humanoids for Robot-Assisted Surgery: Bimanual Base Placement and Tool-Mount Optimization via Capability Maps

author.name: Peihan Zhang, Zekai Liang, Florian Richter, Nikita Thareja, Ryan Broderick, Shanglei Liu, Michael Yip

entry.summary: Quantifies how close contemporary humanoids come to the kinematic demands of robot-assisted laparoscopic surgery, presenting a capability-map-based framework that optimizes humanoid base placement and tool mounting to maximize bimanual reachability under tool-tip kinematics and remote-center-of-motion constraints, evaluated on three humanoid platforms.

entry.title: Conformal Coverage of Time Series: Validity and Inference

author.name: Percy S. Zhai, Maggie Cheng, Wei Biao Wu

entry.summary: A companion to the previous work, this paper develops inference on the realized coverage of split conformal prediction under temporal dependence, deriving non-asymptotic marginal coverage error bounds without mixing assumptions. It establishes the first central limit theorem for realized coverage of split conformal prediction, enabling practitioners to judge whether observed coverage is abnormal.

entry.title: SMARtCARE: Privacy-Preserving Agentic AI Systems for Bounded-Autonomy Clinical Decision Support

author.name: Srini Ramaswamy, Deveeshree Nayak

entry.summary: SMARtCARE proposes a four-state clinical decision-support architecture (Stable, Meta-cognitive, Assisted, Regulated) that avoids automatic retrieval of prior patient records, instead using a lossy six-channel fingerprint of prior trajectories to detect when current vital-sign drift matches past deterioration patterns. Escalation to clinicians and full record retrieval only occur through clinician-mediated controls, balancing safety with privacy. This matters for bounded-autonomy agentic AI in high-stakes medical settings where long-context limitations can cause missed relevant history.

entry.title: Receiver-Conditioned Latent Communication gives 94% CacheBack

author.name: Maximillian Rossi, Prajwal Raghunath, Haoqing Xuan, Yusen Zhang, Eugene Wu

entry.summary: This paper improves multi-agent latent communication via KV-cache transfer by conditioning what is sent on what the receiving agent actually needs for its local task, reported to achieve 94 percent CacheBack (cache reuse/recovery). Full KV caches scale linearly with context and agent count, often exceeding GPU memory and context windows, so receiver-conditioning substantially cuts costs while preserving accuracy and latency benefits. This is a practical systems contribution to efficient multi-agent communication.

entry.title: GameBoyWorlds: A Testbed for Self-Improvement in Embodied Video Games

author.name: Dhananjay Ashok, Adam Shen, Aslan Huo Feng, Chinmay Khanna, Jun Rui Huang, Raghav Sarmukaddam, Surendira Balaji Natarajan, Xiaotong Cui, Xincan Zhang, Thomson Yen, Hongseok Namkoong, Jonathan May, Jesse Thomason

entry.summary: GameBoyWorlds is a testbed for evaluating whether agents can autonomously self-improve in interactive video game environments without demonstrations, documentation, or rewards, requiring self-directed exploration to infer actionable knowledge. It includes an execution track across five game series and evaluates navigation and short-horizon task completion at test time.

entry.title: From Trajectories to Grounded Preferences: Process Preference Synthesis via Interaction Element Graphs for Web PRMs

author.name: Yangzhe Peng, Xiaoyang Wang, Yiyang Zhao, Lijun Wu, Kun He

entry.summary: SURFPRM improves comparative process reward models for web agents by addressing the scarcity of Grounded Minimal Contrastive Pairs, where competing candidates target genuine on-page elements with identical action types. It synthesizes preferences via interaction element graphs, showing that baseline preference data (e.g., WebArbiter) contains only about 24% GMCPs, biasing PRMs toward shallow shortcuts like element hallucination. The result is step-level reward guidance grounded in real page state.

entry.title: ProTTT: Learning to Learn Semantic User Memory with Test-Time Training

author.name: Sejun Park, Hyoungjo Bhang, Hyein Jeong, Yohan Jo

entry.summary: Introduces ProTTT, a profile-supervised meta-learning framework for semantic user memory where memory construction starts from a shared initialization and evolves per user via test-time training on growing history, avoiding the inference-cost growth of context-based approaches and the reconstruction needs of parametric ones. Profile supervision ensures the learned memory actually captures user-specific knowledge rather than generic content.

entry.title: Refinement Symmetry in Multimodal Transformers

author.name: Yuhao Du, Shunian Chen

entry.summary: Defines refinement symmetry for attention: splitting a representation while preserving content, position, visible context, and total mass should preserve its contribution. The authors prove split invariance forces a linear local mass factor for nondecreasing attention kernels, and demonstrate in Qwen2.5-Omni-7B that duplicating visual tokens changes 255 of 3,586 MVBench answers under standard attention, while their measure weighting preserves every answer. Qwen2.5-Omni-7B is an existing open model, so this is analysis of established behavior rather than a new release.

entry.title: World Agent: Can Language Models Keep a World Running?

author.name: Weixing Chen, Weipeng Zhang, Nan An, Yang Liu, Liang Lin

entry.summary: Proposes the world agent task: rather than generating a playable world, a model must keep one running over time, coordinating events and carrying forward their consequences. Existing evaluations of generative worlds stop at generation, delivery, or single-step transitions, and correct local transitions do not guarantee coherent causal event flow. This reframes world-model evaluation around sustained operation.

entry.title: Counterfactual Self-Evolving Agents for Evidence-Grounded Reasoning

author.name: Xing Han, Yuxin Wang, Chen Chen, Wei Dai, Gautham Krishna Gudur, Shijun Li, Hsing-Huan Chung, Gregory D. Hager, Joydeep Ghosh, Paul Pu Liang, Suchi Saria

entry.summary: This paper introduces counterfactual self-evolution for self-play proposer-solver systems on evidence-identifiable tasks, where a trainable Proposer generates targeted counterfactual context edits with causal explanations so answers can be independently verified. The method is supported by an expert-verified counterfactual instruction-tuning dataset. It matters because it addresses a core bottleneck in self-play: generating plausible but verifiable training cases.

entry.title: Trust and Task Completion in the World of Consumer AI Agents

author.name: Jeroen Olieslagers, Eduardo Pujol, Gal Zahavi, Lukas Ingemarsson, Shivani Poddar

entry.summary: The authors built a simulation-based evaluation scoring trust and completion on the same runs for action agents that email, spend money, and call businesses on a user's behalf, in a world of simulated businesses with websites, inboxes, phone lines, and responsive people. They distinguish trust failures (acting without consent or failing to act when told) from completion failures (giving up on hard errands), both heavily dependent on the harness. This is a valuable benchmark for consumer agent deployment safety.

entry.title: CodeSkill: Latent Skill Abstraction for Long-Horizon Code Agents

author.name: Song-Li Wu, Jingyi Wang, Zhaocheng Du, Weinan Gan, Weiwen Liu

entry.summary: CodeSkill adapts hierarchical latent skill modeling to code agents, using a teacher model to distill recurring multi-step behavioral patterns from large trajectory datasets into skill abstractions. This addresses the mismatch between token-level RL optimization and high-level behavioral reasoning, improving exploration and credit assignment under sparse rewards.

entry.title: Reasoning on the Simplex: Geometric Fixed-Point Models

author.name: Talgat Daulbaev, Ilya Glazkov, Maxim Rakhuba, Ivan Oseledets

entry.summary: Proposes Geometric Fixed-Point Reasoning (GFPR), a looped-reasoner formulation where the iterated state is a categorical belief field on products of simplices, so the argmax is always a valid answer and task structure can be imposed via convex relaxations. With roughly 7M parameters, GFPR achieves 95.1% exact match on Sudoku-Extreme and 92.0% on Maze-Hard, competitive with far larger looped reasoning models.

entry.title: R$^2$ Flow: Recursive Self-Improvement via Recursive Skill Evolution

author.name: Mingda Zhang, Qiang Huang, Yanjin Li, Zijia Wang, Qika Lin, Xiaoying Tang, Tiesunlong Shen

entry.summary: R2 Flow is a recursive self-improvement framework for LLM agents that alternates policy learning, independent verification, and versioned skill-library updates, fixing three failure modes of flow-based training: strategy collapse, credit for frequent use rather than benefit, and unverified library edits. It uses flow-based reward sampling to credit skills in library revisions.

entry.title: GUITAR: Structured Failure Diagnosis of GUI Agents via State Transitions

author.name: Shaoqing Zhang, Kehai Chen, Xuefeng Bai, Zhuosheng Zhang, Pengfei Zhang, Yang Xiang, Min Zhang

entry.summary: GUITAR is a state-centric diagnostic framework that analyzes GUI agent failures across states and transitions rather than per-screen step accuracy, addressing blind spots like functionally equivalent screens and long-tailed failure distribution. This matters because current evaluation metrics hide systematic failure patterns critical for building reliable GUI agents.

entry.title: AdaGuard: An Adaptive Guard Model with User-defined Policies

author.name: Yunhao Feng, Yifan Ding, Yuxiang Xie, Zheng Li, Mingrui Lao, Zeyuan Wang, Yanming Guo

entry.summary: AdaGuard introduces guard models that judge agent behavior against user-defined policies rather than fixed risk taxonomies, supported by AdaptiveSafety, a dataset of 10,939 training and 1,000 test examples with 1-100 rule policies, behavioral counterfactuals, and explanations identifying violated rules. This enables policy-dependent judgments of identical actions.

entry.title: Dynamical Parameters: An Interpretability Framework for Time-Series Foundation Models

author.name: Kang Yang, Gaofeng Dong, Liying Han, Mani Srivastava

entry.summary: This paper introduces Dynamical Parameters — properties like trend slope, oscillation frequency, and autoregressive dependence — as a formal framework for interpreting time-series foundation models. The authors compare how well these dynamical properties are accessible in hidden states versus how much forecasts actually respond to changes in those properties, finding across nine frozen TSFMs that representation accessibility is high (42 of 63 cells above 0.95) while forecast response is poor (median 0.46), revealing a representational-use gap.

entry.title: When Does Structured Knowledge Help Neural Theorem Proving?

author.name: Sareh Nabi, Roland Vogl, Marzieh Nabi

entry.summary: MathAgent builds MathKG, a knowledge graph connecting 364 Mathlib theorems and definitions via 9,434 typed semantic edges inferred by LLM relation extraction, to augment LLM theorem provers in Lean 4. A controlled ablation across four augmentation modes examines when structured semantic knowledge actually helps automated proving.

entry.title: TULIP: Targeted LLM Unlearning at Layers Identified Per-Input

author.name: Yejin Kim, William F. Shen, Seokwon Jung, Daeun Park, Seong Joon Oh

entry.summary: TULIP shows through a hidden-state hijacking experiment that forget answers are formed at intermediate layers whose location varies per input, so fixed-layer unlearning is insufficient. It proposes per-input identification of the formation layer for targeted representation-level unlearning.

entry.title: RSI-Router: Evolving Subtask-Level LLM Routing and Skills for Cost-Efficient Agents

author.name: Hao Li, Hangfan Zhang, Zhiyao Cui, Chunjiang Mu, Yiqun Zhang, Bo Zhang, Danyang Jia, Shuyue Hu

entry.summary: Introduces RSI-Router, a framework that assigns large and small LLMs to subtasks within long-horizon agent tasks and learns model-specific skills through recursive self-improvement over accumulated experience. Each iteration mines subtasks from trajectories, evolves routing strategies, and refines assignments to improve the performance-cost trade-off of agent deployments.

entry.title: RISE: Red-teaming via Iterative Strategy Evolution for Modern Text-to-Image Models

author.name: Dmitrii Kharlapenko, Sergei Bratchikov, Konstantin Korolev, Aleksandr Nikolich

entry.summary: This paper identifies two core weaknesses in automated red-teaming of production text-to-image systems: unreliable VLM-based judges that miss true violations or reward borderline images, and poor exploration on hardened guardrails. It proposes RISE, an iterative strategy-evolution framework with strict category-specific success criteria and calibrated judges. The work matters because policy-violation detection on hardened commercial APIs is a real safety bottleneck as image generators scale.

entry.title: Sol-H3: Recursive Self-Improvement for MiniMax-H3 Inference Acceleration on Sol-Engine across Cloud and Edge

author.name: Yitong Li, Jincheng Yu, Junsong Chen, Haopeng Li, Shuchen Xue, Haozhe Liu, Ping Luo, Song Han, Enze Xie

entry.summary: The paper presents a full-stack inference acceleration pipeline for MiniMax-H3, a 33-billion-parameter open-source video diffusion model, targeting both cloud (NVIDIA GB200) latency and edge (DGX-Spark) memory constraints. It integrates algorithmic design with optimized operator implementations and uses a recursive self-improvement loop on a Sol-Engine for tuning. This tackles the practical deployment bottleneck of multi-step iterative denoising in production video generation.

entry.title: Imprint Reader: From Weight-Update Readout to Behavioral Intervention

author.name: Guanxu Chen, Qihao Lin, Jing Shao

entry.summary: Imprint Reader is a model trained with Semantic Mount-and-Read Tuning (SaRT) to describe frozen weight updates in natural language, giving models a way to decode parameter-level traces of their own learning. The work points toward self-reflection over training history and using the resulting readout for behavioral intervention.

entry.title: MechBench: Can AI Scientific Agents Discover Mechanisms Beyond Phenomenal Laws?

author.name: Zihan Yu, Jiadong Zhang, Jialin Cheng, Jingtao Ding, Yong Li

entry.summary: MechBench is a benchmark that explicitly separates recovering observable phenomenal laws from identifying the underlying mechanisms that generate them, defining each task via structured mechanistic models and evaluating recovery through mechanism probes that query consequences not visible in the data. It matters because existing symbolic regression benchmarks only test surface-law fitting, so the field currently cannot measure whether scientific agents understand mechanisms at all.

entry.title: ARISE: Adapting to Evolving Capability Gaps in Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Kun Feng, Yuchen Fang, Yiyang Tan, Shuqi Gu, Yongxiang Zhao, Yu Liu, Xingyu Lu, Lintao Ma, Kan Ren

entry.summary: ARISE is a reinforcement learning framework for long-horizon agents that uses rollout evidence to continually update behavioral rubrics and training priorities as the agent's capability gaps evolve, addressing the misalignment between static training criteria and changing weaknesses. It matters because fixed rubrics and sparse task feedback are known failure modes in agentic RL, and co-evolving rubrics with skills is a plausible general remedy.

entry.title: Signatures of semantic search in the activations of large language models

author.name: Luke Leckie, Peter M. Todd, Jacob G. Foster

entry.summary: Applying mechanistic interpretability to the semantic fluency task, this paper finds that LLMs, like humans, organize output into clusters punctuated by switches and that their internal states show distinguishable signatures for within-cluster exploitation versus between-cluster exploration, using techniques including a Jacobian lens over intermediate layers. It matters because it provides evidence that LLMs internally represent search regimes analogous to human semantic foraging, bridging cognitive science and interpretability.

entry.title: Failure-Transparent Agents: Benchmarking Post-Failure Reporting in Tool-Using Language Models

author.name: Junru Zhu, Shiming Xie, Aime Lu Fan Chen, Xiaoqing Ding, Chunxin Tang, Ruoyu Qi, Yulang Fei

entry.summary: FTA is a controlled benchmark that isolates whether tool-using agents honestly report failure versus claiming unsupported success, by fixing failed observations and required evidence before generation. It spans 100 tasks across five failure families, includes user-pressure conditions, and evaluates 3,600 human-annotated responses across six models. This targets a safety-relevant honesty failure mode that existing benchmarks confound with tool-selection ability.

entry.title: MaD-RL: Matching Distributions for Calibrating LLMs with Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Sourabh Kulkarni, Ksheeraj Sai Vepuri, Basar Demir, Jason Bohrer, Emily Shen, Jianfa Chen, Nan Jiang, Ankit Jain, Harihar Subramanyam, Mannat Singh, Chirag Nagpal

entry.summary: MaD-RL proposes a general RL-based distribution-matching framework for LLM post-training that controls the distribution of a latent categorical attribute of outputs against a target distribution, beyond mere expected-reward maximization. The authors show dominant recipes like GRPO are ill-suited for such distributional control in applications like synthetic data generation, fairness constraints, and exploration. This extends post-training from scalar reward optimization to full output-distribution shaping.

entry.title: Active Causal Discovery Benchmark: Evaluating LLM Agents Under Budgeted Interventions

author.name: Sagar Deb, Devam Shah, Ashwanth Krishnan

entry.summary: ACDB is a new SCM-grounded benchmark evaluating whether LLM agents can recover causal graph structure using budget-constrained interventions, with a three-layer scoring contract separating skeleton recovery, DAG recovery, and intervention efficiency. Results show classical PC with an active heuristic outperforms raw LLM agents like Claude Sonnet 4.6 and GPT-5.4 on directed F1. The benchmark exposes significant gaps between LLM agents and classical causal discovery methods.

entry.title: A Large-Scale Benchmark and Risk Assessment of Traffic Analysis Attacks on Cloud LLM Services

author.name: Shahrooz Pouryousef, Jesus Lopez, Saeefa Rubaiyat Nowmi, Md Mahmuduzzaman Kamol, Moinul Hossain, Muoi Tran, Mohammad Saidur Rahman

entry.summary: This is the first unified measurement study and public benchmark of network-level traffic analysis attacks on encrypted cloud LLM services, showing that a passive observer can infer the serving model, prompt category, and multi-agent task behavior from packet sizes, timing, and burst structure alone. The benchmark covers 60,000 user-LLM interactions across 10 models and 6 prompt categories, plus multi-agent executions. This is a significant security contribution highlighting a real privacy side channel in deployed LLM infrastructure.

entry.title: Is invariance all you need for algorithmic fairness? Removing demographic information can create new bias

author.name: Aditya Parikh, Eike Petersen, Stella Frank, Enzo Ferrante, Melanie Ganz, Aasa Feragen

entry.summary: This paper challenges the assumption that demographic-invariant representations are always desirable for fairness, showing mathematically and empirically that enforcing invariance can hinder bias mitigation or even create new biases when demographics correlate with labels. It distinguishes marginal from class-conditional invariance and connects them to demographic parity and equalized odds. This is a useful corrective to a widely held fairness heuristic.

entry.title: DS-VLA: A Dendritic-inspired Vision-Language-Action Model for Robust Action Control

author.name: Yaxing Lyu, Jingyi Li, Mingkun Xu, Yujie Wu

entry.summary: DS-VLA is a vision-language-action model that incorporates dendritic spiking dynamics into action control, using sparsely connected dendritic branches with learned decay factors to modularize feature processing and integrate temporal information, plus mechanisms to suppress unreliable state updates. The work targets robustness under transiently corrupted actions, a gap between nominal evaluation and closed-loop behavior. It is a novel bio-inspired architectural contribution to robust robot manipulation.

entry.title: What Can a Leaderboard Certify? Compositional Controllability for Fair Evaluation and Training of Biomedical Literature-Review Agents

author.name: Zhaowei Han, Xiang Zhang, Lingxiao Guan, Danqi Hu, Kai Liu, Kevin Chang, Jie Liu

entry.summary: This paper introduces compositional controllability, a formal framework for certifying comparisons of long-horizon agents on leaderboards despite unequal evidence, inputs, or budgets. Its central result bounds the gap between observed and controlled score differences using only nuisance factors outside the comparison window, yielding an admissibility test applied before scores are inspected, with certification only when the score gap exceeds the bound. It is applied to biomedical literature-review agents.

entry.title: DRAM: Delta-rule Recurrent Associative Memory for Robot Manipulation Policies

author.name: Xinyu Zhao, Yixiang Shan, Tao Yang, Runyu Lei, Yiming Zhao, Jiaxin Fan, Zongbao Feng, Peng Jia

entry.summary: DRAM is a plug-and-play memory module that attaches to pretrained robotic manipulation policies, giving them long-horizon memory without modifying the backbone or retraining it. It uses delta-rule recurrent associative memory to avoid the inference cost of multi-frame observation windows and the task-limitations of predefined semantic features. This tackles a genuine gap, since most manipulation policies are memoryless or use short temporal windows.

entry.title: Do Audio LLMs Listen Before They Act? Diagnosing Acoustic-Context Gating in Voice Agents

author.name: Yanjie Zhang, Nanchen Hu, Yushi Sun

entry.summary: VGBench is a 1,018-item diagnostic benchmark for action-level addressedness in audio LLM agents, covering side-talk, self-talk, and speaker-switch scenarios with a shared action space of silence, tool call, or natural-language answer.
