entry.title: Understanding Generalization Requires Universal Induction

author.name: Aram Ebtekar, Marcus Hutter, Danica J. Sutherland

entry.summary: This theory paper argues classical statistical theory cannot explain general-purpose AI generalization because No Free Lunch theorems force any learner with inductive biases to underperform somewhere, and NFL applies even to meta-learning. The authors argue that biasing toward short programs, yielding Solomonoff induction, is a principled starting point that is competitive against all computable learners despite large constants. It provides a theoretical lens on why large pretrained models generalize.

entry.title: Codoku: Renewable Program-Reasoning Challenges for Frontier Coding Agents

author.name: Cong Li, Hao Sun, Zenan Li, Zhendong Su

entry.summary: Codoku (code sudoku) is a renewable benchmark where solvers fill typed cells in a partial program to satisfy global static and dynamic constraints such as a prescribed control-flow graph and execution path. Because partial programs cannot simply be executed and valid fillings are sparse in an exponentially large space, the design blocks shortcutting and mitigates contamination through renewable generation. It targets a real gap in program-reasoning evaluation for coding agents.

entry.title: Dynamic Flow, Static Graph: KV Cache Reuse for Efficient LLM Serving on Mobile NPUs

author.name: Zhengxiang Huang, Shengheng Chen, Chaoyue Niu, Yujie Sun, Zhaode Wang, Zeyu Zhao, Chengfei Lv, Fan Wu, Guihai Chen

entry.summary: The paper presents a compute-storage co-design for KV cache reuse (both prefix and non-prefix) in on-device LLM serving on mobile NPUs, where static compilation and tight memory/bandwidth constraints break cloud-GPU cache designs. It proposes an intra-graph mechanism for sequential KV reuse, advancing private, low-latency local LLM inference.

entry.title: VEX-Bench: Benchmarking Verification Complexity of LLM-Generated Misinformation

author.name: Hanxun Huang, Yutao Wu, Qizhou Wang, Silvia Monta\~na-Ni\~no, Yige Li, Xiang Zheng, Elif Buse Doyuran, Phoebe Matich, Xiao Liu, Xingjun Ma, Sarah Erfani, Christopher Leckie

entry.summary: Introduces VEX-Bench, a unified benchmark measuring how hard it is to verify LLM-generated misinformation during screening, with dimensions drawn from journalistic and fact-checking practice including checkability, harm potential, source credibility signals, imposter legitimacy, and expected verification effort. It targets the growing asymmetry between cheap misinformation generation and costly verification.

entry.title: Teacher-Student Gaps Are Not Enough: Outcome-Guided On-Policy Distillation for Multi-Turn Autonomous Agents

author.name: Tong Zhang, Zhou Liu, Yihao Liu, Jiahua Bao, Xuchen Li, Honglin Lin, Tao Cheng, Zhihan Yu, Kai Tang, Xiaoxi Jiang, Guanjun Jiang

entry.summary: This work shows that teacher-student token-level gaps are poor signals for on-policy distillation of multi-turn agents, since large gaps can be benign while small gaps can be outcome-critical. It proposes outcome-guided intervention that accounts for how current student actions affect future environment interaction.

entry.title: CLIMB: A Clinical Multimorbidity Benchmark for Diagnosing Co-occurring Conditions through Multiturn Conversations

author.name: Yusuf Kesmen, Aniruddha Mukherjee, Yena Chang, David Sasu, Trevor Brokowski, Alexandra V. Kulinkina, Kristina Keitel, Akhil Arora, Lars Henning Klein, Mary-Anne Hartley

entry.summary: CLIMB is a benchmark where a doctor-model interviews a simulated patient to identify a ground-truth set of co-occurring conditions, with cases synthesized from clinical decision algorithms and diagnostic datasets. Across six frontier and open models, none recovers the exact condition set in more than 10% of interactive cases, with performance degrading under multimorbidity.

entry.title: Behavioral Foundation Models for Quality Diversity

author.name: Nazim Bendib, Nicolas Perrin-Gilbert, Olivier Sigaud

entry.summary: Introduces BFM-QD, a framework that runs Quality-Diversity search inside the compact latent behavioral space of Behavioral Foundation Models rather than in high-dimensional policy parameter space. This enables discovery of large repertoires of diverse, high-performing policies with zero-shot and adaptation capabilities inherited from the BFM.

entry.title: Cache-Aware Conv3D Lowering Across Embedded World-Model Decoders

author.name: Jiaming Zhang, Wu Yang, Shuai Tao, Wulong Liu

entry.summary: Introduces a cache-aware lowering that rewrites causal Conv3D operations as batched spatial Conv2D while preserving pretrained weights and temporal-cache semantics, enabling generative world models to run on edge devices. On a full Cosmos3-Edge image-to-video pipeline on a 64-GB Jetson AGX Orin, it accelerates VAE decoding about 7x and cuts complete-generation latency more than 2x.

entry.title: HM-ROUTER: Joint Model and Harness Routing for Agentic Systems

author.name: Hao Mark Chen, Royson Lee, Yasuyuki Okoshi, Dimitris Anastasiou, Wayne Luk, Hongxiang Fan

entry.summary: HM-ROUTER jointly routes each query to a model and a harness (the tool-use and execution scaffolding) in agentic systems, learning shared representations for each with a CP-tensor-decomposition-inspired interaction term to capture model-harness compatibility. Sharing lets samples from observed pairs generalize to unobserved combinations, and the authors curate a benchmark from 12 public agent benchmarks covering 293 model-harness configurations. This addresses a practical gap in agentic cost-performance optimization.

entry.title: Length-Independent State Tracking Under a Parallel Scan

author.name: Julien Brandoit, Arthur Fyon, Thomas Braipson, Tom Clara, Florent De Geeter, Pierre Sacr\'e, Damien Ernst, Guillaume Drion

entry.summary: The paper formalizes finite-state tracking at finite precision for linear RNNs, linear attention, and state-space models, characterizing length independence: correct tracking at every sequence length with precision cost not growing with length. It shows that length-independent tracking requires balancing contraction dynamics for stability with a competing dynamic, and that the parallel scan itself is a source of perturbation. This addresses a real gap between idealized expressivity theory and hardware reality.

entry.title: Does Execution Require Target KV Fidelity? A Mixed-Fidelity KV Runtime for LLM Serving

author.name: Jiantong Jiang, Yue Yang, Peiyu Yang, Feng Liu

entry.summary: ElasticKV is a mixed-fidelity runtime for LLM serving that decouples KV-cache execution from the configured target representation, introducing a compact intermediate KV state so fidelity becomes a runtime-managed property. This prevents memory pressure from causing request stalls and preemptions, combining a pair-structured layout with a paged serving runtime.

entry.title: Where Activation Sparsity and KV-Cache Sparsity Cross in LLM Decoding

author.name: Jungseob Lee, Seungyoon Lee, Seongtae Hong, Sugyeong Eo, Heuiseok Lim

entry.summary: Analyzes how activation sparsity (trimming weight-projection traffic) and KV-cache sparsity (trimming cache traffic) trade off during LLM decoding, deriving a byte crossover context length where their savings are equal, plus ideal speedup bounds for each and their composition. Empirical timing from 2K to 128K tokens on real text validates the analysis across GPUs and kernels.

entry.title: What Does a Stream Model Buy You in Flow Matching?

author.name: Jian Xu

entry.summary: This analysis paper dissects stream-level flow matching, proving a reduction: the stream-level CFM objective depends on the stream law only through the per-time joint law, so Gaussian streams reach exactly the conditional paths standard CFM already parametrizes. It concludes that claimed gains from GP-stream constructions collapse to a two-scalar-curve design space, deflating reported advantages.

entry.title: DisKO: Deep Koopman Learning in Distribution Space from Unpaired Snapshots

author.name: He Ma, Xiaochen Liu, Wanfeng Lu, Ying Wang, Wei Lin, Qunxi Zhu

entry.summary: DisKO extends deep Koopman operator learning to systems observed only through temporally unpaired distribution snapshots, by treating the distribution itself as the dynamical state. It jointly learns predictive distributional observables, a finite-dimensional Koopman representation, and a generative map back to the full distribution space. Evaluated across seven diverse benchmarks, it demonstrates strong performance on a problem setting where trajectory-based dynamical learning methods are not applicable.

entry.title: Don't Forget! Decomposing the Training Dynamics of Memorization in Language Models

author.name: Florian Eichin, Philipp Mondorf, Andrei Mircea, Yupei Du, Barbara Plank, Michael A. Hedderich

entry.summary: Decomposes the loss trajectories of memorized sequences across training and parameters to study how language models memorize duplicated (recitation) and rare (recollection) sequences, using the Pythia model family. It finds memorization is characterized by sequence-level gradient alignment, with recitation suffering misalignment with other training influences that causes forgetting. This offers a mechanistic account of memorization dynamics relevant to data curation and privacy.

entry.title: CacheRepair: Learning to Repair Cross-Chunk Context in RAG for KV Cache Fusion

author.name: Genglin Wang, Wangsong Yin, Yeerzhati Abudunuer, Haoxuan Xu, Guoliang Xing, Zhenyu Yan

entry.summary: The paper targets a practical inefficiency in multi-document RAG: independently precomputed per-chunk KV caches can be concatenated for speed, but they lack cross-chunk attention information, degrading answer quality, and selective recomputation to fix this is expensive. CacheRepair introduces a lightweight learned network that estimates the difference between independently computed caches and jointly processed ones, fusing compressed KV features to repair cross-chunk context with far less online computation. This is a meaningful systems-level efficiency contribution for latency-sensitive RAG deployments.

entry.title: TANGO: Watermarking Masked Diffusion Language Models in Token Pairs

author.name: Kasra Arabi, Nir Weinberger, Micah Goldblum, Niv Cohen

entry.summary: TANGO is a watermarking scheme for masked-diffusion language models that keys each new token to a nearby already-unmasked token, since conventional left-to-right watermarks fail when context tokens may still be masked. It avoids the fixed green-list weakness where attackers can recover the list via token-frequency comparison, using secret-key color classes over token pairs.

entry.title: LLMs are General Asynchronous Agents

author.name: George Yakushev, Denis Mazur, Vladimir Bartenev, Vyacheslav Zhdanovskiy, Timofey Byzov, Vladimir Kaurkin, Vadim Pastushenko

entry.summary: Argues that modern LLM agents are constrained by sequential read-think-act cycles while many applications (voice, embodied, monitoring) require handling concurrent inputs. The paper develops a general asynchronous LLM framework where users or agents define inference-coroutine semantics, generalizing across previously separate solutions like voice architectures, VLAs, and async tool calling. A systems-level reframing of agent architecture.

entry.title: Cartridges++: KV Cache Compression without Off-Context Derailment

author.name: Sonia Laguna, Joao Monteiro, Marco Cuturi, Pierre Ablin, Eleonora Gualdoni

entry.summary: This paper extends Cartridges-style learned KV cache compression by examining off-context behavior, showing prior evaluations ignore whether compressed caches derail model responses to queries beyond the document. Cartridges++ introduces training/evaluation changes that preserve both on-context fidelity and off-context robustness for long-document serving.

entry.title: How to Tame a Multi-Headed Hydra? Adaptive Multi-Category Safety Steering for Large Language Models

author.name: Chenxi Wang, Ruiyang Huang, Li Huang, Yifan Wu

entry.summary: CAM-Steer is an activation steering framework for LLM safety that explicitly coordinates steering direction and strength when multiple harm categories co-occur in a single prompt, a case prior adaptive steering methods did not handle. It modifies internal activations at inference without parameter updates, improving safety across mixed-category harmful prompts.

entry.title: Opera: A Verbal Critic Framework for Long-horizon Coding Agents

author.name: Kai Mei, Zhiyuan Hu, Yutong Dai, Juntao Tan, Yifan Zhang, Dingjie Song, Dimitris N. Metaxas, Silvio Savarese, Ran Xu, Zeyuan Chen

entry.summary: Opera is a verbal critic framework for long-horizon coding agents that treats each correction as a persistent note followed until the diagnosed problem is resolved. It decides when to review via periodic and event-driven triggers, diagnoses issues with typed operators, audits feedback against visible evidence before delivery, and distinguishes mere compliance from actual resolution. As a test-time critic it improves coding-agent reliability where one-shot feedback is ineffective or harmful.

entry.title: Can LLMs Value the Right Evidence? Evidence-Value Misalignment in Dynamic Medical Diagnosis

author.name: Kehua Feng, Yunsheng Lu, Yitong Qiao, Tiantian He, Lei Liu, Yue Shen, Jian Wang, Jinjie Gu

entry.summary: The paper introduces Evidence-Value Misalignment (EVM), the mismatch between a model's diagnostic decisions and the value of available evidence, noting that a correct diagnosis from insufficient evidence can be clinically hazardous. It presents MedEVM, a dynamic benchmarking environment with 1,050 cases across 24 disease systems where observations arrive turn by turn and models must decide whether to gather more evidence or commit to a diagnosis. Evaluating nine LLMs reveals patterns including miscalibrated evidence tracking, where the act of diagnosing fails to properly calibrate with evidence in hand.

entry.title: Octree-based Video Representation

author.name: Rungui Zhou, Chuanzhi Zhou, Yuk-Kit Hou, Peng-Shuai Wang

entry.summary: OctVideo represents video clips as octrees that recursively partition spatio-temporal volumes, keeping smooth regions coarse while allocating finer cells to detailed regions, with each leaf storing RGB values and gradients plus a learned residual. A Conv1D VAE reconstructs serialized cells into a regular latent grid, achieving 36.12 dB PSNR with modest compute and zero-shot generalization to higher resolutions.

entry.title: Preserving DEG Rankings for Gene Discovery in Histology-Based Spatial Gene Expression Prediction

author.name: Kaito Shiku, Kazuya Nishimura, Yasuhiro Kojima, Ryoma Bise

entry.summary: Formulates image-based differential expression ranking (IDER), asking whether histology-predicted spatial gene expression preserves the contrast-specific ranked gene lists needed for differentially expressed gene discovery, rather than per-gene reconstruction accuracy. It shows the standard training objective is misaligned with the key downstream ST use case. This reframes evaluation for histology-to-expression models in a biologically meaningful way.

entry.title: SegBanana: Steering Unified Multimodal Models into Medical Segmenters

author.name: Xiaoye Liang, Ye Yan, Mingze Yin, Shikun Feng, Mai Xu, Haiguang Liu, Lai Jiang, Yiheng Zhu

entry.summary: The paper recasts medical image segmentation as structured visual generation and shows that frontier unified multimodal models such as Nano Banana already exhibit basic segmentation ability across clinical scenarios without task-specific post-training. It then proposes methods to steer these existing UMMs into stronger medical segmenters where annotations for adaptation are unavailable.

entry.title: ConCAD: Constraint-Aware Image-to-CAD Generation with Dual-Granularity Rewards

author.name: Chenxi Zhai, Xi Cheng, Hang Cheng, Zhicheng Guan, Mingyu Fan, Yanzhe Tang, Pingfa Feng, Long Zeng

entry.summary: ConCAD generates executable parametric CAD programs from images using GRPO with two reward granularities: a code-level constraint reward and an execution-level geometric reward, disambiguating structurally distinct but volumetrically similar shapes. It introduces a B-rep geometric constraint verifier to check both geometry and design intent recovery.

entry.title: CapField-OPD: Learning Continuous Capability Fields via Joint-Anchored Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Flow Models

author.name: Pengyang Ling, Yujie Zhou, Jiazi Bu, Yibin Wang, Xiaoxiao Ma, Yi Jin, Huaian Chen, Yuhang Zang

entry.summary: CapField-OPD is a multi-teacher on-policy distillation framework for flow-based generative models that integrates several reward-specialized experts into a continuous capability field via explicit capability coordinates, rather than routing each prompt to a single teacher by semantic category. This decouples capability invocation from prompt content and enables users to control capability strength at inference time.

entry.title: RefineDrive: Reliable Failure-Guided Learning for Vision-Language-Action Driving

author.name: Zhe Sun, Ziyi Luo, Yehao Lu, Lei Zhou, Xi Li

entry.summary: RefineDrive is a post-training framework for vision-language-action driving models that learns from self-generated failures using simulator-derived structured feedback on collisions and drivable-area violations, plus safety-aware reinforcement learning. It retrieves minimal human-trajection corrections from a clustered trajectory bank satisfying hard-safety constraints. Turning model-specific failures into a training signal addresses a real gap since expert demonstrations dominate current VLA driving training.

entry.title: Many Eyes, One World: Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction from Mixed Cameras

author.name: Qiaoge Li, Yifan Zhan, Haijun Yang, Haiyang Liu, Yiyi Cai, Chenchi Luo

entry.summary: MEOW is a feed-forward system that jointly reconstructs metric pointmaps and camera poses from an N-view tuple mixing perspective, fisheye, and full-panorama images in a single pass, from images alone — no calibration, distortion parameters, or camera-type hints. This is the first single-pass method handling mixed-camera tuples with full panoramas.

entry.title: DeltaWAM: Change-Centric Visual Foresight via Delta Tokens for an Efficient World-Action Model

author.name: Tianyun Jiang, Wenrui Bao, Bingxin Xu, Yu Tian, Yuzhang Shang

entry.summary: DeltaWAM restructures world-action models for robotic manipulation so that prediction operates on compact delta tokens, single vectors encoding changes between consecutive dense DINO feature maps, rather than reconstructing full future frames. Built on DeltaWorld, a pretrained latent world model, it autoregressively predicts one delta token per future frame and connects to a flow-matching action expert. This targets the high computational cost and spatio-temporal redundancy of pixel-space world models.

entry.title: Humanoid Badminton: Learning Dynamic Racket Skills from Limited Human Motion Data

author.name: Jingzhi Cui, Zhexiong Wang, Bangjie Xu, Pengyu Zhao, Youyuan Li, Zhi Su, Peng Ren, Mengdi Xu, Chao Yu, Yi Wu, Luyang Wang, Zhongyu Li

entry.summary: The paper presents a three-stage hierarchical framework for humanoid badminton, learning time-critical racket skills from limited and imperfect human motion references. It combines motion priors with task-driven optimization to achieve precise striking and whole-body coordination across a broad 3D striking workspace under fast-changing shuttle trajectories.

entry.title: Is Online Interaction Necessary for Recovery? A Minimalist Approach to Robust Planning via Perturbation

author.name: Bumgeun Park, Donghwan Lee

entry.summary: Proposes PARS, a training approach improving recovery from covariate shift in behavior cloning by perturbing the robot's proprioceptive state and anchoring recovery supervision using only existing demonstrations, requiring no additional online interaction or expert access.

entry.title: Where Memory Belongs: Ledger, an Object Ledger for Memory-Augmented VLAs

author.name: Tanguy Dieudonn\'e, Jack B. Jedlicki, Heng Yang

entry.summary: This work argues that memory for long-horizon, partially observed manipulation should be split by type: short-term perceptual memory belongs inside the policy, while long-term object memory (persistent spatial state, containment, event history) belongs outside as an explicit readable record. The authors present Ledger, a harness realizing this split for vision-language-action models, motivated by benchmarks showing no single in-policy memory mechanism covers all spatio-temporal dimensions. This architectural insight could reshape how memory is added to VLA systems.

entry.title: Self-Evolving Coding Agents: From Digital Programs to Physical-World Intelligence

author.name: Hongcheng Gao, Jingjing Zhou, Zelin Zheng, Shijia Ge, Jay Zhu, Yazhe Wang, Jianshu Zeng, Xuan Shangguan, Di Wu, Lingyu He, Zhiqi Jia, Sihang Wu, Xiao He

entry.summary: This position/framework paper argues that direct observation-to-action mapping in VLA and world-action models ties policies to training layouts and hinders generalization because task state and recovery are implicitly encoded in action sequences. It proposes transferring the coding-agent working pattern of explicit state, tool calls, verification, and revisable executable code from digital agents to physical-world intelligence, enabling self-evolving robot procedures. This articulates a direction for inspectable, generalizable robot control.

entry.title: Guided Uncertainty-Aware Robust Domain Transfer

author.name: Xin Xiong, Zijian Guo, Tianxi Cai

entry.summary: GUARD is a statistical framework for updating deployed clinical decision support models using limited labeled target data and multiple heterogeneous sources, while guarding against future distributional shift. It formulates robust multi-source transfer as a minimax optimization problem, addressing covariate shift, concept drift, and cross-institution heterogeneity where full retraining is infeasible.

entry.title: BioDyad: Synchronize Biomedical Discovery and Machine Learning Engineering

author.name: Xingbo Du, Fadli Aulawi Al Ghiffari, Leonard Song, Loka Li, Duzhen Zhang, Zixiao Wang, Xiuying Chen, Le Song

entry.summary: BioDyad couples biomedical evidence discovery with executable program search using two coordinated hierarchies within Monte Carlo graph search, so that new biomedical evidence guides candidate construction and execution outcomes feed back into discovery and reuse. It maintains memory linking biomedical plans to execution outcomes across candidates, with validation calibrated to the search budget. This targets a real coordination challenge in agentic biomedical ML.

entry.title: When Does a Skill Add Value? Task-Conditional Gain Prediction for Selective Skill Use

author.name: Anjie Xu, Zhiyu Zhang, Ruiqing Ding, Fengli Xu, Leye Wang

entry.summary: The paper finds that agent skills often provide no benefit or even hurt performance while adding token costs, and introduces SkillDelta, a framework predicting task-conditional skill gains from paired executions with and without the skill. A local predictor transfers historical gains to new tasks, with analysis linking support coverage and representation mismatch to prediction error and decision regret across five benchmarks and three agents.

entry.title: RLHarness: Co-evolving Procedural Skills with Reinforcement Learning for Long-horizon Multimodal Reasoning

author.name: Ziqiao Shang, Zian Xu, Ji-Chen Yan, Weiming Wu, Ziyi Jia, Jie Meng, Tao Huang, Shan Huang, Lan-Zhe Guo

entry.summary: RLHarness tackles the program cold-start problem in multimodal RL, where a policy must discover reusable reasoning procedures while learning to execute them. It co-evolves a Skill Bank together with the policy so that skills, their triggers, and execution protocols stay compatible as the policy improves. This improves long-horizon multimodal reasoning where terminal-only verifiers give no procedural guidance.

entry.title: MergeHEIR: Mitigating Multimodal Hallucinations as the Tax of Model Merging

author.name: Jinyu Li, Hao Fang, Zhiming Zhang, Jiawei Kong, Bin Chen, Shu-Tao Xia

entry.summary: The paper shows across 8 model-merging methods that every merged multimodal checkpoint exhibits a higher hallucination rate than the average of its constituent experts, a merging tax. MergeHEIR is a post-merge adaptation framework that reduces this hallucination increase while preserving expertise inherited from the initial experts, avoiding the tension where unconstrained hallucination-mitigation disrupts merged capabilities. This is a novel finding at the intersection of model merging and multimodal reliability.

entry.title: When Helpful Text Hurts: Option-Redirecting Bias in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Tam Le Thi Thanh, Hoang Tran Van, Hong-Hanh Nguyen-Le, Thanh Duc Ngo

entry.summary: Studies tri-modal visual question answering and shows that the most damaging auxiliary text is not the most factually wrong but text that agrees with the question, contradicts the image, and points to a specific distractor, systematically redirecting model predictions. The Textual Reliability Ladder provides a controlled diagnostic protocol to isolate different unreliability types in auxiliary text.

entry.title: Beyond Prompt or Skill? Attribution-Guided Optimization of Modular LLM Programs

author.name: Haoran Shou, Haoyue Liu, Yu Huo, Kun Zeng, Xiaoying Tang

entry.summary: Proposes SPARO, a framework that jointly optimizes task prompts, reusable skill blocks, and skill-use routing policies for modular LLM programs, using attribution to decide which component to update when failures occur. This unifies previously separate optimization approaches (monolithic prompt tuning vs. skill induction from traces) into one design space.

entry.title: CUE-Mem: Benchmarking Long-Term User Memory via Implicit Cues in Multimodal Conversations

author.name: Yulin Hu, Yanyan Zhao, Zimo Long, Xing Fu, Mengtong Ji, Weixiang Zhao, Yutai Hou, Qianchao Wang, Dandan Tu

entry.summary: Presents CUE-Mem, a text-image-audio benchmark with 2,674 questions evaluating long-term user memory from implicit multimodal cues such as recurring background objects and ambient sounds, covering explicit and implicit evidence settings across Entity Recall, Long Pattern, Personalized Recommendation, and Answer Refusal tasks. It fills a gap left by text-only and explicit-evidence memory benchmarks.

entry.title: MixBench-TS: A Multivariate Time Series Forecasting Benchmark Where Channel Mixing Pays Off

author.name: Ibram Abdelmalak, Mischa Putzke, Jungmin Choi, Tom Hanika, Vijaya Krishna Yalavarthi, Lars Schmidt-Thieme

entry.summary: Introduces MixBench-TS, a time-series forecasting benchmark built around measurable cross-channel coupling, testing candidate coupling measures (Granger causality, transfer entropy, lagged mutual information, and a new model-based CD gain) on synthetic data with planted ground truth. It then evaluates whether standard MTSF datasets actually exhibit such coupling. This addresses the criticism that channel-mixing models are evaluated on datasets whose cross-channel structure is rarely examined.

entry.title: Expected Reasoning-Step Return Unifies On-Policy Learning from Rewards and Teachers

author.name: Qiangqiang He, Jin Li

entry.summary: Introduces Expected Reasoning-Step Return (ERSR), which treats semantic reasoning steps as macro-actions and uses Monte Carlo rollouts of the student policy to estimate expected final task reward of student-generated versus teacher-proposed actions in a common return space. ERSR reveals an outcome-dependent asymmetry: student actions help more on successful trajectories, teacher replacements help more on failed ones. This unifies reward-based and teacher-based step-level learning.

entry.title: Mandela-Bench: Multimodal Models Remember Canonical Images Instead of Seeing Them

author.name: Yicheng Bao, Zhenkun Gao, Xiahui Guo, Mingqian Yang, Xueheng Li, Bangwei Liu, Mingang Chen, Lijun Li, Xuhong Wang, Xin Tan

entry.summary: Mandela-Bench tests whether multimodal models can detect edits to canonical images (e.g., historical photographs) using world knowledge rather than pixel-level artifacts, comprising 1,507 edits including 1,359 knowledge-only forgeries that contradict a verifiable fact and 148 anchor-free controls. Existing benchmarks rely on generator artifacts or caption inconsistencies, which this benchmark deliberately avoids. It probes a genuinely distinct detection capability relevant to misinformation and image-manipulation forensics.

entry.title: Relic: From Multi-Agent Collaboration to Persistent Organizational Capability

author.name: Hongyi Du, Tianyi Zhang, Weijia Zhang, Yi Yang, Haofei Yu, Kunlun Zhu, Tianxiang Dai, Shang Jiang, Zhelun Gao, Jiaxin Pei, Shang Zhu, Jiaxuan You

entry.summary: Relic converts recurring multi-agent collaboration failures into organization-owned, executable protocols: members reflect on work, propose rules, and govern adoption, with protocols binding triggers, responsibilities, evidence, and consequences to the runtime while remaining revisable. This addresses the question of how lessons persist when individual agents in a team change. It matters as an early take on organizational memory and governance for agent collectives.

entry.title: SeOPD: Self-Evolving LLMs via Online Policy Distillation from Self-Generated Chain-of-Thought

author.name: Xiaoshu Chen, Xiangyu Wong, Sihang Zhou, Ke Liang, Xinwang Liu

entry.summary: SeOPD extends online policy self-distillation so that LLMs can self-improve without external privileged information by exploiting multiple reasoning modes within a single model, such as deep-thinking versus fast modes. The model distills from self-generated chain-of-thought to achieve gains comparable to methods requiring manual annotations or external environments.

entry.title: CORTEX: A Verified Experience Layer for Generalist Agents

author.name: Garapati Keerthana, Manik Gupta

entry.summary: CORTEX is a framework connecting specialized agents through an external layer of verified experience, where each episode records task conditions, tool state, proof traces, and outcomes, and a meta-controller chooses between exact replay, checked adaptation, fresh synthesis, or escalation. This gives agents a principled way to decide when prior solutions remain valid under changed conditions.

entry.title: DISCERN: Can AI Agents Work Like Scientists and Guide Discovery?

author.name: Nan Huang, Mario Tapia-Pacheco, Kun Zhou, Yiming Huang, Kevin Jos\'e Barrientos D\'iaz, Tiffany Amariuta, Jingbo Shang

entry.summary: DISCERN is a controlled benchmark on real public datasets evaluating three levels of an automated research workflow: data integrity, analysis verification under confounds and tool traps, and hypothesis generation grounded in trustworthy evidence. Unlike benchmarks that score task completion in isolation, it tests whether reliable evidence supports valid and novel claims. This targets reliability rather than capability in AI-driven science.

entry.title: Just Let Linear States Forget the Distant Past: Prefix Caching via Suffix Replay for Hybrid LLMs

author.name: Yirui Liu, Ruoling Qi, Xuaner Wu, Yuxin Jin, Jian Chen, Penghang Liu, Yafei Huang, Jiawei Shao, Xuelong Li

entry.summary: SuffixReplay is the first prefix caching system enabling hybrid LLMs that interleave full-attention and linear-attention layers to reuse cached prefixes at every cache-supported page boundary without materializing recurrent-state checkpoints. The key insight exploits decay in modern linear-attention recurrence: letting linear states forget the distant past while replaying suffixes restores accurate attention for recent context. This directly reduces long-context inference cost.

entry.title: Trajectory Unlearning on LLM-based Agents

author.name: Yingdan Shi, Ren Wang

entry.summary: Introduces trajectory-level unlearning as a new problem: rather than removing factual knowledge, an agent should not reproduce undesired action trajectories in long-horizon tasks. The paper identifies fundamental challenges distinguishing this from knowledge unlearning, since the target is what the agent does rather than what it knows.

entry.title: Dual-Vocabulary Language Model for Cross-Tokenizer Distillation

author.name: Kedi Chen, Chen Lin, Yutao Sun, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: DVLM enables on-policy distillation between teacher and student models with different tokenizers by replacing the teacher's LM head with a student-vocabulary projection head, producing full-dimensional student logits. This avoids the distribution loss of prior span-matching or byte-conversion approaches.

entry.title: HyperMCTS: Hypergraph-Augmented MCTS for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

author.name: Tingsong Xiao, Nithish Balachandar Moudhgalya, Chandrayee Basu, Lichao Wang, Luyang Kong, Benjamin Z. Yao, Zhe Jiang, Jie Hao

entry.summary: HyperMCTS augments MCTS for LLM agents with a cross-trajectory hypergraph whose hyperedges group recurring canonical decisions and accumulate outcomes across paths, enabling reuse of trajectory feedback that standard prefix-specific MCTS statistics miss. It is training-free and targets the high cost of search in long-horizon tasks.

entry.title: Waggle: Learning One Anonymous Local Law for Self-Organizing LLM Swarms

author.name: Mingxi Zou, Wei Zhu, Zhuo Wang, Langzhang Liang, Zhiwen Tang, Yinghui Xu, Zenglin Xu

entry.summary: Waggle learns a single shared anonymous policy over bounded local views that jointly selects task actions, semantic communication, and commitment updates, letting LLM swarms self-organize without explicit roles, hierarchies, or global topology definitions. Coordination forms, persists, and reorganizes online as populations change.

entry.title: Efficient Reasoning via Constrained Optimization in Latent Space

author.name: Zhinan Hou, XingChen Li, Keyou You

entry.summary: The paper observes that efficient reasoning steps cluster in a concentrated latent-space region while verbose ones deviate, and uses a quadratic penalty in latent space to keep reasoning focused, mitigating overthinking without the underthinking induced by keyword suppression or forced length reduction. This offers a latent-space alternative for efficient reasoning in large reasoning models.

entry.title: ControlScope: Workflow Revision and Reliability in LLM Agents

author.name: Jingjie Ning, Xueqi Li, Yibo Kong, Dongting Li

entry.summary: ControlScope studies how much of an LLM agent's running workflow should be revised mid-execution, comparing continuing generated code, editing the next tool call's arguments, and replacing the unfinished workflow from the same execution state. Evaluations across filesystem tasks, ALFWorld, and AppWorld show different revision scopes win under different reviewer budgets and task types.

entry.title: OSPD: On-Policy Self-Distillation for Persona-Consistent Dialogue

author.name: Rui Xu, Yikai Zhang, Aili Chen, Zicheng Zhao, Xu Yinghui, Libo Wu

entry.summary: OSPD is an on-policy self-distillation framework for persona-consistent role-play where one model acts as both teacher and student under asymmetric information: the teacher sees a full character profile while the student sees only a brief summary and generates from its own policy. Exploiting bimodal teacher confidence, the method avoids off-policy distribution mismatch and ambiguous RL rewards.

entry.title: Nudgeability: Reasoning Models Follow Confidence Signals Without Tracking Their Own Competence

author.name: Rohit Saxena, Utkarsh Upadhyay

entry.summary: This paper shows via counterfactual interventions that reasoning models follow injected first-person confidence or doubt signals when deciding to answer directly versus call tools, without genuinely tracking their own competence. It isolates how presented confidence signals change downstream action in otherwise identical trajectories.

entry.title: Before the Token Commits: Trajectory-Level Benchmarking of Visual Hallucinations in Diffusion VLMs

author.name: Yadong Wang, Siping Yue, Yu Tian, Chuanxing Geng, Xiang Chen

entry.summary: Introduces DynaHall, a trajectory-level benchmark for visual hallucinations in multimodal diffusion language models, with annotation-backed binary propositions and controlled hard negatives. Its commitment-aware protocol records intermediate answer tendencies before tokens are revealed, enabling analysis of whether hallucinations stabilize early or emerge late in the unmasking process.

entry.title: ProofLoom: Proof-Obligation-Driven Theory Construction for Autoformalizing Research-Level Stochastic Optimization

author.name: Feiming Wang, Daibo Li, Kun Yuan

entry.summary: ProofLoom is a fully automated LLM-agent system that formalizes research-level stochastic optimization algorithms and theorems in Lean, driven by open proof obligations that guide construction of definitions, lemmas, and proof plans. It includes signature contracts and an independent Judge to reject unsupported assumptions and weakened conclusions. This targets the hard frontier of autoformalizing research mathematics rather than competition-level problems.

entry.title: What Drives Citations in Production Large Language Models? An Observational Multi-Method Study of Two Million AI Citations Across Ten Thousand Web Pages

author.name: Ben Moore, Liam Dunne

entry.summary: This observational study analyzes roughly 2 million LLM citations from four commercial engines (ChatGPT, Claude, Google AI, Gemini) over six months, joined to 10,000 crawled pages, testing sixty-plus features via a nine-method consensus framework including mixed-effects regression, double machine learning, and stability selection. Four robust findings survive all checks, beginning with prompt-content alignment (Jaccard overlap). It offers an unusually rigorous picture of what makes pages get cited by production LLMs.

entry.title: ASCT: Attentive Search over Counterfactual Trees for Credit Assignment in Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yang Li, Jinhan Yang, hai liu, Di Wan, Xiyu Chen, Zongsi Xu, Tuo Zhou, Sheng Zhong, Sergey Volkov, Ye Luo, Hao Sun

entry.summary: ASCT turns training-time multi-step search into local action credit by building auxiliary counterfactual trees at actor-visited states, evaluating alternative legal actions from recoverable prefixes, and supplying centered action values for PPO on actor-sampled trajectories. Instantiations with uniform, UCT, and cost-aware AgentUCT search all improved held-out performance on HotpotQA agentic RAG.

entry.title: Why Deterministic PRM Guidance Underperforms in Discrete Diffusion Reasoning

author.name: Yan Zhan, Shaobo Liu, Zhijun Gao

entry.summary: This paper shows that for discrete diffusion language models, process reward model (PRM) guidance loses to simpler baseline methods when all approaches are charged the same forward-pass budget: on Dream-v0-Instruct-7B with GSM8K, best-of-N PRM selection reaches about 65 percent versus about 75 percent for independent sampling with an outcome reward model reranker. The work explains why deterministic PRM guidance is a poor way to spend test-time compute for dLLMs. This matters because test-time compute allocation for diffusion LMs is an emerging area and negative results clarifying misleading intuitions are valuable.

entry.title: RareDx: Controlled Knowledge Integration and Graph-Grounded Policy Optimization for Rare-Disease Diagnosis

author.name: Bo Zhang, Yuchen Wang, Dongbai Li, Matthew Yu Heng Wong, Qingkai Zeng, Lijun Wang, Tien-Yin Wong, Peng Cui, Tianyu Liu

entry.summary: RareDx frames rare-disease diagnosis as a long-tail reasoning problem and combines a harness that normalizes heterogeneous records into a ranked-diagnosis task with knowledge-graph-grounded policy optimization, comparing direct inference, static retrieval, adaptive tools, and structured phenotype-gene-disease reasoning on a shared knowledge layer. Its training pipeline includes Top-10 post-training and a KG-based policy optimization method. It matters because rare diseases are a high-stakes setting where LLMs systematically favor common conditions and hallucinate invalid disease names.

entry.title: From Search to Research: Exploring Search Scaling in Autonomous Quantitative Factor Mining

author.name: Kangcheng Deng, Hui Cai, Jiacheng Lu, Chester Zhongshu Qian, Rui Sun, Beidi Luan, Jing Li, Daxin Jiang, Zuo Bai

entry.summary: This paper studies search scaling for autonomous LLM research agents: how increasing search budgets affects end-to-end research performance, using 50 quantitative factor-mining tasks grounded in financial research reports where agents run full hypothesis-to-evaluation research loops. It characterizes mechanisms and limits of scaling in autonomous research, an understudied regime compared to single-shot inference scaling. It matters because it extends inference-scaling science to genuinely open-ended research workflows.

entry.title: Reinforcing Agentic Creativity in Scientific Ideation with Night Science

author.name: Priyanka Kargupta, Silviu Cucerzan, Shweti Mahajan, Allen Herring, Jiawei Han, Ryen W. White, Sujay Kumar Jauhar

entry.summary: AI Night-Scientist is an agentic framework using reinforcement learning to teach LLMs when and how to depart from predictable, low-entropy reasoning during open-ended scientific ideation. Grounded in cognitive science, it models creativity along action, process, and outcome axes, distinguishing structured day science from serendipitous night science. It addresses the known problem that LLM outputs are homogeneous in creative tasks.

entry.title: Agentic Video Understanding: A Survey

author.name: Xinyu Deng, Siwen Luo, Daochang Liu

entry.summary: A survey of agentic video understanding systems that actively decide what information to inspect, retain, verify, and act upon, moving beyond fixed video-language inference. It formalizes an agent loop for video understanding and organizes the literature through a challenge-to-design taxonomy linking context bottlenecks to architectural designs. This consolidates a fast-moving research area and identifies open directions.

entry.title: SNIP++: Fine-Grained Symbolic-Numerical Alignment for Symbolic Regression

author.name: Benjamin L\'eger, Shubham Gupta, Samy Mammeri, Kazem Meidani, Cem Subakan, Christian Gagn\'e

entry.summary: SNIP++ identifies a granularity gap in multi-modal symbolic regression models: their shared embedding spaces are only globally aligned, so the model cannot predict how a local edit to an expression changes its numerical behavior. The paper proposes fine-grained symbolic-numerical alignment so that sub-expressions and their corresponding behavioral fragments are represented consistently. This could materially improve symbolic regression quality, which is central to AI-assisted scientific discovery.

entry.title: Empowering Hybrid Attention Models on NPUs

author.name: Yinyuan Zhang, Daliang Xu, Xiaolong Huang, Wangsong Yin, Yun Ma, Mengwei Xu, Gang Huang

entry.summary: HA-NPU is the first system enabling efficient hybrid-attention LLM inference on edge Neural Processing Units without algorithm changes, fixing severe memory-system inefficiencies and architectural mismatches in linear-attention layers that bottleneck prefill. It reorganizes dataflow and execution to exploit the memory and compute efficiency of hybrid attention models (e.g., of the kind used in the Qwen3.5 and Kimi series) on on-device NPUs. This makes strong on-device LLM deployment far more practical.

entry.title: AutoPDEBench: Benchmarking LLM Auto-Research for Neural PDE Solver Design

author.name: Ruoyan Li, Wei Wang, Yizhou Sun

entry.summary: AutoPDEBench is a benchmark that evaluates whether autonomous AI research agents can design specialized neural PDE solvers, targeting the bottleneck of manually iterating on architectures for domain-specific challenges like varying parameters and high-speed flows. It matters because automated research on scientific ML is a rapidly growing area and rigorous benchmarks for it are scarce.

entry.title: SkillDRE: Dual-Stage Red-Team Evolution of Agent Skills via Pre-Execution and Runtime Feedback

author.name: Pengyu Zhu, Jingyi Yang, Yi Liu, Li Sun, Sen Su

entry.summary: SkillDRE is a fully automated red-teaming framework that evolves complete malicious agent skill packages through a dual-stage feedback loop exploiting both pre-execution scanning and runtime defenses, autonomously constructing task-conditioned malicious objectives and verifiable judgments. It demonstrates how the same skill-improvement mechanisms that benefit benign agents can be weaponized by attackers to make malicious skills more effective and harder to detect. This is important attack-surface research for the emerging agent skills ecosystem.

entry.title: Activation Flow: Manufacturing Activations for Steering

author.name: Hong Kiat Tan, Linh Le, David Williams-King

entry.summary: ActFlow manufactures the activations needed for difference-in-means steering directly from k correct labels without fine-tuning, which matters when a sandbagging model withholds the desired behavior. It sets target logits ranking each labeled item's correct answer first and solves a family of ODEs to find a single vector added to all k residual streams at one layer. This connects interpretability-style steering with safety-relevant scenarios like detecting sandbagging.

entry.title: DraftAttention2: Fast Video Diffusion with Low-Resolution-Guided Mixed-Precision Attention

author.name: Rui Ding, Haopeng Li, Weize Ma, Yufa Zhou, Yitong Li, Xiaoling Zhou, Jiashuo Cao, Liyang Li, Hua Geng, Jiuxiang Gu, Jun Lin, Enze Xie, Xuan Shen

entry.summary: DraftAttention2 is a training-free method to accelerate video diffusion transformers by using a low-resolution draft attention map to both select attention blocks and assign numerical precision. Pooled queries and keys estimate block importance, with a shared ranking assigning higher precision to important blocks and skipping unimportant ones. This addresses the growing cost of spatiotemporal attention as video resolution and length increase.

entry.title: The Extender: A Log-Structured Transformer

author.name: Jakob Eriksson (UIC)

entry.summary: The Extender is a Transformer variant adding a concatenation channel alongside the residual stream: each layer emits a small extension appended to a growing x-channel, which becomes the sole input to kv projections across layers. This log-structured design reduces persistent attention memory, offering an alternative approach to long-context efficiency. It is a single-author architectural proposal with potentially broad implications for attention cost.

entry.title: ASCEND: Personal AI Agents for Autonomous Scientific Computing Across HPC Clusters and GPU Workstations

author.name: J. Paul Liu, Uthpala Herath, Andrew Petersen

entry.summary: ASCEND is an AI agent interface that lets researchers translate computational intent directly into environment configuration, job scheduling, and failure diagnosis on Slurm-managed HPC clusters and GPU workstations. It runs locally on the researcher's laptop with the language model hosted remotely and holding no credentials, using local tools to enforce site-specific execution policies. This lowers the operational barrier to large-scale scientific computing.

entry.title: DynamicDx: Evaluating Evidence Acquisition in Video-Based Diagnosis

author.name: Jiahui Li, Yutong Guo, Nan Yang, Wenzhan Song, Jin Lu, Fei Dou

entry.summary: DynamicDx is a benchmark evaluating vision-language models on video-based diagnosis across 71 neurological consultations and 11 sign categories, testing whether models can convert observations into hypotheses, questions, and tests rather than merely recognize signs. Across five models, video improves accuracy by 9.9-22.5 points over blind input, but the gain is not explained by recognition or temporal order. This diagnostic-process-level evaluation is more demanding than static recognition benchmarks.

entry.title: TCMQA: A 38K-Question Traditional Chinese Medicine Benchmark with a Licensed-Practitioner Reference

author.name: Tzu-Heng Huang, Jet Lin, Eric Lin

entry.summary: TCMQA is an open benchmark of 38,279 Traditional Chinese Medicine licensing exam questions paired with 15,151 responses from 101 licensed practitioners, evaluating 29 instruction-tuned models across 9 families. Accuracy spans over 59 points with no model near saturation, and pretraining data predicts TCM ability far better than scale. This fills a major gap in non-Western medical evaluation of LLMs.

entry.title: Improving the Diversity of LLM Outputs without a Trade-off

author.name: Ryoma Sato

entry.summary: DAST increases LLM output diversity without changing the marginal distribution and with negligible generation-time overhead by reassigning token IDs so that semantically similar tokens appear consecutively, then combining that order with arithmetic sampling or quasi-Monte Carlo methods so similar tokens are less likely to co-occur across runs. The reordering costs a few hundred seconds once per model and is reused thereafter. This addresses a long-standing diversity-quality trade-off in sampling.

entry.title: Which Self-Improvements Should We Trust? Reliable Self-Improvement When Agents Reuse Their Benchmarks

author.name: Xiaojing Sun, Yuhan Zeng, Zihua She, Xiao Wang

entry.summary: Analyzes how recursive self-improvement overfits when finite benchmark resources are repeatedly reused, since candidate modifications are proposed based on feedback from the same evaluation set, causing adaptive overfitting that existing multiple-comparison corrections do not handle. Develops methods to distinguish genuine population improvement from empirically inflated gains in RSI search trajectories.

entry.title: Scope-WM: Scoped Computation for Efficient Visual World Models

author.name: Chunzheng Li, Zesheng Jia, Hongda Zhang, Jiaying Tang, Yuntian Wang, Siao Liu, Jin Wang

entry.summary: Scope-WM accelerates visual world models for robotic planning by concentrating computation on prediction-relevant latent regions and promising action sequences, distilling relevance into lightweight modules rather than heavy auxiliary components. This reduces inference latency and memory, enabling real-time deployment on constrained hardware. It addresses a key barrier to practical world-model-based robot control.

entry.title: Recursive Harness Distillation across Agents for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Seungyeon Kim, Junhoo Lee, Minkyu Kim, Baekseung Kim, Nojun Kwak

entry.summary: Recursive Harness Distillation lets a strong agent distill its intervention experience into a reusable 'playbook' for a lighter agent, then recursively refines the playbook using the light agent's execution feedback — all without parameter updates. This enables VLA-based manipulation systems to reuse accumulated failure-diagnosis and intervention knowledge across new task instances. It offers a parameter-free path to cumulative robot learning.

entry.title: Beyond Timestamps: Decision-Aligned On-Policy Distillation for Long-Horizon Agents

author.name: Mingju Chen, Can Lv, Jinrong Liu, Huan Zhang, Heng Chang, Shiji Zhou

entry.summary: The paper identifies a Decision-Timestamp Mismatch in on-policy self-distillation for long-horizon agents: privileged guidance is often misaligned in both context and temporal scope with the student's actual decisions, which can span multiple timesteps. AlignOPSD aligns supervision with functional decisions rather than timestamps, complementing sparse RLVR rewards with denser, better-placed feedback. This improves dense-feedback training for agents.

entry.title: HESP: Separating What to Probe from When to Stop in Local LLM Alert-Triage Agents

author.name: Zhuowen Liu, Zhixuan Wang

entry.summary: HESP is a controller for small open-weight LLM agents in security operations centers that externalizes the investigation procedure from the model, maintaining a ledger of competing explanations and selecting read-only probes by expected information gain per cost. It forces evidence-backed verdicts and can end investigations itself, addressing failures of small local models that probe without converging or dismiss real attacks.

entry.title: MA-JEPA: Joint-Embedding World Models for Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Brandon Gary Kaplowitz, Osaze James Obahor, Christian Schroeder de Witt

entry.summary: MA-JEPA is a stochastic world model for multi-agent RL that replaces observation reconstruction with prediction of target representations, using a categorical latent state and causal Transformer trained with posterior and action-conditioned dynamics objectives. It enables model-based multi-agent RL with centralized training and decentralized execution.

entry.title: BOReFT: Manifold Steering of Language Models for Black-box Optimization

author.name: Dhruv Agarwal, Rico Angell, Kavitha Srinivas, Tahira Naseem, Horst Samulowitz, Willie Neiswanger, Andrew McCallum

entry.summary: BOReFT learns a compact low-dimensional space of hidden-state interventions in a frozen language model and uses that space as the search domain for Bayesian optimization with an external scoring function. This gives principled control over exploration of the model's proposal space for black-box search tasks like program optimization and molecular design. It bridges activation steering with continuous optimization.

entry.title: JIVE: Jacobian-Informed Volume Expansion for Diverse Generative Sampling

author.name: Guangxun Zhang, Brian Cai, Boxuan Zhang, Chao Chen, Ruixiang Tang

entry.summary: JIVE is a training-free framework that combats mode collapse and improves sample diversity by injecting velocity perturbations aligned with the leading right singular subspace of the generator's endpoint Jacobian. It provably maximizes endpoint diversity while preserving quality, and computes directions efficiently via matrix-free numerical linear algebra. The work offers a principled geometric alternative to heuristic batch-repulsion methods.

entry.title: When Known Physics Helps Neural PDE Models: Residual Constraints Out-Regularize Generic Priors for Nonlinear Dynamics

author.name: Zahra Farazpay, Aniruddha Bora

entry.summary: This paper evaluates structural priors in neural PDE surrogates under a common protocol against a matched baseline, finding that known-equation residual constraints consistently outperform the best generic regularizer at equal tuning budget. A capacity sweep reveals the advantage persists and grows for nonlinear PDEs (Burgers, KdV, Allen-Cahn) but collapses toward parity for linear dynamics. This clarifies when physics information has durable value versus when generic regularization suffices.

entry.title: UOPD: Uncertainty-Aware Intervention for On-Policy Distillation of Multi-Turn Agents

author.name: Wenbo Zhang, Pengcheng Xu, Weizhi Du, Jing Zhang, Hengrui Cai

entry.summary: UOPD improves on-policy distillation for multi-turn agents by using low teacher confidence on student actions to select high-uncertainty steps for corrective intervention, while applying standard OPD losses at low-uncertainty turns. A controlled ALFWorld study shows that a single teacher correction at a low-confidence step improves subsequent behavior and task success. This targets the problem that early mistakes can derail entire multi-turn rollouts.

entry.title: The Devil is in the Spectrum Bias: Spectrum-Balanced Feature Matching for Robust Representation Distillation

author.name: Kuniaki Saito, Yoshitaka Ushiku

entry.summary: The paper shows that L2-based feature matching distillation is biased toward reconstructing dominant spectral directions of teacher representations while under-optimizing low-variance directions that often carry task-relevant information. SpecMatch adaptively emphasizes these under-optimized directions to improve label-free distillation from large visual foundation models to smaller students. A clean analysis-plus-fix contribution to efficient deployment of foundation models.

entry.title: WAM-OPD: Sharpening World Action Models via On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Panjun Liu, Xiaohan Lei, Shiqi Zhang, Yikun Wang, Yongxin Zhang, Mingyi Hu, Shida Sun, Jiateng Shou, Wengang Zhou, Jiajun Deng, Zhiwei Xiong

entry.summary: WAM-OPD applies on-policy distillation to pretrained world action models for robotic manipulation, transferring task-specific teacher knowledge under the student's own induced distribution while addressing the costly repeated environment rollouts that closed-loop on-policy training requires. The goal is expert-level target-task performance without degrading pretrained generalist skills. Advances the practical post-training of generalist robot policies.

entry.title: When World Models Lie: Adaptive Safety Analysis Under Wrong Imaginations

author.name: John Cao, Somil Bansal

entry.summary: This work studies how latent-space safety filters built on world models fail when the model's predictions are confidently wrong, since Hamilton-Jacobi value functions inherit model errors and become overconfident. The authors propose an adaptive safety analysis method that improves on ensemble disagreement and consistency residual signals, which can stay small even under wrong predictions. It matters for deploying learned world models in safety-critical robotics.

entry.title: ABC-Align: Prediction-Powered Alignment with Adaptive Bias Control

author.name: Eric Frankel, Banghua Zhu, Sewoong Oh, Lillian J. Ratliff

entry.summary: ABC-Align addresses bias in RLAIF-style alignment that uses pseudo labels instead of expensive human preference data. It leverages abundant pseudo-label signal to minimize variance while applying a lightweight, automatically tuned adaptive bias correction grounded in a small human-labeled subset. This improves the cost-quality tradeoff in language model post-training.

entry.title: Nereus: Adaptive Parallelism for LLM Post-Training

author.name: Songlin Jiang, Tuo Shi, Sitong Zhang, Zeke Wang, Mario Di Francesco, Bo Zhao

entry.summary: Nereus is a cost-aware runtime that adapts RL post-training jobs for LLMs into efficient execution plans as resource availability, sequence lengths, memory pressure, and stage bottlenecks change during a run. It handles plan transition costs, distributed state reuse, and GPU transfer coordination across models sharing GPUs. This addresses real systems challenges in scaling RLHF-style post-training on clusters.

entry.title: Just MLPs: Efficient Visual State Reconstruction for Multimodal Language Models

author.name: Jingdi lei, Junxian Li, Di Zhang, Zhanqiu Zhang, Yiwen Guo, Soujanya Poria

entry.summary: Shows that in multimodal LLMs the influence of long visual token sequences is concentrated in a low-dimensional subspace: after blocking visual-to-text attention, restoring only a few directions via low-rank interventions recovers most lost accuracy. This enables preserving all visual tokens while reducing Transformer compute through efficient MLP-based state reconstruction.

entry.title: Spatial Grafting: Grounding 3D Features for Flow-Matching Robot Policies

author.name: Dingsheng Liu, Yangzheng Wu, Mahboubeh Asadi, Zhiyuan Li, Jinbang Huang, Yixin Xiao, Tongtong Cao, Yingxue Zhang

entry.summary: Spatial Grafting is a lightweight module that binds frozen 3D reconstruction features to metric, robot-relative geometry and injects them into flow-matching action experts via cross-attention without modifying pretrained weights. It addresses the gap between reconstruction features that describe local shape and policies that need spatial grounding.

entry.title: AwarenessBench: Assessing Cognitive Capabilities of Language Models

author.name: Xiaojian Li, Rongwu Xu, Tianyun Zhang, Yue Wang, Shuo Chen, Qiner Lyu, Briana Zhang, Peiran Yang, Kyle Xue Chen, Haoyuan Shi, Yu Wang, Wei Xu

entry.summary: AwarenessBench is the first comprehensive benchmark for LLM cognitive abilities across metacognition, self-awareness, social awareness, and situational awareness, with 15 functions and 14,381 samples. Evaluating 18 frontier and open models shows all beat random baselines and the best exceeds human averages overall, but most models lag humans markedly in metacognition and self-awareness.

entry.title: FactorEngram: Factorized N-gram Memory with Basis-Level Gating for Language Models

author.name: Bowen Yang, Jingbo Zhou, Qinghong Miao, Hua Wu

entry.summary: Proposes FactorEngram, an improvement on lookup-based n-gram memory for LLMs that factorizes retrieved embeddings and applies basis-level contextual gating instead of treating each memory embedding as a monolithic unit with a single scalar gate. This allows polysemous token patterns to selectively read context-relevant memory components and enables semantic parameter sharing beyond hash collisions.

entry.title: X-Reset: Scaling Object-Centric Reinforcement Learning via Cross-Embodiment Resets

author.name: Prithwish Dan, Chenyang Ma, Wei Zhan

entry.summary: Proposes X-Reset, which resolves the exploration problem in dexterous manipulation RL by using human hand-object demonstrations to kinematically retarget and reset the environment into useful states, rather than imitating human motion or relying on reward shaping. This enables training generalist policies with task-agnostic rewards across diverse objects.

entry.title: When Keywords Drop but Classifiers Hold: Soft Refusals under KV Cache Compression

author.name: Kang Chen, Xiuze Zhou, Hong Chen, Yuanguo Lin

entry.summary: Investigates whether KV cache compression preserves agreement between lightweight keyword refusal monitors and stronger refusal classifiers in LLM serving, using a paired protocol on 200 harmful prompts with long filler contexts. Findings show keyword heuristics can drop refusal signals under compression (soft refusals) while learned classifiers remain more consistent, revealing a monitoring risk in deployed systems.

entry.title: SAMBAR: Selective Anchoring via Method of Multipliers for Balanced Knowledge Acquisition and Retention in Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Aayushi Shrivastava, Xunlan Zhou, Hongrui Zhao, Ziyu Chen, Negar Mehr

entry.summary: SAMBAR is a continual learning algorithm for vision-language-action (VLA) robot policies that prevents catastrophic forgetting during finetuning on new tasks without replaying old demonstrations. It uses selective anchoring via a method-of-multipliers formulation to balance acquiring new skills against retaining generalist capabilities. This is practically important since old task demonstrations are often unavailable in deployment.

entry.title: When Can Old Evaluations Certify a New Model? Label-Efficient Release Decisions under Evaluator Drift

author.name: Joyanta Jyoti Mondal, Mridul Banik, Md. Shifatul Ahsan Apurba, Md Masud Al Mahmud

entry.summary: The paper formalizes when historical errors from a cheap evaluator (such as an LLM judge) can substitute for fresh trusted labels when certifying that a new model's population risk stays below a release threshold. It shows that if evaluator errors can drift invisibly, every valid certifier must keep buying labels at a characterized rate, while bounded drift enables label-free certification at explicit error cost; a portfolio-vigilance betting-based sequential certifier handles the untrusted-but-informative middle ground. This gives a rigorous decision theory for model release audits.

entry.title: A Comparative Analysis of Attention versus State-Space Models for In-Context Learning

author.name: Enes Arda, Semih Cayci, Atilla Eryilmaz

entry.summary: The paper develops belief geometry, a unified analytical framework comparing attention and state-space models via cumulative Bayes regret on in-context linear regression. It abstracts three capabilities (evidence assembly, belief maintenance, addressing) and studies three cases isolating these to determine what each architecture can represent. This moves the attention-vs-SSM comparison from purely empirical to theoretical ground.

entry.title: Scaling Properties of Same-Family On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Yuntai Bao, Qinfeng Li, Guoqing Jiang, Liwei Chen, Zhiheng Qin, Xuanping Li, Wenqi Zhang, Xuhong Zhang

entry.summary: The paper systematically studies on-policy distillation across weak-to-strong, same-base, and strong-to-weak teacher-student setups, finding early training dynamics exhibit a useful-transfer regime where held-out gold score rises approximately linearly in the square root of token-level reverse KL divergence from the student initialization. It quantifies how RL-induced reasoning capability transfers across model scales.

entry.title: Change the Product, Keep the Parameters: Associative Algebra Layers for Transformers

author.name: Ilya Koziev, Ivan Oseledets

entry.summary: Instead of searching for faster matrix multiplication algorithms, the authors replace a Transformer's learned projections with a sparser interaction product from an associative-algebra construction over the same weight blocks, achieving quadratic arithmetic in matrix dimension for fixed block size. The construction is provably rank-optimal via the Alder-Strassen bound and supports causal masking and KV-cached decoding, with empirical results provided.

entry.title: Saturation-Insensitive Dueling Bandits with General Function Approximation

author.name: Chenggong Zhang, Xuheng Li, Qiwei Di, Weitong Zhang, Quanquan Gu

entry.summary: The paper addresses preference-model saturation in contextual dueling bandits, where confident reward models yield weakly informative feedback and sample complexity blows up via the inverse-derivative factor. It introduces SI-CDB, which selects opponent arms carefully to avoid saturation, achieving guarantees under general function approximation. This removes a fundamental obstacle in preference-based online learning.

entry.title: CFLoRA: Federated Fine-tuning of LLMs with Complementary Factors for Error-free Aggregation

author.name: Yanan Ma, Qiyuan Chen, Zihan Fang, Xianhao Chen, Yuguang Fang

entry.summary: CFLoRA solves the structural mismatch in federated LoRA averaging, where averaging LoRA factors separately does not equal averaging their products. It partitions latent LoRA channels into two complementary sets each round so columns and rows are updated simultaneously without aggregation errors or increased communication ranks, unlike prior freezing or alternating approaches.

entry.title: Perturb-and-Solve: Efficient Learned-Operator Conditioning for Latent Diffusion Inverse Problems

author.name: Abduragim Shtanchaev, Arip Asadulaev, Luiza Labazanova, Aidar Alimbayev, Karim Salta, Eric Moulines

entry.summary: PASEO uses a small (1M parameter) learned network to degrade diffusion model predictions in latent space, enabling support for arbitrary learned degradation operators in inverse problems like deblurring and inpainting without backpropagating through the diffusion network. This breaks the trade-off between fixed-operator speed and general-but-slow gradient-based conditioning.

entry.title: AG-CoT: Verified Algorithmic Traces for LLM Program Synthesis on Clifford Circuits

author.name: Lu Wei, Yufeng Wang, Chenfeng Cao, Lu Pang, Haibin Ling

entry.summary: The paper targets language-model synthesis of Clifford circuits, where exact classical verification is possible, using Aaronson-Gottesman chain-of-thought traces checked by an exact verifier and continued training on verifier-accepted model generations. Across two model families (3B and 7B), verified AG-CoT supervision multiplies greedy-decode state-equivalence accuracy.

entry.title: The Price of Locality: Why Forward-Forward Underperforms Backpropagation?

author.name: Zhaoxian Wu, Haichuan Liu, Tianyi Chen

entry.summary: The paper diagnoses two structural failure modes of the Forward-Forward algorithm versus backpropagation: an optimization floor from concurrent local updates inducing inter-layer representation-distribution drift, and a geometric collapse of layer representations driven by the local contrastive mechanism. It proves per-layer PL inequality satisfaction while explaining the persistent depth-worsening gap.

entry.title: Towards Identifiable Representations under Misspecified Structure

author.name: Yuke Li, Yujia Zheng, Ziyi Chen, Kun Zhang, Heng Huang

entry.summary: The paper extends latent variable identifiability theory to misspecified structure, where conditional independence of observations given latents fails, treating misspecification as a perturbed factor analysis problem. It establishes subspace and component-wise identifiability under spectral separation, structural sparsity, and controlled perturbation, plus approximate guarantees when precise conditions fail.

entry.title: MoGround: Measuring and Mitigating Modality Distraction in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Luca Zhou, Bo Zhao, Rose Yu, Emanuele Rodol\`a, Roberto Dess\`i

entry.summary: MoGround is a vision-language dataset across four domains where every question is answerable from exactly one modality, enabling clean measurement of modality distraction (correct single-modality answers flipping wrong when irrelevant cross-modal content is added). Across seven open-source VLMs, distraction is model-dependent, tracks the weaker-grounded modality (r = +0.86), and scales inversely with grounding quality.

entry.title: Geometric Identification in Predict-Then-Optimize Learning

author.name: Jiaxiao Xu, Changhong Mou, Keji Liu, Dinghua Xu, Yeyu Zhang

entry.summary: This paper provides theoretical characterization of when decision-focused learning surrogates, specifically the convex SPO+ population risk, uniquely identify the underlying optimal decisions without recovering the quotient report itself. The authors derive conditions under central symmetry under which the centered mean class is the unique Bayes minimizer, separating face-crossing behavior from selected-oracle disagreement, and extend identification results to non-symmetric and conditional settings. This deepens the foundations of predict-then-optimize learning, an area relevant to decision-making under prediction uncertainty.

entry.title: Hamiltonian JEPA: Action-Conditioned World Models with an Inherited Control State

author.name: Tamim Zoabi, Ameen Ali, Lior Wolf

entry.summary: H-JEPA separates perception from control in action-conditioned JEPAs: a wide perceptual code is regularized with a Bures-Wasserstein prior, and a fixed orthonormal slice serves as a control state evolving under phase-conditioned dissipative port-Hamiltonian dynamics. This organizes the planner-scored state by how actions move the system, improving planning from pixels.

entry.title: Approximating Softmax in Pretrained LLMs: Model Sensitivity and Kernel Acceleration

author.name: Shangzhen Zhu, Muyan Hu, Tomasz Kozlowski

entry.summary: This study characterizes how accurately pretrained LLMs actually need softmax evaluated, testing ten frozen decoder-only models from 0.5B to 72B on NVIDIA Blackwell B200 hardware where exponential throughput lags tensor cores by two orders of magnitude. It finds that the number of positions assigned probability and within-row resolution can be cut substantially, with placement near the row maximum mattering as much as budget size.

entry.title: Rethinking Contextualization by Reinterpreting Attention Head Channels

author.name: Hakaze Cho, Haolin Yang, Zhun Sun, Naoya Inoue, Benjamin Heinzerling, Kentaro Inui

entry.summary: Proposes a global principle for how transformer contextualization works: words carry different amounts of information, and less-informative words absorb more contextual information, with channel-level selectivity enabling precise routing between matched words. The work reinterprets attention head channels to characterize contextualization behavior beyond per-head dictionary views.

entry.title: MISHAP-Bench: A Hallucination Benchmark for Large Audio-Language Models

author.name: Zhi Wen Soi, Giulio Segalini, Jian-Jia Chen, Lydia Chen

entry.summary: Introduces MISHAP-Bench, a 12,000-question benchmark with open-ended audio-question pairs that distinguishes context hallucinations (claims not grounded in the audio) from knowledge hallucinations (claims lacking external factual support), with a rigorous evaluation pipeline for open-ended responses. This disentangles hallucination from simple audio-understanding failures in large audio-language models.

entry.title: Vision--Language Signals in Constrained RL: Safety Gains Without Anticipation

author.name: Samuel Tetteh, Cody Fleming

entry.summary: VLM-Safe-RL integrates frozen CLIP signals into PPO-Lagrangian via reward shaping and an augmented multiplier update for safe reinforcement learning in driving. Notably, the paper's analysis questions whether VLM scores actually anticipate collisions, finding safety gains arise without genuine hazard anticipation, and it addresses the failure mode where episodic costs favor policies making little task progress.

entry.title: Transfer Calibrated Prediction Powered Inference

author.name: Aditya T. Vadlamani, Jae Ho Chang, Srinivasan Parthasarathy, Subhadeep Paul

entry.summary: TC-PPI extends prediction-powered inference to settings where the AI predictor was trained on a different source domain, adapting it to the target via cross-fitting with gold-standard samples using methods like linear calibration, LoRA, or fine-tuning. The proposed Joint-TC-Cross-PPI++ preserves unbiasedness while remaining at least as efficient as classical baselines.

entry.title: X-MoD: Practical Scaling Laws for Sparse-Depth Routing Beyond Mixture-of-Depths

author.name: Bowen Dong, Yilong Fan, Tengyu Pan, Yike Zhang, Zhenyu Li, Zijian Zhang, Xuewei Li, Mei Yu, Jianyong Wang

entry.summary: X-MoD extends Mixture-of-Depths by decoupling token sparsity from anchor stride so total parameter count can grow while active-equivalent capacity stays fixed, combining dense anchors, variance-scaled gating, and depth-wise token balancing to make deep sparse routing trainable. It also formulates sparse-depth routing as a conditional architecture-design problem and derives practical scaling laws.

entry.title: Epistemic Learning from Imprecise Annotation

author.name: Kaizheng Wang, Siu Lun Chau

entry.summary: This paper proposes learning from credal supervision, where convex sets of plausible labelling distributions (credal sets) are used as training supervision and the model learns sets of predictive distributions rather than collapsing ambiguity into one. It instantiates this with a pessimistic-optimistic credal classifier combining two heads trained on worst- and best-case losses, whose output spread provides calibrated epistemic uncertainty.

entry.title: ZonoGPT: Towards An Abstract Domain for Verifying Large GPT Models

author.name: Hai Duong, Thanh Le, ThanhVu Nguyen

entry.summary: ZonoGPT introduces an abstract domain for formal verification of large Transformer models whose space complexity is independent of network depth, using structured zonotopes and generator reduction to preserve correlations, plus block-wise precision techniques. This extends neural network verification beyond the small or restricted Transformers that prior work has been limited to.

entry.title: Brain-Conditioned Action Policies for Neural Motor Decoding

author.name: Luyao Jin, Running Zhao, Huan Zhao, Vincent C. K. Cheung, Wei-Hsin Liao

entry.summary: BrainVLA adapts a pretrained vision-language-action model (OpenVLA-OFT) to motor brain-computer interfaces via language-mediated alignment, constructing datasets pairing neural activity, actions, language instructions, and rendered visual observations. This mitigates the scarcity of paired neural-action data for paralyzed users controlling devices.

entry.title: AgentPerfBench: A Benchmarking and Evaluation Suite for Inference Performance of Agentic LLMs

author.name: Cheuk Hang Lau, Zeyu Cao, Kevin Wong Cheuk Yin, Yao Lai, Haoran Wu, Nicholas D. Lane, Robert D. Mullins, Ilia Shumailov, Yiren Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces AgentPerfBench, a benchmark suite for LLM serving performance in the agentic era, using real traces from SWE-Bench and TerminalBench alongside chat baselines to capture multi-turn requests with growing context lengths. It exposes the mismatch between existing single-turn chatbot workload benchmarks and modern agentic serving demands.

entry.title: When Sparse Reward Meets Dense Distillation: Training Dynamics of On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Xinke Jiang, Tao Feng, Zhibang Yang, Zhixin Zhang, Weixuan Xu, Haoyu Zhang, Xu Chu

entry.summary: Studies the interaction between sparse verifiable-reward RL and dense token-level teacher KL distillation in LLM post-training, using neural tangent kernel analysis to explain why joint training can destabilize. The work identifies dynamics of hybrid reward-distillation training and presumably proposes stabilization. It is timely given the growing use of on-policy distillation to complement RLVR.

entry.title: GraphHCA: Closed-Form Hindsight Credit Assignment for Long-Horizon LLM Agents

author.name: Haodong Zhu, Yangyang Ren, Changbai Li, Sheng Xu, Linlin Yang, haiguang liu, Baochang Zhang

entry.summary: GraphHCA provides a model-free realization of hindsight credit assignment for LLM agent training, eliminating the need for explicit hindsight-distribution estimation via auxiliary models or extra passes. It attributes credit through ratios of hindsight to behavior-policy probabilities in a closed form, targeting sparse terminal-reward agentic tasks.

entry.title: $\lambda$-JEPA Spectral Anti-Collapse Regularization for Self-Supervised Learning

author.name: Berker Demirel, Cl\'ementine Domin\'e, Valentino Maiorca, Marco Fumero, Marco Mondelli, Francesco Locatello

entry.summary: Identifies that joint-embedding self-supervised learning can suffer dimensional collapse in the backbone even when the projection head prevents it, limiting downstream transfer. The paper introduces SACReg, a spectral anti-collapse regularizer grounded in an analysis of lambda-balance of weight matrix scales, with theory in two-layer linear networks. This addresses a known failure mode of SSL methods with a principled fix.

entry.title: Persistent Partners Raise Prices Among Learning Agents

author.name: Paul-Peter Arslan, Yubin Kim, Xiao Xiao

entry.summary: A pre-registered randomized experiment on algorithmic collusion in the Bertrand duopoly setting of Calvano et al., testing how platform matching policy affects learned pricing. Keeping the same partner raises average profits by 0.27 of the competitive-to-monopoly gap, with tight confidence intervals across all twenty paired runs, while randomizing partner persistence, price visibility, and messaging. Directly relevant to economics and AI policy on algorithmic collusion.

entry.title: Deep Epistemic Value Functions for Optimistic Exploration

author.name: Leander Diaz-Bone, Marco Bagatella, Jonas H\"ubotter, Andreas Krause

entry.summary: This systematic study examines how epistemic uncertainty over value functions is represented, propagated, and optimized in deep RL, identifying distinct failure modes on each axis.
