entry.title: CRISP: Cultural Reward Modeling for Implicit Situated Propriety

author.name: Zekun Yuan, Yangfan Ye, Baohang Li, Shuaibo Zhao, Zekun Zhou, Ziming Li, Qichen Hong, Kun Chen, Xiaocheng Feng

entry.summary: CRISP-RM is a culturally situated reward model assigning rewards based on cultural appropriateness in open-ended social scenarios, addressing the underexplored space of open-ended culturally situated behavior beyond predefined response spaces. During policy optimization it adds Norm Grounding Supervision to enhance policy sensitivity to relevant cultural norms. The work supports LLMs deployed across diverse regions responding appropriately to local norms.

entry.title: OpenWhistle: A Large-Scale Longitudinal Dataset and Benchmark of Bottlenose Dolphin Vocalizations

author.name: Faadil Mustun, Chiara Semenzin, Roberto Dessi, Pablo Robin Guerrero, Pierre Orhan, Alexis Emanuelli, Emanuele Rossi, Yair Lakretz, Gonzalo de Polavieja, German Sumbre

entry.summary: OpenWhistle is the largest publicly available dolphin vocalization dataset, comprising about 180,000 whistles (114 hours) recorded over five years from a stable pod of five individuals in a semi-natural environment. It addresses the fragmentation and closedness of prior cetacean datasets and enables deep study of a single species' communication system.

entry.title: Who Is Left of Whom? Tracing Spatial Evidence and Role Binding in Relative-Position Reasoning

author.name: Yingjin Song, Denis Paperno, Albert Gatt

entry.summary: This mechanistic study investigates how vision-language models and their language backbones reason about relative object positions, separating location tracking of input objects from representing their query roles. Using activation patching across three VLMs, the authors reveal a staged progression from early-layer source representations through intermediate-layer query-object representations to late-layer answer states, and targeted interventions establish causal links along this progression. High instance-level accuracy can mask inconsistencies when object positions or roles are swapped.

entry.title: RPA: Residual Patch-Token Adapter for Image Retrieval from EEG and MEG

author.name: Yuhui Jin, Yonghao Song, Bingchuan Liu

entry.summary: Introduces the Residual Patch Adapter, which aligns EEG and MEG brain signals with all patch tokens from an intermediate ViT layer rather than a single global embedding for visual decoding. Ablations show pooling or masking patch tokens degrades representations, demonstrating the value of granular patch-level alignment for neural image retrieval.

entry.title: VisionPsy-Nano: Improving Accuracy, Efficiency, and Reliability in On-Device Vision-Language Models

author.name: Khurram Azeem Hashmi, Mohammadreza Zolfaghari, Changdae Park, Rishabh Jain, Nicholas Moratelli, Pengfei Wei, Louis Lu, Tianchi Liu, Amril Nazir

entry.summary: VisionPsy-Nano presents a diagnosis-driven post-training recipe for sub-billion-parameter vision-language models in which a teacher VLM stress-tests the student, uncovers failure modes such as doom loops and adversarial safety gaps, and converts them into targeted supervision and preference alignment. The work argues on-device usability requires accuracy, efficiency, and behavioral reliability, the last of which standard benchmarks miss.

entry.title: ReAL: Accelerating Flow Matching through Segment Advancement with Shared Lookahead

author.name: Xuanhua Yin, Chuanzhi Xu, Haoxian Zhou, Shunqi Mao, Weidong Cai

entry.summary: ReAL is a training-free sampler for flow-matching models that determines how far to skip neural network evaluations using a single shared lookahead, deriving a span-dependent selection criterion directly from the observed velocity mismatch. This avoids the costly per-endpoint checks that standard evaluation-skipping approaches require.

entry.title: M3-Score: Fidelity, Memorization and Coverage as Separate Axes for Evaluating Generative Radiology Image Models

author.name: Sathiyamohan Nishankar, Pubudu Sanjeewani, Asanka Perera

entry.summary: Proposes M3-Score, an evaluation framework for generative radiology image models reporting fidelity, memorization, and coverage as separate axes using RadioDINO-s16, a frozen vision transformer pretrained on radiology images, with an unbiased multi-bandwidth RBF MMD and nearest-neighbor measures. It argues single summary scores conflate fidelity and diversity. This improves how medical generative models are judged.

entry.title: Geometric Encoding for Spatial Reasoning in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Antonio Jun, Haoshui Yu, Zhengyi Lu, Huirong Fu, Yao Qiang

entry.summary: This paper presents a perception-to-geometry pipeline that recovers depth, camera pose, and object structure from monocular RGB video, then converts them into an explicit spatial code of positions, dimensions, distances, and room geometry supplied as context to vision-language models. The goal is to improve metric spatial and temporal reasoning that VLMs handle poorly when relying on raw video.

entry.title: RoGSW4RLD: Feed-Forward 4D Gaussian Lifting for Robot World Model Rollouts

author.name: Jin Hyun Kim, Min Young Kim, Soohwan Song, Daekyum Kim

entry.summary: RoGSW4RLD lifts synchronized multi-camera world-model rollouts into a unified, time-queryable metric 4D Gaussian field, enforcing cross-view consistency that independent per-camera reconstruction misses, especially with mixed moving robot-mounted and fixed external cameras. This turns disparate video predictions into a shared metric scene queryable across viewpoints and time. It is a meaningful step toward spatially grounded robot world models for reinforcement learning.

entry.title: FlowAct-R2: Beyond Talking Avatar via Streaming Multimodal References and Proactive Agent Planning

author.name: Ziyao Huang, Zhengkun Rong, Shiyang Qin, Shuang Liang, Wentao Hu, Yuxuan Luo, Yuan Zhang, Mingyuan Gao

entry.summary: FlowAct-R2 is a framework for interactive humanoid video generation combining a Streaming Multimodal Reference Diffusion Transformer (adapting the Seedance 2.0 Mini reference-to-video backbone to rolling action prompts and streaming audio/image/video references) with a Proactive Interaction Agent that separates pre-online planning from online response.

entry.title: ArticulateArena: A Metric for Articulated Kinematics

author.name: Yumeng He, Yongfei She, Huanyu Chen, Chun Yuan, Peihao Li, Joseph Masterjohn, Yin Yang, Ying Jiang, Chenfanfu Jiang

entry.summary: The paper identifies a fundamental evaluation flaw in articulated object reconstruction and generation: articulation specifies a motion, and existing protocols score joint type, axis, origin, and limits separately even though the same physical motion can have different parameter encodings, so a joint can score maximally wrong against an equivalent encoding of itself. ArticulateArena proposes a metric that compares predicted and ground-truth articulation as motions rather than parameter vectors. This should improve benchmark quality for simulation-ready articulated object methods.

entry.title: End-to-end QP-based policies: A unified perspective on robust control and robot learning

author.name: Fausto Vega, Priyanka Supraja Balaji, Chase Dunaway, Joe Koszut, Jon Arrizabalaga, Zachary Manchester

entry.summary: This paper presents a framework for end-to-end QP-based policies that supports both domain-randomized model-based auto-tuning and black-box policy construction without explicit states, inputs, or dynamics knowledge. It establishes connections between QP policies, robust control, MLPs, and robot learning, preserving model-based transparency and interpretability.

entry.title: SwingRL: Adaptive Observation Reinforcement Learning with World-Model Prediction for Cable-Suspended Hoisting Control

author.name: Guangming Wang, Xiaoyu Zhang, Yucheng Xin, Wanli Ma, Jiucai Liu, Yunxiang Ma, Joe Ingham, Haibing Wu, Yixiong Jing, Olaf Wysocki, Brian Sheil

entry.summary: A residual RL framework for robotic cable-suspended hoisting combining an age-aware world model (handling delayed or lost visual observations), a classical anti-swing prior, and a recurrent residual policy. Targets precise insertion of suspended payload sockets onto rebar pins in construction.

entry.title: GuardPIBT: Counterfactually Gated Neural Guidance for Ultra-Large-Scale 3D Multi-Agent Path Finding

author.name: Yuan Zhou, Zhenyu Hou, Guangtong Xu, Xiaoqiang Ji, Yuqing Tang, Jialiang Hou, Fei Gao

entry.summary: GuardPIBT augments the PIBT executor for large-scale 3D multi-agent path finding by using neural predictions only to propose residual reorderings of PIBT's native candidate priorities, with a counterfactual group gate filtering reorderings that could degrade coordination. It combines local graph attention with global source-goal transport features for population-level context. This preserves PIBT's guarantees while adding learned guidance at ultra-large scale.

entry.title: ConflictVLA-Bench: Benchmarking Behavioral Responses of Vision-Language-Action Models to Premise Conflicts

author.name: Liyu Hou, Yuan Wu, Yi Chang

entry.summary: ConflictVLA-Bench is a benchmark built on LIBERO with 2,826 prompt-conditioned conflict tasks that evaluate how vision-language-action models behave when given invalid task premises. Crucially, it distinguishes behavioral disengagement from Failed Persistence, where a model continues pursuing an impossible task and then errors. This adds an important safety-relevant behavioral dimension to VLA evaluation beyond task success rates.

entry.title: Goal-Persistent Coding Agents as Scientific Performance Engineers: A Fixed-Radius Nearest-Neighbor Case Study

author.name: Xiangyang Ju

entry.summary: This case study shows that off-the-shelf coding agents (Codex and Claude Code) can perform rigorous scientific performance engineering: given an executable goal with correctness tests and profiling requirements, the agents autonomously removed a PyTorch dependency from a CUDA particle-tracking implementation and ran hypothesis-driven optimization experiments. The result is a standalone high-performance implementation produced without prescribed code transformations. It provides evidence that general-purpose agents can do goal-persistent scientific optimization.

entry.title: EngramRAG: Dynamic Usage-Weighted Topology and Synaptic Consolidation for Multi-Hop Agentic Memory

author.name: Bhavyateja Potineni, Lohit Giri, Anu Jain, Vadim Kutsyy, Rajasekhar Pentakota

entry.summary: EngramRAG is an adaptive agent-memory architecture grounded in Complementary Learning Systems theory, coupling a fast Waking State reflex with an asynchronous Dreaming State consolidation cycle. It introduces usage-modulated Personalized PageRank with Hebbian plasticity and addresses named failure modes: Associative Blindness, Scaffolding Amnesia, and Static Topology Stagnation. The neuroscience-inspired design targets multi-hop, multi-session agent memory.

entry.title: Noisy Test-Time Reinforcement Learning for Code LLMs

author.name: Xikai Yang, Hieu Trung Nguyen, Dunyuan Xu, Yuzhi Zhao, Jinpeng Li, Wenao Ma, Pheng-Ann Heng

entry.summary: NTRL-Code is a test-time reinforcement learning framework that improves robustness of code LLMs to vague and error-prone real-world user instructions using only unlabeled noisy data. It uses conservative self-denoising to avoid the costly curation of paired clean-noisy samples required by robustness-oriented fine-tuning.

entry.title: LAM: Efficient Lossy Agent Memory Framework With A Retrieval-Score Error Bound

author.name: Baixi Sun, Le Chen, Anjir Ahmed Chowdhury, Xiaolong Ma, Chih-Hsuan Yang, Mingze Xia, Syed Zawad, Sheng Di, Rajkumar Kettimuthu, Huihuo Zheng, Rajeev Thakur, Venkatram Vishwanath, Feng Yan

entry.summary: LAM is a lossy agent memory framework combining deterministic deduplication with a provable bound on retrieval-score perturbation, a memory manager that preserves the cached prefix and overlaps compaction with inference, and a performance model for pre-deployment cost estimation. On 600 agent trajectories it removes 22.47% of observation tokens while retaining 99.984% of measured performance.

entry.title: Beyond Scripted Search: Sample-Efficient Reward Discovery via Agentic Black-box Optimization

author.name: Minghao Li, Rui Tan, Ruihang Wang

entry.summary: ARBO is an agentic black-box optimization framework for discovering dense reward functions in low-level RL, where an LLM agent builds the search strategy at run time from a persistent evaluation-history workspace. This improves sample efficiency over scripted LLM-driven reward search, which is critical because each candidate reward requires a full RL training run. The framework combines oracle-maintained observations with agent-maintained context.

entry.title: PULSE: Identifying Demonstration-Utility Features with Sparse Autoencoders

author.name: Chenduo Hao, Chuanbao Gao, Pinjun Zeng, Jingze Zhu, Chonghan Liu, Zidong Liu, Xu Yang

entry.summary: PULSE is an SAE-based framework that identifies model-internal features associated with in-context demonstration utility and uses them for demonstration selection. It samples candidate demonstration sets on a small labeled discovery set, measures their zero-shot-relative utility under the target model, and scores SAE features by how activation differences align with utility differences. This captures model-specific signals that external query-demonstration similarity misses.

entry.title: Learning from Others, Acting for You: Cross-User Memory Sharing for LLM Agents

author.name: Jinming Hu, Haodong Zhao, Qi Jia, Die Chen, Tianhang Zhao, Sufeng Duan, Gongshen Liu

entry.summary: Introduces ShareMem, a memory architecture that lets LLM agents serving different users share reusable experience while grounding its application in the receiving user's own preferences, with two-stage consolidation and scope-first retrieval over local and shared pools. This addresses the tension between isolated per-user memory (no reuse) and pooled memory (preference conflicts).

entry.title: Can Open-Weight Large Language Models (LLMs) Simulate Human Survey Populations? A Cross-Instrument Calibration Study

author.name: Grandee Lee, Wang Yue

entry.summary: Evaluates whether open-weight LLMs can serve as synthetic survey respondents by conditioning personas on real answers to one psychometric instrument and measuring correlations on a second, validated against a 2,058-person human panel across a 139-pair grid. Simulated cross-instrument correlations track human correlations at r = 0.70-0.73. The study provides much-needed calibration evidence for open-weight models, where prior evidence came mostly from proprietary systems.

entry.title: CAIRN: Dynamic Fact-Intent DAGs for Multi-Agent Exploration

author.name: Zuyao Xu, Yuyang Jia, Junwei Guan, Xiang Li, Kaiwen Shen, Zhiqiang Dong

entry.summary: Presents CAIRN, a multi-agent paradigm for goal-directed exploration that represents observations and planned investigations as a dynamic directed acyclic graph: a reasoner proposes intents from facts, workers execute them, and the persistent graph preserves goals, dependencies, and findings across workers. This supports knowledge reuse and parallel exploration for LLM-powered systems in domains like math, engineering, and cybersecurity.

entry.title: CUA-Sandbox: Efficient Environments for Computer-Use Agent Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Xin Yan, Zhengbo Jiao, Jiaqi Liu, Zhenglin Wan, SiYuan Ma, Xuliang Yu, Tianyi Jiang, Chubin Zhang, Pengfei Zhou, Wangbo Zhao, Xingrui Yu, Bo An, Yang You, Ivor Tsang

entry.summary: CUA-Sandbox improves the efficiency of RL training for computer-use agents by observing that parallel rollouts need independent mutable state, not independent application runtimes, so initialized software runtimes can be shared across concurrently evolving environments. This reduces memory and initialization costs that otherwise scale with the number of parallel environments. The insight could substantially lower the compute cost of training computer-use agents.

entry.title: The Epistemics of Agent Memory: Measuring, and Governing, the Consolidation Decision in Long-Horizon LLM Agents

author.name: Sasank Annapureddy, Anjaneya Prasad Thamatani

entry.summary: A four-phase research program on how long-horizon agents decide what to keep, compress, abstract, or forget in memory, culminating in governance of the consolidation decision itself. Highlights include learning episodic boundaries from traces, a +22.7% verified task-success gain for promotion decisions under token budgets, and an anti-leakage protocol. The central contribution is shifting memory evaluation from how much is remembered to whether consolidation decisions are trustworthy.

entry.title: Unlocking Latent Personalization in LLMs

author.name: Wei Chen, Guanghui Zhu, Zhongliang Cai, Yihua Huang

entry.summary: This paper proposes LatentPersonal, a framework that treats personalization as navigation in a shared latent adaptation space, inferring a compact latent user representation from a few samples with variational information regularization. The premise is that pretrained LLMs already hold latent personalization capacity that small user data can unlock.

entry.title: ActiveMem: Dynamic Latent Memory Trees for Long-Horizon Agents

author.name: Song-Li Wu, Jingyi Wang, Zhaocheng Du, Weinan Gan

entry.summary: ActiveMem organizes agent experiences into dependency-aware latent execution trees that abstract trajectories into reusable subtask nodes while preserving execution transitions. This hierarchical memory addresses context fragmentation and cross-task interference found in flat retrieval systems for long-horizon agents.

entry.title: COEVO: Co-Evolving Context and Parameters for Recursive Self-Improvement

author.name: Siwei Chen, Xinping Bao, Xinyu Cai, Yuan Cao, Wan Jiang, Shaohong Chen

entry.summary: COEVO formulates recursive self-improvement as co-evolution of model parameters and external context, noting that context shapes the experience a model learns from while an evolving model interprets the same context differently over time. Existing approaches update parameters through online learning or improve context via search and reflection independently. Unifying the two mechanisms is a step toward systems that improve their own future behavior.

entry.title: Auditing Agent Actions through Query-Conditioned Attribution

author.name: Yifan Liu, Praveen Venkateswaran, Abdulhamid Adebayo, Dong Wang

entry.summary: Formulates query-conditioned agent action attribution as a new task: given a natural-language auditing query, recover the source and ordered intermediate evidence behind a realized action, even with API-only access to the acting model. This enables question-specific audit traces without costly input perturbations or full-trajectory LLM analysis.

entry.title: Is your uncertainty map wrong, or is its target? Exact diagnostics for the Tweedie diagonal, and a gradient-free alternative

author.name: Vicent Ribas, Anna Oliveras Tous

entry.summary: The paper computes exact Tweedie posterior covariance diagonals for diffusion models in medical image prediction, showing that in some real-image conditions the exact diagonal is anti-correlated with denoising error, meaning faithful estimators can reproduce misleading uncertainty maps. It provides exact diagnostics and a gradient-free alternative estimator.

entry.title: PhysFieldBench: Can Multimodal Models Understand Physical Fields?

author.name: Yuezhou Ma, Huikun Weng, Jialong Wu, Chenyi Zhao, Hang Zhou, Haonan Shangguan, Jianmin Wang, Mingsheng Long

entry.summary: PhysFieldBench is a benchmark of 24 tasks and 1,160 examples testing whether multimodal LLMs can interpret continuous physical fields, covering equation-derived, simulated, and observed fields across mechanism identification, latent variable comparison, and outcome prediction. It fills a gap beyond textbook-style physics benchmarks relevant to scientific agents.

entry.title: Self-Evolving Agents via Likelihood-Guided Tool-Space Optimization

author.name: Xuanqi Zhang, Ruinan Jin, Running Yang, Yuxuan Zhang, Minghui Chen, Wenlong Deng, Xiaoxiao Li

entry.summary: The paper studies tool-space self-evolution, where each recurring task type maintains a persistent tool space built from accumulated output experience instead of exposing the full tool library, addressing output-unaware selection and statelessness in existing methods. This improves tool-use decisions by reducing irrelevant context and consolidating observed tool outputs.

entry.title: Stashbird: Efficient Speaker-Indexed Memory for Conversational Agents

author.name: Chidera Biringa, Lucas Yannul, Xiaowen Wang, Marco Ayala, Nicholas Yi, Alex Moyse, Nishant Manchanda, Vivek Gupta

entry.summary: Stashbird is an agent memory system linking source episodes to derived memory state through explicit provenance, organizing memory into episodic records, semantic relations, community summaries, and graph state with lifecycle operations for updates and deletion. It uses 76.4x fewer ingestion prompt tokens than Graphiti on LoCoMo while maintaining QA accuracy across four benchmarks.

entry.title: MoSPR: Histology-to-Gene Expression Prediction with Morpho-Spatial Macrostates and Low-Rank Molecular Programs

author.name: Dongmyung Shin, Geongyu Lee, Yesung Cho, Park Jong Bae

entry.summary: MoSPR is a linear regression framework predicting gene expression from histopathology slides by clustering frozen patch embeddings into morphology microstates, grouping them into spatial-adjacency macrostates, and mapping slide representations to low-rank molecular program coefficients. This offers an interpretable, computationally light alternative to deep histology-to-omics models.

entry.title: A General Harness for Protein Foundation Model Fitness Prediction

author.name: Yang Tan, Qijia Tian, Gangyu Sun, Bozitao Zhong, Mingchen Li, Yuanxi Yu, Nanqing Dong, Liang Hong

entry.summary: VenusREM-Harness (VRH) is a training-free, model-agnostic retrieval-enhanced harness that fuses frozen protein foundation model scores with MSA evolutionary evidence weighted by model uncertainty to improve fitness prediction for protein engineering. It counters shared corpus-driven biases and unreliable inputs in PFM-based predictions.

entry.title: PDE-JEPA: Predictive Representation Learning of Latent Dynamics Modeling for Parametric PDEs

author.name: Zhentao Tan, Jianrong Zhang, Ruijie Quan, Yi Yang

entry.summary: Applies joint-embedding predictive architecture (JEPA) style pretraining to parametric partial differential equations, replacing reconstruction-based objectives with masked-latent prediction of physical dynamics. The authors show predictive representations preserve physical information better and build an encoder targeting accurate field evolution.

entry.title: BV Loss: Block Verification-Aware Loss for Block Diffusion Speculative Decoding

author.name: Suyoung Kim, Jahyun Koo, Hyeonjin Kim, Inhyeok Bang, Seunghyun Lee, Hyunjae Oh, Baeseong Park, Dongsoo Lee

entry.summary: Introduces BV loss, a training objective for diffusion drafters in speculative decoding that directly maximizes expected accepted sequence length under block verification, rather than optimizing token-level objectives. Across math, code, and chat benchmarks it increases the mean number of tokens accepted per draft.

entry.title: APEX-Voice: Can Voice Agents Complete Professional Workflows Through Full-Duplex Interaction

author.name: Puneet Mathur, Dinesh Manocha

entry.summary: APEX-Voice is a benchmark of 120 interactive professional workflows (form completion, negotiation, consulting, interviewing) executed in a stateful Voice Workbench with typed tools, authorization constraints, and validated user simulation. It measures both artifact field accuracy and end-to-end workflow success for full-duplex voice agents. This moves voice-agent evaluation beyond dialogue fluency to actual professional task completion.

entry.title: DuplexCadence: Exact State and Execution from a Speech Model's Declared Timelines

author.name: Haixiao Gao, Yimin Zheng, Linyou Xiao, Zeke Xie

entry.summary: DuplexCadence addresses serving of full-duplex speech models, where conversation advances on a strict one-second cadence and every second of input must become a second of speech before the next arrives. Profiling shows the autoregressive stages fit the period while the token-to-audio synthesis tail causes overruns due to orchestration slack and wasted memory. The system extracts exact state and execution from the model's declared timelines to eliminate the tail bottleneck.

entry.title: Narrowing the Horizon: Quantifying Topic Saliency Shifts in Generative Monoculture

author.name: Oriane Peter, Elena Simperl, Kate Devlin

entry.summary: The paper introduces a method to measure shifts in topic saliency across LLM model families, tracking which topics gain or lose prominence during post-training, and applies it to climate change discourse as a case study. It demonstrates how homogenization affects representational diversity in what the authors call generative monoculture.

entry.title: AutoBCI: Forecast-Guided Agentic Neural Architecture Discovery for EEG-Based Brain--Computer Interfaces

author.name: Muyun Jiang, Yi Ding, Wei Zhang, Jinbo Chen, Chenyu Liu, Zhenjie Yang, Yuxin Li, Jingyuan Chen, Yuhao Lu, Yong Li, Shuailei Zhang, Cuntai Guan

entry.summary: AutoBCI is an agentic framework where a Designer Agent discovers EEG decoding architectures via pool-guided search across tasks like emotion recognition and motor imagery, while a Forecaster Agent predicts full-budget performance from early learning curves to select candidates cheaply. This automates a laborious architecture-design step in brain-computer interfaces. It matters because EEG decoding lacks the AutoML maturity of vision or language, and early-curve forecasting could substantially reduce search cost.

entry.title: Open-Qwen-Music: An Auditable Framework for LLM-Based Music Composition and Diffusion Rendering

author.name: Yangbin Yu, Mingyu Yang

entry.summary: Open-Qwen-Music is an open reconstruction of Qwen-Music, a text-to-music system coupling a 3B autoregressive Music LLM with a 25 Hz single-codebook tokenizer and a diffusion renderer producing 48 kHz stereo audio, following reported cross-module interfaces. It argues that closed top systems and open projects lacking training corpora or end-to-end training code impede independent study of how information loss propagates from semantic composition to audio. The full training implementation is released.

entry.title: Unsupervised spiking feature learning for event-based pedestrian crossing detection: approaching supervised accuracy without labelled training data

author.name: Henok Teklu, Mustafa Sakhai, Matej Mertik, Maciej Wielgosz

entry.summary: The paper reports the first unsupervised results on the DVS-PedX pedestrian-crossing benchmark using a single spiking layer trained with winner-take-all spike-timing-dependent plasticity, followed by a linear classifier. It approaches supervised accuracy without frame-level labels, which are costly to collect. This demonstrates viable label-free learning for event cameras and neuromorphic vision.

entry.title: Same Probe, Different Numbers: Are Activation Probes Robust to Inference-Time Numerical Non-Determinism?

author.name: Alizishaan Khatri

entry.summary: This work measures how activation probes used to monitor deployed LLMs degrade when inference configuration (batch size, floating-point precision) differs from the training configuration, since GPU kernels are not batch-invariant and float formats round differently. Training 768 probes on Llama-3.1-8B, Qwen3-8B, and Gemma-3-4B across three batch sizes and three precisions, the author finds probes are stable at the individual example level but aggregate accuracy is a misleading instrument for measuring stability. This is a practically important caveat for anyone deploying probes for LLM monitoring and safety.

entry.title: When Should a Human Take Back Control? Optimal Delegation under Turbulent AI Risk

author.name: Haoze Yan, Julien Roze, Ved Upadhyay, Unal Tatar, Thibaut Mastrolia

entry.summary: This paper introduces a continuous-time framework for adaptive human oversight of AI systems under turbulent risk, where failures self-excite and cluster (a hallucination can trigger further errors). It jointly models incident clustering, its suppression by supervision effort, and the human delegation decision, filling a gap in existing oversight formulations. The work provides principled guidance on when humans should intervene or take back control from AI.

entry.title: Rank Confidence Sequences:Anytime-valid Leaderboards

author.name: Hamed Khosravi, Xiaoming Huo

entry.summary: This paper addresses a subtle statistical flaw in model leaderboards: confidence intervals for a model's rank are valid only if computed once at a pre-chosen sample size, but leaderboard evaluations are consulted repeatedly and stopped when results look decisive, inflating error rates. It introduces anytime-valid rank confidence sequences that maintain guarantees at all sample sizes and under any stopping rule, extending anytime-valid inference to rankings when all models are scored on the same items. This is directly relevant to LLM benchmark methodology.

entry.title: Bison: Cross-Dataset Learning for Unseen-Compound Perturbation Prediction

author.name: Yunfan Liu, Kasra Ghorbani, Yufei Huang, Zicheng Liu, Jiangbin Zheng, Jingbo Zhou, Shaorong Chen, Chang Yu, Stan Z. Li

entry.summary: Bison benchmarks eight perturbation-dataset combinations with 16,771 compounds to test molecular generalization to unseen compounds, revealing that high overall response agreement can coexist with weak prediction of drug-specific differences. The proposed method connects gene panels via a shared gene representation and uses two discrete diffusion models to compose context-dependent responses. This is relevant to computational drug discovery and transcriptomics.

entry.title: REFINE: A Resilient Evolution Framework for Intelligent Enterprise Alert Triage in Security Operations Centers

author.name: Huimin Chen, Quan Long, Yanhao Wang

entry.summary: REFINE is an LLM-agent framework for SOC alert triage that encodes analyst expertise as structured skills and continuously adapts from analyst disposition feedback. It enforces recall of 1.0 as a hard constraint during evolution to maximize auto-closure of false positives and identifies judgment blind spots from alert distributions and model error boundaries. Evaluated on four real industrial settings, it tackles a concrete high-value cybersecurity workflow problem.

entry.title: GAUGE: Group-Wise View-Inconsistency Rectification for Feed-Forward 4D Tracking

author.name: Zhuoqian Feng, Weixing Chen, Ziliang Chen, Yang Liu, Liang Lin

entry.summary: The paper provides a structural explanation of residual error in feed-forward 4D tracking from monocular video: error concentrates along the view direction as group-wise radial degrees of freedom that 2D observations cannot constrain, with predicted displacement direction supporting reliable motion grouping. GAUGE estimates and rectifies this group-wise view inconsistency in an unsupervised adaptive gauge framework. This is a principled diagnosis-and-fix for a systematic error mode in a new modeling paradigm.

entry.title: Ask Without Telling: Local SLMs Consult Cloud LLMs Without Revealing Task Intent

author.name: Yanmeng Wang, Yunxuan Li, Shilong Fan, Yuhan Zheng, Tsung-Hui Chang

entry.summary: The paper addresses privacy in local SLM to cloud LLM collaboration, noting that hiding sensitive values still leaks what the user is trying to accomplish. It proposes a method allowing local small models to consult cloud LLMs without revealing task intent, going beyond decoy-based approaches. This targets a subtle privacy threat in hybrid edge-cloud inference.

entry.title: How Far Do Persona Effects Generalize in Language Models?

author.name: Yufan Zhou, Yuxuan Liu, Enze Ma, Lyumanshan Ye, Zhongqi Yue, Robin De Croon, Yucheng Jin, Katrien Verbert, Zhao Wang

entry.summary: The paper tests whether persona-prompt effects in language models are predictable and portable, across 57 attributes, three behavioral domains, and seven pairs of 7-9B open checkpoints including OLMo-3 and Qwen2.5. It finds persona effects can be predictable without being portable, with attribute- and task-specific gains improving prediction beyond shared scaling, especially in OLMo-3. This clarifies the limits of transferring persona-related behavioral knowledge across models.

entry.title: Algorithmic Harms Associated with Generative Model-Augmented Recommendation Systems

author.name: Christine Herlihy, Xumei Xi, Shloka Desai, Kevin Bannerman Hutchful, Pedro Silva

entry.summary: Extends existing harm taxonomies and threat models to cover generative models embedded in recommendation platforms, identifying novel causal drivers of representational and quality-of-service harms plus endogenous harms like sanitization when inputs conflict with designer objectives or model priors. Provides a causal analysis of how problematic input subsets produce downstream harms in non-conversational recommender settings.

entry.title: Toward Comprehensive 3D Grounding: Orientation Grounding through Vision-Language Models

author.name: Tuo Liang, Disheng Liu, Nengbo Wang, Vipin Chaudhary, Yu Yin

entry.summary: Introduces orientation grounding, a new 3D referring task requiring prediction of an object's 6D orientation and axial symmetry from language or box queries, since existing 3D VLM grounding covers only location. Contributes ReferOri, a large dataset with 331K multi-view and 387K single-view queries built via scalable reconstruction and human verification, plus a corresponding model.

entry.title: Dynamic Manipulation with World-Action Models via Counterfactual Planning

author.name: Sunwoo Park, Wonbin Lee, Seonghyun Jin, Youngmin Kim, Jangho Park, Jong Chul Ye

entry.summary: Identifies target-response collapse in World-Action models trained on static demonstrations, where policies become biased toward their learned behavior continuation and unresponsive to moving targets. Proposes Dynamic Predictive Planning, formulating dynamic manipulation as counterfactual planning that decouples plan-generation context from execution-time physical state, using the WAM rollout to estimate when to intervene.

entry.title: Domain Generalization under Sampling Pattern Shifts in Irregular Time Series

author.name: Changhun Kim, Joohyung Lee, Kwanhyung Lee, Donghwee Yoon, Grigorios Chrysos, Eunho Yang

entry.summary: The paper introduces HAR-C, the first controlled benchmark for sampling pattern shifts in irregularly sampled multivariate time series, showing sampling shifts alone substantially degrade model performance and induce sampling-specific shortcuts. It proposes PRISM, a domain generalization framework combining complementary feature-centric and distribution-centric learning. Relevant to healthcare and sensor applications where observation patterns differ across sites.

entry.title: Robust Hierarchical Structures for Agentic Document Analysis

author.name: Ruiying Ma, Yiming Lin, Aditya G. Parameswaran

entry.summary: The paper proposes extracting robust and compact hierarchical structure from PDFs and Word documents so that LLM agents can process only task-relevant sections rather than treating documents as flat text. It targets a structure variant that is feasible to infer and comes with formal guarantees on match quality, unlike prior structure-extraction work. This improves both efficiency and effectiveness of agentic document analysis.

entry.title: TTRSD: Test-Time Reinforcement Learning with Self-Distillation for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Shuning Wang, Zhiheng Wu, Xun Zhou, Chongyang Cui, Chen Jia, Bowen Liu, Chuanjie Li, Xiang Chen, Yi Yang, Yumeng Zhang, Wenjie Huang

entry.summary: TTRSD is a test-time reinforcement learning framework for vision-language models that combines multi-view answer-level self-distillation with visual contrastive token selection. It prevents the reinforcement of shared perceptual errors across samples and protects pretrained reasoning capabilities from degradation.

entry.title: SpatialSpeak: QA-Native Reconstruction with Local and Global Context for Spatial Chain-of-Thought Reasoning

author.name: Yang Cao, Jiaxin Zhang, Dave Zhenyu Chen, Yingji Zhong, Ruiyuan Gao, Lanqing Hong, Dan Xu

entry.summary: SpatialSpeak is a two-stage framework connecting QA-native 3D reconstruction pretraining with spatial chain-of-thought learning for vision-language models. Stage I combines marked-point local geometry queries with object-center global scene queries in reconstruction, followed by spatial CoT supervision for quantitative multi-view spatial reasoning.

entry.title: An Active-Bottleneck Mechanism for Weak-to-Strong Generalization

author.name: Mohammad Zeinalpour, Amir Najafi

entry.summary: This theoretical paper characterizes when weak-to-strong generalization occurs in two-stage ridgeless linear regression, showing the student outperforms the teacher exactly when the number of pseudo-labels m lies in an explicit intermediate range — too few leave insufficient signal, too many overfit the teacher's errors. The analysis holds under fully converged learning with no early stopping or regularization and without assuming a more expressive student. It grounds an empirical alignment phenomenon in clean theory.

entry.title: Diffusion-Based Rollouts as a Stabilization Mechanism for Long-Horizon Environmental Forecasting

author.name: Marina Vicens-Miquel, Amy McGovern, Aaron J. Hill, Efi Foufoula-Georgiou, Samuel S. P. Shen

entry.summary: This study investigates diffusion-based rollouts as a stabilization mechanism for recursive forecasting in environmental applications, using both low-dimensional water-level series and high-dimensional precipitation fields. It finds diffusion suppresses recursive error growth most where deterministic rollouts are most unstable, but also shows that stabilization does not guarantee forecast fidelity, with event-level skill degrading as rollouts lose access to external information. The nuance matters for anyone deploying generative rollouts in forecasting.

entry.title: Unknown is not normal: separating language-model extraction from rule-based decision logic for clinical risk scores

author.name: Nicol\'as Vera Z\'u\~niga

entry.summary: The paper proposes separating three-state extraction (present, absent, unknown) by an LLM from deterministic rule-based decision logic for clinical risk scores, so the system only asks clinicians about missing inputs that can change the decision. On 1,200 synthetic emergency cases across six calculators, the bounds policy outperformed missing-equals-normal schemas and an end-to-end LLM agent. Directly relevant to safe deployment of LLMs in clinical settings where undocumented findings are risky to assume normal.

entry.title: SAGE: Symbolic Action-Gating and Editing for LLM Task Planners

author.name: Trung Minh Bui, JongSul Moon, YoungOuk Kim, Quang-Ngoc Phung, Se-Woong Jun, Dongin Shin

entry.summary: SAGE augments a single-LLM household-task planner with a domain-agnostic symbolic gate (roughly 250 lines of Python, zero token cost) that blocks precondition-violating actions with typed reasons, plus a local edit mechanism that regenerates only the failed sub-goal's suffix while preserving completed work, and a hybrid seed-plus-live memory system. It also critiques saturated embodied-agent benchmarks where methods cannot be distinguished. Combines symbolic safety monitoring with LLM planning.

entry.title: PlaylistEval: Can Video-Language Judges Be Trusted at Day Scale and Beyond?

author.name: Shayekh Bin Islam, Hwanjun Song

entry.summary: PlaylistEval is an agentic framework that builds video-language judge benchmarks over 100-hour playlists without human annotation, generating question-answer pairs whose separability is controlled by causal degradation. It tests whether video-LM judges remain reliable when evidence is buried in day-long videos, a regime existing benchmarks of a few minutes cannot probe. This is relevant given video-LM judges are used for evaluation and reward modeling.

entry.title: DPS: Dual-Mode Precision LLM Serving with Semi-Unified Memory

author.name: Xuan Truong Nguyen, Tien Son Pham, Tuan Duc Chu, Wookeun Jung, Thanh Tuan Dao

entry.summary: DPS is an LLM serving system that makes weight memory elastic under bursty workloads: under normal load it serves the full-accuracy model, and under KV-cache pressure it switches to a nested lower-precision variant and repurposes freed weight memory for the KV cache. This exploits multi-precision model representations to improve throughput and SLO compliance. It challenges the assumption that model weights are fixed at runtime.

entry.title: Modeling Whole-Slide Images as Dynamic Tumor Microenvironment Fields

author.name: Lei Wu, Jiashuai Liu, Di Zhang, Zhangpeng Gong, Yingkang Zhan, Yi Niu, Jiusong Ge, Chunze Yang, Kai Yi, Mireia Crispin-Ortuzar, Chen Li, Zeyu Gao

entry.summary: TMEvolve models whole-slide pathology images as dynamic tumor microenvironment fields using a reaction-diffusion-inspired framework, forming and evolving spatially coherent tissue regions rather than aggregating isolated patches. This captures region interactions across heterogeneous boundaries for diagnostic and prognostic tasks. It offers a biologically motivated alternative to standard multiple-instance learning on gigapixel slides.

entry.title: Using LLMs to Detect LLM-Generated Texts: A Cross-Generation Analysis

author.name: Haiyue Yuan, Jie Guo, Weidong Qiu, Zheng Huang, Ruizhe Li, Shujun Li

entry.summary: This work systematically evaluates 15 LLMs across three generations as both generators and detectors of LLM-generated text, using 1,000 human-written texts and 15,000 machine texts with over 233,000 classifications plus natural-language rationales. Findings show detection efficacy is driven mainly by detector capability rather than self-detection advantages, offering a large-scale map of detector-generator dynamics.

entry.title: LongPuzzleBench: Evaluating GUI Agents on Long-Horizon Visual Puzzles

author.name: Bingo Zhang, Haochuan Lu, Zongjie Li, Genjian Li, Ari Yu Zhang, Chaozheng Wang

entry.summary: LongPuzzleBench is a benchmark of 114 levels across six puzzle games played through native GUI actions, designed to test whether GUI agents maintain coherent multi-step plans where early moves can silently make puzzles unsolvable. It exposes long-horizon reasoning failures that existing grounding and computer-use benchmarks miss.

entry.title: RoboFL: Federated Expert Assembly for World Action Models

author.name: Rongyu Zhang, Ruizhi Fan, Yunfan Lou, Hengyu Fang, Shenli Zheng, Chenrui Wu, Yili Jin, Li Du, Dan Wang, Yuan Du, Shanghang Zhang

entry.summary: Presents RoboFL, a federated learning framework for vision-language-action and world-action models that installs locally trained LoRA adapters into a Mixture of Slotted Adapters (MoSAIC), avoiding entanglement of incompatible updates while preserving expert specialization. It targets the scarcity and institutional siloing of physical interaction data for robot foundation models.

entry.title: ReCAT: Remember, Count, and Time: Structured Recurrent Memory for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Pankhuri Vanjani, Mostafa Hatab, Can Mizrakli, Vaisakh Shaj, Zhuoyue Li, Moritz Reuss, Rudolf Lioutikov

entry.summary: ReCAT is a language-conditioned robot manipulation policy with structured recurrent memory built from Mamba-2 layers and causal attention, decoding actions with a flow-matching Transformer that cross-attends to current and historical representations separately. It achieves 95.3% average success on LIBERO and 62.4% on RMBench.

entry.title: From Data to Program: Fast & Direct Generative Program Inference from Empirical Data

author.name: Simon Kl\"uttermann, Xueying Ding, Leman Akoglu

entry.summary: PRODiGI is a pretrained data-to-program model that infers an explicit, executable generative program from samples in a single forward pass, using template prediction and non-autoregressive parameter decoding across diverse generative families. It also introduces program-space fine-tuning that refines differentiable program parameters by matching generated and empirical samples.

entry.title: Rethinking Causal Action Tokenization with Conditional Annealing in Flow Matching

author.name: Chenyu Zhang, Yuhang Cao, Daru Du, Yingxi Lu, Jing Shao, Ruoqu Chen, Jiajun Liu, Liu Cao, Yicheng Liu, Hang Zhao, Mengdi Xu

entry.summary: CATok reframes action tokenization for VLA models as a causally structured generative process rather than pure compression. A conditional annealing mechanism over flow matching produces coarse-to-fine causal tokens aligned with autoregressive backbones, improving robot learning.

entry.title: Beyond Token Scale: Chunk-Level Sparse Autoencoders for Reliable Semantic Feature Discovery

author.name: Xu Wang, Yifan Yang, TingHao YU, Difan Zou

entry.summary: The paper argues token-level SAE objectives spend sparse budget on lexical and formatting details, and introduces a family of chunk-level SAEs encoding mean-pooled activations over token spans with Mean-, Cross-, and Joint-Chunk variants. This separates the effect of observation scale from cross-passage prediction, yielding more reliable semantic feature discovery.

entry.title: MS-GLA: Multi-Scale Gated Linear Attention for Addressing Representational Bottlenecks via Multi-Temporal Resolution

author.name: Prasoon Dev, Anirudh Sankar, Vasudeva Varma

entry.summary: Introduces MS-GLA, which extends Gated Linear Attention Transformers by distributing heads across multiple temporal resolutions so coarse heads pool longer spans and specialize in long-range dependencies while fine heads retain local sensitivity. This addresses the bottleneck of a fixed-capacity single-resolution memory that must encode both local syntax and long-range semantics.

entry.title: seq2cause: One Autoregressive Backbone, Four Causal Discovery Tasks in Event Sequences

author.name: Hugo Math

entry.summary: Presents Seq2Cause, a unified autoregressive framework that handles four structurally distinct causal discovery regimes in discrete event sequences, spanning event-to-event and event-to-outcome dependencies at single-sequence and population scales. Prior methods each address only one regime and fail to scale beyond a few hundred event types.

entry.title: CAFE: Counterfactual Prediction via Fast Posterior Estimation

author.name: Xinyan Han, Xiaoyu Lin, Hao Zou, Xingxuan Zhang, Bo Li, Peng Cui

entry.summary: CAFE targets counterfactual prediction under structural uncertainty: even among fully observed additive noise models, different plausible causal graphs imply different individual counterfactual outcomes. The method computes a Bayesian counterfactual posterior predictive distribution that combines predictions across plausible SCMs via fast posterior estimation, rather than committing to a single estimated graph. This improves the reliability of individual-level causal predictions.

entry.title: Refresh or Realize? Compute Allocation in Drifting Models

author.name: Sipeng Chen, Xu Zheng, Shibo Li

entry.summary: The paper examines Drifting Models, one-step generators where a drift field is recomputed each iteration, asking whether extra compute should fit the current target more closely or recompute the field. On ImageNet 256x256, holding the target fixed for k steps and measuring realized displacement reveals how quickly the network actually realizes prescribed motion. This is a foundational question for an emerging generative training paradigm.

entry.title: PolyStepOR: Learning to Decide Without Optimal Decisions

author.name: Viet The Nguyen, Gunther Gust, An Thai Le

entry.summary: PolyStepOR trains decision-focused learning predictors directly from realized decision costs without pre-computed optimal decisions, handling piecewise-constant losses via parameter perturbation and optimal transport to favor lower-cost directions without derivatives. It also extends to in-constraint predictions through repair or infeasibility penalties, performing strongly on classical benchmarks and competitively on real-world problems without task-specific tuning. This removes a major barrier to decision-focused learning at scale.

entry.title: Robust Bayesian Optimization with Q-Exponential Surrogates

author.name: Richard Cornelius Suwandi, Zhidi Lin, Feng Yin, Abdelhak M. Zoubir

entry.summary: q-ED-BO replaces the Gaussian process surrogate in Bayesian optimization with a q-exponential distribution whose shape parameter controls tail heaviness, retaining closed-form posterior moments. This yields closed-form q-UCB and q-EI acquisition functions with sublinear regret, and improves robustness to outliers and heavy-tailed noise.

entry.title: Staying on the Attractor: Supervising Neural Surrogates of 3D Turbulence Where They Leave It

author.name: Yilong Dai, Shaswata Mitra, Raj Patel, Yiming Sun, Shengyu Chen, Jiaqi Gong, Sudip Mittal, Shahram Rahimi, Xiaowei Jia, Runlong Yu

entry.summary: The paper proposes off-attractor supervision (OAS) for neural surrogates of 3D turbulent flows: when predictions drift off the flow's attractor, the model is trained on how true Navier-Stokes dynamics would evolve from those off-attractor states. This targets the blow-up, freezing, and statistical drift that plague long-term rollout of chaotic-flow surrogates.

entry.title: Generative Priors Conditioned on Natural Language for Bayesian Inversion in PDEs

author.name: Pengyu Zhang, Mark Girolami, Arnaud Vadeboncoeur

entry.summary: This work learns natural-language-conditional Bayesian priors for inverse problems in PDEs, exploiting correlations between qualitative text descriptions (e.g., experimental setup notes) and quantitative quantities of interest. The resulting data-driven prior can incorporate human-written context alongside noisy sensor or simulation data. This bridges LLM-era text conditioning with scientific machine learning and Bayesian inference.

entry.title: Correct then Forecast: Observer State-Space Models for Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Alexis-Raja Brachet, Guillaume Clavier--Fr\'emond, Abdelhakim Ziani, Pierre-Yves Richard, C\'eline Hudelot

entry.summary: Observer State-Space Models (OSSMs) reinterpret forecasting by treating observed inputs as measurements of an underlying autonomous dynamical system, explicitly separating latent-state propagation from measurement assimilation. A single transition governs dynamics across both context and forecast intervals, eliminating the regime change that occurs when observations become unavailable at prediction time.

entry.title: TGRL: Temperature-Grouped Reinforcement Learning for Efficient Exploration in LLMs

author.name: Zihan Lin, Xiaohan Wang, Jie Cao, Jiajun Chai, Wei Lin, Guojun Yin, Ran He

entry.summary: TGRL improves exploration in reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards by partitioning each prompt's rollout group into low- and high-temperature subsets and converting the reward contrast between them into an explicit exploration signal. It allocates this group-level signal as token-level credit using Jensen-Shannon divergence between temperature subsets, without expanding the rollout budget.

entry.title: Binding Multiple Modalities via Multimodal Wasserstein Barycenter

author.name: Xiaole Tang, Jiayi Xu, Xiang Gu, Yan Yang, Jian Sun

entry.summary: Introduces BaryBind, which builds a balanced n-modality representation space by transporting a reference modality toward a Wasserstein barycenter computed across all modalities, plus a volumetric alignment objective to unify the semantic space. This offers an alternative to text-anchored binding of many modalities, respecting the joint geometry of multimodal data.

entry.title: On the Two Faces of Adam in Separable Linear Classification

author.name: Chen Fan, Csaba Szepesv\'{a}ri

entry.summary: Gives a quantitative characterization of Adam's behavior in separable linear classification under log-loss for small fixed positive stability constant epsilon, showing sufficient conditions for near max-norm-margin optimality before updates become gradient-like, while reaching a target Euclidean margin only much later. This sharpens the known zero-epsilon versus positive-epsilon dichotomy for Adam.

entry.title: Future Information-Directed Sampling for Bayesian Nonstationary Bandits

author.name: Yichen Song, Alessio Russo, Aldo Pacchiano

entry.summary: Proposes FIDS, a Bayesian nonstationary bandit algorithm that explicitly explores to gather information about future optimal arms rather than only reducing uncertainty about the currently best arm. FIDS matches Thompson Sampling regret up to a small constant while exploiting its forward-looking exploration to adapt when the optimal arm changes over time.

entry.title: Fisher-Informed Recalibration for Feedback-Based On-Policy Self-Distillation of LLMs

author.name: Seohyun Lee, Dong-Jun Han, Seyyedali Hosseinalipour, Christopher G. Brinton

entry.summary: FIRE addresses unstable optimization in feedback-based on-policy self-distillation of LLMs, where a single model is both teacher and student and training can collapse. It uses Fisher information to recalibrate supervision separately for correct responses (re-weighted on-policy SFT) and incorrect ones (targeting disproportionate feedback components).

entry.title: Counterexamples to Local Reconstruction Gain as a Proxy for Final Fidelity in Residual Completion

author.name: Yasuto Hoshi, Daisuke Miyashita, Jun Deguchi

entry.summary: This paper provides counterexamples showing that improving a layer's attention-output reconstruction in sparse-attention residual completion does not necessarily improve final model output fidelity. Using RESA and Top-K+phi with frozen Qwen3-0.6B language models, the authors find interventions with positive local reconstruction gain but worse final KL fidelity than an all-abstain exact Top-K baseline, even on held-out requests.

entry.title: DreamingGoose: Staged Distillation from Autoregressive Transformers to Bidirectional Recurrent Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Julian Boesch, Andrew Wee, Alexander Stranzl

entry.summary: DreamingGoose converts pretrained Qwen3 teachers (1.7B and 8B) into attention-free bidirectional gated-delta-rule diffusion students via three-stage distillation, changing both architecture and objective. The honest negative results are notable: language modeling transfers only partially, in-context retrieval does not transfer (students score 0.000 on a recall probe where teachers score 0.34-0.58), and diffusion pretraining alone does not restore retrieval.

entry.title: FORGE: Form-Optimal Routing of Grounded Evidence for Frozen LLM Agents

author.name: Xi Xiao, Yunbei Zhang, Chen Liu, Lin Zhao, Jialin Chen, Tianchen Zhao, Xiang Xu, Youngeun Kim, Tianyang Wang, Min Xu

entry.summary: FORGE adapts frozen, closed-weight foundation models through per-query routing over a joint action space spanning both the form of grounded evidence provided and the reasoning depth allocated, finding that fixed defaults misallocate support on roughly 80% of queries. The framework operates under an entropy-regulated scheme to jointly optimize answer quality and token cost for deployed API models.

entry.title: Q-learning Penalized Transformer for Safe Offline Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Shengchao Hu, Peng Wang, Jifeng Hu, Qiyang Zhou, Anning Hu, Li Shen, Ya Zhang, Dacheng Tao

entry.summary: QPT is a training-inference consistent Transformer framework for safe offline RL that balances safety constraints, reward maximization, and behavior regularization by conditioning action generation on trajectory context and target return/cost with constraint-aware value estimation. It addresses the difficult interplay of three competing objectives in offline settings.

entry.title: On Parameter Symmetries and Conservation Laws in Gradient Flow

author.name: Khang Nguyen, Guido Mont\'ufar

entry.summary: This theory paper develops a unified geometric framework clarifying the precise relationship between parameter-space symmetries and conservation laws under gradient flow in neural networks, including when Noether-style correspondence holds. It introduces compositional identifiability and an inheritance principle for multilayer networks, with applications to loss landscape and implicit bias analysis.

entry.title: QuantForge: Discovering Residual Decompositions for MXFP4 Post-Training Quantization

author.name: Qiulin Shang, Zhoutong Wu, Jie Hu, Kun Yuan

entry.summary: Introduces QuantForge, an LLM-driven program evolution system for discovering effective design choices in strict MXFP4 W4A4 four-bit post-training quantization of LLMs. It records competing explanations, selects discriminating controls, and verifies that successor code implements conclusions, coordinating coordinate transforms and residual propagation decisions.

entry.title: Teach to Learn: Hint Annealing for Self-improving LLM Reasoning

author.name: Zile Wang, Zijian Li, Haodong Wang, Jian Liu, Qianli Liu, Lucas Muli, Blaze Chen, Song Guo

entry.summary: Identifies hinted reward shift in GRPO-based LLM reasoning training: when hints are used to rescue queries with all-incorrect rollouts, policy updates concentrate on hinted trajectories that are unavailable at evaluation, limiting genuine improvement. The proposed Hint Annealing gradually removes assistance so the model self-improves without dependence on hints. This improves the reward contrast problem for difficult training queries.

entry.title: DRIFT: Disentangled Responsive-Invariant Flow Transport for Single-Cell Perturbation Prediction

author.name: Mustapha Bounoua, Giulio Franzese, Pietro Michiardi

entry.summary: DRIFT predicts cellular responses to perturbations using flow matching with an explicit disentanglement of responsive from invariant cell-state components, avoiding confounding of perturbation effects with intrinsic cell-to-cell variability. Unlike prior disentangled approaches that impose prescribed perturbation mechanisms, it learns the response transport flexibly.

entry.title: Weighting Schedules Govern What and When Score-Based Generative Models Learn from Multimodal Data

author.name: J\'er\'emie Klinger, Rapha\"el Urfin, Giulio Biroli, Marylou Gabri\'e

entry.summary: Analyzes how the time-weighting schedule in the score-matching loss of diffusion/score-based models controls which features of multimodal data are learned and when. The work decomposes the integrated loss into single-time contributions at fixed signal-to-noise ratio and connects the schedule to a speciation time window in which trajectories commit to modes. This gives theory-grounded guidance for designing training schedules in generative models.

entry.title: Inductive Feedback for Mixed-Policy Distillation

author.name: Amir Moeini, Huaijiang Zhu, Daniel Havir, Shangtong Zhang

entry.summary: Analyzes on-policy distillation where verbal feedback from a capable model conditions the teacher, and identifies two failure modes of the standard objective: transferring unmotivated teacher preferences and underusing the feedback's guidance. The proposed method changes both the divergence minimized and the target distribution to address these limitations. Useful for post-training LLMs when programmatic verifiers are unavailable.

entry.title: Reward-Aligned Reweighting for On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Haofeng Xu, Junwei Su, Lansong Diao, Wenchao Zhou, Chuan Wu

entry.summary: The paper identifies that standard on-policy distillation weights token-level distillation uniformly, mismatching actual decision utility, and proposes R2-OPD, which uses verified trajectory outcomes to reweight token-level distillation terms. This avoids suppressing viable student strategies or reinforcing unreliable paths in LLM reasoning distillation.

entry.title: Statistical Testing for Multiple Instance Learning via Selective Inference with Applications to Computational Pathology

author.name: Noriaki Hashimoto, Shuichi Nishino, Teruyuki Katsuoka, Tomohiro Shiraishi, Daiki Miwa, Hiroyuki Hanada, Jun Sakuma, Hidekata Hontani, Hiroaki Miyoshi, Ichiro Takeuchi

entry.summary: Formulates evaluation of high-attention instances in attention-based multiple instance learning as statistical hypothesis testing using selective inference, determining whether selected patches significantly deviate from normal tissue. Applied to whole-slide image analysis in computational pathology, it adds statistical rigor to attention-as-explanation.

entry.title: The Judge Is Not Its Twin: Post-training makes a model's writing more predictable but barely moves its taste, as a judge, toward predictable writing

author.name: Arman Nik Khah, Arvin Bahreini

entry.summary: Following OLMo-2 and Zephyr 7B families through their public training stages, this study measures each stage both as a short-story writer and as a pairwise judge. As writers, fully trained models do drift toward finding earlier-stage outputs more familiar, confirming predictability concerns, but as judges the models barely shift toward rewarding predictable writing, so LLM-judged creativity evaluations are less compromised than feared. An empirical answer to an important question about automated evaluation of creativity.

entry.title: One-Step Generative Modeling via Unbalanced Optimal Transport

author.name: Yirong Shen, Mengfei Xia, Junpeng Jing, Lu Gan, Cong Ling

entry.summary: The paper improves one-step generative models based on drifting-transport training by treating generated and real samples asymmetrically: allowing the mass assigned to real samples to adapt while keeping every generated sample fully transported, replacing the exact mini-batch mass matching of balanced optimal transport. This improves generation quality across several feature settings.

entry.title: SynCo: Learning Cross-Modal Synergy by Contrasting Interaction Residuals

author.name: Yavuz Yarici, Ghassan AlRegib

entry.summary: Proposes SynCo, a multimodal contrastive learning method that directly addresses synergy undertraining by supervising an interaction residual, grounded in Partial Information Decomposition's redundancy-uniqueness-synergy decomposition. Standard contrastive objectives mostly capture redundant cross-modal information, and SynCo is designed to learn synergistic information that only emerges jointly.

entry.title: Byzantine-Robust Federated RAG via Aligned Calibration and Fixed-Membership Conformal Prediction

author.name: Prasanjit Dubey, Xiaoming Huo

entry.summary: Proposes a conformal-prediction framework for federated retrieval-augmented generation that maintains guaranteed answer coverage even when an unknown subset of nodes is Byzantine, compromised, or misled by prompt injections hidden in documents. Aligned calibration and fixed-membership techniques deliver statistical robustness guarantees for privacy-preserving federated RAG.

entry.title: Geometry-Adaptive Mechanisms for Private Synthetic Data

author.name: Raoof Zare Moayedi, Amir R. Asadi, Mohammad Hossein Yassaee, Gholamali Aminian

entry.summary: The paper proposes Adaptive Pruned-PMM, a pure epsilon-differentially private mechanism for synthetic data whose Wasserstein error adapts to a multiscale packing-growth dimension of the data support. While worst-case error in d dimensions scales as (epsilon n)^(-1/d), the method escapes this curse of dimensionality when data lie on a lower-dimensional set. This gives geometry-aware utility guarantees for private data release.

entry.title: Reliable Replay through Spatial Coherence in Online Continual Learning

author.name: Haixiang Sun, Jiefu Zhang, Yinghao He, Yang Xu, Vaneet Aggarwal, Bharat Bhargava, Andrew L. Liu

entry.summary: SPHERE is a general replay-allocation method for online continual learning that aggregates signed prospective loss changes using a representation kernel to distinguish coherent risk increases from isolated spikes, then redistributes replay budget via entropy-regularized transport. This improves on loss-increase-based memory prioritization that overweights individual outlier samples.

entry.title: Multi-Marginal Inverse Optimal Transport for Contrastive Learning Via Explicit Anchor-Positive-Negative Coupling

author.name: Ngoc-Hai Nguyen, Thuan Nguyen, Prakash Ishwar, Shuchin Aeron

entry.summary: Neg-MMIOT-CL extends inverse optimal transport approaches to representation learning by incorporating negative pairs through a multi-marginal OT coupling between anchor, positive, and negative distributions, which the authors show prevents dimensional collapse suffered by negative-free IOT methods. This yields a genuinely contrastive formulation grounded in global transport couplings.

entry.title: Annealed Sinkhorn with Momentum: Certified Unregularized Optimal Transport in Linear Memory

author.name: Samuel J. K. Chin, Maximilian Schiffer

entry.summary: The paper characterizes Bregman Douglas-Rachford splitting for unregularized discrete optimal transport, showing it coincides with warm-started inexact proximal point IPOT with one inner Sinkhorn iteration and can be rewritten as annealed Sinkhorn with an implicit inverse-linear temperature schedule and log-scaling momentum. The dual formulation eliminates the primal transport plan, cutting memory from quadratic to linear while providing anytime primal-dual certificates.

entry.title: Kafila: Serving Large Language Models on a Trusted Set of Heterogeneous Commodity Machines

author.name: Murtaza Rangwala, Richard O. Sinnott, Rajkumar Buyya

entry.summary: Kafila is a system for serving LLMs pooled across a trusted, bounded set of heterogeneous consumer machines, such as a research group's computers, forming a ring protocol that assembles from behind NATs and handles the pipeline-pacing problem where every admitted device must contribute. It addresses the gap left by open swarm systems that untrusted-membership groups cannot use, carefully partitioning the model before serving begins.

entry.title: Natural State-Prediction Accuracy can Hide Weak Controlled Responsiveness in VLA Readouts

author.name: Hyungjoon Kim, Wonbin Son, Mi Young Lee, Jun Young Lee, Seungmin Rho

entry.summary: The paper introduces an evaluation framework for vision-language-action (VLA) model readouts that separates prediction accuracy, target-state responsiveness, and context stability using physically validated observations that cross target coordinates with robot contexts. It demonstrates that high natural-trajectory accuracy can coexist with weak controlled target-state responsiveness, because natural observations confound object state with robot configuration, occlusion, and task progress. This exposes an important flaw in how VLA representation quality is typically evaluated.

entry.title: From Perception to Integration: Revisiting the Internal Dynamics of Reasoning in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Rong Yu Xu, Prayag Tiwari, Shaolei Zhang

entry.summary: The paper probes the internal dynamics of vision-language models on controlled tasks involving feature binding, numerosity, spatial relations, and amodal completion, plus a composite task combining them, using matched counterfactual image pairs. Across four models, direct answers, hidden-state readouts, and state interventions show individual judgments can be made without explicit reasoning and that intervening on corresponding states affects answers. The composite answer becomes decodable from hidden states and usable from shortened traces, often before explicit reasoning concludes.

entry.title: Continuous Variational Synthesis

author.name: Alan N. Amin, Mattia G. Gollub, Andrei Slabodkin, Elizabeth B. Wood, Eli N. Weinstein

entry.summary: The authors train variational synthesis models for DNA design in continuous space with stochastic gradient descent, then apply post-training quantization to satisfy chemical synthesis and hardware constraints. This avoids the discrete optimization bottleneck and enables models to meet stringent reward criteria while maintaining diversity across quadrillions of synthesizable sequences.

entry.title: Which the Eye Fears: Writing with Read-Blindness Explains Massive Activations in Transformers

author.name: Swagatam Mukhopadhyay, Vishal Vivek Saley, Vraj Parikh, Mausam

entry.summary: The paper provides a mechanistic explanation for massive activation features in transformers: attention and feed-forward blocks systematically ignore MA coordinates when reading but not when writing, creating a read-write asymmetry that blocks corrective feedback while allowing continued accumulation. This operator-level analysis validates and refines prior hypotheses about FFN amplification as the primary cause.

entry.title: ScopeIF: Improving Scope-Aware Precise Instruction-Following in Large Language Models via Graded Reward Modeling

author.name: Bosi Wen, Yilin Niu, Xiaoying Ning, Ying Zhang, Hongning Wang, Minlie Huang

entry.summary: ScopeIF is a training framework for precise instruction-following that factorizes objective constraints into three decoupled dimensions under a unified schema, capturing constraints that govern specific response segments rather than the whole output. It replaces binary per-constraint rewards with graded reward modeling to increase data diversity and provide denser supervision for complex constraints. This targets a common failure where models over- or under-apply scoped constraints.

entry.title: Self-Reports Do Not Identify Self-Models: An Identifiability Test for Counterfactual Reports

author.name: Phongsakon Mark Konrad, Toygar Tanyel, Serkan Ayvaz

entry.summary: This paper argues that LLM self-reports are only evidence about behavior in the prompt environment, not about an internal self-model, and introduces an identifiability test for counterfactual reports about affect-like states under activation interventions. Across three open instruction models, wrong-source demonstrations pull reports toward the source answer family, though explicit mechanism binding reduces this pull. It offers a rigorous caution for interpretability work that treats self-report accuracy as evidence of self-monitoring.

entry.title: CertMark: Distortion-Free Multi-Bit Watermarking with Certified Decoding

author.name: Pawe{\l} Batorski, Przemys{\l}aw Spurek, Paul Swoboda

entry.summary: Introduces CertMark, a distribution-preserving multi-bit watermark for LLMs that seeds an exact Gumbel-max sampler with the embedded message rather than biasing next-token probabilities, eliminating the text-quality trade-off of prior watermarking schemes. It provides certified decoding with a bounded abstention rule via model-agnostic text-only and model-aware decoders. Advances both watermarking robustness and formal guarantees for AI-generated text provenance.

entry.title: LLMs Trust Their Own: Identity-Dependent Conformity in Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Liron Soffer, Ravid Shwartz-Ziv, Chen Shani

entry.summary: Studies whether LLM conformity to incorrect answers in multi-agent settings depends on other agents' social identity (AI vs human, model family, or arbitrary minimal group). Across 12 open-weight models and nine tasks, it finds a bidirectional identity effect: in-group consensus increases conformity beyond what consensus alone predicts. Directly relevant to AI safety and multi-agent deployment, suggesting identity cues can distort collective correctness.

entry.title: MAS-OPD: On-Policy Distillation for Multi-agent Systems

author.name: Qiyong Zhong, Mao Zheng, Mingyang Song, Houcheng Jiang, Jiajie Su, Huwei Ji, Li Zhang, Junfeng Fang

entry.summary: MAS-OPD extends on-policy distillation to multi-agent systems, replacing RL whose team-level rewards leave credit assignment undetermined, or per-task local rewards requiring redesign. Token-level teacher supervision on student-sampled trajectories gives a denser signal for training interdependent agents with stable role competence and collaboration. This addresses the costly inference-time orchestration that dominates current MAS deployments.

entry.title: Rewarding Novel Deductions: Solver-guided Process Rewards for Logical Reasoning

author.name: Muhammad Asif Ali, Wenqing Wang, Huan Wang, Mohammad Raza

entry.summary: SPRING uses an SMT solver as a training-time verifier of intermediate reasoning steps, providing process-level rewards rather than only final-answer supervision for logical reasoning. The approach targets small LLMs prone to inconsistent multi-step deductions on structured constraint problems.

entry.title: TRACE: Single-Pass Decoding-Trace Risk Localization for Generation Calibration

author.name: Yuebin Xu, Xuemei Peng, Junlan Chen, Zhiyi Chen, Zeyi Wen

entry.summary: TRACE is a single-pass confidence estimator for LLM outputs that preserves decoding-time uncertainty signals instead of compressing them into a global score. It records token-level surprisal and predictive entropy during decoding, applies local risk operators to keep uncertainty signals localized, and uses these to flag responses that fail at critical tokens like numbers or factual claims. This targets answer-level calibration, where fluent responses can still be locally wrong.

entry.title: From Script to Drama: An Agentic Framework for Controllable Multi-Speaker Dialogue TTS

author.name: Kangxiang Xia, Xinfa Zhu, HangRui Hu, Kexin Huang, Wenjie Tian, Ziyue Jiang, Bingshen Mu, Jingbin Hu, Ting He, Lei Xie, Jin Xu

entry.summary: Proposes an agentic framework for multi-speaker dialogue TTS built on ControlEdit-TTS, which unifies instruction-following synthesis with natural-language attribute editing so expressive errors can be fixed without regenerating speech. A critique-driven loop performs utterance-level and scene-level refinement for long-form dialogues.

entry.title: One Evaluation, Any Operating Point: Hypernetwork-Amortized MeanFlow for 3D MRI Reconstruction

author.name: Ruibo Wang

entry.summary: Fine-tunes a one-step 3D MeanFlow patch model for accelerated MRI reconstruction through a differentiable conjugate-gradient projection, with a hypernetwork mapping the full operating point (weight, acceleration, sampling pattern) to per-channel modulation. Notably, learning the acquisition mask yields larger gains than any other operating-point choice.

entry.title: PanOVOcc: Panoramic Embodied Open-Vocabulary Occupancy Mapping with Long-term Spatial Voxel Memory

author.name: Di Kuang, Mengfei Duan, Yuhang Wang, Weixing Peng, Kailun Yang

entry.summary: PanOVOcc is a training-free framework combining panoramic SLAM, open-vocabulary perception, and long-term voxel memory to build persistent, language-queryable semantic occupancy maps from panoramic sequences. It also introduces two new benchmarks, Pan-Replica and Pan-Holo360D, for evaluating this setting.

entry.title: SelfCue: Making a 3D CT Report Generator Say What It Already Knows

author.name: Renjie Liang, Yang Yang, Jinqian Pan, Zhengkang Fan, Chengkun Sun, Jie Xu

entry.summary: SelfCue exploits the gap between what a 3D CT report generator encodes in hidden states versus what it writes, showing macro AUROC drops from 0.848 in hidden states to 0.739 in generated reports across 18 CT-RATE abnormalities. Using contrastive decoding to promote hidden-state-supported content and suppress unsupported content raises clinical F1 to 0.481 and GREEN score to 0.510, with a distilled student retaining most gains.

entry.title: Federated 3D Gaussian Splatting for Large-Scale Scene Reconstruction at Wireless Edge

author.name: Guanlin Wu, Chao Hu, Pu Chen, Juyong Zhang, Han Hu, Shuguang Cui, Jie Xu

entry.summary: This paper proposes a resource-efficient federated learning framework for training large-scale 3D Gaussian Splatting models across wireless edge devices, addressing limited communication, computation, and GPU memory, cross-model structural inconsistency, and privacy leakage of raw visual data. It enables collaborative scene reconstruction without pooling images.

entry.title: SPACE: Sparse Predictive Attractor via Counterfactual Eviction for Streaming Video Memory

author.name: Hongjin Niu, Weizhan Zhang, Shuo Bao, Jiahao Wang, Muyan Jiao, Kairui Wen, Yong-Jin Liu

entry.summary: Defines streaming video memory eviction as counterfactual control over the future representations a memory supports, and introduces SPACE, which uses a frozen multi-horizon JEPA to predict futures induced by alternative eviction actions. Counterfactual utility and sloped scoring identify which entries to evict so the memory keeps supporting useful futures.

entry.title: Hierarchical Frequency-Domain Compression of Implicit Geometric Representations for Large-Scale Point Clouds

author.name: Manlin Yao, Jiabin Liu, Guan Wang, Haixu Liu, Hui Li

entry.summary: The paper proposes a unified framework for compressing large-scale point clouds into implicit geometric representations: the cloud is mapped to an implicit field in its bounding box, a Fourier pyramid captures global geometry in low-frequency components, and inter-scale high-frequency residuals plus conditional prediction preserve fine detail. This addresses the prohibitive memory and compute costs of implicit representations for complex geometry. It is a technically substantive contribution at the intersection of neural compression, implicit fields, and 3D geometry processing.

entry.title: FloodDiffusion 2: Efficient and Path Controllable Streaming Motion Generation

author.name: Yiyi Cai, Yuhan Wu, Kunhang Li, Tu Fangyuan, Xiangyue Zhang, Qiaoge Li, Zhixiang Wang, Kaipeng Zhang, Haiyang Liu

entry.summary: FD2 improves on FloodDiffusion, a state-of-the-art streaming motion generation model, with Partial Attention enabling KV-cached inference and shared-history packing, a Bregman criterion for path controllability, and a third advance for generation quality. It targets precise trajectory control and efficiency for real-world motion generation applications.

entry.title: Native Association: Confidence-Aware Human Perception in the Wild with a Foundation VLM

author.name: Igal Dmitriev, Ofir Liba

entry.summary: The authors fine-tune a small 0.77B vision-language model (Florence-2) to emit all per-person attributes (team, jersey number, etc.) as one grammar-constrained sequence, eliminating the error-prone detector-OCR-classifier stitching step. This makes binding errors structurally impossible and reduces residual misassociation to about 4x lower than zero-shot frontier VLM APIs (0.057 vs 0.21-0.24).

entry.title: MAD-Guard: Controlled Study of Autoregressive Generation versus Direct Decision Interfaces for Closed Multimodal Forensic Tasks

author.name: Hao Chen

entry.summary: A controlled study comparing autoregressive generation versus direct decision heads for closed multimodal forensic tasks on a matched Qwen3-VL-8B backbone, evaluating a progression of interfaces and decomposing latency into backbone, vocabulary, and head components. It asks when token generation is actually necessary for decisions with low output entropy. Findings inform efficient deployment of MLLMs for classification-style tasks.
