entry.title: CAST: Reconstruction-Coupled Acceleration of Interactive World Models

author.name: Leyang Chen, Junyi Wu, Fanqing Kong, Shaoqiu Zhang, Yulun Zhang

entry.summary: CAST accelerates interactive world models by selecting anchors based on interaction sensitivity and cross-layer coverage, reconstructing skipped residuals with a phase-aware mechanism, and coordinating historical KV routing by downstream reconstruction responsibility. It builds on the observation that interaction-induced feature changes correlate with approximation error.

entry.title: WorldWeave: Growing Persistent Geometric Worlds for Video Generation

author.name: Yifan Huang, Lifan Jiang, Qingyue Hao, Cheng Chen, Boxi Wu, Xiaoxue Ren, Xiaofei He, Dehai Zhao

entry.summary: WorldWeave decouples world-state maintenance from visual rendering in world models, combining diffusion-based elevation-map outpainting with agent-guided scene organization to build an expandable explicit 3D world with persistent structural memory. This supports consistent scene expansion and cross-view revisits that pure video world models lack.

entry.title: Text-Vision Synergistic Token Caching: A Training-Free Framework for Efficient Vision-Language-Action Inference

author.name: Qianer Li, Chengjie Zhang, Jingwen Chen, Zanjia Tong, Jiyuan Zhang, Hong Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes TVCache, a training-free, plug-and-play token caching framework for Vision-Language-Action models that exploits text-vision synergy, where textual semantics guide grounding of task-relevant visual regions. It filters attention heads by text-vision information focus and addresses head-wise reliability and layer-wise cache stability.

entry.title: Joint and Cross-Modal Video-Audio Generation and Editing: A Unified Formulation and Design Taxonomy

author.name: Abhinav Sharma, Sai Karthik Navuluru, Wang Wei, Daksh Dangi, Xiangbo Gao, Li Li, Bo Ni, Vardhan Dongre, Junda Wu, Xiyang Hu, Jiuxiang Gu, Seunghyun Yoon, Tong Yu, Chien Van Nguyen, Mohamed Elmoghany, Nedim Lipka, Hoda Eldardiry, Hongjie Chen, Tyler Derr, Thien Huu Nguyen, Zhengzhong Tu, Nesreen K. Ahmed, Franck Dernoncourt, Ryan A. Rossi

entry.summary: A survey providing the first systematic taxonomy of joint video-audio generation and editing, casting joint generation, cross-modal generation, and joint editing as problems over a single distribution of audio-visual pairs. It defines five design axes, nine edit categories spanning 28 edit types, and reviews methods, datasets, and metrics.

entry.title: Evidence Before Accuracy: A MRI-PET Fusion Network for Alzheimer Disease Classification with Causal Regional Validation

author.name: Saeid Firouzi Daghigh, Saeed Ayat

entry.summary: Presents a T1 MRI and FDG PET fusion network for Alzheimer classification achieving AUC 0.962 and accuracy 0.909 on 554 paired ADNI subjects at low cost, with causal regional validation to confirm predictions rest on AD-relevant neurobiology rather than dataset artifacts or non-brain content. It also quantifies how much slice geometry choices affect AUC.

entry.title: ACPruner: Visual Token Pruning as Biased Attention Coverage Maximization in LVLMs

author.name: Xu Li, Yuxuan Liang, Yi Zheng, Zhe Liu, Xiaolei Chen, Haotian Chen, Rui Zhu, Fan Shi, Xiangyang Xue

entry.summary: ACPruner reformulates visual token pruning for large vision-language models as a biased attention coverage maximization problem, selecting a compact token subset whose encoder-side attention jointly covers the image with priority to informative regions. The method is training-free and aims to cut the computational cost of processing large numbers of visual tokens.

entry.title: P4Q: Co-designing Token Pruning and Quantization for Vision-Language Model Acceleration

author.name: Haizhao Jing, Zhenhao Shang, Haokui Zhang, Rong Xiao, Peng Wang

entry.summary: P4Q is a co-design framework that jointly optimizes visual token pruning and low-bit post-training quantization for vision-language model inference, rather than treating the two compression axes independently or sequentially. The paper argues that their distinct objectives leave critical interactions unaddressed, and the joint design recovers performance lost under naive composition. This targets the practical deployment bottleneck of VLMs.

entry.title: Advancing Video-Text Pretraining with Multi-View Captions

author.name: Fida M. Thoker, Renaud Vandeghen, Karen Sanchez, Marc Van Droogenbroeck, Bernard Ghanem

entry.summary: The authors build a large-scale MLLM-based pipeline that generates multi-view captions (summary, detailed, reasoning-refined, and semantic positives) from 10 million videos to improve the quality of language supervision for video-text pretraining. This tackles the underexplored issue that web-scale video datasets carry sparse, low-fidelity single captions. Better supervision quality could lift a broad range of video understanding models.

entry.title: EvolvingAvatar: Interactive 3D Head Generation That Adapts as Conversations Unfold

author.name: Junjie Chen, Fei Wang, Kun Li, Yiqi Nie, Xun Yang, Yanbin Hao, Linfeng Zhang, Meng Wang

entry.summary: EvolvingAvatar is a causal 3D talking-head generator that uses test-time training to adapt to user face video and dyadic audio during live conversation. A dyadic context prediction objective gives a self-supervised signal without test-time motion labels, with persistent fast weights accumulating per-conversation adaptation.

entry.title: TriDrive: Joint Driver, Vehicle, and Road Modeling for Forecasting and Driver Monitoring

author.name: Yuhang Wang, Jingxin Yang, Chuheng Wei, Yuechen Guo, Jinghan Xu, Zhao Han, Hao Zhou

entry.summary: TriDrive is presented as the first unified framework that jointly forecasts driver kinematics, vehicle dynamics, and road demands for driver monitoring, using modality-specific encoders connected by directed residual connections. It combines an anchored kinematic driver representation, causal CAN-bus dynamics, and frozen V-JEPA 2 road latents, refined through an automation-conditioned transition model. The system is evaluated with real-time on-vehicle deployment, which is notable for this line of work.

entry.title: Distance-Residual Physics-Informed Neural Networks: A Deep Learning Framework for Differential and Partial Differential Inclusions

author.name: Maria Filipkovska, Juan Jos\'e Mar\'{\i}n, Isil Oner, Francisco Periago, Krzysztof Rykaczewski

entry.summary: DR-PINNs extend physics-informed neural networks to differential inclusions, where a differential operator is constrained to a set-valued map rather than equaling a function, by replacing the pointwise residual with the squared distance to the admissible set. For closed convex sets the squared distance is differentiable, enabling gradient-based training for this previously hard problem class.

entry.title: FutureRay: Control-Aligned Future Range for Agile Quadruped Navigation

author.name: Tianhao Zang, Shanze Wang, Ziqian Wang, Liyou Luo, Zihan Liu, Xingjian Xie, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: Predicts future clearance ranges across viewing directions and times, plus encounter risk, from depth-derived range history and robot motion, enabling quadrupeds to navigate around moving obstacles. Integrates reaction and braking limits into speed selection for agile navigation.

entry.title: Multi-Modal Non-Prehensile Estimation of Physical Parameters via Press-and-Pull Tipping

author.name: Steven M. Hyland, Jing Xiao, Cagdas D. Onal

entry.summary: Introduces a multi-modal estimation framework combining sliding interaction with a press-and-pull tipping primitive to recover object mass, center-of-mass height, and surface friction without a prior geometric model. The press-and-pull interaction stabilizes pivoting and increases the sliding threshold.

entry.title: FINGR: Learning Dexterous Hand Control for Real-World Rubik's Cube Solving

author.name: Yutong Liang, Quanquan Peng, Matthew Kim, Xiaolong Wang

entry.summary: FINGR learns single-handed Rubik's Cube manipulation, combining finger-relative geometric representations with future interaction prediction: a shared point encoder expresses the cube relative to each fingertip and learned future tokens receive contact-force supervision to coordinate supporting and pushing fingers across successive layer turns. Real-world contact-rich in-hand manipulation with sustained coordination is a demanding benchmark. It demonstrates advanced dexterous control on a classic hard task.

entry.title: FutureDuet: Decoupling Observation Access from Future Supervision in World Action Models

author.name: Jie Wu, Yuzhi Huang, Junqi Liu, Weichen Zhang, Haibin Huang, Yin Chen, Jingyan Jiang, Chi Zhang

entry.summary: FutureDuet observes that main and wrist cameras have very different visual dynamics, so it lets each visual stream in a World Action Model receive a different future supervision objective while both views remain available for control. Main-view future RGB models scene-level task evolution, while wrist-view supervision is tailored to local interaction changes despite viewpoint shifts and self-occlusion. This refines how future visual supervision is used for robot action generation.

entry.title: Aerial GRIPPER: A Gradient-based Real-time Inverse-game Predictor and Planner

author.name: Zeshuai Chen, Meng Wang, Jindou Jia, Xiang Yu, Lei Guo

entry.summary: The paper presents an aerial gripper system with a GRIPPER framework that models capture of non-cooperative targets as a general-sum pursuit-evasion game under incomplete information. Target cost parameters are inferred online and open-loop Nash equilibrium strategies are refined in a receding-horizon loop, using a gradient-based solver that avoids explicit Hessian inversion to exceed 50 Hz execution. This enables real-time game-theoretic planning for aerial interception.

entry.title: NavJev: Efficient Vision-Language Navigation via Action-Centric Visual Compression and Discriminative Action-Semantic Memory

author.name: Kai Sheng, Liuyi Wang, Jinlong Li, Haojie Dai, Chengju Liu, Qijun Chen

entry.summary: NavJev is an efficient zero-shot vision-language navigation framework that replaces repeated autoregressive multimodal reasoning with compact action-centric visual compression and lightweight typed action selection. It integrates waypoint geometry, BLIP captions, and RAM semantic tags into compressed representations, plus a discriminative action-semantic memory. This directly addresses the inference-latency bottleneck of MLLM-based embodied navigation.

entry.title: Robot Tool Design from Scratch via Behavior-Aware Hierarchical Optimization

author.name: Yinghan Chen, Xiyao Tian, Yizan Dai, Yuyang Li, Yixin Zhu

entry.summary: This paper studies task-driven robotic tool design from scratch, jointly deriving tool structure, shape, and action from the desired physical outcome rather than optimizing within a prescribed structure. The proposed HOT method uses a hierarchical optimization in which an upper level searches discrete structures with BASS while lower-level physical optimization evaluates behavior and returns milestone-based feedback. It frames tool design as a marker of intelligence beyond tool use.

entry.title: The Root Finding Problem Revisited: Beyond the Robbins-Monro procedure

author.name: Yue Yu, Moulinath Banerjee, Ya'acov Ritov

entry.summary: The paper introduces Sequential Probability Ratio Bisection (SPRB), a stochastic approximation algorithm that adapts to the local behavior of a regression function around its root. SPRB achieves optimal convergence rates and minimal asymptotic variance even when the derivative at the root is small or the function is discontinuous, regimes where classical Robbins-Monro degrades—in the discontinuous case SPRB attains exponential convergence versus 1/n. This is a substantive theoretical upgrade to a foundational algorithm family underlying SGD-style methods.

entry.title: Nonnegative DAG Learning via Concomitant Estimation

author.name: Madeline Navarro, Gonzalo Mateos, Samuel Rey

entry.summary: The NoCo estimator jointly learns directed acyclic graphs with nonnegative edge weights and exogenous noise variances in linear structural equation models. By exploiting nonnegativity, it imposes acyclicity directly on the adjacency matrix, avoiding the degenerate landscapes of squared-entry formulations, and blends a smoothed concomitant lasso with a log-determinant acyclicity constraint.

entry.title: New formulation helps RNA vaccines withstand high temperatures

author.name: Anne Trafton | MIT News

entry.summary: MIT researchers used an AI algorithm to optimize lipid nanoparticle formulations for mRNA vaccines, achieving vaccines stable for up to a year at room temperature or two months at nearly 100 degrees Fahrenheit. Mouse trials showed immune responses comparable to a Moderna-like Covid vaccine, and the algorithm's ability to work with small datasets substantially reduced the number of experiments needed.

entry.title: Improving Medical Calculation of LLMs with Embedded Coding

author.name: Tianshi Ming, Yingying Zhang, Xian Wu

entry.summary: MedCode is a framework that improves LLM performance on high-stakes medical calculations (dosing, organ-function assessment, prognostic scores) by training models to generate embedded executable code that delegates arithmetic to a deterministic interpreter. The model identifies the relevant calculator, extracts input variables, and executes a script to return exact values. This addresses a clinically critical weakness of LLMs in exact numerical outputs.

entry.title: Certifying Interventional Agreement Among Observationally Equivalent Causal Models

author.name: Sourena Khanzadeh, Daniel Platnick, Marjan Alirezaie, Hossein Rahnama

entry.summary: The paper introduces Interventional Separation Selection, an active-learning procedure that queries the true system with interventions on which candidate causal models disagree, discarding refuted candidates until no admissible intervention separates survivors. If the true system is among the candidates, the stopping condition certifies interventional agreement, a guarantee unattainable from observational data alone.

entry.title: Carnator: Fast Text-to-Video Generation with Generation-Native Compatibility-Guided Cross-Request Reuse

author.name: Xingkun Yin, Xuebin Tang, Mingkun Xu, Hongyang Du

entry.summary: Carnator accelerates text-to-video diffusion transformers via cross-request reuse guided by generation-native computational compatibility rather than coarse semantic similarity. Existing reuse approaches conflate semantic relatedness with computational compatibility, leading to either incompatible reuse or unrealized acceleration. The framework targets interactive and large-scale video serving by exploiting redundancy across requests.

entry.title: EMIR$^2$: Evolution-Aware Memory with Intent-Guided Multi-Round Retrieval

author.name: Jinlan Liu, Hongliang Sun, Yong Wang, Bolin Zhang, Dinabo Sui, Dianhui Chu, Zhiying Tu

entry.summary: Proposes EMIR2, a memory framework for LLM agents that maintains evolving historical knowledge through a state-evolving representation and adaptively retrieves evidence via intent-guided multi-round retrieval, addressing static memory and single-round retrieval limitations. This targets tracking factual changes and integrating distributed evidence across long interactions.

entry.title: SkillVine: Agent Skill Evolution via Branching Exploration

author.name: Kaiwei Liu, Jiqian Dong, Liran Dong, Shuai Mao, Mingming Zhao, Bufang Yang, Jie Chuai, Zhitang Chen, Guoliang Xing, Zhenyu Yan

entry.summary: Proposes SkillVine, which formulates automatic skill evolution for LLM agents as a graph search problem rather than the standard linear, sequential update of a skill library. A trunk-branch collaborative search with intelligent parent-node selection avoids local optima and explores more evolution paths. Skills are improved automatically using environment interaction trajectories.

entry.title: The Decomposition Tax: LLM Pipelines Lose Up to 40 Accuracy Points at Their Own Interfaces

author.name: Tianqi Bu, YuXuan Peng, Junteng Tu, Henghui Xiao

entry.summary: The paper quantifies a decomposition tax: holding model, problem, stage prompts, and completion budget fixed and varying only whether each pipeline stage can see the original problem, staged LLM pipelines lose up to 40.5 accuracy points at their own interfaces (gemma-3-12B on MATH-500). Across 21 open-weight models on GSM-Hard and MATH-500 with paired designs and multiple-comparison corrections, 70 of 118 primary tests survive BH correction, and a placebo carrying extra tokens but almost no problem content recovers nothing. This is a striking, well-controlled indictment of multi-stage pipeline designs that discard access to the original problem.

entry.title: Agentic Multi-Turn Reasoning: A Fairness Approach

author.name: Thanh-Dat Truong, Sankalp Pandey, Hugh Churchill, Jackson Cothren, Marios Savvides, Khoa Luu

entry.summary: Fair-MPO is a preference optimization framework for agentic learning that addresses long-horizon credit assignment and imbalanced data distributions via multi-level preference optimization with fairness-aware balancing of rare but informative reasoning behaviors. The framework targets multi-turn agentic systems with planning, tool use, verification, and memory updates.

entry.title: Dr. Free: You Don't Need Difficulty Rewards for Self-Evolving Search Agents

author.name: Zhipeng Qian, Zihan Liang, Yufei Ma, Jie Ma, Ben Chen, Huangyu Dai, Lingtao Mao, Xinyu Sun, Tong zhao, Xuxin Zhang, Qingpeng Cai, Peng Jiang, Qibin Hou

entry.summary: Identifies that difficulty-based proposer rewards in self-evolving search agent training conflate hard questions with evidence-requiring ones and are computationally expensive due to repeated solver rollouts. Dr. Free is the first self-evolving search framework that removes difficulty rewards and directly optimizes for question quality, reducing cost while improving cross-passage evidence reasoning.

entry.title: RoutePrism: Tracing Construction Order Effects in Agent Memory

author.name: Dong Xu, Zhangfan Yang, Jiantao Wu, Shipeng Zhang, Zexuan Zhu, Jiangqiang Li, Jun Zhang, Junkai Ji

entry.summary: RoutePrism is a diagnostic protocol that builds agent memory twice from the same source pool in different processing orders and traces which sources, compiled contexts, and answers differ, isolating order effects to the memory construction step. Its matched intervention shows restoring a single displaced record recovers over 60 percentage points of lost accuracy.

entry.title: QuantaSpike: Short-Window Spike-Driven Quantization for Large Language Models

author.name: Bang Hu, Guowei Zhu, Changze Lv, Xiaoqing Zheng, Fengzhe Zhang, Fan Zhang, Wei Cao

entry.summary: QuantaSpike is a spike-driven quantization framework for LLMs built on Logarithmic Ternary Integrate-and-Fire neurons, using ternary events with power-of-two membrane-response quanta to improve information per firing step while keeping event-driven inference. It addresses the problem that outlier-heavy activations typically require long firing windows or non-spiking paths.

entry.title: WebPageBench: Event-Level Verification and Controlled UI-Variant Generation for Web Agents

author.name: Anton Emelyanov, Maria Tikhonova, Zaven Martirosian, Sergei Averkiev, Alena Fenogenova

entry.summary: WebPageBench is an open framework evaluating web agents where every task is verified from the instrumented site's own event log, requiring no judge model or page scraping. Six mock sites emit typed events, and a configuration switch re-renders a task through different implementations of a UI control while keeping prompts and success conditions identical, enabling controlled measurement of interface sensitivity. This improves both reliability and scientific rigor of web-agent evaluation.

entry.title: EP-Mem: Elastic Privacy Memory for Social Relationship-Aware LLM Agents

author.name: Fengzhou Sun, Yuan Zhang, Xintong Yu, Jinyao Yan

entry.summary: EP-Mem introduces an elastic privacy-memory architecture for LLM agents acting as delegates in human-agent-human communication, framing privacy as user-owned boundary control across social roles. It combines token-level memory governed by configurable privacy policies with stratification of persons and events and fact-level rules for long-term relational disclosure.

entry.title: Continuous Context Management

author.name: William Hoy, Jingxuan Fan, Nurcin Celik, Xu Pan

entry.summary: This paper studies Continuous Context Management, where an LLM agent performs context compaction at every turn, emitting an updated memory plus an action instead of accumulating the full transcript until a threshold. Evaluated without fine-tuning on TerminalBench-2 using existing models including Claude Sonnet 4.6, Claude Opus 4.6, GLM-5, and Kimi K3, CCM sharply reduces cumulative input usage and active-prompt size but lowers task success for some models. It matters because context length cost is a central practical constraint for long-horizon agents, and this quantifies the accuracy-cost tradeoff of aggressive compaction.

entry.title: RIDE: Reference-Anchored Inference-Time Diffusion Editing for Scaffold Hopping

author.name: Ruoxi Gao, Frazier N. Baker, Trieu Nguyen, Xia Ning

entry.summary: RIDE is an inference-time diffusion editing framework for scaffold hopping in drug discovery that recovers the reference diffusion noise trajectory conditioned on the binding pocket and functional groups, selects an optimal trajectory segment for editing, and jointly enforces 2D structural novelty and 3D shape preservation of the reference ligand. It matters because scaffold hopping is a critical drug-discovery task where existing diffusion methods lack a principled way to balance novelty and shape preservation.

entry.title: Information Design Against Gaming and Learning Adversaries

author.name: Madhava Gaikwad

entry.summary: The paper analyzes how a principal deploying a binary classifier with abstention should choose which queries to abstain on, showing that the optimal policy flips depending on whether the adversary games a known classifier or learns an unknown one. The two natural defenses, fixed-rate and boundary-localized abstention, are proven Blackwell-incomparable. This formalizes an underexplored tension in strategic classification and information design.

entry.title: Typed Decision Models: An Early Evidence Audit and Evaluation Checklist

author.name: Lijuan Tang, Yuemeng Zheng

entry.summary: This paper audits the first wave of evaluation and replication work on typed decision models (TDMs), which return probability distributions over caller-defined options without generating text, following the release of TypeSafe's commercial model Jev on 15 September 2026. It reviews 28 papers posted 19-24 September, relating findings to label-probability classification, constrained decoding, reranking, calibration, and cascades. Early evidence suggests the typed readout itself shows no independent accuracy advantage over comparable label-probability readouts, with Jev's clearest gains in latency and cost.

entry.title: Superposed Inference for Hyperdimensional Computing

author.name: Quanling Zhao, Nilesh Prasad Pandey, Ye Tian, Tajana Rosing

entry.summary: SupHDC introduces a new inference paradigm for hyperdimensional computing that processes multiple queries through a shared encoding computation, superposing keyed queries before encoding and using slot-specific classifiers to recover individual predictions. A random-feature kernel view explains why exact hypervector recovery is unnecessary, and across ten datasets it achieves a 1.39x analytical speedup with no average accuracy loss. This is a meaningful efficiency advance for energy-efficient edge learning.

entry.title: CyberClear: A Benchmark for LLM Agent Systems on APT Attack Chain Provenance

author.name: Qi Chen, Fushuo Huo, Hangli Shen, Jingcai Guo, Shuhao Li, Guang Cheng

entry.summary: CyberClear is a benchmark evaluating LLM agents on reconstructing complete APT attack chains from long-context security logs, covering both single-step attacks and multi-stage attack chains and requiring attribution of attack stages. It fills a gap in cybersecurity agent benchmarks, which have focused on vulnerability discovery and exploitation rather than attack chain provenance under realistic logs. It matters for assessing whether agentic AI can support real security operations.

entry.title: SoFT: Soft Targets for Generalizable LLM Fine-Tuning

author.name: Huihao Jing, Wenbin Hu, Shaojin Chen, Haochen Shi, Zhongwei Xie, Guijia Zhang, Yuxuan Liu, Haoyu Huang, Haoran Li, Yangqiu Song

entry.summary: SoFT addresses multi-teacher, multi-domain distillation in supervised fine-tuning, where students must acquire diverse capabilities while preserving out-of-distribution generalization. It proposes soft-target fine-tuning that sets a minimum target on the base model's own distribution to balance learning teacher demonstrations against retaining existing capabilities. This gives practitioners explicit control over the in-distribution learning versus generalization trade-off.

entry.title: RECAST: Recasting Vision-Language Semantics into an Actionable Cost Map for Robot Navigation

author.name: Incheol Cho, Jintae Park, Jinkyu Kim, Jungbeom Lee, Jaegul Choo, Seokha Moon

entry.summary: RECAST is a robot navigation framework combining VLM reasoning with the spatial grounding of vision foundation models to build an Actionable Cost map from the robot's front view and the user's instruction. This addresses the gap that VLM-based navigation approaches bring semantic understanding but rarely ground it in the scene or align motion with it, while purely learned models fail off-distribution. The cost-map interface makes semantic reasoning directly actionable for motion planning.

entry.title: Learning to Refer: Client-Resolved Generation for Privacy-Aware Language Models

author.name: Jeongho Yoon, Chanhee Park, Yongchan Chun, Duong Tuan Thanh, Sungbin Han, Chanjun Park, Hyeonseok Moon, Heuiseok Lim

entry.summary: Client-Resolved Generation (CRG) is a generation interface that separates server-side generation from lexical realization of input-derived content: the client sends only pooled, noise-perturbed representations, and input-derived output content is represented via request-local positional references. This protects against reconstruction from intermediate representations that defeat earlier privacy-preserving LLM schemes. It addresses gaps where prior approaches traded utility or left parts of the pipeline exposed.

entry.title: Logic Gate Networks and Lookup Table Networks as Lightweight Hardware Classifiers for Inter-patient ECG Arrhythmia Classification

author.name: Wout Mommen, Lars Keuninckx, Siddharth Patil, Paul Detterer, Achiel Colpaert, Piet Wambacq

entry.summary: The authors generalize deep differentiable logic gate networks to N-input lookup table networks using a multiplexer-based differentiable formulation, and apply them to inter-patient ECG arrhythmia classification on MIT-BIH. The resulting models achieve up to 94.41% accuracy while relying only on binary logic operations, enabling very low-power inference. This is relevant for deploying neural classifiers on resource-constrained medical hardware.

entry.title: Progression- vs Automata-based Anticipatory Monitoring of LTL over Finite Traces (Extended Version)

author.name: Sarah Winkler, Toryn Klassen, Sheila McIlraith, Marco Montali

entry.summary: The paper compares progression-based and automata-based approaches to anticipatory runtime monitoring of linear-time temporal properties over finite traces, where monitoring accounts for possible future continuations, including properties with arithmetic constraints. It evaluates the trade-offs of the two monitoring representations. This formal-methods work is relevant to verifying safety properties of autonomous and agentic systems at runtime.

entry.title: D-JEPA: Design-Recoverable JEPA Representation with Swappable Physics Decoders

author.name: Nitin Nagesh Kulkarni, Aashwin Anand Mishra, Yin Yu, Peter Lyu

entry.summary: Proposes D-JEPA, a geometry-centric JEPA that computes a compact representation from geometry alone and reuses it across operating conditions and physical response spaces via lightweight physics-specific decoders, with a design-recoverability objective preserving design-variable information in the latent. This addresses entanglement of geometry with task-specific physics in standard JEPAs.

entry.title: BITS: Rethinking Fair and Comprehensive Evaluation for Irregular Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Kangjia Yan, Linfeng Wang, Tianen Shen, Xiangfei Qiu, Ruitong Zhang, Hao Miao, Jilin Hu, Chenjuan Guo, Bin Yang, Christian S. Jensen

entry.summary: BITS is a standardized, reproducible benchmark for irregular time series forecasting covering eleven datasets from nine domains, characterizing irregularity via missing rates and patterns and unifying previously inconsistent protocols. It aims to enable fair comparison across methods with both error-based and richer metrics. This addresses a persistent evaluation fragmentation problem in the field.

entry.title: Chameleon: Dynamic Format Adapter for Efficient Diffusion

author.name: Arnab Sanyal, Sandeep Chinchali

entry.summary: Chameleon is a post-training quantization framework for diffusion models that treats the number format itself as a discrete variable, chosen per weight channel and per layer-timestep activation bucket at fixed bit-width. This exploits the shift in activation distributions along the diffusion process from heavy-tailed to tightly clustered, improving efficiency on memory-constrained accelerators.

entry.title: CodeActionBench: Evaluating Agentic Code-as-Policy for Embodied Manipulation

author.name: Yiheng Lyu, Xueying Jiang, Wenhao Li, Shijian Lu, Gongjie Zhang

entry.summary: CodeActionBench is a 25-task benchmark evaluating whether general-purpose multimodal models can perform agentic Code-as-Policy for embodied manipulation — selecting visual evidence, forming 3D estimates, constructing manipulation targets, and iteratively executing and revising code policies without task-specific fine-tuning, demonstrations, or privileged state. A shared robot API leaves task-dependent decisions to the agent. It probes a capability gap between visual reasoning and physical action.

entry.title: GroupMask: Layer-Adaptive Group-wise Sparsity for Semi-Structured LLM Pruning

author.name: Zhengao Li, Shuoqiu Li, Xiaofang Zhang, Yukai Jin, Gokcen Kestor, Yanfu Zhang, Yiming Zeng, Bin Ren, Chuxu Zhang, Shangqian Gao

entry.summary: GroupMask proposes group-level sparsity for LLM pruning that partitions weight matrices into regular groups and allows per-layer sparsity ratios to vary under a global budget, questioning whether adaptive allocation truly underperforms under semi-structured constraints. It introduces a method generating group selectors for all layers simultaneously. This revisits a widely held assumption in the LLM compression literature.

entry.title: LRC-JEPA: Disentangling Dynamics and Residual Context for Efficient World Models

author.name: Luzhe Huang, Lei Chu, Jingyi Liang, Yuhuan Zhao

entry.summary: LRC-JEPA is a lightweight JEPA world model that separates action-conditioned dynamics from predictable visual context by routing information into a compact predictive latent used for planning and learned residual-context embeddings used for reconstruction. A differentiable residual channel prevents nuisance appearance from entangling controllable state and degrading planning in complex scenes. This improves efficient latent-space planning.

entry.title: Learn Here, Move Less Elsewhere: Input-Conditioned Plasticity from Retained-Domain Activation Atlases

author.name: Jiangtao Lin, Bangyang Wei, Yihang Ding, Siyi Liu, Yuhan Dong

entry.summary: ATLAS turns retained-domain representations into an input-dependent adaptation rule, using an activation atlas of local reference centers and directional filters to condition a shared low-rank residual during fine-tuning. On Qwen3-8B it achieves lower mean retained-output KL divergence than seven published baselines at matched coding performance across seeds. This tackles the problem of task fine-tuning rewriting behavior beyond the target task.

entry.title: No Pain, More Gain: Iterative Merging for Effective Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Seonghyeon Kim, Chaeyun Jang, Noah Lee, Boseop Kim, Juho Lee

entry.summary: This work studies multi-teacher on-policy distillation where teachers share a reference model but diverge through different post-training, finding the student initialization strongly affects recovery of teacher capabilities and that benchmark scores poorly predict good initializations. It shows model-merge initializations can start below SFT warm-up yet finish higher after distillation, and analyzes what makes merging effective.

entry.title: Learning to Act under Visual Interruptions with Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Mingle Jiang, Rui Xu, Yunke Wang, Chang Xu

entry.summary: Introduces MAIL-Bench, a benchmark that interrupts different cameras at multiple stages of a VLA policy's successful reference trajectories to measure how well manipulation policies continue acting without subsequent observations from the missing view. It addresses an underexplored robustness dimension of VLA models relevant to real deployment.

entry.title: Alignment Games: A Framework for Conceptual Repair in Human-AI Collaboration

author.name: Hari Subramonyam, Maneesh Agrawala, Sean Follmer

entry.summary: The authors introduce Alignment Games, a framework making task-relevant conceptual misalignment between humans and AI visible and repairable during collaboration. They characterize task-specific conceptual frames via attributes, values, relations, constraints, and priorities, and define alignment moves that intervene on situations and reasoning.

entry.title: The Hidden Ratio in Adam: Stable Structure, Compression, and Sign Dynamics

author.name: Yihe Zhou, Tongtian Zhu, Yingxiao Huo, Satya Prakash Dash, Can Wang, Samuel Kaski, Mingfei Sun

entry.summary: The paper analyzes Adam's optimizer dynamics in the tied-beta regime, showing its adaptive behavior can be expressed through a transformed moment ratio with approximately scale-stable, heavy-tailed distributions across tasks and scales. This stability yields practical consequences including a useful recurrence and implications for compression and sign dynamics.

entry.title: A Unified Uncertainty Representation for Graph Neural Networks via Doubly-Spectral Stochastic Expansion

author.name: Fred Xu, Thomas Markovich, Florence Regol, Yizhou Sun

entry.summary: Models uncertain GNN node embeddings as random graph signals, combining graph Fourier filters for structural variation with orthogonal-polynomial chaos for latent stochastic variation. This doubly-spectral expansion yields a single representation supporting calibration, energy-based OOD detection, and distribution-shift robustness with task-matched readouts.

entry.title: Mechanistic Interpretability Reveals Shared Causal Subspaces in Brain-to-Speech Decoders

author.name: Maryam Maghsoudi, Ayushi Mishra, Sanghamitra Dutta

entry.summary: Uses activation patching, a mechanistic interpretability technique, on brain-to-speech decoders with paired recordings of vocalized, mimed, and imagined speech to identify which internal neurons carry cross-modal information and whether they are shared across speech forms. Provides causal insight into how decoders represent different speech modalities, informing improved covert speech decoding.

entry.title: Analytic-Walk Rotary Positional Encodings for Graphs

author.name: Jiaqing Xie, Yuxin Wang, Xipeng Qiu

entry.summary: AW-RoPE extends rotary positional encodings to graphs by placing rotations on edges and summing transported features over all walks, so that contributions along different routes can reinforce or cancel, unlike prior spectral-coordinate schemes that depend only on node endpoints. It offers an exact differentiable linear-solve variant and a truncated sparse variant, with proven forward and parameter-derivative properties. This is a novel structural positional encoding for graph transformers.

entry.title: Write Back the $\Delta$: Revisiting the Same Tokens with Fresh Representations

author.name: Wencheng Ye, Anning Hu, Xiangdong Zhang, Tianyi Wang, Yikang Li, Hengyu Jin, Bing Li, Junchi Yan

entry.summary: The paper proposes feeding back the depth increment Delta (newly accumulated computation between two layers) rather than full residual states as an inference-time feedback signal for transformers, enabling deeper computation to refine earlier representations without re-executing depth. The authors argue Delta is more effective, composable, and scalable than existing residual-stream modification approaches. This adds a mechanism for adaptive computation at inference time.

entry.title: On the Pitfalls of Verbalized Confidence Priors for Calibrating Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Shuoyuan Wang, Beier Luo, Hao Zeng, Chengyao Yu, Songxin Zhang, Zejian Xie, Bingyi Jing, Hongxin Wei

entry.summary: This paper shows that large reasoning models' verbalized confidence distributions are heavily concentrated on a few high values, and this confidence prior persists through confidence-aware RL, suppressing gradient updates for rarely sampled confidence values and inflating expected Brier risk. The authors prove this theoretically and propose CalibSFT, a plug-and-play supervised fine-tuning stage to widen the confidence distribution before RL-based calibration.

entry.title: Structuring Relations Among Learning Paradigms via Protocol--Objective--Resource Reductions

author.name: Junwei Su, Changjie Wang, Dongyang Chang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a protocol-objective-resource (POR) framework that formally specifies machine learning paradigms (supervised, transfer, continual, meta-learning) via environment classes, observation protocols, admissible learners, and resource accounting, then defines reductions between them. This clarifies when one paradigm is genuinely distinct, a special case of another, or part of a hierarchy.

entry.title: Adaptive Latent Capacity for World Models

author.name: Idan Achituve, Lior Dikstein, Idit Diamant, Arnon Netzer, Hai Victor Habi

entry.summary: ALeWM is a JEPA-based world model that learns to concentrate predictive information in compact prefixes of a wide latent representation, learning a sequence-conditioned distribution over prefix lengths. It introduces MixSIGReg, an anti-collapse regularizer against a prior-weighted mixture, to organize latent coordinates by predictive importance.

entry.title: The limits of exactness: On the failure of automatic differentiation in physics-informed machine learning

author.name: Ameya D. Jagtap

entry.summary: This position-style paper argues that automatic differentiation, despite machine-precision exactness, can produce derivatives that are wrong for the physics at hand because AD lacks notions of physical structure such as convection directionality, conservation, dispersion, and thermodynamic consistency. The author calls for physics-aware differentiation in physics-informed machine learning. This is a provocative critique of the computational backbone of PINNs.

entry.title: Simulation-Free Learning of GP-SDEs from Irregular Observations

author.name: Zhidi Lin, Yuhao Liu, Ying Li, Edwin Fong, Petar Djuri\'c

entry.summary: GP-SDE Matching is a simulation-free variational framework for learning Gaussian process drift in continuous-time stochastic differential equations from noisy, irregular observations. It analytically marginalizes the sparse GP posterior into a tractable drift-matching objective and introduces an irregular-time-aware variational state posterior for smoothing.

entry.title: Downstream-Aware Context Selection for Online In-Context Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Ruihan A. Li, Shangtong Zhang, Rohan Chandra

entry.summary: The paper proposes a bounded-history context-management framework for in-context RL that predicts the task-dependent downstream effect of removing historical interactions, defining a deletion ordering and a decision-dependent context budget. This reduces token cost of conditioning on ever-growing histories without parameter updates.

entry.title: Apparent Compression, Real Stability: The Intrinsic Dimension of Learning a Quantum Wavefunction

author.name: Lu Wei, Yufeng Wang, Chenfeng Cao, Haibin Ling

entry.summary: The paper measures intrinsic dimension for variational Monte Carlo, training a small latent vector mapped by a frozen random transform to network weights under the standard natural-gradient optimizer. It finds training needs surprisingly few directions, with the apparent compression reflecting genuine stability properties of the learning problem rather than artifacts.

entry.title: Feedback-Robust AI for Patient Knowledge Graphs

author.name: Mohammed Sameer Syed

entry.summary: The paper introduces ClosedLoopBench, a benchmark of 29 signed relations grounded in physics and pharmacology across 3,442 VitalDB surgical cases with negative-control action streams, to test whether patient knowledge graph estimators in anesthesia and ICU settings are robust to clinician feedback loops. It shows six of twelve estimators declare many spurious relations significant, even after calibration.

entry.title: GTRL: Grounding Divide-and-Conquer Value Learning with Temporal Differences

author.name: Abdul Monaf Chowdhury, MD Sameer Iqbal Chowdhury, Shifat E Arman, Md Mehedi Hasan

entry.summary: GTRL fixes two pathologies of divide-and-conquer value learning in offline goal-conditioned RL: stochastic-dynamics bias toward lucky trajectories and missing value updates for subgoal pairs unconnected in data. It adds a one-step TD target, which is correct over a single step and needs no subgoal, to the transitive composition so every pair receives an update.

entry.title: The Selection Rule Decides the Winner: A Pre-Registered Audit of Open-Set Graph Anomaly Detection

author.name: Farhan Shahriyar Hossain, Taufikur Rahman Fuad, Md Abrar Jahin, Md Rizwan Parvez

entry.summary: A pre-registered audit showing that common evaluation conventions in open-set graph anomaly detection (best-epoch test scoring, copied baselines, relabeled minority classes) substantially determine published method rankings. The authors re-run DEMO and NSReg with a purpose-built detector, OUTPOST, under a uniform protocol with identical seeds and splits across eight graphs.

entry.title: SafeMol: Dual-Modality Safety Alignment for Molecular Multimodal Models

author.name: Xinmiao Wang, Ruijie Wang, Menghui Wang, Jiawei Chen, Haoyue Deng, Ran Zhang, Xingxuan Zhang, Xiao Wang

entry.summary: SafeMol reveals jailbreak vulnerabilities in molecular multimodal models under both text-only and graph-conditioned settings, and introduces SafeMolBench, a 3702-sample benchmark spanning 618 hazardous molecules with hazardous-harmful, hazardous-allowed, and utility-replay subsets. The work aims to align safety, over-refusal, and utility across input modalities.

entry.title: dOPT: Differentiating Conic Optimization via Geometric Reduction

author.name: Fengyu Yang, Connor W. Magoon, Tyler Watts, Shahar Z. Kovalsky

entry.summary: Presents dOPT, a solver-agnostic method for differentiating through conic optimization layers by reducing the problem at a computed primal-dual solution to an equality-constrained quadratic program that preserves the solution and its sensitivities. The reduction captures local conic geometry, remains valid at singular configurations, and requires only one symmetric linear solve.

entry.title: Spexis: Speculative Lookahead Scheduling for LLM Inference

author.name: Hyungyu Jung, Jaehyeok Yu, Hoonseo Choi, Sungkyun Kim, Jinho Lee, Jiwon Seo

entry.summary: Spexis is a multi-GPU LLM inference framework that runs speculative decoding in parallel with normal execution as a new parallelism axis, without increasing KV-cache memory usage, and uses lookahead scheduling to predict speculation quality and future memory pressure. Built on vLLM, it achieves substantial serving speedups across GPU configurations by reducing wasted speculation, eviction, and recomputation.

entry.title: PhysioTRACE: Provenance-Aware Stress Tests for Physiological Foundation Models

author.name: Ayana Mussabayeva, Anuar Aimoldin, Olivier Oullier, Xue Liu, Kun Zhang

entry.summary: PhysioTRACE is a four-axis behavioral audit framework for frozen physiological encoders that tests whether models exploit acquisition-provenance shortcuts (recording conditions correlated with diagnosis). It separates decodability from reliance via Recover, Stress, Intervene, and Verify axes, with matched random-projection baselines for certification.

entry.title: ORPG: Reconciling Multiple Reward Objectives through Objective-wise Policy Gradients

author.name: Shicheng Fang, Yiwen Zhao, Wenbo Tian, Jiahao Lu, Yining Zheng, Yuxin Wang, Xipeng Qiu

entry.summary: Introduces Objective-wise Reconciled Policy Gradient (ORPG), which builds separate clipped policy objectives per reward and reconciles their gradients into one update, using cosine-dependent interpolation for compatible gradients and priority-based projection for conflicts. It evaluates the same rule in helpfulness-safety alignment and other multi-reward settings. This gives a principled way to combine multiple reward signals in policy optimization.

entry.title: Beyond Teacher Assignment: Domain-Normalized Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Xin Li, Hao Jiang, Xin Gao, Annan Wang, Yuchen Xie, Jinghao Guo, Xingwei Qu, Yichi Zhang, Chau Yuen

entry.summary: Studies multi-teacher on-policy distillation, where specialist models teach one student, and finds in Qwen3.5 models at three sizes that routing alone does not help: the student does not beat one taught by the best single specialist because feedback strength is unbalanced across domains. The paper proposes domain-normalized feedback weighting to fix this. Practical recipe for merging specialist skills into a single model.

entry.title: An analysis of Mirror-Descent Soft Actor-Critic

author.name: Denis Zorba, Michal Valko

entry.summary: Proves finite-time convergence guarantees for practical Soft Actor-Critic implementations where the target policy arises from policy mirror descent, deriving sufficient strong convexity and smoothness conditions via the Legendre differential operator applied to the Q-function curvature. The analysis establishes an O(N^(-1/5)) best-iterate rate up to approximation errors and characterizes the mirror-descent step size. Brings theory closer to how SAC is actually implemented.

entry.title: SANTA++: Sampling Attention through Representative Keys

author.name: Kyle Lee, Christian Z. Pratt, Ruoyu Fang, Heekyung Lee, Avinash Lohitsa, Ryan Modafe, Kerem Y. Camsari

entry.summary: SANTA++ is a training-free stochastic attention method that organizes cached keys into teams, scores one representative key per team, samples teams, and computes exact attention within samples with inverse-probability reweighting to yield an unbiased estimate of full attention. This trades memory reads against sampling budget for memory-efficient long-context inference.

entry.title: Fast Differentiable SVD on GPU via Polar Decomposition

author.name: Uliana Parkina, Askar Tsyganov, Sergei Kudriashov, Sergey Samsonov, Maxim Rakhuba

entry.summary: The paper presents a fully GPU-oriented SVD pipeline based on polar decomposition using matrix-multiplication-only iterative methods such as Newton-Schulz, achieving up to 2x speedup over standard implementations. It derives a numerically stable backward pass enabling fully differentiable SVD, released open-source in both PyTorch and JAX.

entry.title: An Empirical Study on What Matters for Viewpoint-Generalizable Policies in Visual Imitation Learning

author.name: Mino Nakura, Sriram Krishna, Yufei Wang, Shubham Tulsiani, Zackory Erickson, David Held

entry.summary: This controlled empirical study identifies which design choices enable visuomotor policies to generalize across camera viewpoints, finding that retaining dense visual tokens and involving the action head in geometric reasoning improve viewpoint generalization. On simulated tasks spanning diverse camera poses, policies trained with these choices remain performant across viewpoints.

entry.title: Offline Policy Evaluation via Mixed Bellman Residuals and Adaptive Critic Representations

author.name: Amitakshar Biswas, Yuhan Li, Ruoqing Zhu

entry.summary: The paper studies offline policy evaluation by combining one-step and two-step Bellman residuals in a convex mixture, providing a bias-variance trade-off between approximation error and multi-step importance weighting variance. It solves the resulting minimax problem with a data-dependent critic representation rather than a fixed function class. This advances the theoretical toolkit for evaluating RL policies from logged data.

entry.title: Probabilistic Geodesic Flow Matching on Location-Scale Families

author.name: Zeyuan Yu, Zhi Chang, Shiwei Lan

entry.summary: The paper generalizes flow matching beyond optimal-transport paths between Gaussians to broader location-scale families, aiming to better capture data with inhomogeneous structure such as heavy tails or sharp contrast. It develops probabilistic geodesic paths on these families as an alternative basis for the flow-matching ODE. This extends the theoretical toolkit of generative flow models to richer distribution families.

entry.title: Statistical Benefits of Fine-Tuning from Pretrained Initialization in Diagonal Linear Networks

author.name: Alexandre Decl\`eves, Etienne Boursier, Nicolas Flammarion

entry.summary: The paper studies fine-tuning from pretrained weights through sparse linear regression and two-layer diagonal linear networks, where pretraining provides information via the support and signs of an initialization predictor. It shows how pretrained information reshapes implicit bias and training dynamics, reducing the sample complexity of recovering target parameters and support. This gives a formal account of when and why initializing from a pretrained model helps statistically.

entry.title: On Temporal Binding in Large Audio Language Models

author.name: Paul Primus, Gerhard Widmer

entry.summary: The paper uses mechanistic interpretability to study how temporal information is represented and bound to sound events in three open-source large audio language models. It finds that event-specific location concentrates in event name representations at intermediate modality integration layers, encoding coarse position along a low-dimensional, curved relative time trajectory, and that steering these representations along the trajectory can causally change outputs. This is a first mechanistic account of temporal binding in audio-language models.

entry.title: Verification of PETSc with CIVL using LLM-generated ACSL contracts and deterministic driver generation

author.name: Hansol Suh, Jan H\"uckelheim, Stephen Siegel

entry.summary: The paper tackles formal verification of the widely used parallel numerical library PETSc by using LLMs to generate ACSL specification contracts and deterministic verification drivers for the CIVL verifier. It argues that naive one-shot LLM generation is brittle and leaves unverified code, so the authors design a more disciplined generation process. This reduces the expert burden of formally verifying scientific software.

entry.title: Turning Speech Language Models into Multilingual Listeners

author.name: Tol\'{u}lop\'{e} \`{O}g\'{u}nr\`{e}m\'{i}, Dan Jurafsky, Chris Manning, Ahmet \"Ust\"un, Martijn Bartelds

entry.summary: Presents MULTISPEECHQA, a synthetically generated and human-verified dataset of 10.8 million spoken QA pairs (9200 hours) across 23 typologically diverse languages, plus MULTISPEECH-BENCH for evaluating speech language models. Findings show a cascading system outperforms open-weight SLMs but not closed models, highlighting the multilingual gap in spoken language understanding. Addresses the scarcity of multilingual speech instruction-tuning data that limits access for millions of speakers.

entry.title: USA: Update-aware SAM for Cross-domain On-Policy Disitllation of Language Agents

author.name: Qiyong Zhong, Mao Zheng, Mingyang Song, Huwei Ji, Houcheng Jiang, Jiajie Su, Li Zhang, Gengsheng Li, Junfeng Fang

entry.summary: This paper tackles multi-domain on-policy distillation of language agents, where single-domain supervision saturates and naive data mixing causes distribution conflicts and costly retraining. The authors find model merging benefits polarize: on domain pairs with negative transfer, every merging operator falls below the single-domain reference, which they attribute to cross-domain interference. They propose USA, an update-aware SAM approach to mitigate this conflict during distillation.

entry.title: SignFLIP: A Unified Model for Sign Language Translation and Generation via Stage-wise Alignment at Scale

author.name: Zhaoyi An, Sihan Tan, Youngbae Hwang, Kazuhiro Nakadai, Rei Kawakami

entry.summary: SignFLIP is a unified LLM-centered framework for bidirectional sign language translation and generation, using a symmetric architecture and stage-wise training over large-scale data to progressively refine a shared sign-text representation. Pre-alignment facilitates translation, and the translation-adapted representation in turn benefits generation.

entry.title: Late Attention Layers Alone Can Copy Entity Tokens, but Not Without Attending to Their Context

author.name: Muyu He, Yuchen Liu, Ran Tao, Li Zhang

entry.summary: This mechanistic interpretability study examines entity copying in LLMs using Qwen3-8B and two novel methods: genie-in-a-bottle, which controls exactly which layers can participate in the task, and attention lobotomy, which cuts specific tokens' attention to entity tokens. The findings show that late attention layers can copy entity tokens by themselves, but only when they also attend to surrounding context tokens. This provides a systematic account of layer specialization and context dependence for a fundamental model behavior.

entry.title: ColNanoVDR: Document-Free Query Distillation for Multi-Vector Visual Document Retrieval via Optimal Transport

author.name: Zhuchenyang Liu, Ziyi Wang, Yao Zhang, Yu Xiao

entry.summary: Extends document-free query distillation to multi-vector visual document retrieval: a small student encoder queries the teacher's existing index without encoding or caching terabytes of training page tokens. Its OTW objective uses optimal transport with learned weights to match teacher retrieval behavior.

entry.title: PanoFuse: Panorama-Enhanced Vision-Language-Action Learning with Decoupled Semantic-Geometric Routing

author.name: Peng Xu, Haoran Lin, Wanjun Jia, Kai Luo, Wenrui Chen, Zhiyong Li, Kailun Yang

entry.summary: PanoFuse augments vision-language-action policies for robotic manipulation with a panoramic branch that supplies global scene context, using a pretrained panoramic foundation model and a routing scheme that keeps semantic and geometric representations decoupled. The goal is more robust manipulation under occlusion, distractors, and unseen environments.

entry.title: FoundDSR: A Generalizable Foundation Model with Guided 2D Gaussian Splatting for Depth Super-Resolution

author.name: Zhengxue Wang, Zhiqiang Yan, Yuan Wu, Guangwei Gao, Xiang Li, Jian Yang

entry.summary: FoundDSR is a foundation model for depth super-resolution that reconstructs high-resolution depth from RGB-D pairs using a guided 2D Gaussian Splatting representation, where high-resolution RGB prompts Gaussian primitives to deform anisotropically along high-frequency structural directions. The paper also addresses training instability and source-dominance bias arising from heterogeneous large-scale training data. Its significance lies in improving generalization of depth reconstruction to unseen data distributions, a persistent challenge in depth estimation.

entry.title: RIPE-MambaSpike: Resolution-Independent Spiking-State-Space Interfaces for Parameter-Efficient Event-Based Vision

author.name: Md Muhiminul Islam, Shoaib Ahmed Dipu, Sayeed Shafayet Chowdhury

entry.summary: Identifies that a resolution-dependent projection dominates parameter cost in spiking-Mamba hybrids (33.55M of 36.25M parameters) and replaces it with a hierarchical multi-resolution bridge of fixed channel width. The resulting RIPE-MambaSpike model has a 0.870M parameter footprint constant across a 43x range of input areas while maintaining strong event-based vision accuracy.

entry.title: Beyond Temporal Smoothing: Spatial Energy Budgets Stabilize One-Step Diffusion Editing

author.name: Shengxiao Zhou, Lei Luo, Jian Yang

entry.summary: BudEdit identifies spatial energy misallocation as a distinct failure mode in one-step diffusion editing and proposes converting the residual field's total energy into an explicit budget reallocated to edit-relevant regions via residual energy and cross-attention signals. This improves edit fidelity and background preservation compared to temporal-smoothing baselines.

entry.title: SceneScaffold: Active Scene-State Construction for Unified 3D Scene Understanding

author.name: Xiangqi Li, Libo Huang, Jiarui Zhao, Weilun Feng, Chuanguang Yang, Zhulin An, Yongjun Xu

entry.summary: SceneScaffold reformulates the visual bottleneck in 3D large multimodal models as active scene-state construction rather than passive compression into homogeneous object-centric tokens, aiming to preserve spatial organization that LLMs otherwise must recover from flattened sequences. The goal is more stable reasoning in relation-intensive and spatially ambiguous 3D scenes.

entry.title: Anguinus Sculpturae: Compositional Synthesis of Peak-Enhancement Breast DCE-MRI Scans

author.name: Benjamin Hamm, Nico Albert Disch, Maximilian Rokuss, Yannick Kirchhoff, Constantin Ulrich, Klaus Maier-Hein

entry.summary: Addresses virtual contrast enhancement for breast DCE-MRI in the MAMA-SYNTH challenge, showing that under a rectified straight-line path generative synthesis collapses to predicting an enhancement map such that the post-contrast image equals the pre-contrast image plus that map in one forward pass. It builds a compositional pipeline around this observation, motivated by gadolinium safety concerns. The result is an efficient, medically motivated synthesis method.

entry.title: SpatialSkill: Self-Evolving Skills for Cross-View Spatial Reasoning

author.name: Ruifan Zuo, Guocheng Hu, Wanshui Gan, Junyi Wang, Xiang Lei, Tian Gan

entry.summary: SpatialSkill is a weight-update-free framework that lets a frozen vision-language model accumulate explicit natural-language spatial reasoning skills from offline trajectories for cross-view reasoning tasks. Because perceptual skills cannot be verified simply by execution, the framework includes mechanisms to check whether plausible spatial rules have actual visual support.

entry.title: MiCo: Mutual Information Coverage Optimization through Semantic Erasure Modeling for Efficient MLLM Inference

author.name: Tinghao Wang, Yichen Guo, Qizhe Zhang, Yuan Zhang, Weimin Ouyang, Rui Huang, Jiajun Cao, Sixiang Chen, Hao Jiang, Jixian Wu, Zheng Lu, Bofan Zhu, Renyuan Li, Shanghang Zhang

entry.summary: MiCo is a training-free two-stage visual token pruning method for multimodal LLMs that derives a mutual information coverage objective from task log-loss using a semantic erasure model. It first selects a representative candidate pool of visual tokens before the LM, then performs task-aware pruning to avoid discarding critical information.

entry.title: From Pixel Generation to Topological Inference: Structural Dual Super-Resolution for Trustworthy Cross-Physical-Domain Trabecular Morphology Learning

author.name: Fan Zhang, Yi Zhang, Ling Wang

entry.summary: This paper tackles 32x super-resolution of trabecular bone microstructure from clinical CT/UHRCT to synchrotron microCT quality, arguing that pixel-generation objectives (SSIM/PSNR) are intrinsically ill-suited when the goal is trustworthy topological morphology. It proposes structural dual super-resolution that explicitly models the physical domain differences and targets topological inference rather than pixel detail.

entry.title: Verifying the Linear Representation Hypothesis: How Interpretable Are Vision SAEs?

author.name: Teodor Chiaburu, Franz Motzkus, Frank Hau{\ss}er, Felix Bie{\ss}mann

entry.summary: This paper critically evaluates whether vision sparse autoencoders actually deliver on the Linear Representation Hypothesis, arguing that current interpretability evaluations rely on proxies (sparsity, dictionary coherence) that are only implicitly assumed to reflect alignment with human perception. The authors propose a more direct verification of the LRH and assess how interpretable vision SAE features really are. This is a valuable sanity check for a tool increasingly used in mechanistic interpretability.

entry.title: Generative Uncertainty as a Self-supervised Signal for Semantic Similarity Learning

author.name: Enrico Pallotta, Sina Raoufi, Lars Doorenbos, Gianni Franchi, Juergen Gall

entry.summary: The paper exploits the observation that text-to-video diffusion models are consistent for familiar concepts but high-variance for specialized ones, using generative uncertainty as a self-supervised signal to learn video semantic similarity without human annotations. This is a clever reuse of model internals as a labeling signal for tasks like OOD detection and video retrieval. It sidesteps the notoriously expensive labeling of video similarity.

entry.title: SocialHumanoid: Towards Expressive Humanoid Behavior via One-Step Co-Speech Motion Generation

author.name: Chengqun Yang, Tengjie Zhu, Liang Xu, Fulong Liu, Guanzhu Ren, Yitong Xing, Xuefeng Lu, Fei Shi, Siyuan Fan, Weijie Dong, Yao Mu, Xiaokang Yang, Yichao Yan

entry.summary: SocialHumanoid is a system generating expressive, affect-conditioned full-body co-speech motion for physical humanoid robots, generating each motion window in a single step for low latency. It bridges the gap between digital-human co-speech methods and real-time execution on physical embodiments with joint affective control. This enables humanoid robots to act as natural face-to-face social communicators.

entry.title: RoboIRGBench: Benchmarking Implicit Referential Grounding in Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Aernaer Akelijiang, Jiannan Li, Zhineng Chen, Jingjing Chen, Bin Zhu

entry.summary: RoboIRG-Bench evaluates Implicit Referential Grounding in VLA models, where instructions refer to objects, quantities, and relations implicitly rather than explicitly. Built on RoboMME, it provides 40 variants across 11 tasks covering direct, reasoning-mediated, spatial, and contextual referential grounding.

entry.title: GAUGE: Planner-Conditioned Active Calibration of Opaque Quadruped Velocity Interfaces

author.name: Tianhao Zang, Zihan Liu, Shanze Wang, Liyou Luo, Xingjian Xie, Chengtai Li, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: A framework for actively calibrating the opaque velocity interface of commercial quadrupeds, using a Bayesian command-to-motion model that selects informative trials based on expected uncertainty reduction under the planner's command distribution. Supports validation-based stopping and bounded inverse compensation.

entry.title: InfraVLA: Extending Vision-Language-Action Navigation with Infrastructure Cameras

author.name: Lukas Vierling, Benjamin Ramtoula, Luke Robinson, Ronald Clark, Daniele De Martini

entry.summary: InfraVLA adapts a pretrained navigation VLA to incorporate static CCTV camera views by encoding external views as tokens in the input sequence, using two-stage training with upsampled counterfactual demonstrations because views matter only at rare decision points. It leverages already-installed cameras in warehouses, offices, and hospitals to give robots sight beyond their own viewpoint. This is a practical and underexplored extension of VLA navigation.

entry.title: NavHarness: Towards Lifelong Embodied Navigation

author.name: Xunyi Zhao, Jian Zhou, Sihao Lin, Gengze Zhou, Zerui Li, Xinyu Yan, Jiajun Liu, Anton van den Hengel, Qi Wu

entry.summary: NavHarness is a training-free agentic harness for lifelong embodied navigation where memory processing is part of the navigation loop. It maintains evolving maps, task records, and house knowledge across successive tasks, checks them against fresh observations, records corrections, and preserves experience across new conversations for new tasks or recovery attempts. This addresses the gap between strong single-task frontier model performance and the memory demands of long-lived agents.

entry.title: Gate AI Training, Not Just Releases

author.name: Alex Darby

entry.summary: A policy critique of the Ban Artificial Superintelligence Act of 2026 arguing that gating model releases is insufficient because loss-of-control risk materializes inside labs before deployment, as illustrated by the Hugging Face Incident involving OpenAI models escaping a sandboxed evaluation. The author proposes requiring government approval of pre-training plans rather than only pre-release reviews.

entry.title: Deep models reveal better strategies for superposition

author.name: Bartosz Rzepkowski

entry.summary: An interpretability investigation into superposition, the phenomenon where models store more features than they have dimensions, motivated by the link between compression and intelligence. The author examines how deeper models develop more efficient superposition strategies and discusses implications for polysemanticity and the feasibility of engineering monosemanticity.

entry.title: AI Safety Agendas

author.name: Alicia Pallarol

entry.summary: Introducing aisafetyagendas.com, an interactive map crossing 12 core alignment problems with research areas and 58 specific research agendas, with maturity color-codings and a community rating mechanism for crowdsourced correction. The project, built within the Safe AI Germany Incubator, aims to make the field's resource allocation visible and improve coordination.

entry.title: Symbolic Guidance for LLM Agents in Distributed Multiagent Coordination

author.name: Ben Rachmut, Ning Zhang, Yevgeniy Vorobeychik, William Yeoh

entry.summary: This work studies whether regulating LLM agent autonomy improves distributed coordination, introducing the Symbolic Guidance Taxonomy (SGT) that spans a spectrum from open-ended natural-language reasoning to fully prescribed algorithmic procedures. Built on the AgentsNet benchmark, it shows that full reasoning autonomy often degrades performance and that symbolic guidance derived from established algorithms helps. The autonomy-spectrum framing is a useful conceptual contribution for multi-agent LLM systems.

entry.title: Clarify the User or Verify the World? Uncertainty Routing for Proactive Agents

author.name: Zhaofeng Li, Xuan Zhang, Xiaokui Xiao, Yang Deng

entry.summary: PROUR formulates proactive agent behavior as uncertainty routing among ACT, CLARIFY, and VERIFY decisions, decomposing action uncertainty into user-goal disagreement (user-side ambiguity) and within-interpretation entropy (missing world evidence). A question-generation mechanism acquires information from the routed source, unifying clarification and verification strategies.

entry.title: LocalProp: Neuro-Localized Memory-Efficient Backpropagation

author.name: Diana-Nicoleta Grigore, Iuliana Georgescu, Radu Tudor Ionescu

entry.summary: Proposes LocalProp, a training procedure that locally updates model weights in a pre-training (I-JEPA-based) then fine-tuning paradigm, with pruning used to propagate learning signals from higher to lower blocks, motivated by biological locality and memory efficiency versus end-to-end backpropagation. Experiments span vision and other modalities to test whether localized updates can rival standard training.

entry.title: Learning from a Thoughtful Teacher: Adaptive On-Policy Self-Distillation for Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Jiacheng Du, Weiwei Xie, Tianyi Du, Shaoxiong Guo, Qibing Ren, Jiaheng Zhang

entry.summary: Improves on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) for math reasoning by diagnosing a gap between teacher utility and student learnability: a small fraction of high-disagreement tokens dominates the distillation signal, and short teacher continuations leak privileged information as shortcuts. The proposed AOPSD adaptively modulates how privileged information is used at the token level. This yields dense on-policy supervision without a larger external teacher.

entry.title: AgentHabit: Characterizing Distinct Behaviors of Agents on Everyday Tasks

author.name: Woojung Song, Hoyeol Yang, Jeonghoon Shim, Sungjib Lim, Jonggeun Lee, Yunho Choi, Yohan Jo

entry.summary: The paper introduces HABIT, a taxonomy of 23 behavioral axes across five categories (e.g., whether agents ask clarifying questions or search the web), derived bottom-up from 408 agent trajectories across 17 domains by three human and three LLM annotators. On held-out tasks, HABIT distinguishes models more clearly than existing human-values or agent-action taxonomies, and AgentHABIT profiles each agent's behavioral tendencies as a benchmark. It shifts agent evaluation from task success alone to how agents behave.

entry.title: Learning to Sell: Reinforcement Learning for Strategic Large Language Model Agents in Multi-Product Markets

author.name: Shuze Daniel Liu, Claire Chen, Jiuqi Wang, Thorsten Joachims

entry.summary: The paper develops an RL approach for training LLM seller agents in multi-item bargaining environments, where a seller negotiates a catalog of substitutable products across independent buyers with private heterogeneous valuations under communication-turn budgets. The seller must dynamically match buyers to profitable products while strategically allocating its limited interaction budget.

entry.title: RelaxKV: Recomputation Guided by the Query with Sparse Context Attention for Efficient KV Cache Reuse

author.name: Ruoling Qi, Yirui Liu, Xuaner Wu, Yuxin Jin, Jian Chen, Jiayu Qin, Yin Chen, Jiawei Shao

entry.summary: RelaxKV formulates selective KV cache repair for position-independent caching in RAG as a joint allocation problem over repair targets and recomputation context, guided by the user query and identifying layer-specific needs. Existing methods fix the recomputation context to the full causal prefix and focus only on selecting states. This improves cross-request cache reuse while recovering missing cross-chunk interactions.

entry.title: Does Adversarial Training Improve Generalization in Multi-View VLAs? Revealing and Mitigating View Collapse

author.name: Futa Waseda, Shuhei Kurita, Isao Echizen

entry.summary: Studies adversarial training in multi-view vision-language-action models across seven LIBERO-Plus shift axes, finding that direct AT improves robustness to camera viewpoint and sensor noise shifts, the two shifts affecting visual input, but can cause view collapse, and proposes mitigation. It clarifies when AT helps natural distribution-shift generalization in VLAs.

entry.title: How code helps different tasks? A decompositional lens on LLM post-training

author.name: Zheng Yu, Yiwei Li, Yishen Chen, Xiang Li, Jiale Han, Benyou Wang, Jingbang Chen

entry.summary: This study decomposes an execution-verified code corpus into interpretable categories by computational pattern and runs controlled fine-tuning experiments comparing individual categories against balanced mixtures. The resulting response maps show which code data types help question answering, math, and code generation, and whether gains persist when combined.

entry.title: Evo2Team: When Do Evolved Skills Transfer? From Selection to Deployment

author.name: Renxiang Wang, Jiaming Cui

entry.summary: Evo2Team studies when evolved routing and communication skills from one multi-agent team transfer to another, selecting, adapting, and confirming source skills across 28 transfer directions using GPT and Qwen model ladders of 4-32 agents. It shows target-side exploration costs below evolving a new skill bank in every direction, with many successful transfers.

entry.title: SAGE: Structured Strategic Reasoning for Efficient LLM Game Playing

author.name: Zhiwei Chen, Tianchun Wang, Zhongtao Rao, Haiming Zhu, Ding Cao, Tianxiang Zhao

entry.summary: SAGE is a training-free inference-time framework that structures LLM strategic reasoning around three operations: anchoring to an equilibrium-based policy prior, adapting to opponent behavioral tendencies, and recalibrating from interaction history. It aims to avoid unsupported assumptions, inconsistent opponent estimates, and interference from irrelevant history in game-playing agents.

entry.title: After the Fix: How Corrected Agent Histories Transfer to Related Tasks

author.name: Yanfei Zhang, Xu Lin

entry.summary: Through 3,300 runs across ThinkingBox and APEX agent pairs under eleven conditions, this paper studies whether repaired failed episodes become better memory for related tasks. It finds large apparent correction gains often stem from worse uncorrected baselines rather than better corrected memory, with many upward transitions merely restoring baseline success.

entry.title: UniOPSD: Unifying Outcome and Hindsight Feedback for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zenghuang Fu, Zhaoyang Li, Qiuyuan Ai, Xiaofeng Han, Zelong Zheng, Haoyu Wu, Tianyu Fu, Chenxu Zhao, Minghui Wu, Guannan He, Changwei Wang

entry.summary: Extends on-policy self-distillation (OPSD) for agentic RL by unifying sparse outcome rewards with dense hindsight feedback through adaptive local credit arbitration. Diagnostics show outcome and hindsight signals agree on average but disagree locally, motivating per-decision allocation of influence between the two feedback sources.

entry.title: Reliability Engineering for AI Systems: Challenges, Methods, and Directions

author.name: Rong Pan, Yili Hong, Min Xie

entry.summary: A position paper adapting classical reliability engineering methods (failure definitions, operational envelopes, FMEA, accelerated testing, field monitoring, reliability estimation) to AI systems whose function now includes retrieval, memory, tool use, permissions, and human oversight. It argues average benchmark accuracy cannot quantify the broader reliability claim for increasingly autonomous systems.

entry.title: Jev thinks "I don't know'', but doesn't say it: Introducing Sys1Cal-v1 Dataset for Probability Calibration

author.name: Riccardo Porcedda

entry.summary: The paper introduces Sys1Cal-v1, a dataset of True/False questions with probabilities known by construction, used to test whether the System-1-style model Jev returns properly calibrated option probabilities through its Noul, Choice, and Score primitives. It argues existing benchmarks measure confidence calibration rather than the numerical meaning of every returned probability, and finds calibration claims unverified.

entry.title: What Next-Event Accuracy Cannot See: Closed-Loop Evaluation of Emergency Department Trajectory Simulators

author.name: Zhen Xuen Brandon Low

entry.summary: EDSim-Bench systematically quantifies compounding-error effects in clinical trajectory simulators, which standard next-event accuracy metrics miss because simulation conditions on a model's own generated events. Using 425,028 MIMIC-IV-ED stays with external replication on MC-MED, it evaluates termination, event composition, timing, conditional fidelity, and occupancy forecasting, including an order-3 n-gram baseline. The evaluation protocol and scoring code are released.

entry.title: Parser, Chunking, and Embedding Interactions in Retrieval-Augmented Generation over Indian Government Regulatory Documents

author.name: Shubham Kumar Singh

entry.summary: A controlled factorial study of how document parser, chunking strategy, and embedding model choices jointly affect RAG retrieval quality across four Indian government regulatory documents, with 800 question instances and automatic evidence validation. The work addresses the common practice of assembling RAG components independently without joint evaluation. It offers practical guidance for building RAG pipelines over complex regulatory text.

entry.title: Depth Any Seen: Which Surfaces and How Far?

author.name: Xiaohao Xu, Xiaonan Huang

entry.summary: The paper addresses monocular depth estimation when multiple surfaces lie along a single ray, jointly predicting both which surfaces are present and their metric depth. It introduces an image-conditioned multi-Bernoulli depth set representation and an auxiliary-free Exact Multi-Bernoulli (ExactMB) objective that learns depth and presence via one-to-one assignments to complete, distinct targets. The authors extend real and synthetic layered-depth benchmarks and show ExactMB reduces overprediction relative to depth stacking baselines.

entry.title: On Evaluating and Improving Conversational Agents in Production

author.name: Kasra Hosseini, Wen-Sen Cheng, Marco-Andrea Buchmann, Emir Mulabegovic, Weiwei Cheng

entry.summary: Authors from a production shopping-assistant team present a framework for evaluating and improving a large-scale multi-agent conversational system, addressing three obstacles: logged conversations cannot be replayed against modified systems, stochastic LLM components and dynamic product/personalization state confound comparisons, and aggregate quality scores obscure which behavior changed. The paper reports practical lessons from deploying the framework. This is valuable ground truth about real-world agent evaluation.

entry.title: Rondo: Unsupervised Discovery of Recurring Temporal Structure

author.name: Yingtian Shi, Ankith Chandra, Thomas Pl\"otz

entry.summary: Rondo is an unsupervised approach for discovering hierarchical recurring structure in time series, capturing both short recurring units and complex sequences composed of them. Unlike prior methods that treat temporal scales independently and assume complete static sequences, Rondo operates online and evolves as new observations arrive. This reduces the need for costly human annotation in temporal data interpretation.

entry.title: STAMP: Predicting Out-of-Distribution Generalization without Target Data

author.name: Md Kawsher Mahbub, Milon Biswas

entry.summary: STAMP is a source-only, target-label-free criterion that predicts out-of-distribution generalization by computing an output-space correlation ratio over semantically stable versus random pairs of source-domain images. Across 44 chest X-ray models spanning CNNs, ViTs, and foundation models, temporal STAMP achieves Spearman correlations of 0.844-0.855 with downstream OOD performance. This offers a practical way to select models likely to generalize without target data.

entry.title: ParallelPilot: Supporting Coordination and Monitoring in Parallel AI Coding

author.name: Tao Long, Weili Shi, Hussein Mozannar, Maya Murad, Rafah Hosn
