entry.summary: TQTS-Bench is a benchmark of 6,125 QA pairs for text-to-query over time-series databases, spanning 97 TSDBs, 23 query syntaxes, 22 application domains, and 4 time-specific intent types. It was built with a human-centric AI-assisted workflow and targets a previously unassessed capability area for LLMs.

entry.title: When Words Speak Louder than Images: Towards Understanding Language Bias in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yizhou Fang, Siyue Chen, Zimo Qi, Zhiyu Xue, Xi Chen, Guangliang Liu

entry.summary: The paper proposes a diagnostic framework that decomposes VLM inference into four interdependent stages to trace how language bias propagates, building on a word completion task. It examines how key factors influence whether linguistic cues override visual evidence, helping reconcile conflicting prior findings.

entry.title: Distributional Metrics for Evaluating Spoken Conversational Systems

author.name: Shree Harsha Bokkahalli Satish, Erica Cooper, Patr\'icia Schmidtov\'a, Maike Z\"ufle, \'Eva Sz\'ekely, Nicholas Sanders, Ond\v{r}ej Klejch

entry.summary: The paper introduces the Conversational Distribution Score (CDS), which evaluates conversational systems by comparing distributions of conversational behavior against human reference conversations, using eight interpretable features covering speech rate, syllabic rhythm, and turn interaction plus a semantic baseline. Tested with listener judgments from out-of-domain goal-oriented dialogues, the composite CDS recovers five of six listener system rankings and supports system ranking, pairwise preference, and ranking-stability analysis.

entry.title: ForensicZoom: Adaptive Visual Inspection with Multimodal LLMs for Industrial-Grade Face Forgery Detection

author.name: Hang Zhou, Yiming Tang, Kun Yu, Qian Zhu, Minghao Li, Weigao Wen

entry.summary: Proposes ForensicZoom, which adaptively selects where to inspect at high resolution within multimodal LLMs for face forgery detection, avoiding the cost of uniformly processing all cases at high resolution. Aims to combine MLLM interpretability with specialized forensic detector accuracy for identity-verification security.

entry.title: Where Does the Watermark Hide? Push-Pull Disentanglement for Invisible Watermark Removal

author.name: Jidong Yang, Huaike Yu, Qi Li, Chunpeng Wang, Yuantian Miao, Suo Gao, Xiao Chen

entry.summary: The paper studies a paired-training attack on invisible image watermarks where an adversary learns from clean-watermarked pairs and then removes watermarks at single-image inference without the key or decoder. A push-pull disentanglement scheme separates structural and auxiliary latents, achieving reasonable image quality while raising bit error rates for watermark decoding.

entry.title: Does Vision-Language Pretraining Granularity Matter? A Controlled Evaluation of Vision-Language Objectives Across Chest X-Ray Interpretation Tasks

author.name: Denis Musinguzi, Andrew Katumba, Prasenjit Mitra

entry.summary: A controlled study trains nine vision-language pretraining objectives spanning global and local contrastive learning and captioning, holding encoder and data fixed, then evaluates across five chest X-ray tasks of increasing spatial granularity. Findings include alignment of pretraining and task granularity at the extremes and surprising competitiveness of local objectives on global-level generation.

entry.title: Geometry-Preserving Blind Watermarking for Raw 3D Point Clouds

author.name: Rungui Zhou, Chuanzhi Zhou, Ruihuan Wang, Peng-Shuai Wang

entry.summary: This paper presents a blind watermarking framework for raw 3D point clouds that embeds ownership messages directly in xyz coordinates and recovers them from observed point clouds alone, without the original geometry, colors, or mesh connectivity. A feed-forward octree-based architecture learns joint embedding and extraction robust to resampling and preprocessing.

entry.title: GeoCR: Learning a Generalist Cloud Removal Prior from Heterogeneous Observations

author.name: Jeonghyeok Do, Munchurl Kim

entry.summary: GeoCR unifies RGB-only, multispectral, and SAR-guided cloud removal across single- and multi-temporal inputs in one generalist network, using compact input/output stems around a frozen pretrained RGB autoencoder and a shared latent interface. A single flow transformer jointly models clean and auxiliary modality latents.

entry.title: SV2V-RSim: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Self-Selective V2V Cooperative Perception with Near-Realistic Data

author.name: Yulu Wu, Chao Wei, Jujun Cheng, Zhangkai Ni, Haowen Wang, Dengyang Suo, Cong Chen, Xinyi Liu, Shangce Gao

entry.summary: SV2V-RSim is a large-scale multi-modal simulation benchmark for vehicle-to-vehicle cooperative perception with diverse agents and reduced sim-to-real gap, generated with Unreal Engine. It also contributes a Select Vehicles Adaptively (SVA) module that balances perception gains against communication bandwidth by optimizing collaborator selection.

entry.title: VaME: Exploring Variational Latent Reasoning for Multimodal Embeddings

author.name: Peixi Wu, Mingzhou Jiang, Feipeng Ma, Biao Yang, Yunhao Zhou, Wei Yuan, Bosong Chai, Huizu Lin, Jie Chen, Zhangchi Hu, Fan Yang, Wenwu Ou, Hebei Li, Xiaoyan Sun

entry.summary: VaME models latent reasoning for universal multimodal retrieval as a learnable distribution over trajectories rather than a single deterministic latent path. It introduces Variational Latent Reasoning with autoregressive exploration in latent space, guided by answer reconstruction through a lightweight module, to produce more robust multimodal embeddings.

entry.title: Printability-Constrained Adversarial Decals for Near-Nadir Aerial Perception: Measured Ink Gamuts, Nested Realism Constraints, and a Physical-World Bound

author.name: Sandesh Shrestha, K. T. Yasas Mahima, Asanka G. Perera

entry.summary: This work studies physical adversarial decals against aerial perception systems under three real-world constraints imposed during optimization: printer-measured ink gamuts, vehicle panel size limits, and altitude-induced detail loss. A controlled comparison isolates the ink set, finding measurable differences between a uniform color cube and a physically measured gamut across thirteen victim configurations.

entry.title: Revisiting Diffusion Fine-Tuning for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation

author.name: Xuan Qi, Yi Wei, Daniele Berardini, Vito Paolo Pastore, Vittorio Murino

entry.summary: Proposes MUSE, a method for multi-target unsupervised domain adaptation where a single source-guided diffusion fine-tuning process is reused to generate target-specific synthetic data for multiple unlabeled target domains, avoiding per-pair fine-tuning. This reduces training, storage, and deployment costs that otherwise scale with the number of targets. It revisits diffusion-based UDA from a scalability perspective.

entry.title: Beyond Geometry: Benchmarking and Consistency Reasoning for 3D Logical Anomaly Detection

author.name: Zhiqiang Qin, He Xie, Junfei Yi, Yang Yang, Hao Wang, Yunkang Cao, Hui Zhang, Yaonan Wang

entry.summary: The paper defines 3D logical anomalies in industrial inspection as violations of object-level design or assembly rules rather than local geometric deviations, and introduces ILGAD, a benchmark with 2,774 point-cloud samples across 15 categories covering existence, specification, pose, and assembly errors. It also proposes a consistency reasoning framework checking whether local geometry, structure coverage, and spatial relations conform to normal design.

entry.title: PACER: Progressive Availability-Conditioned Evidence Routing for Radiology Report Generation under Incomplete Clinical Context

author.name: Yulong Chen, Yadong Liu, Haoyu Cao, Sen Xu, Yueying Wang, Jie Wen

entry.summary: PACER handles radiology report generation when the availability of clinical evidence such as multi-view radiographs and prior reports varies, using a Refine-Calibrate-Commit pipeline with availability-conditioned routing across frozen encoder depths. It aims to reduce omissions and inaccuracies in clinically relevant findings regardless of input combinations.

entry.title: Revitalizing Medical Time Series with Vision-Informed Retrieval: A Vision-Language Perspective

author.name: Guoqi Yu, Juncheng Wang, Shujun Wang

entry.summary: ViRe uses a frozen vision-language model to extract morphology-aware queries from waveform plots of medical time series, then performs attention-based cross-modal retrieval to select morphology-relevant temporal and channel evidence from raw numerical features. This bridges the gap between numerical time-series representations and the morphology clinicians read from waveform inspection.

entry.title: ORAV: Benchmarking Audio-Video Generation from Multimodal Contexts

author.name: Jiacheng Hua, Xiaokun Feng, Jiaqi Hua, Chang Liu, Biao Wang, Miao Liu

entry.summary: ORAV Bench is a benchmark for audio-video generation driven by heterogeneous multimodal references, with 380 task instances spanning 2-10 references, 9 semantic roles, and 30 role compositions. It includes a reference-aware pairwise evaluation protocol that compares each reference's intended contribution using visual and auditory evidence. As audio-video generative models proliferate, this addresses the clear need for compositional, reference-grounded evaluation.

entry.title: Rethinking Visual Token Compression for Video Large Language Models: A Simple Yet Strong Baseline

author.name: Xiao Zhang, Wang Zeng, Sheng Jin, Wentao Liu, Chen Qian, Shichao Kan

entry.summary: SimpleCluster is a training-free video token compression baseline that performs position-aware cross-frame clustering in visual feature space and represents each cluster by the mean of its original features. The paper asks how much of sophisticated compression performance can be achieved simply by preserving structure in visual representations. Simple, strong baselines that challenge complex methods are valuable for the efficient Video-LLM community.

entry.title: Beyond Sparsity: Weight Location and Network Context in Pruned MRI Reconstruction

author.name: Mohammed Wattad, Tamir Shor, Alexander M. Bronstein

entry.summary: The paper studies what pruning removes in MRI reconstruction networks beyond raw sparsity, analyzing 120 U-Net and vision transformer models with controlled weight edits before retraining. Key findings include that preserving high-resolution computation in U-Net improves reconstruction at equal deletion counts, and that pretrained weight energy correlates with quality in transformers while the same masks transfer poorly across contexts. This reframes pruning decisions around weight location and network context rather than sparsity alone.

entry.title: Mask2Restore: Self-Supervised Ultrasound Despeckling via Inpainting

author.name: Xuesong Li, Yingtai Xu, Zhongliang Jiang, Nassir Navab, Yuan Bi

entry.summary: Mask2Restore performs self-supervised ultrasound despeckling via inpainting, motivated by the observation that speckle is spatially dependent and deterministic coherent scattering rather than i.i.d. random noise, which breaks blind-spot network assumptions. Instead of pixel-wise masking, the method uses inpainting-style masking matched to speckle's correlated structure. Since speckle-free ultrasound targets do not exist, self-supervised approaches are essential here.

entry.title: Adaptive Safety Filtering for Frozen ACC Policies via Conformal Residual Calibration

author.name: Zhiruo Zhou, Rigaudiere Z. Li, Chen Xiwen, Yucheng Chen, Xiaojun Zhu, Houde Liu

entry.summary: RACF (residual-aware conformal action filtering) wraps a frozen adaptive cruise control policy with a safety filter that calibrates residuals of the nominal predictor and converts their quantiles into operating margins for action projection, updating margins online from completed transitions without retraining. In a 2,400-unit registered comparison, it achieves 94.3% episode safety, a 19.9-point improvement over a CBF-QP baseline while reducing projection frequency.

entry.title: SOR-Nav: Search or Relocate? Context-Gated Exploration and Cross-Region Relocation for Object Navigation

author.name: Yuan Ji, Zirui Li, Yuxin Cai, Shuge Wu, Boon Siew Han, Chen Lv

entry.summary: SOR-Nav is a hierarchical navigation system that explicitly arbitrates between continuing exploration of the current context and relocating to a more promising reachable region when searching for objects in unseen environments. It builds persistent 3D object clusters and organizes frontiers into a cluster decision graph, then uses a context-gated LLM-driven supervisor for the search-versus-relocate decision. This departs from prior work that only ranks candidate destinations under partial observability and motion budgets.

entry.title: RoboCompiler: Graph-Native Compilation of Closed-Chain Robots for Consistent Modeling, Control, and Simulation

author.name: Mehdi Heydari Shahna, Joongheon Kim, Jouni Mattila

entry.summary: RoboCompiler is a graph-native framework that compiles a canonical mechanism graph for robots with kinematic loops and coupled actuators into a shared mechanical interface usable consistently across modeling, control, and simulation. It constructs closure paths, analytic residual Jacobians, and feasible configurations via rank-checked continuation, with actuator-port maps preserving consistency. This tackles a genuine pain point where control and simulation interfaces are reconstructed separately and drift apart.

entry.title: IndustryLLM: Failure-Driven LLM Training for Industrial Procurement

author.name: Liang Ding (Project Lead), Zhiang Xu, Yuyang Sheng, Bin Chen, Songlin Bai, Run Zhu, Dingjun Wu, Hui Xu, Yandi Wang, Fulin Shi, Leilei Gan, Linlin Yu, Qihuang Zhong, Keqin Peng, Yalong Li, Chengfu Huo

entry.summary: IndustryLLM is an open-weight industrial language model fine-tuned from a Qwen 3.5 base model using a failure-driven adaptation recipe over a roughly 100 billion token corpus mixing national standards, de-identified industrial transactions, and synthetic data. It targets industrial procurement, bridging informal buyer jargon, sparse marketplace attributes, and engineering standards under strict safety tolerances. The failure-driven training recipe is the main methodological contribution beyond domain adaptation.

entry.title: Memory as Middleware for Self-Improving AI Agents

author.name: K. R. Jayaram, Vatche Isahagian, Vinod Muthusamy, Gegi Thomas, Punleuk Oum, Gaodan Fang, Ashwath Vaithinathan Aravindan

entry.summary: The authors argue that agent memory should be treated as a first-class, pluggable middleware layer rather than bespoke logic hand-wired into individual agents, enabling memory to be swapped, shared, isolated, and reasoned about independently. This position paper draws an analogy to how data access and persistence became middleware concerns in software engineering.

entry.title: GLIDE: Generalized Layer-wise Intrinsic Distributional Evaluation for Heterogeneous LLM Agents

author.name: Wei Zhu, Yiming Wang, Rui Wang, Lixing Yu, Kun Yue, Zhiwen Tang

entry.summary: GLIDE provides lightweight step-level evaluation for LLM agents by deriving intrinsic evidence from layer-wise residual coherence, measuring whether local residual updates consistently support the global residual change of a candidate step. It avoids costly external verifiers and miscalibrated self-evaluation, especially for heterogeneous-agent settings.

entry.title: HyperReCo: Retrieving and Connecting Evidence with Hypergraph Neural Networks for LLM Multi-hop Reasoning

author.name: Zicheng Zhao, Linhao Luo, Junnan Dong, Haoran Luo, Xiaoli Li, Shirui Pan, Chen Gong

entry.summary: HyperReCo improves retrieval-augmented multi-hop reasoning by using hypergraph neural networks to preserve higher-order entity associations and explicitly connect retrieved evidence. It overcomes limitations of prior hypergraph retrievers that rely on predefined expansion and leave inter-evidence connections implicit for the LLM to reconstruct. The framework jointly retrieves and connects query-dependent evidence.

entry.title: LLMAdBench: A Human Preference Benchmark for Advertising in LLM Responses

author.name: Rui Ai, Yuqing Liu, Sitao Qiu, Yun Qiao, Yuhan Wang, Jessica Xiwen Wang, Yiqi Yang, Lihong Huang, Ruiyao Sun, Kaifeng Zhang, Shengze Ding, Jiaqi He, Xinman Wang, Tianhao Gao, Jimmy Qin, Jianghao Lin, Chonghuan Wang

entry.summary: Introduces LLMAdBench, a human-preference benchmark isolating the decision of where to place an advertisement in an LLM response, comparing response pairs that differ only in ad position under fixed query, answer, ad, and disclosure conditions, evaluated by human annotators on six criteria. This provides the first shared evidence base for a nascent business model at the intersection of LLM deployment and advertising.

entry.title: Business Compromise Detection with Agentic AI and LLM-driven Knowledge Discovery

author.name: Diego Palma, Kyu Bin Kim, Zhen Han, Allbright Dsouza, Zhiyuan Liu

entry.summary: Presents a hybrid system for detecting compromised business ad accounts in digital advertising: an LLM agent acts as an investigator emitting interpretable structured signals, while final verdicts are delegated to a neuro-symbolic stage combining FOIL-based rule discovery, Naive Bayes calibration, and a contradiction layer. This design mitigates hallucination-driven friction on ambiguous cases. It demonstrates a practical pattern of keeping LLMs as signal extractors rather than final decision makers.

entry.title: Retrospective Distillation Attribution via Normalized Response Similarity

author.name: Minwoo Jang, Jaechang Kim, Minhyeon Oh, Jeongyeon Hwang, Jungseul Ok

entry.summary: This paper introduces SCOUT, an output-only method for attributing whether a model was distilled from a particular teacher, even when the student has undergone additional post-distillation training (SFT, preference optimization, RL) and the pre-distillation checkpoint is unavailable. It aggregates recurring syntactic patterns into candidate profiles and calibrates student-candidate distances against inter-candidate baselines. The work addresses a practical auditing question about model provenance in an era where distilled models are often released long after the distillation step.

entry.title: Learning response-aware patient dynamics for respiratory support

author.name: Xiaolei Lu, Shamim Nemati

entry.summary: The authors propose a response-aware patient dynamics model for critically ill patients undergoing respiratory support, which explicitly models physiological change during autoregressive state updates instead of encoding it only in predicted future states. The model decomposes predicted physiological change into a state-dependent baseline dynamic plus deviations attributable to respiratory support, using room air as a reference condition, and includes a formal analysis of the decomposition.

entry.title: When Can First-Order Models of Fine-Tuning Bound Forgetting?

author.name: Jianchang Su, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: This theory-plus-empirics paper asks whether measurements taken at fine-tuning start can bound the probability that a protected fact will be forgotten. In LoRA fine-tuning on models from 0.6B to 14B parameters, a first-order response model from finite-difference probes predicts per-fact margin changes with correlation 0.974-0.998, yet direct forgetting predictions fail because forgetting requires parameter changes outside the validated region; the probes can, however, bound the probability that a margin first crosses a near-zero boundary. The result delineates precisely when first-order analysis is and is not valid for forgetting.

entry.title: StraTune: Adaptive Selection of Revision Operators for Self-Evolving LLM Skills

author.name: Zeping Liu, Yan Li, Ni Lao, Gil Wolff, Gengchen Mai

entry.summary: StraTune lets a frozen optimizer LLM choose among revision operators each round based on execution feedback and recorded past strategy outcomes, rather than committing to a single fixed revision operator for skill libraries. This addresses the observation that no single operator dominates across tasks. The work targets non-parametric, inference-time self-improvement of LLM skills.

entry.title: When Pair Count Is Not the Sample Size: What All-Pairs Agent Comparisons Estimate

author.name: Wei-Jung Huang

entry.summary: This paper examines a statistical pitfall in AI agent leaderboards where all-pairs comparisons make the number of comparisons appear far larger than the independent evidence supporting them. The author shows that when benchmark entries are treated as draws from a population of future configurations, the all-pairs mean is an order-two U-statistic whose uncertainty scales with the number of configurations rather than the number of pairs. The work clarifies what such comparisons can and cannot validly claim, including the role of near ties.

entry.title: Not Too Hard, Not Too Easy: Learning from Intermediate States for LLM Structured Reasoning

author.name: Hongbo Chen, Guohua Lu, Ting Dang, Hong Jia

entry.summary: Applying the zone-of-proximal-development learning principle to structured reasoning, this paper trains LLMs to revise intermediate candidate solutions (e.g., in Sudoku and mazes) that lie at the model's current frontier of achievable progress. Training on these frontier states improves reasoning compared to states that are already solved or beyond repair.

entry.title: ANTMAN: Adaptive Need Tracking for Multi-Agent Navigation in Large Information Spaces

author.name: Jerry Wang, Haibo Jin, Xiaopeng Yuan, Peng Kuang, Haohan Wang

entry.summary: ANTMAN is a coordination framework for multi-agent information-seeking systems that tracks unresolved information needs in a revisable Need Graph rather than relying on static partitions of the search space. This state drives worker selection, routing, and task-local recovery as new evidence arrives. The work matters because coordination cost in large information spaces often scales with how data is segmented rather than with what a query actually still requires.

entry.title: Probe to Act: Elevating Browser-Use Agent via Active Visual Probing

author.name: Keliang Li, Heng Wang, Chen Hu, Daxin Jiang, Hong Chang, Shiguang Shan

entry.summary: Introduces P2A, an active probing framework for browser agents that resolves DOM-to-pixel alignment at decision time by rendering symbolic DOM hypotheses back into pixels and issuing lightweight probes before committing state-changing operations. This replaces static Set-of-Marks overlays or pure screenshot prediction.

entry.title: Evidence-Inference Reconstruction: When The Evidence Is Recalled But The Reasoning Goes Wrong

author.name: Megan Diehl, Ser-Nam Lim

entry.summary: EIR is a method for multi-hop retrieval agents that uses structured state to guide a single retrieval trajectory and reconstruct answers from accumulated evidence in one final model call, avoiding costly retry loops when intermediate reasoning fails. It shows correct answers can be recovered even when some collected evidence is erroneous.

entry.title: K-OPSD: Verifiable On-Policy Self-Distillation for Post-Training Vision-Language Models on AEC Drawings

author.name: Yunfei Bai, Enrico Chionna, Akash Amol, Kawaljit Singh KC, Joern Tinnemeyer

entry.summary: K-OPSD is a VLM post-training method for architecture/engineering/construction drawing understanding, building on On-Policy Self-Distillation with process-level verification: a teacher is constructed from the model's own best-of-N generations certified by a verifier, failed prompts are rescued via hinted resampling, and training uses verified completions with a cross-entropy inner loss outperforming bounded JSD.

entry.title: TableSeek: Structure-Preserving Agentic Evidence Seeking over Heterogeneous Table Corpora

author.name: Jiaming Tian, Liyao Li, Wentao Ye, Haobo Wang, Lihua Yu, Zujie Ren, Gang Chen, Junbo Zhao

entry.summary: TableSeek is an agentic framework for open-domain table retrieval that iteratively follows sparse clues, inspects schema-preserving previews, and refines searches over heterogeneous table corpora instead of one-shot ranking. It tackles the problem that topically similar tables often lack required answer-bearing evidence.

entry.title: Query Expansion and Key Specialization in Transformer Attention Geometry

author.name: Vidit Gupta, Siddhesh Nadkarni, Mihik Chaudhari, Vinaya Sawant, Prachi Tawde

entry.summary: This paper studies whether the mathematically symmetric query and key projections in Transformer attention develop different geometric structure during training. By training small GPT-like models on character-level WikiText-103 across depths, initializations, and seeds (36 runs), the authors track effective dimensionality via participation ratios and find divergent geometric development between queries and keys.

entry.title: EOPSA: Efficient On-Policy Self-Distilled Safety Alignment

author.name: Qirui Liu, Yichen Sun, Yan Wang, Yu Mi, Wei Cao, Yue Shen, Zhixuan Chu, Kui Ren

entry.summary: This paper identifies two efficiency bottlenecks in On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) safety alignment: supervisory collapse over long rollouts and gradient dilution from stylistic shifts. It proposes EOPSA, an improved alignment method that addresses these issues to preserve both safety and general reasoning capability.

entry.title: Privacy-Preserving Full-Body Meshing from mmWave Radar via Mesh Foundation Model Supervision

author.name: Shuxing Zhang, Yongquan Ni, Zhenyu Ding, Yawen Lin

entry.summary: Presents a cross-modal teacher-student framework that reconstructs full-body 3D meshes with per-joint uncertainty from extremely sparse commercial mmWave radar (~6.5 points/frame). It uses SAM 3D Body as a zero-training teacher to generate dense mesh ground truth from single RGB frames, plus a StudentPoseFormer architecture with masked attention pooling.

entry.title: Dual-Stream Simultaneous Translation via 2D Grid Attention

author.name: Yu Pu, Wei-Qiang Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes representing source and target streams in simultaneous machine translation as a two-dimensional grid of hidden states with four structurally distinct attention types merged via joint QK Softmax normalization. Complexity-reducing approximations with provably decaying error and a self-guided training loop using per-cell loss heatmaps replace post-hoc read-write policies.

entry.title: PDEU-Bench: Benchmarking the Personalized Planning Lifecycle of Tool-Calling LLM Agents

author.name: Huayi Lai, Shichao Song, Qingchen Yu, Simin Niu, Mengwei Wang, Hanyu Wang, Xun Liang

entry.summary: PDEU-Bench evaluates the full personalized planning lifecycle of tool-using LLM agents: plan definition, execution, and revision across long multi-step interactions while preserving user preferences. It fills a gap left by benchmarks that only test isolated tool calls. The benchmark highlights whether agents can maintain and adapt explicit plans over sustained interaction, a key capability for practical assistants.

entry.title: PEARL: Adaptive Prefill-Decode Execution with Elasticity for Agentic Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jiaan Zhu, Wei Gao, Youhui Bai, Zewen Jin, Ju Huang, Siran Yang, Jiamang Wang, Lin Qu, Cheng Li

entry.summary: PEARL is an asynchronous agentic RL systems contribution that jointly optimizes GPU resource elasticity and prefill-decode configuration during multi-turn rollouts, which dominate RL training cost. It exploits transient resource-availability windows and adapts colocation versus disaggregated PD execution per workload.

entry.title: Just Initialize: A Training-Free Initialization Component for Large-Scale Routing Optimization

author.name: Jiale Zhao, Sirui Mao, Zimu Chen, Wentao Yang, Zihan Wang, Xuefeng Huang, Junji Cheng, Liyuanjun Lai

entry.summary: The authors propose Just Initialize, a training-free, solver-agnostic component that compresses large routing instances into a compact surrogate space, optimizes the global routing structure there, and uses the recovered solution as a warm start in the original space. This reframes progress on large-scale routing away from more expensive optimizers toward better initialization. It matters for combinatorial optimization with neural methods, where scaling to large instances remains costly.

entry.title: Report: Progressive Disclosure of Agent Skills

author.name: Guilin Zhang, Kai Zhao, Priyanka Mudgal, Waleed Ammar, Xiquan Cui, Xu Chu, Alet Blanken

entry.summary: A Workday industry report empirically studies progressive disclosure (lazy-loading) of skills for deployed LLM agents, where growing skill libraries inflate operational cost. The authors find that lazy-loading skill definitions improves skill-retrieval quality but marginally degrades end-to-end latency. This offers practical deployment guidance for scaling agent capabilities cost-effectively.

entry.title: Cross-Dataset Transfer and Unknown-Class Detection in Imbalanced SAR Ship Classification

author.name: Ch Muhammad Awais, Marco Reggiannini, Davide Moroni, Giulio Del Corso

entry.summary: This paper evaluates six pretrained models for SAR ship classification across in-domain, cross-dataset transfer, and unknown-class detection settings on FUSARShip, OpenSARShip, and SARDet100K. It reveals severe cross-dataset failures and provides balanced-accuracy benchmarks, highlighting how fragile these models are under deployment shifts. This matters for practical remote-sensing applications where training and deployment corpora differ.

entry.title: Does Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture Pretraining Help Time Series Forecasting?

author.name: Yutong Feng, Bowen Liao, See Kiong Ng, Yuxuan Liang

entry.summary: The authors conduct a large-scale evaluation of JEPA self-supervised pretraining for time series, testing one JEPA instantiation across nine backbones and eleven benchmarks covering temporal and spatio-temporal forecasting. This is billed as the most extensive cross-architecture assessment of JEPA for time series to date. The work aims to clarify whether JEPA pretraining delivers reliable benefits or whether gains depend heavily on the downstream model, addressing previously mixed evidence.

entry.title: SynDORBench: Evaluating LVLM Perceptual Robustness Under Physically Constrained Visibility Conditions

author.name: Jeremy Stephen Gabriel Yee, Zhengkui Wang, Zhiyuan Zhang, Avinash Anand, Timothy Liu, Benedict Chan, Aik Beng Ng, Simon See

entry.summary: SynDORBench is the first benchmark evaluating large vision-language model perceptual robustness under physically grounded, DORI-calibrated visibility conditions (camera distance, illumination, viewpoint, pixel density) aligned with human visual capability standards. It comprises over 54k question-answer pairs generated via a controllable synthetic pipeline. This addresses a real gap since existing LVLM benchmarks assume ideal visual inputs, and it quantifies how imaging conditions affect semantic recoverability.

entry.title: FARE: Deep Reinforcement Learning For Fair Exposure Constrained Uncertainty Aware Financial Content Personalization

author.name: Arundeep Chinta, Lucas Vinh Tran, Jay Katukuri

entry.summary: This paper frames fair exposure-constrained content ranking in financial services as a deep reinforcement learning problem, using Share of Voice (SOV) constraints to guarantee each content category a target fraction of top-position exposure. The approach draws an analogy to constrained trade execution in algorithmic finance and adds uncertainty awareness to prevent high-CTR content from dominating visibility. It matters because it offers a principled alternative to common re-ranking layers for enforcing contractual fairness and product diversity obligations in personalized recommendation.

entry.title: CaptchaArena: A Large-Scale, Fine-Grained Dataset for Training Computer-Use Agents on Interactive CAPTCHAs

author.name: Zhenhao Zhang, Zhaoyu Fan, Haohan Ying, Jingwen Hu, Hancen Fan, Junhao Zhou, Zitian Chen, Linchao Zhu

entry.summary: CaptchaArena is the first large-scale fine-grained training dataset for interactive CAPTCHA solving: 50K puzzles across 20 CAPTCHA types and 5 interaction modes, all solutions verified by execution, with 50K screenshot-action trajectories (46K with step-by-step reasoning) and pixel-mask annotations. The authors train CaptchaAgent, a single 9B policy for all 20 types using SFT followed by RL. This advances computer-use agent capabilities, though CAPTCHA solving is dual-use and raises security-ethics considerations.

entry.title: KeyRec: Bounded Visual Memory for Streaming and Long-Video Understanding

author.name: Zihan Chen, Xuejian Rong, Xiaojuan Wang, Boqing Gong, Adi Zicher, Yael Pritch, Nikhil Karnad

entry.summary: KeyRec is a training-free framework for bounded visual memory in vision-language models processing long videos and continuous streams, preserving fine-grained recent observations in a visual cache while organizing historical evidence into a structured event bank with novelty-based candidate events. This avoids the prohibitive cost of accumulating dense visual tokens and the evidence loss of naive token selection. It targets coherent long-horizon video understanding at bounded memory.

entry.title: LaMET-Agent: An Agent Framework for Large-Momentum Effective Theory Analysis

author.name: Jinchen He, Xiangyu Jiang, Fei Yao, Dian-Jun Zhao

entry.summary: This paper presents an open-source LLM agent framework that organizes the multi-stage LaMET workflow for computing parton distributions from lattice QCD into a reproducible, inspectable analysis pipeline, currently supporting collinear quark distributions with steps like renormalization, Fourier transformation, and perturbative matching. It matters as a concrete demonstration of LLM agents automating expert-level nuclear physics calculations that traditionally require substantial repeated human judgment.

entry.title: Affordance-Conditioned Decision Making: Bridging the Semantic-Spatial Gap in Zero-Shot Cross-Floor Vision-and-Language Navigation

author.name: Xuekang Yang, Lu Chen, Shuang Luo, Jialing Zhu, Qi Zhang, Yue Gao, Xiang Zhang

entry.summary: The paper introduces PACE, a supervised local execution module that augments frozen zero-shot semantic planners for cross-floor vision-and-language navigation by grounding transition semantics such as staircases and doorways into agent-centric traversable affordance poses, with preference-refined short-horizon action generation. It addresses the gap between correct high-level intent and reliable physical traversal in spatially constrained transitions, including recovery from accumulated action errors.

entry.title: DiffPTS: Rethinking Diffusion ELBO for Probabilistic Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Weiwei Ye, Dongyuan Li, Hangchen Liu, Haotong Jiang, Yoshihide Sekimoto, Renhe Jiang

entry.summary: DiffPTS rethinks the diffusion evidence lower bound under a Location-Scale Noise Model, showing it naturally induces a Gaussian negative log likelihood objective for pretrained mean and variance estimators, thereby integrating estimator training into variational inference rather than treating it as a separate regression task. This yields a more principled framework for DDPM-based probabilistic time series forecasting under distributional shift.

entry.title: TimeES: Probabilistic and Deterministic Time Series Forecasting via Evolutionary Spectra

author.name: Weiwei Ye, Renhe Jiang, Hangchen Liu, Dongyuan Li, Yoshihide Sekimoto

entry.summary: TimeES is a forecasting framework grounded in evolutionary spectra theory that explicitly models the evolution and randomness of Fourier spectra for non-stationary time series, providing both probabilistic and deterministic prediction. It parameterizes the evolutionary spectrum formulation, recasting non-stationary random process modeling as learning an evolving spectral representation. This brings classical time-frequency theory into modern deep forecasting.

entry.title: DashAct: A Progressive Diagnostic Benchmark for GUI Agents in Interactive Dashboard Analysis

author.name: Chuhan Zhang, Qi Xie, Ziyue Wang, Jianing Yin, Yunfan Zhou, Dazhen Deng, Yingcai Wu

entry.summary: DashAct is the first benchmark to diagnose GUI agent failures at a fine-grained level within interactive dashboard analysis tasks, containing 357 human-verified interaction trajectories with milestone dependencies and hierarchical target annotations. Its progressive diagnostic cascade separates failures in maintaining the analytical process, selecting actions, and grounding visual targets, going beyond final-answer success metrics. It is valuable for understanding where stateful GUI agents actually break.

entry.title: Learning an Anchored Prompt Space for Continual Adaptation of Large Language Models

author.name: Rongguang Ye, Zhan Zhuang, Yichen Wu, Ming Tang, Kede Ma

entry.summary: LAPS targets continual adaptation of LLMs by jointly adapting model parameters and task-specific soft prompts while preserving prior capabilities. It aligns historical prompts with the updated model via self-distillation and constructs an anchored prompt space whose vertices correspond to task prompts to enable positive transfer. This addresses the known problem of stale prompts as models evolve during continual learning.

entry.title: Not Every Term Adds New Structure: Sobolev Novelty for Symbolic Regression

author.name: Boxiao Wang, Kai Li, Yuheng Jing, Tianyi Liu, Chen Li, Yifan Zhang, Jian Cheng

entry.summary: Sobolev Novelty is a term-level measure of structural independence for symbolic regression: for each candidate term it builds an empirical Sobolev signature from function values and exact derivatives over observed inputs and quantifies how much new structure it adds beyond the rest of the expression. This addresses the limitation of expression-level fitting-error objectives that cannot tell whether an individual term is genuinely informative or redundant. A mathematically principled search signal for equation discovery.

entry.title: Self-Evolving Multi-Agent Symbolic Discovery for Financial Fundamental Analysis

author.name: Kelvin J. L. Koa, Filip Orestav, Shengqiong Wu, Michael J. Wooldridge, Ke-Wei Huang

entry.summary: MUFASA is a hierarchical multi-agent framework for symbolic regression in financial valuation, introducing specialized agents representing distinct valuation perspectives and adaptive learning for non-stationary, noisy market conditions. It adapts symbolic discovery to a domain where multiple valid perspectives exist and there is no objectively correct equation. The approach targets interpretable fundamental analysis signals.

entry.title: Finding Emotions Where They Belong: Rethinking Audio Emotion Recognition through Masked Temporal Affective Grounding

author.name: Abdelrahman Mohamed, Lars Kai Hansen, Zheng-Hua Tan

entry.summary: The paper reformulates audio emotion recognition as Temporal Affective Grounding, associating emotions with temporally bounded speech spans and tone descriptions instead of single labels for whole recordings. The authors curate temporally annotated datasets and construct multi-span recordings with overlapping speech, showing that naive longer-format training degrades both recognition and grounding. This resolves ambiguity when multiple speakers and affective events co-occur.

entry.title: PolyTopoBench: A Benchmark for Complex Vector Polygon Generation from Remote Sensing Imagery

author.name: Zeping Liu, Ni Lao, Weiwei Sun, Gil Wolff, Yiqun Xie, Liang Zhao, Junfeng Jiao, Gengchen Mai

entry.summary: PolyTopoBench is a unified benchmark for evaluating vector polygon generation from remote sensing imagery, with explicit focus on complex polygons containing holes and preserving topology. It addresses limitations of raster-mask post-processing pipelines and of recent direct-generation methods that only handle simple exterior contours. A standardized evaluation here could accelerate progress in mapping and autonomous-driving-relevant perception.

entry.title: More than 83.69% of the zeros of the Riemann zeta function are distinct

author.name: Kristian Muri Knausg{\aa}rd

entry.summary: This pure mathematics paper improves the lower bound on the asymptotic proportion of distinct nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function to at least 0.8369928814, up from 0.83625, using an unconditional Montgomery pair-correlation estimate plus a new matrix inequality with a free clipping parameter. It is categorized under Artificial Intelligence but contains no AI content. The result is a genuine incremental advance in analytic number theory.

entry.title: Scoring the Wrong Question: Readout Failures in Constrained-Option Evaluation

author.name: Jiaxuan Guo, Kejia Zhang, Shuo Xin, Jingxin Yang, Youran Sun, Haizhao Yang

entry.summary: Shows that constrained-option scoring reads model probabilities for permitted answers even when the model is about to write something else, demonstrating on Qwen3 checkpoints that a quoted multiple-choice item can hijack the answer token and make forecasts of reader correctness indistinguishable from chance. Contributes a label-free diagnostic of declared options' support and first-token mass in context.

entry.title: AquaWAM: A Dynamics-aware World Action Model for Underwater Embodied Agents

author.name: Cunhao Zhu, Yifeng Wang, Dongliang Xu, Yunzhong Hou, Yue Yao, Chi Harold Liu

entry.summary: AquaWAM is presented as the first World Action Model for underwater robots, explicitly modeling passive dynamics such as inertia, buoyancy, hydrodynamic drag, and persistent drift that persist after actions complete. Rather than only predicting action-conditioned images, it models action effects alongside environmental dynamics. This addresses a real gap for embodied agents in aquatic environments.

entry.title: ViCoR: Reliable Molecular Structure Extraction via Spatially Aligned Verification and Executable Revision

author.name: Yujian Yuan, Xin Cai, Yufan Chen, Jiaxin Xu, Mengdi Liu, Zhichao Tan, Long Chen, Hanyu Gao

entry.summary: ViCoR addresses optical chemical structure recognition through a repair-before-reject setting, using spatially aligned verification and executable revision to correct recognized molecular structures and reject only unresolved cases. This improves reliability of chemical data curation from scientific literature beyond what rejection-only approaches achieve.

entry.title: Tsubame: Tree Replay for Diffusion-Based Speculative Decoding

author.name: Yepeng Weng, Qiao Hu, Takehisa Yairi

entry.summary: Tsubame improves context-aware dynamic tree speculative decoding by decoupling tree topology from token selection: after the tree structure is fixed, its nodes are repopulated by sampling rather than deterministic high-score tokens. This retains the structural budget-allocation advantages of dynamic trees while recovering acceptance gains from stochastic sampling with advanced verification. It targets faster LLM inference via diffusion-based speculative decoding.

entry.title: Validating Memory-Optimal Transformer Kernels on Real Hardware: From Formal Derivation to Measured Performance Across Two HPC Clusters

author.name: Lenore M. Mullin, Gaetan Hains

entry.summary: This paper validates formally derived memory-optimal transformer kernels (attention forward/backward, fused variants, decode, and full blocks) from the Mathematics of Arrays framework against measured performance on two HPC clusters, CPU and GPU. It identifies and fixes a GPU regression where a fused forward+backward kernel proven to avoid O(n^2) intermediates initially ran slower than naive implementations. The work connects formal specification methods to real-world systems performance.

entry.title: FLARE: Flow Matching with Local Axis-Angle Representations for Stochastic Micromagnetic Evolution

author.name: Pengyu Li, Renjie Tong, Xuanlue Jiang, Jianmin Li, Yuanyuan Zhou

entry.summary: FLARE is a flow-matching framework for stochastic micromagnetic simulation that predicts full magnetization fields directly at a target horizon rather than integrating Landau-Lifshitz-Gilbert dynamics step by step. It represents rotations in a local axis-angle space that respects the geometry of magnetization and preserves unit norm by construction. This matters because long-horizon micromagnetic simulation is computationally expensive and learned solvers have so far been limited to stepwise or deterministic prediction.

entry.title: Investigating Human--AI Discrepancies via Multiple-Solution Problems

author.name: Zihao Wang, Francesco Insulla, Andrea Montanari

entry.summary: This arXiv paper studies whether human and AI reasoning produce different distributions over valid answers, using 270 puzzles across five families where each puzzle has 3 to 8 correct solutions. Rather than scoring models only on correctness, the authors compare the distribution of answers from humans and from resampled frontier models, finding that model distributions diverge sharply from human ones and that different models resemble each other far more than any resembles humans. This matters because it introduces a distributional lens on human-AI alignment beyond simple benchmark accuracy, with implications for how model diversity and mode collapse are measured.

entry.title: SyncRA: Learning Temporal Correspondence in Omni-Modal Models

author.name: Zelong Xu, Yan Li, Wenhe Hu, Xiyang Hu

entry.summary: SyncRA diagnoses a temporal correspondence weakness in omni-modal models, which produce plausible answers grounded in incorrect audio-visual pairings when inputs are swapped. The proposed lightweight contrastive method aligns intermediate audio-visual representations within each video to strengthen what-hears/what-sees binding. This improves reliability of multimodal models in synchronized contexts.

entry.title: Zero-Shot Cue-Grounded Topic Segmentation of Spoken Documents

author.name: Suhwan Choi, Myeongho Jeon, Myungjoo Kang

entry.summary: This paper introduces Cue-Grounded Segmentation (CGS), a training-free framework that segments spoken documents by first identifying phrases that explicitly signal a new topic and using their positions as boundaries, falling back to semantic segmentation when cues are sparse. It addresses the granularity problem in LLM-based segmenters that either merge subtopics or over-segment coherent themes. The work matters for improving navigation and downstream understanding of long-form spoken and transcribed content.

entry.title: Evidence-Aligned Multimodal On-Policy Self-Distillation for Fine-Grained Visual Understanding

author.name: Nanxing Hu, Qiwei Yan, Jinchao Zhang, Guoliang Kang

entry.summary: This paper proposes a multimodal on-policy self-distillation method where a teacher conditioned on evidence-centered crops supervises a student viewing full images along student-generated trajectories, targeting fine-grained visual understanding. It analyzes how teacher designs trade off training stability against evidence relevance and model-state gap, and introduces mechanisms to align teacher corrections with task-relevant visual evidence.

entry.title: Reference-Tail Trust:Certified Probability Floors for Learned Updates Inside a Deployed Network

author.name: Abdolvahab Khalili Sadaghiani, Jose Nunez-Yanez

entry.summary: Introduces Reference-Tail Trust (RTT), a framework that allows learned updates inside a frozen graph neural network while certifying per-node prediction probability floors and a call-level budget on distributional change. It couples graph-based proposal states with a constrained optimizer that charges each displacement for worst-case terminal cross-entropy increase through the remaining message-passing layers.

entry.title: TIDE: Teacher-Student Transition via Informative Distillation and Exploration for Agentic RL

author.name: Yibin Huang, Xinming Xu, Conghui Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes TIDE for training multi-turn agents with GRPO, dynamically scheduling on-policy distillation from a stronger teacher rather than keeping a fixed mixture. It observes that constant distillation pressure constrains the student beyond the teacher's capabilities globally and misaligns with reward signals locally at different interaction turns.

entry.title: From Normative Frameworks to Alignment Data: Constructing and Evaluating SFT and Preference Data

author.name: Husrev Taha Sencar, Rezart Beka, Danish Naeem, Seda Ozalkan, Majd Hawasly, Ji Lucas, Ala AlFuqaha, Mohamed Abdallah, Recep Senturk

entry.summary: Seven domain experts spent about a year constructing Arabic-English alignment datasets grounded in Islamic ethical, theological, and jurisprudential traditions, yielding roughly 2.8K SFT examples and 5.4K preference pairs. The methodology translates abstract normative principles into concrete training and preference signals.

entry.title: From Pixel to Poses: Object-centric Tool Manipulation Learning from Human Demonstrations

author.name: Bangjun Wang, Longyan Wu, Yukun Wei, Shenghe Shao, Chaoyi Huang, Wenze Cui, Zetong Xu, Hanlin Wu, Long Chen, Yi Ma, Hongyang Li

entry.summary: P2P-T is a data-efficient, object-centric framework for learning tool manipulation from human video demonstrations without paired human-robot data. It uses a two-stage approach with object-centric pretraining to bridge the gap between cognitive understanding and precise physical execution, addressing a known weakness of long-horizon imitation approaches.

entry.title: QC-Stark: A Multi-Task Benchmark Revealing Capability Dissociations in LLMs Evaluated on Quantum Computing Tasks

author.name: Pranav Gupta

entry.summary: Introduces QC-Stark, a benchmark of 11 auto-verifiable quantum computing tasks spanning circuit construction, debugging, compilation, and error correction, evaluated across 10 models with IRT-based measurement validation. The key finding is that aggregate rankings mask substantial per-task variation, with ranking correlations statistically insignificant for several tasks.

entry.title: Replay in the Silent Degrees of Freedom: Continual Learning Without an Offline Phase

author.name: Zhang Yanhai

entry.summary: Explores whether biologically constrained local learning rules can consolidate memories without any offline phase, inspired by local sleep. Using an isolation rule confining replay updates to hidden synapses under k-winner-take-all dynamics, a refractory rotation rule, and homeostatic/novelty gating, the network consolidates during wakefulness alone.

entry.title: Symmetry-quotient Flatness and Generalization

author.name: Taiki Miyagawa

entry.summary: Develops a symmetry-aware theory of flatness on quotient spaces of neural network parameters, showing that quotient linear stability implies quotient flatness, which implies input smoothness and generalization under covering assumptions. Addresses the fact that standard flatness measures are not invariant under function-preserving symmetries such as positive rescaling.

entry.title: Depth Laws for the Precision Floor of Trained Neural Networks: Amplification, Residual Scaling, and a Quantization-Aware Training Paradox

author.name: Ahmad S. Tarawneh

entry.summary: This paper develops a first-order theory for the precision floor — the bit-width or perturbation level at which network accuracy collapses halfway to chance — across MLPs, CNNs, Vision Transformers, and nine pretrained language models under post-training quantization and quantization-aware training. It shows the floor is governed by a single quantity, predictive amplification G, whose square grows linearly with depth at a rate tied to the squared residual branch scale. The theory predicts a depth-exponent equality that holds empirically in most trained architectures and also reveals a surprising QAT paradox.

entry.title: Playing to Par: Reinforcement Learning for Provably Optimal Quadrilateral Block Decompositions

author.name: Arjun Narayanan, Per-Olof Persson

entry.summary: The authors train a reinforcement learning agent to construct quadrilateral block decompositions of planar domains that provably reach the discrete Gauss-Bonnet lower bound on total vertex irregularity, which they call par. The agent acts on a half-edge mesh data structure with a connectivity-aware policy network that generalizes unchanged to larger domains than seen in training. This connects RL to mesh generation with a provable optimality target.

entry.title: Learning Through Game: Skewed Transfer of Tabular Knowledge to Strengthen Image Model

author.name: Longfei Huang, Shangdong Yang, Yang Yang

entry.summary: The paper proposes Skewed Knowledge Transfer (SKT), which asymmetrically transfers tabular knowledge into image models during training so the image model works standalone at test time when tables are unavailable. It addresses modality imbalance and asymmetric cross-modal relationships via adaptive gradient integration in a shared parameter space. This addresses a practical gap in multimodal tabular-image learning where tabular data is missing at inference.

entry.title: Recovery-Directed Symbolic Distillation of Neural Likelihoods

author.name: Kiant\'e Fernandez, Xinwei Li

entry.summary: The paper introduces a symbolic distillation pipeline converting black-box amortized neural likelihoods into explicit, interpretable expressions optimized for parameter estimation. A recovery-directed objective guides symbolic regression toward preserving parameter-recovery accuracy rather than merely approximating the likelihood, with selection jointly weighing complexity, recovery, and distributional fit. This improves interpretability of simulation-based inference models.

entry.title: Quantization-Aware Pre-Training with Constrained Empirical Weight Distribution

author.name: Ningfeng Yang, Tor M. Aamodt

entry.summary: The paper identifies rounding boundary weight oscillation as a key source of training noise in quantization-aware pre-training and proposes CEWT, a hyperparameter-free, memory-overhead-free optimizer post-update step that projects weights to suppress oscillations. The authors claim it is the first such method to consistently improve QAPT accuracy.

entry.title: Distributionally Robust Average-Reward Reinforcement Learning: Finite-Sample Guarantees under Weak Communication

author.name: Chenyu Lu, Zijun Chen, Nian Si

entry.summary: This paper provides finite-sample guarantees for distributionally robust reinforcement learning in the average-reward setting when the Markov decision process is only weakly communicating. It derives explicit radius conditions for divergence-based and distance-based uncertainty sets under which the robust Bellman equation admits a solvable constant-gain solution, and proposes a prior-knowledge-free algorithm.

entry.title: Efficient Dynamic Algorithms for Graph Neural Networks with Non-Linear Propagation

author.name: Kiarash Banihashem, MohammadTaghi Hajiaghayi, Mahdi JafariRaviz, Silvio Lattanzi, Danny Mittal

entry.summary: This paper develops residual-based dynamic algorithms to efficiently maintain node representations for non-linear GNN propagation when edges are inserted or deleted, extending prior work that was limited to linear Personalized PageRank propagation. Because the propagation is parameter-free and only the classifier is trained, exact or near-exact maintenance under graph updates becomes feasible. This matters for applications on evolving networks where retraining after each edge change is impractical.

entry.title: Mycelium: A Generalizable Cross-Grid Multi-Task Model for Electrical Distribution Systems

author.name: Zhengyang Wei, Shourya Bose, Helgi Hilmarsson, Elena Carnio, Dhruv Suri

entry.summary: Mycelium defines a unified grid ontology representing heterogeneous distribution networks as graphs that preserve topology, asset types, and electrical relationships, plus a physics-based simulation pipeline with faults and reconfigurations. The goal is a single multi-task model grounded in grid physics that generalizes to unseen distribution networks from sparse, noisy measurements.

entry.title: From Grey-Box to Green-Box: When can Physics-Informed Machine Learning Reduce Carbon Footprints in Structural Health Monitoring?

author.name: Daisy R. Bradley, Nathan A. Hinchliffe, Daniel J. Pitchforth, Matthew R. Jones, Elizabeth J. Cross

entry.summary: This paper investigates whether physics-informed grey-box models in structural health monitoring offer a lower environmental footprint than black-box machine learning, by relating training data quantity and training time to compute-associated carbon emissions. It reframes the well-known data-efficiency benefits of physics-informed approaches through a sustainability lens, coining the notion of green-box modeling. The work matters because it quantifies the environmental cost dimension of an increasingly compute-heavy engineering ML practice.

entry.title: FoldAttention: Declared-Reference Softmax for Fast Decode and Deterministic Backward

author.name: Sriman Achanta

entry.summary: FoldAttention proposes an additive softmax formulation that fixes a finite normalization reference before scanning the KV cache, so each computed weight is final and contributions add across disjoint key ranges, matching softmax attention exactly in real arithmetic. This enables faster decode and deterministic backward passes.

entry.title: LLM4Trust: Exploring the Capabilities of Large Language Models for Trust Evaluation

author.name: Jie Wang, Yanbo Sun, Zheng Yan, Jiahe Lan, Elisa Bertino

entry.summary: This paper introduces LLM4Trust, presented as the first benchmark framework for systematically evaluating whether LLMs can perform trust evaluation in cybersecurity contexts. It constructs diverse trust graphs modeling five basic trust properties and leverages LLM zero-/few-shot reasoning to address limitations of prior learning-based trust evaluation methods, such as heavy ground-truth requirements and poor explainability.

entry.title: StatD2GAN: When Calibration Masks Generator Quality in Held-Out Evaluation of Synthetic Weather Sequences

author.name: Mustafa Ozaytac, Ozge Karadag Atas

entry.summary: Demonstrates that pooled distributional metrics computed after marginal calibration can invalidate architectural conclusions when evaluating generative weather models, and rebuilds StatD2GAN evaluation around a strict held-out protocol with embargoed years and corrected statistical testing across climate zones. The paper exposes a methodological flaw likely affecting the broader synthetic-weather literature.

entry.title: ICMAPE: In-Context Multiagent Pure Exploration

author.name: Xinyi Hu, Alessio Russo, Aldo Pacchiano

entry.summary: ICMAPE is a Bayesian learning framework for decentralized multi-agent pure exploration, addressing a gap where active sequential hypothesis testing has been mostly single-agent and finite. It converts fixed-confidence identification objectives into inference-confidence-derived rewards so standard RL machinery can be applied in-context.

entry.title: On the Relation Between Interval Regret and Dynamic Regret

author.name: Yi-Han Wang, Peng Zhao, Zhi-Hua Zhou

entry.summary: This theory paper clarifies the long-standing relationship between interval regret and dynamic regret, two key performance metrics for non-stationary online learning. It challenges the common intuition that interval regret is the stronger notion, providing a precise characterization of when each metric dominates. This matters for guiding algorithm design in changing environments.

entry.title: Compute Time Scaling with Recursive Models for Combinatorial Optimization

author.name: Zhengxi Zhang, Paul Swoboda

entry.summary: Proposes Tiny Recursive Models for Combinatorial Optimization (TRM-style), a neural method that scales both recursion depth and parallel sampling width, using a graph-aware tiny recursive network with adaptive halting and a lightweight problem-specific decoder. It improves the quality-efficiency balance of general neural solvers over prior heatmap-based approaches.

entry.title: Learning Regional Snow Water Equivalent and Snow Height Variations from Sentinel-1 InSAR Acquisitions

author.name: Luca Barco, Lorenzo Innocenti, Bianca Bartoli, Claudio Rossi, Edoardo Arnaudo, Paolo Garza

entry.summary: This paper evaluates three machine learning architectures (XGBoost, U-Net, and SegFormer) for jointly estimating Snow Water Equivalent and Snow Height variations from Sentinel-1 InSAR satellite data over the Italian Alps, using the IT-SNOW reanalysis dataset as ground truth. SegFormer achieves the best performance on both targets with the lowest variability across runs, and a feature sensitivity analysis reveals that adding all available features does not necessarily reduce error. The work matters because reliable snow monitoring at scale is critical for water resource management in mountainous regions.

entry.title: Instance-Adaptive Prompts as Context for Time-Series Foundation Models

author.name: Zehao Xiao, Shifeng Xie, Lei Zan, Jianfeng Zhang, Lujia Pan, Ievgen Redko, Malik Tiomoko, Keli Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces PaCTS, a method that replaces long input histories for time-series foundation models with a compact set of learned, instance-adaptive latent prompt tokens conditioned on visible context. The prompts combine global statistics with segment-level temporal information and are trained jointly for heterogeneous time-series domains. This addresses the inference-cost problem of feeding long histories to frozen TSFMs.

entry.title: Explaining Hyperbolic Neural Networks via Geometry-Aware Relevance Propagation

author.name: Ping Xiong, Shanglin Li, Yi Ding, Thomas Schnake, Shinichi Nakajima

entry.summary: This paper addresses how to produce faithful feature attributions (explanations) for hyperbolic neural networks, where geometric operations complicate standard relevance propagation. The authors identify a new issue called Geometric Representation Invariance, where mathematically equivalent geometric realizations yield different attributions, and propose LRP-radial-all, a rule for origin-centered radial modules that conserves relevance and remains invariant to equivalent factorizations while satisfying zero-curvature consistency. This extends explainability methods to non-Euclidean architectures, an underexplored area as hyperbolic networks see growing use for hierarchical data.

entry.title: Fiona: Accelerating FHE Inference with Packing-Aware Ternary Weights

author.name: Yiteng Peng, Zhibo Liu, Dongwei Xiao, Shuai Wang

entry.summary: Presents FIONA, an offline optimizer that accelerates fully homomorphic encryption inference by ternarizing plaintext-ciphertext weight multiplications in a packing-aware manner, targeting only weight groups whose weights can share ternary values without accuracy loss. Since PMults account for over half of FHE inference time, this could substantially speed privacy-preserving neural inference. A systems contribution at the intersection of quantization and cryptography.

entry.title: Output-aware Residual Stream Pruning for Large Language Models

author.name: Chayne Thrash, Kevin Chen, Soheil Kolouri

entry.summary: The paper proposes a sensitivity-aware residual stream pruning method for LLMs that replaces activation-reconstruction criteria with a second-order approximation of output KL divergence, coupling activation covariance with downstream output sensitivity. This direction-dependent subspace selection better preserves model behavior at reduced hidden dimension.

entry.title: Rethinking Personalized Generation: Test-Time Alignment via Factorized Ranking Models

author.name: Qiyao Ma, Junshan Zhang, Zhe Zhao

entry.summary: The paper empirically shows large untapped headroom for personalized LLM generation via test-time alignment, framing personalization as a candidate-matching problem suited to Best-of-N scaling. It proposes small factorized ranking models as efficient, better-calibrated replacements for billion-parameter reward models when scoring large candidate pools.

entry.title: Be Careful Who You Trust: Coordination Dynamics under Corrupted Communication in LLM Multi-Agent Games

author.name: Xuanyi Liu, Niall Dalton, Hairi Amin, Xiyuan Yin, Lydia Lim

entry.summary: Studies iterated N-player Stag Hunt games among homogeneous LLM groups under programmatic action inversion of public communication, across group sizes, thresholds, corruption levels, and seven LLMs. It finds, for example, that in an N=5, M=3 setting pre-flip coordination success remains 78% even at 80% corruption, with much of the public performance drop being mechanical rather than behavioral.

entry.title: Evasion Attacks on Cost-Utility-Based Adversarial Training for Online AutoML in IoT Networks

author.name: Chukwunonso Henry Nwokoye, Wajiha Zaheer, Khalil El-Khatib, Li Yang

entry.summary: This paper evaluates how black-box evasion attacks affect cost-utility-based adversarial training defenses when applied to online machine learning models (such as Hoeffding Trees, Leveraging Bagging, Streaming Random Patches, and Hoeffding Adaptive Trees) used for intrusion, malware, and anomaly detection in IoT networks. It sits at the intersection of streaming/online learning, adversarial robustness, and IoT security, testing whether a defense strategy holds up under attack in an Online AutoML setting.

entry.title: Continuous-Time Trajectory Generation from Discrete Observations with Stochasticity

author.name: Ruifeng Shang, Shu Liu, Yuhua Zhu

entry.summary: PhiBE-Flow is a framework that estimates the probability velocity field induced by the stochastic differential equation governing continuous-time distributional evolution, enabling trajectory generation consistent with observed densities from discrete-time data. The method is model-free, requiring neither known SDE coefficients nor score estimation, and comes with convergence guarantees. This addresses the gap between discrete observations and continuous-time dynamics in generative modeling of stochastic systems.

entry.title: What Should the Reflector See? An Empirical Study of Evidence in Reflective Prompt Optimization

author.name: Xiaofan Zhou, Lu Cheng

entry.summary: This empirical study examines which evidence composition a reflector should receive in reflective prompt optimization, evaluating nine reflection strategies across five datasets using Qwen3.5-9B as both task model and reflector. Findings show failures-only evidence yields the largest mean test gain while no-examples reflection works best for improving sampled parents, revealing that different objectives favor different evidence policies.

entry.title: Schur-Neural KF: Learned Schur-Consistent Corrections to the Extended Kalman Filter

author.name: Min Kim, Lianghao Cao, Soon-Jo Chung, Andrew M. Stuart

entry.summary: SN-KF is a learning-based correction to the extended Kalman filter that preserves the EKF's probabilistic conditioning interpretation by perturbing cross-covariance and Cholesky factors via a Schur complement parametrization guaranteeing positive semidefiniteness. The authors prove that incorporating a measurement never increases state uncertainty and that no measurement can induce arbitrarily large updates, instantiating the parametrization with a recurrent neural architecture with amplitude gates.

entry.title: Is H&E Image-to-Spatial Transcriptomics Simpler Than It Looks?

author.name: Duc T. Nguyen, Thanh Ha Do, Phuong M. Cao, Hieu Pham

entry.summary: Analyzes why simple estimators often match sophisticated architectures in predicting spatial gene expression from H&E histology, using an MSE error decomposition. It shows differences in average gene expression account for much of aggregate performance, and the key unresolved challenge is recovering within-slide variation, clarifying where model complexity is actually needed.

entry.title: Schr\"odinger--F\"ollmer Actor--Critic: Diffusion Policy Improvement with Finite-Sample Analysis

author.name: Yuling Jiao, Lican Kang, Jerry Zhijian Yang, Jincheng Ying

entry.summary: This paper proposes SFAC, an offline-to-online reinforcement learning method that performs KL-regularized policy improvement using conditional diffusion policies. It combines a minimax Bellman critic for advantage estimation with a Doob h-transform framework that expresses the policy update as a correction to a reference diffusion drift, estimated via paired self-normalized importance sampling, and provides finite-sample statistical guarantees for the resulting actor-critic algorithm.

entry.title: Let CSP Be Your ANCHOR: Adaptive Crystal Search over Frozen Structure Priors

author.name: Emma Lei Hovmand, Jonas Elsborg, Melih Kandemir, Arghya Bhowmik

entry.summary: ANCHOR separates where to search from how to generate in de novo crystal discovery: a frozen crystal structure prediction model acts as a fixed physical prior while a GRPO-trained composition policy explores with multi-objective rewards. It introduces continuous adaptive novelty (CAN), a graded novelty score against known structures and a growing discovery history. The approach targets more reliable materials-discovery pipelines.

entry.title: Prompt-Anchored Residual Adaptation for Biomedical Vision-Language Models

author.name: Jingxuan Kang, Qianying Yue, Che Liu, Chen Qin

entry.summary: The paper proposes PARA, a few-shot adaptation method for biomedical vision-language models that keeps the frozen prompt-based prediction as a support-invariant semantic anchor while learning a visual residual prediction on top. This addresses the sensitivity of few-shot adapted predictions to the composition of the small labeled support set, which matters for biomedical classification tasks that hinge on subtle visual differences.

entry.title: Recursive LLM Degradation in Biomedical Question Answering: A Cross-Generation Study

author.name: Bibek Bhandari, Kshitij Lingthep

entry.summary: This study empirically examines model collapse from recursive synthetic-data training in biomedical QA using two Qwen2.5 sizes (0.5B and 3B), comparing recursive generations G0-G3 against a human-controlled condition across multiple seeds and a fixed expert-labeled evaluation set. It measures degradation in extraction, QA quality, and distributional properties as errors and biases are reintroduced across generations.

entry.title: On the Numerical Reliability of Differentiable Physics-Based Optimization for Robotic Material Manipulation

author.name: Xintong Yang, Minglun Wei, Yu-Kun Lai, Ze Ji

entry.summary: The paper studies the numerical reliability of gradients propagated through long, contact-rich differentiable physics simulations used in robotic material manipulation, using two Material Point Method system-identification benchmarks. It shows that GPU many-to-one sums whose order depends on thread scheduling can change long-horizon gradients and even reverse the sign of a parameter gradient. These findings raise important caveats for gradient-based optimization built on differentiable simulation.

entry.title: Beyond Reconstruction Loss in Post-Training Quantization: Balanced Fitting for Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Minchan Kang, Kyeonghye Park, Seungyeon Sa, Seoyoung Cho, Daeshik Kim, Yucheol Cho

entry.summary: The paper proposes Balanced Fitting, a post-training quantization framework for large vision-language models that treats quantization effects as potentially beneficial regularization for certain layers and modalities rather than purely an error to minimize. Standard PTQ minimizes reconstruction loss against the full-precision model, which can over-preserve FP behavior and calibration-specific bias. The framework balances precision and regularization beyond reconstruction loss.

entry.title: When Text Matters: Design Principles for Visual Token Pruning in Vision-Language Model

author.name: Minchan Kang, Kyeonghye Park, Seoyoung Cho, Daeshik Kim, Yucheol Cho

entry.summary: The paper studies visual token pruning in large vision-language models and finds that applying textual guidance too early limits its ability to identify answer-relevant visual regions, while text-to-visual attention becomes more informative at intermediate decoder depths. Motivated by this analysis, it proposes a training-free method that separates early vision-guided pruning from later text-guided selection. This yields design principles for when and where text guidance helps in token pruning.

entry.title: G$^3$-LoRA: Organizing Reward-Weighted Video Data with Gradient-Guided Grouped LoRA

author.name: Jia Song (The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology), Wenhow Li (The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology), Lichen Bai (The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology), Bada Ye (Tencent), Zeke Xie (The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology)

entry.summary: This work tackles post-training text-to-video models on heterogeneous reward-weighted data by probing category-level gradients, removing the shared update direction, and clustering categories by residual gradient compatibility. It trains group-specific LoRA experts per compatible cluster and consolidates them, avoiding the fragile assumption that all data categories induce compatible updates.

entry.title: Beyond Energy: When Sustainability Dimensions Reshape LLM Serving Decisions

author.name: Tianyao Shi, Xipeng Shen, Yi Ding

entry.summary: PRISM is a unified framework for characterizing and optimizing LLM serving across energy, carbon, water, and biodiversity impacts. The key finding is a fundamental distinction: computing configurations determine energy use, while deployment location and timing determine carbon, water, and biodiversity outcomes, which can change optimal serving decisions.

entry.title: CoSE-E: A Benchmark for Code-switched Speech Evaluation in Enterprise Settings

author.name: Shama Gupta, Hoang H Nguyen, Chelsea Huang, Lindsay Devon Brin, Fanny Riols

entry.summary: This paper introduces COSE-E, a synthetic benchmark and multidimensional evaluation framework for code-switched automatic speech recognition in enterprise contexts, covering five language pairs. Its key contribution is evaluating how code-switching transcription errors propagate into downstream voice agent task failures rather than just measuring edit-distance WER. This operational framing is useful for organizations deploying multilingual voice agents.

entry.title: Quantization Thresholds Replicate, Failure Modes Do Not: A Three-Model Study of Agentic Tool Use in Polish from 8-bit to 2-bit

author.name: Jakub Prejzner

entry.summary: Using PolAgentBench, a deterministic Polish-language agentic tool-use benchmark with adversarial probes and an arithmetic isolation ladder, the author measures three models (Bielik-11B, its distilled 7B variant, and Llama-PLLuM-8B) at six GGUF precisions from Q8_0 to Q2_K. The central finding is that while all models collapse between 3-bit and 2-bit quantization, the specific failure modes do not replicate across models. This suggests collapse thresholds generalize but downstream degradation is model-specific.

entry.title: A model of rational interlocutors: Unification of comprehension and production

author.name: Hanlin Wu, Zhenguang G. Cai

entry.summary: The paper proposes the rational interlocutor model, a computational account unifying speaker modeling in comprehension and audience design in production as a single rational computation. An interlocutor maintains a partner model defined by identity, fidelity, and knowledge parameters that govern expected messages, forms, and reliability of message-to-utterance mappings. The framework bridges two previously separate psycholinguistic literatures.

entry.title: KinyaMed: Seeds, Not Rows -- What a Corpus Requirement Written in the Wrong Unit Fails to Constrain

author.name: Marius Bayizere

entry.summary: This paper describes a failed attempt to build a Kinyarwanda medical triage urgency classifier, showing that a corpus requirement specified as one million generated rows was satisfiable in 130 seconds while violating four to six of nine quality gates, because the binding constraint should have been the count of distinct authored seed sentences. The authors report the specification failure and the per-language instruments that detect it rather than a working classifier. It matters because it exposes how dataset-scale requirements written in the wrong unit can create a false appearance of adequate low-resource language data.

entry.title: FA-Bench: A Benchmark for Word-Level and Phone-Level Forced-Alignment and ASR Timestamps Under Clean and Noisy Conditions

author.name: Wei Chu, Yuanzhe Dong, Ke Tan, Dong Han, Yichao Zhou, Ruchao Fan, Bingshen Mu, Jingbei Li, Vishwas Shetty, Sarthak Bisht, Ziyue Qiu, Massa Baali, Rita Singh, Bhisha Raj

entry.summary: This paper introduces FA-Bench, an open benchmarking framework for forced alignment and ASR timestamp prediction that standardizes transcript normalization, data splits, phone mapping, and boundary scoring so results across studies become directly comparable. It evaluates 21 open models and 9 commercial APIs under a unified protocol across clean audio and four degradation types, with two tracks (reference transcripts vs. recognizer outputs) and fine-grained scoring of every boundary alongside its neighboring labels.

entry.title: ExpVoyager: Direct Experience Navigation for Dynamic Agent Skill Synthesis

author.name: Kwangwook Seo, Dongha Lee

entry.summary: ExpVoyager reframes agent skill synthesis as dynamic navigation of raw experience, deferring abstraction of past trajectories until downstream demands are known, rather than compressing experience into fixed procedural knowledge upfront. This avoids discarding knowledge that later becomes critical while retaining irrelevant instance details. The idea contributes to the growing area of self-evolving LLM agents that build reusable skill libraries.

entry.title: Knowing Is Not Choosing: What Explicit Verification Adds Beyond Generative Preference

author.name: Yilong Li, Chengpo Yan, Aayan Arish, Suman Banerjee

entry.summary: Decomposes factual recall in LLMs into candidate generation, ranking, and selection, showing pre-generation readouts predict recall but not final selection. Explicit verification via P(True) improves within-question ranking over mean log-likelihood across Gemma, Qwen3, and Llama families, with AUROC gains of 0.08-0.12 and several-point accuracy improvements in a prospective Gemma cohort. This clarifies a real gap between knowing and choosing that matters for reliable QA systems.

entry.title: Calibration, Not Answer Selection: Distilling Internal Confidence in Reasoning Models

author.name: Yadong Xi, Rongsheng Zhang, Tangjie Lv, Ziyang Luo, Ruochen Zhao

entry.summary: This paper examines why reasoning models trained with binary correctness rewards verbalize systematically overconfident confidence scores, showing the issue reflects commitment willingness rather than answer likelihood. The authors use a linear probe on hidden states between the chain of thought and the answer to extract better-calibrated internal confidence, achieving 5 to 38 times lower expected calibration error than verbalized confidence across four benchmarks and two model families. They also probe the limits of this approach when the internal signal is used downstream.
