author.name: Xander Staelens, Alb\'eric Loos, Bert Ramlot, Hannes Mareen, Peter Lambert, Glenn Van Wallendael

entry.summary: The authors introduce DeformView, a wide-baseline multi-view dataset with pixel-level annotations of geometric inconsistencies, and use it to show that multi-view consistency-scoring methods developed for novel view synthesis evaluation transfer poorly to localizing geometric inconsistencies. The work positions multi-view consistency as a tool for multimedia forensics, targeting detection and localization of manipulated or geometrically inconsistent images. This matters for detecting AI-generated or altered imagery as generative view synthesis becomes widespread.

entry.title: Implicit Neural Representation for Hyperspectral Video Compression

author.name: Alfredo Scalera, Paul Murray, Jaime Zabalza

entry.summary: The paper extends an implicit neural representation-based RGB video compression model to hyperspectral video, achieving +4.99 dB BD-PSNR and -88.88 percent BD-rate gains over frame-by-frame hyperspectral compression. It also evaluates downstream task performance via object tracking to show practical utility.

entry.title: Evaluating Cultural Awareness of LLMs for Haitian Creole

author.name: Christelle Clervilsson, Yanzhu Guo

entry.summary: The paper presents the first systematic evaluation of cultural awareness in LLMs for Haitian Creole, using a benchmark of culturally salient prompts curated by native speakers in a text-infilling setting across four dimensions: specificity, bias, diversity, and variation. Results show a clear gap between Haitian Creole and higher-resource French cultural awareness.

entry.title: HybridInfer: Thermal-Aware Reinforcement-Learning Tier Routing for On-Device, Edge, and Cloud LLM Inference

author.name: Simran Koul

entry.summary: The paper documents that sustained on-device LLM inference on mobile GPUs destabilizes the runtime due to thermal and toolchain constraints, and proposes HybridInfer, a reinforcement-learning router that dispatches queries across on-device, edge, and cloud tiers with thermal awareness. This matters because most existing multi-tier routers ignore thermal state, leading to crashes and wedged inference on real devices.

entry.title: NeuralCert: certified computational discovery of extremal mathematical constructions

author.name: Mark Patrick Roeling

entry.summary: NeuralCert proposes a discovery-to-certification pipeline where neural networks propose high-dimensional trial functions for extremal math problems in a compact separable form, which are then spectrally pruned and certified exactly via multimodular evaluation, making proofs fully verifiable. It runs on a standard personal computer and demonstrates three use modes: discovering improved constructions, exposing invalid conjectures, and supporting rigorous proofs. This matters as a template for trustworthy AI-assisted mathematics.

entry.title: Benchmarking the Connectomes of Caenorhabditis elegans within the Reservoir Computing Framework

author.name: Felix S. Reimers, Ola Huse Ramstad, Aliaksandr Hubin, Stefano Nichele

entry.summary: This work implements connectomes of C. elegans, derived at different developmental ages and via three distinct measurement methods, as echo state networks to evaluate their computational properties within the reservoir computing framework. Using the worms' biological neural wiring maps with minimal preprocessing, the study probes how biological network structure supports computation. It offers a computational lens on the first fully mapped nervous system.

entry.title: Population loss in shallow ReLU networks: Bias & families of critical points

author.name: Michael Field

entry.summary: The paper derives a closed-form formula for the population loss of shallow ReLU networks with bias in the student-teacher kernel model, extending prior results of Choo and Saul and Brutzkus and Globerson using Owen's T-function, with high-precision numerical support. It shows that known families of spurious minima extend to biased networks and that adding bias strictly decreases the loss while changing the loss landscape geometry only mildly. This sharpens the theoretical understanding of why bias terms affect nonconvex training landscapes.

entry.title: Quantizing Looped Transformers: Feedback Exposure and Calibration Blindness

author.name: Nux Li

entry.summary: The paper identifies two failure modes of post-training quantization in looped transformers: feedback exposure, where quantization error at the non-residual loop-entry adapter is amplified through recurrence (shown on Huginn-3.5B), and calibration blindness, where one-step GPTQ builds Hessians from unrepresentative step-0 activations. The authors show feedback exposure also affects linear filters and Mamba state-space models, suggesting a general principle for recurrent computation.

entry.title: Robust Successor Features

author.name: Erik Nikulski, Yamen Habib, Vicen\c{c} Gomez, Anders Jonsson, Rub\'en Moreno-Bote, Javier Segovia-Aguas

entry.summary: The paper unifies successor-feature transfer in RL, which traditionally handles reward-only task variation, with robust RL, where the transition kernel is uncertain, through robust successor features. This enables generalization to unseen tasks under transition-kernel uncertainty, maximizing expected reward under the uncertainty set.

entry.title: ALF: An Active Learning Framework for Scientific Discovery

author.name: Shikha Surana, Alex Hawkins-Hooker, Olivia Gallup, Christoph Brunken, Jules Tilly, Paul Duckworth

entry.summary: ALF is a modular open framework that runs the full active learning data-acquisition loop via five components, offering one API for both offline benchmarking against existing datasets and online deployment with real oracles. It targets data-bound scientific discovery under budget constraints.

entry.title: BeatGraph: Self-Supervised Heartbeat Graphs for Infant ECG Representations from the Home Environment

author.name: Mohammad Nur Hossain Khan, M. S. Krafczyk, Beverly G. Bolster, Nancy McElwain, Mark A. Hasegawa-Johnson, Bashima Islam

entry.summary: BeatGraph replaces fixed-length ECG patch tokenization with heartbeat-level representation, modeling each 30-second window as a graph of beats with a shared beat encoder and Transformer. It targets infant ECG from home environments, where higher heart rates and non-clinic conditions break adult-oriented foundation model assumptions.

entry.title: Common-Mode Collapse and Recovery in Direct Feedback Alignment

author.name: Varun Reddy, Bernardo L. Sabatini, Houman Safaai

entry.summary: This work explains why direct feedback alignment (DFA) can stall at the loss of a constant class-frequency predictor with tanh units and sigmoid outputs. The authors identify a common-mode component of the error signal, formalize it via a mean-covariance decomposition, and show it drives tanh units into saturation, proposing a reduced model that characterizes the failure and its recovery.

entry.title: Ordinary Nonconvex SGD under Distance-Dependent Moments: Finite-Horizon Stationarity and Nagaev Bounds

author.name: Wei Biao Wu

entry.summary: This paper analyzes vanilla single-sample stochastic gradient descent on smooth, nonconvex objectives when gradient noise moments depend on distance to the initial point rather than being uniformly bounded. Using a descent-displacement argument, the author derives finite-horizon stationarity rates (T^-1/3 expected average squared gradient norm under second moments alone) and an explicit oracle-complexity corollary that matches the known smooth lower bound, including its dependence on initial objective gap and variance terms. Nagaev-type concentration bounds are also developed. This matters because uniform moment assumptions in SGD theory are often unrealistic, and this work extends tight complexity guarantees to a more general, distance-dependent noise regime.

entry.title: Seeing Speech: Learning Visible Articulatory Dynamics for Speech-Driven 3D Facial Animation

author.name: Hyung Kyu Kim, Byungchan Hwang, Hak Gu Kim

entry.summary: The paper proposes an articulation-aware framework for speech-driven 3D facial animation that models visible speech through three directional articulatory motions (spreading, opening, protrusion), using a Speech-Articulatory Memory module to capture coordination patterns. This structured approach addresses the one-to-many mapping from acoustics to motion and improves speech-consistent visible articulation over vertex-level reconstruction methods.

entry.title: Query-Conditioned Prototype Adaptation for Cross-Domain Few-Shot Learning: Single-Query Inference, Controlled Comparisons, and Failure Modes

author.name: Rushab Rasik Karania, Tomas Maul

entry.summary: This arXiv paper introduces the Within-Instance Prototypical Transformer (WIPT), a method for cross-domain few-shot learning that adapts prototypes at test time by jointly transforming a single unlabelled query image with labelled support embeddings to form query-specific class means, without updating target-domain parameters. Built on a frozen ViT-S/16 encoder trained on miniImageNet and evaluated on CUB, EuroSAT, and ISIC, the paper reports 1-shot improvements over a frozen-prototype baseline, with results replicated across five seeds and an explicit analysis of failure modes.

entry.title: Equation discovery with Bayesian tree-adjoining grammars

author.name: Christopher A. Lindley, Nikolaos Dervilis, Keith Worden

entry.summary: Extends TAG-based nonlinear system identification to a Bayesian setting, defining a generative prior over model structures and parameters and using Reversible-Jump MCMC with structure-preserving tree moves to infer the joint posterior over structure, parameters, and predictions. Two training objectives, including a one-step-ahead objective with conjugate handling, are considered.

entry.title: Retrainable physics-integrated neural differentiable modeling of sintering across material systems

author.name: Zeping Chen, Ani Aprahamian, Khachatur V. Manukyan, Tengfei Luo

entry.summary: Sinter-PiNDiff is a physics-integrated neural differentiable framework predicting density and grain-size evolution during sintering, with neural networks learning coefficients inside coupled rate equations. The same governing structure was fitted independently to MgO, Al-doped ZnO, and CaO-doped ThO2 data, showing strong held-out performance. This demonstrates retrainable physics-informed modeling that generalizes across material systems.

entry.title: REALMS: An AI-Assistant Conversational System for Real-Time Exact Audience Sizing over High-Dimensional Nested Profiles

author.name: Haixu Ma, Aditya Bansal, Shubham Lohiya, Sumit Ranjan

entry.summary: This paper presents REALMS, a production-deployed conversational system on an enterprise customer data platform that lets marketers obtain exact audience counts over millions of profiles and thousands of attributes using natural language queries. It replaces traditional skeleton audiences, sampling, and predictive modeling approaches that suffer from delays and estimation errors. The work matters as a concrete example of LLM-assisted systems translating natural language into precise, scalable analytics over high-dimensional structured data.

entry.title: Enhancing Assessment of Self-Consistency in LLM Explanations using Perturbation Strength

author.name: Phuong Q. Le, Kemal Kurniawan, Jey Han Lau

entry.summary: The paper proposes an LLM-as-a-judge measure of perturbation strength, unifying input and chain-of-thought perturbations so self-consistency of LLM explanations can be compared under controlled strength conditions. Experiments show the LLM-based strength measure outperforms embedding- and probability-based alternatives, and that input perturbations affect LLMs more than CoT perturbations. This improves the rigor of consistency-based explanation evaluation.

entry.title: Coupled Usage-Sense Processes: Temporal and Attributable Lexical Semantic Change

author.name: Haruka Ezoe, Ryohei Hisano

entry.summary: CUSP is a new framework for lexical semantic change that goes beyond scalar distance measures to determine when a word changed, which mechanisms carried the change, and which usages support the attribution. It uses hierarchical coupling of contextual distributions through latent usage components with Markov composition and displacement operators. This represents a methodological advance in computational historical linguistics.

entry.title: Muslim: A Deployed Arabic Voice AI Platform for Grounded Islamic Knowledge

author.name: Yahya Mohamed Elnawasany

entry.summary: The paper describes a production Arabic voice AI platform delivering sourced Islamic knowledge, combining NeMo Arabic ASR, an OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoint, self-hosted TTS, and deterministic multi-source retrieval routed across six Model Context Protocol servers. It also releases fine-tuned artifacts including a 5.94B-parameter tool-routing model (Muslim-6B-PRO) and an Arabic TTS model (Fasih-TTS-V1) that ranks second among open-weight systems on the Arabic TTS Arena, plus an account and metering layer for real users.

entry.title: Don't CLAP: Are Music-Text Models Bag-of-Words?

author.name: Yuan-Chiao Cheng, Alexander Lerch

entry.summary: The paper questions the standard CLAP score for text-to-music faithfulness by testing whether music-text embeddings capture attribute bindings (e.g., distorted guitar) via an attribute-swap perturbation. Testing four contrastive music-text models and one audio-language model, it probes whether embeddings reflect precise text semantics or behave like bag-of-words. The results have implications for how text-to-music systems are evaluated.

entry.title: AlphaEarth distinguishes cities but compresses urban variation

author.name: Andrew Renninger

entry.summary: This paper audits AlphaEarth satellite foundation-model embeddings across 1,000 urban areas in 162 countries, probing the geometry and geography of the representation space. It finds that cities occupy a shifted but overlapping region on the hypersphere and that the embeddings distinguish cities broadly but compress fine-grained urban variation, reflecting training targets that do not emphasize urban function. The findings inform how Earth-observation embeddings can and cannot be used for urban analysis.

entry.title: EviDETR: Preserving Query-Relevant Temporal Evidence for Moment Retrieval and Highlight Detection

author.name: Haoran Sun, Yufan Li, Qichen Zhang, Haoran Zhao, Shuqi Wang

entry.summary: EviDETR improves joint video moment retrieval and highlight detection with three components: semantic-aware feature reweighting that enhances query-relevant clips, a temporal top-2 mixture-of-experts decoder for query-adaptive sparse refinement, and MR-to-HD fusion that transfers span-level retrieval evidence to clip-level highlight prediction. The unifying idea is explicitly preserving query-relevant evidence across encoding, decoding, and cross-task prediction in DETR-style pipelines.

entry.title: Self-Supervised Perceptually Interpretable Monocular Depth Estimation

author.name: Zain Ul Abidin, George Dimas, Dimitris K. Iakovidis

entry.summary: Proposes a self-supervised framework for perceptually interpretable monocular depth estimation that links depth predictions to distinct perceptual components of the input image rather than opaque RGB features. The goal is to enable systematic failure-case analysis and build trust in safety-critical settings without requiring ground-truth depth supervision. Sits at the intersection of depth estimation and interpretability.

entry.title: Seeing Semantic Shift: Difference-Aware Sentence-Level Temporal Segmentation of Sign Language Videos

author.name: Bowen Guo, Shiwei Gan, Yafeng Yin, Xiao Liu, Kuizhuang Liu, Zhiwei Jiang, Lei Xie

entry.summary: Tackles visual-only sentence-level segmentation of continuous sign language videos, partitioning them into non-overlapping sentence segments without caption assistance as a prerequisite for recognition and translation. Notes that sentence transitions are smooth and visually ambiguous so static frame representations fail, and proposes a difference-aware approach to detect semantic shifts. Important accessibility-oriented problem largely ignored in favor of short-clip settings.

entry.title: How Far Can INRs Go? Cross-Domain Parameter-efficient INR-Based Semantic Segmentation for Brain MRI

author.name: Ziyao Shang, Pouya Sadeghi, Letian Jiang, Alexander Wong, Sirisha Rambhatla

entry.summary: This work systematically studies implicit neural representations for brain MRI segmentation in low-parameter regimes, comparing scaling behavior and domain generalization against conventional pipelines. It clarifies where INRs are competitive under annotation, memory, and cross-site shift constraints.

entry.title: TinyCVIO: A Constellation-Aided Visual-Inertial Odometry System for Nanodrones

author.name: Derin Ozturk, Kaan Akan, Irwin Wang, Christopher Batten

entry.summary: TinyCVIO is a visual-inertial odometry system co-designed for nanodrones running on a commodity dual-core microcontroller with only 520 kB SRAM. It uses lightweight LED constellations with known geometry as landmarks, a streaming visual frontend tracking at 29.2 FPS, and a rigid-board measurement model with streaming QR decomposition for fixed-size filter states. Across 19 hardware-in-the-loop datasets, the rigid-board model reduces estimation error.

entry.title: SoGuDiff: Socially Guided Diffusion for Steerable, Norm-Grounded Robot Navigation

author.name: Christian Schaible, Haoran Ji, Yash Vardhan Pant, Stephen L. Smith

entry.summary: SoGuDiff is a diffusion-based robot navigation framework whose social behavior can be tuned at deployment time: desired style parameters such as passing distance, yielding side, and deference to groups are specified continuously, and the planner adapts accordingly. Continuous style axes can be followed independently or composed, moving beyond policies that learn a single fixed normative behavior from fixed rewards or demonstrations.

entry.title: Frequency-Modulated Piezoelectric Haptic Display

author.name: Boyuan Liang, Lingfeng Sun, Masayoshi Tomizuka

entry.summary: This paper proposes a frequency-modulated (FM) haptic display using piezoelectric actuators, encoding haptic intensity through vibration frequency rather than per-pixel deformation amplitude. The Shared-Source Frequency Modulation (SSFM) structure simplifies the driving electronics, enabling scalable high-density, large-area wearable haptic displays. It matters because it addresses a key hardware bottleneck in wearable haptics and teleoperation feedback.

entry.title: SeA-RVINS: Semantic-Aware Tightly Coupled RTK-Visual-Inertial System with Correlation-Preserving Robust Estimation for Urban Navigation

author.name: Wang Hu, Bo Wu

entry.summary: SeA-RVINS is a fixed-lag factor-graph RTK-visual-inertial navigation system for urban environments, using a semantic-aware learned stereo frontend to reject unreliable tracks and dynamic covariance scaling for GNSS measurements under multipath. It targets robust absolute pose estimation where outliers and false visual associations corrupt tightly coupled estimators. This addresses persistent reliability issues in urban GNSS-denied or degraded navigation.

entry.title: DualManip: Agentic Dynamic Manipulation via Dual-Path Semantic Reasoning and Geometric Adaptation

author.name: Chengxi Li, Yan Di, Yingyue Li, Ruida Zhang, Mingyang Li, Xiangyang Ji

entry.summary: DualManip decouples slow VLM-based semantic reasoning from a fast geometric path that continuously updates shape-adaptive template-to-observation correspondences from live RGB-D data, enabling responsive manipulation in dynamic scenes. The geometric path transfers task-relevant grasp contacts across observations while semantic constraints are updated infrequently. This addresses the latency bottleneck of VLM-driven manipulation in changing environments.

entry.title: ExoLaN: Physics-Consistent Context-Aware Dynamics Learning for Exoskeletons

author.name: Lucas Schulze, Maximilian Schwarz, Jona Hoppe, Jan Peters, Oleg Arenz

entry.summary: ExoLaN extends Deep Lagrangian Networks with temporal context to learn coupled human-exoskeleton dynamics that adapt to individual users and intermittent locomotion contacts without retraining, enabling task-agnostic assistance via human joint torque estimation. This addresses limitations of prior physics-consistent torque estimation methods that could not personalize or handle contact changes. Relevant to wearable robotics and physical human-robot interaction.

entry.title: MACBT: A Multi-Agent Cognitive Behavioral Therapy Decision Support System with Longitudinal Memory

author.name: De Jiang, Shuo Zhang, Weiwei Liao, Jianying Zhang, Chuanhui Yu, Hongen Liao, Kehong Yuan

entry.summary: Presents a clinician-facing CBT decision-support system combining a five-agent framework mirroring the CBT workflow (assessment, Socratic questioning, cognitive restructuring, behavioral experiments, monitoring) with a longitudinal memory module tracking cognitive-distortion type, frequency, severity, and restructuring efficacy across sessions. It generates pre-session pathology reports and post-session documentation to reduce clinician workload. Targets real clinical deployment rather than autonomous therapy.

entry.title: SPO: Discovering Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search Operators via Stackelberg Program Optimization

author.name: Xinyi Ke, Kai Li, Junliang Xing, Yifan Zhang, Jian Cheng

entry.summary: SPO is an LLM-based framework that discovers adaptive executable destroy-repair programs for large neighborhood search, conditioning operator decisions on compact LNS state. It organizes discovery as a Stackelberg interaction with role-specific credit assignment, treating destroy programs as leaders and repair programs as conditional followers. This couples program discovery with combinatorial optimization, a promising direction for automated algorithm design.

entry.title: When Does Advection-Aware Graph Nowcasting Help? A Controlled Study of Distributed Solar Ramp Forecasting with a Self-Supervised Cloud-Motion Estimator

author.name: Phillip Jiang

entry.summary: This controlled study tests whether making a graph neural network advection-aware, connecting sites upwind with edge lags set by cloud-motion vectors, improves solar ramp forecasting across distributed PV sensor networks. On a synthetic testbed with a known wind field, explicit advection graphs do not beat static or learned-adjacency GNNs with realistic CMV estimates, and roughly half the benefit of perfect motion information comes simply from accurate motion prediction. The negative result clarifies when physics-informed graph structure helps.

entry.title: Causal Retention in Interactive Agents: Interface Factorization and Selective Adaptation

author.name: Shengjun Zhang, Tingyi Liu, Dong Xie, Yunlong Dong, Xiang Wang, Cheng Zeng

entry.summary: This theoretical paper studies causal retention: whether a frozen learned state of an interactive agent answers mechanism-probe queries (action, context, target, value, delay) fixed independently of training. It derives Bayes-risk characterizations for finite structural causal model classes, a posterior-coverage theorem for budgeted retesting, and an exact edit decomposition, implemented in a system called Causal Core. The work connects agent adaptation with causality and model editing.

entry.title: XPhysICS: Cross-Physical-Domain Threat Grounding for Industrial Control Systems Security

author.name: Sangshin Park, Jainta Paul, Lawrence Ponce, Md Raihan Ahmed, Mu Zhang, Luis Garcia

entry.summary: XPhysICS is a provenance-aware, target-conditioned method for grounding industrial control system threats across physical domains, separating analyst-guided abstraction from deterministic mapping into target-specific validation slices. It uses five eligibility criteria such as role compatibility and slice viability to judge whether a documented threat's cyber-physical effects are admissible on a new target. This supports systematic transfer of ICS threat intelligence.

entry.title: Pocket-STVG: lightweight architecture for Spatio-Temporal Video Grounding

author.name: Alberto Presta, Michal Byra, Grzegorz Stefa\'nski, Karol Szurkowski, Eryk Ko{\l}odziejczyk, Krzysztof Arendt

entry.summary: Pocket-STVG is a lightweight cascade architecture for spatio-temporal video grounding that combines efficient pretrained components, including a temporal-aware MobileViCLIP video encoder and an MDETR-derived spatial encoder-decoder, instead of large end-to-end multimodal LLMs. It aims to match heavier methods across supervised, weakly supervised, and zero-shot settings at much lower compute.

entry.title: OC-GS: Gaussian Splatting for Irregular Turntable Capture

author.name: Jae Joong Lee, Bedrich Benes

entry.summary: OC-GS performs object-centric Gaussian splatting that jointly refines each image's capture angle while maintaining a shared camera, rotation axis, and pivot, enabling reconstruction from sparse, irregular turntable views. It outperforms four pose-free Gaussian splatting baselines across 12, 8, and 6 view conditions, with angle refinement yielding large PSNR gains.

entry.title: Adaptive Multi-Value Control in LLMs via Causal Activation Steering

author.name: Payel Bhattacharjee, Ravi Tandon

entry.summary: AIMES is a framework for adaptive multi-value activation steering in LLMs, constructing layer-specific bipolar directions for moral-foundation values and modulating intervention strengths based on the model's evolving internal state, unlike prior methods that steer values in isolation with fixed strengths. This enables simultaneous control of multiple, interacting human values at inference time without retraining. It matters as a lightweight alternative or complement to training-based alignment.

entry.title: OpenHail: An Event-Driven Gymnasium Environment for Electric Ride-Hailing Fleet Control

author.name: Tommaso Schettini, Nicholas D. Kullman, Jorge E. Mendoza

entry.summary: OpenHail is an open-source Gymnasium environment for joint control of electric ride-hailing fleets, exposing request assignment, repositioning, and charging through a single fixed-size observation-action interface. Its event-driven simulator captures the interaction among stochastic demand, vehicle operations, and capacitated charging infrastructure, including pickup deadlines. It provides a standardized benchmark for reinforcement learning research in this domain.

entry.title: CacheReforge: Bounded Recovery for Stale KV Caches under Evolving Adapters

author.name: Yuhang Cao, Yanzhou Mu, Chunrong Fang, Zhenyu Chen

entry.summary: CacheReforge addresses stale KV caches when lightweight adapters evolve during long-context or interactive LLM serving, representing caches as layerwise mixed-version objects and computing minimal recomputation needed to recover current adapter behavior. This sits between full suffix recomputation, which is costly, and naive stale reuse, which distorts outputs.

entry.title: Scaffold: Support Graph Theory Based Sparsification for Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Siddhartha Shankar Das, Sai Karthik Navuluru, S M Ferdous, Ryan A. Rossi, Baris Coskunuzer, Lakshman Tamil, Edoardo Serra, Alex Pothen, Robert Rallo, Mahantesh M Halappanavar

entry.summary: Scaffold is an unsupervised graph sparsification framework derived from support graph theory preconditioners that jointly controls dilation and congestion of rerouted paths when edges are removed. This preserves communication structure for GNN message passing while cutting computational and memory costs.

entry.title: AC Power Flow Contingency Analysis Using a Single Deep Neural Network

author.name: Md Obaidur Rahman, Junjie Qin, Vassilis Kekatos

entry.summary: Proposes a framework where a single DNN trained only on base-case AC power flow data estimates post-contingency states for arbitrary single-line outages via fixed-point iteration, avoiding outage-specific training costs. The authors derive sufficient conditions for convergence of the fixed-point scheme when the model is a DNN.

entry.title: Geometric Moment Contraction for Stochastic Nesterov Acceleration

author.name: Wei Biao Wu

entry.summary: Analyzes geometric moment contraction of the constant-parameter stochastic Nesterov recursion, proving synchronous L^p contraction criteria under mean strong monotonicity and stochastic Lipschitz continuity, including infinite-variance gradient settings. A complementary power-Lyapunov argument yields positive step-size intervals for any fixed beta and p>1 using only finite p-th gradient moments.

entry.title: CG-Probes: Recovering Guardrail Directions from Patient Query Embeddings

author.name: Marko \v{R}eh\'a\v{c}ek, V\'it\v{e}zslav Du\v{s}ek, Martin Rusinko, V\'it Nov\'a\v{c}ek

entry.summary: CG-Probes are linear probes in the embedding space of frozen embedders that detect medical risk along three ordinal axes (Medical Urgency, Psychological Urgency, Topic Sensitivity) defined with oncologists. The authors train probes using BERTopic clusters of 79,658 Czech oncology queries and contrastive query pairs generated via few-shot prompting. This offers a lightweight, interpretable guardrail mechanism for patient-facing medical AI.

entry.title: Learning Polarization Image Restoration with General Restoration Priors

author.name: Chenggong Li, Jinhao Liu, Caiyun Wu, Yidong Luo, Junchao Zhang, Degui Yang

entry.summary: The paper develops an all-in-one restoration framework for polarization images subject to diverse and composite degradations, identifying normalized Stokes representation as effective for separating intensity and polarization information. It leverages general restoration priors rather than degradation-specific models, addressing the limited scale and quality of polarization training data. The work aims to make polarization vision practical under real-world acquisition conditions.

entry.title: Motion Style Slider: Endpoint-Supervised Continuous Style Control for Human Motion Diffusion

author.name: Chen-Chieh Liao, Yichen Peng, Yiyi Cai, Y\^ui Ono, Hiroki Hanaoka, Erwin Wu, Hideki Koike, Shuichi Kurabayashi

entry.summary: Motion Style Slider provides continuous, monotonic control of style intensity in motion diffusion by constructing a style direction in a learned motion-style embedding space and conditioning generation with a scalar intensity. Training combines diffusion denoising with endpoint supervision so the scalar acts as a reliable relative control axis, matching production needs where style intensity is subjective. The framework performs motion-to-motion style transfer with fine-grained intensity control.

entry.title: TaskIR: Task-Driven Image Restoration via Degradation Adaptation and Task Feedback

author.name: Yanjie Tu, Qingsen Yan, Axi Niu, Wenxuan Cai, Tao Hu, Wei Dong, Haokui Zhang

entry.summary: Presents TaskIR, a two-stage task-driven unified restoration framework combining degradation-adaptive restoration via a Degradation Representation Module with task feedback refinement, handling diverse real-world degradations rather than a single degradation type. The motivation is that insufficient restoration leaves artifacts that impair object boundaries and downstream task performance. Bridges restoration quality and downstream vision performance.

entry.title: Image Reconstruction from Phase with Untrained Neural Priors

author.name: Ene Meco, Ahmet Enis Cetin

entry.summary: A two-stage projection-based framework recovers images from Fourier phase alone by combining phase and spatial-support constraints with untrained image-specific neural priors, with guaranteed convergence in the refinement stage. It achieves around 31 dB pooled PSNR on microscopy images, outperforming constraint-only baselines.

entry.title: Privacy-Preserving Prompted Policy Search for Robotic Control

author.name: Ali Irshayyid, Feng Lin, Chong Li, Jun Chen

entry.summary: PP-ProPS addresses the privacy risk of LLM-guided reinforcement learning policy search, where transmitting raw policy parameters and reward histories to cloud LLM APIs exposes proprietary control strategies. The framework encodes policy parameters and reward values using secret client-side transformations so that LLM-guided optimization can proceed while keeping policy and environment parameters confidential from the service provider.

entry.title: Learning to Leverage Compliance: A Policy-Admittance Learning Framework for Robotic Insertion

author.name: Chongren Wang, Minghe Li, Honghua Dai, Zhicheng Lin, Shiyang Wei, Xiaokui Yue

entry.summary: LeCo addresses the coordination failure when combining learned insertion policies with compliant admittance control, where the policy pushes while the controller yields. It introduces a policy-admittance learning framework with multirate contact-interaction rewards, an integrated conflict cost penalizing sustained policy-loading/controller-unloading opposition, and directional terms. This improves reliable autonomous assembly under pose errors and contact uncertainty.

entry.title: MA-WAM: Multi-Agent World-Action Model for Test-Time Planning

author.name: Guowei Zou, Haitao Wang, Guoxin Wang, Beiwen Zhang, Zhiquan Chen, Guojie Wang, Hejun Wu

entry.summary: MA-WAM is a test-time planning framework that enables a frozen multi-agent flow policy to evaluate candidate joint actions via a world model that captures dependencies among simultaneous actions of multiple agents. Naive per-agent world-model extensions fail to model these simultaneous-action dependencies for team-return prediction. It claims to be the first test-time multi-agent planning approach of this kind.

entry.title: UQ-LOB: Uncertainty-Aware Limit Order Book Mid-Price Forecasting

author.name: Derrick Gilchrist Edward Manoharan, Eljas Linna, Kestutis Baltakys, Hao Dong, Juho Kanniainen

entry.summary: UQ-LOB is a lightweight, encoder-agnostic uncertainty quantification module for limit order book mid-price forecasting that attaches to any pretrained LOB encoder and conditions forecasts on a context set of recently completed windows, inspired by attentive neural processes. It provides calibrated Gaussian regression outputs and categorical down/up/stationary distributions, indicating which forecasts can be trusted. This addresses the fact that most deep LOB forecasters output point predictions only.

entry.title: VLALight: Lightweight Vision-Language-Action Models for Emergency-Aware Traffic Signal Control

author.name: Kemou Jiang, Maonan Wang, Xingchen Zou, Jiayue Zhu, Yuhang Fu, Sicheng Wang, Xi Chen, Yirong Chen, Zhiyong Cui

entry.summary: VLALight is a lightweight end-to-end vision-language-action framework that maps multi-view intersection observations and signal-phase information directly to discrete traffic signal actions, enabling visual-context-aware and emergency-aware control. It avoids the latency and fine-grained visual detail loss caused by loosely coupled VLM modules with repeated information conversion. This demonstrates efficient deployment of VLA models in a real urban system.

entry.title: FLIP: Final Layer Inference-Time Probing for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Drandreb Earl O. Juanico, Rowel O. Atienza

entry.summary: FLIP is an inference-time probe that applies elementwise flooring to the final normalized hidden state of an open-weight VLM before logit computation, testing whether behavioral changes under intervention reflect genuine use of visual evidence versus generic instability or degradation. Sweeping intervention strength on a detection/counting probe reveals distinct regimes including a bounded interior region with improved detection recall. It offers a lightweight interpretability methodology for VLMs.

entry.title: Teacher-Anchored Selection of Post-Training Quantized Models under Domain Shift

author.name: Alejandro Rodriguez Dominguez, Muhammad Shahzad, Xia Hong

entry.summary: This paper studies how to select which quantized model from a compression family to deploy when target labels are absent or scarce under domain shift. It finds that minimum teacher distortion behaves as an almost-constant selection rule, while confidence-based estimators can order candidates nearly backwards in overconfident-collapse regimes.

entry.title: Auditing System-1 Models on Biosecurity-Relevant Benchmarks: Calibration, Selective Prediction, and Permutation Instability in a Non-Generative Model

author.name: Kimon Antonios Provatas, Ilias Georgakopoulos-Soares

entry.summary: This paper audits a commercial non-generative System-1 model on 6,020 biosecurity-relevant multiple-choice items from WMDP and LAB-Bench, measuring accuracy, calibration, error detection, selective prediction, and answer-order sensitivity. It finds strongly task-dependent accuracy and characterizes reliability properties relevant to using such cheap models inside larger pipelines. It matters because System-1 components are increasingly embedded in AI systems handling sensitive content.

entry.title: Distribution of hitting times for dissipative random dynamical systems on $\mathbb{R}^d$, with application to stochastic gradient descent

author.name: St\'ephane Galatolo, St\'ephane Chr\'etien

entry.summary: The authors develop a dynamical-systems approach to understanding convergence of gradient-type algorithms, studying hitting-time distributions for dissipative random dynamical systems and applying the theory to stochastic gradient descent. The work extends a line of research on long-time behavior of optimization methods toward explaining why SGD succeeds on large-scale nonconvex problems.

entry.title: Deep-Learning Solvers and Surrogates for Infinity and p-Laplace Problems

author.name: Tak Shing Au Yeung, Ka Chun Cheung, Hannah Potgieter, Steven J. Ruuth, Simon See

entry.summary: Applies PINNs and DeepONets to infinity-Laplace and p-Laplace PDEs for p values from 2 to 1000 on 2D and 3D domains, where mesh-based solvers become very costly. The paper also establishes conditional convergence results for PINN approximations and a universal approximation result for DeepONet on the parametric p-Poisson problem.

entry.title: Conformal Prediction under Exponential-Tilt Joint Shift

author.name: Seungjin Choi

entry.summary: Studies conformal prediction under joint covariate and label shift using labeled source data and unlabeled target inputs, applying ExTRA exponential-tilt reweighting to estimate structured shifts. The paper compares using estimated weights in conformal calibration versus additionally tilting the source predictive distribution, isolating effects in a controlled setup.

entry.title: Training-Free Bottleneck Width Planning for Convolutional Autoencoders

author.name: Guannan Guo

entry.summary: MS-SRD estimates the required bottleneck channel width of convolutional autoencoders directly from training images and an NMSE bound, without training any network, via multiscale spectral rate-distortion analysis. Its covariance-tail rule is exact for shared linear block-convolutional autoencoders under squared error, and predictions show 0.84% mean absolute percentage error against nonlinear patch-autoencoder boundaries across thirteen datasets. The method also reports a Pareto frontier of activation parameters versus latent size.

entry.title: Refining Cytology Predictions with Conditional Random Fields

author.name: Manon Dausort, Tiffanie Godelaine, Karim El Khoury, Maxime Zanella, Christophe De Vleeschouwer, Beno\^it Macq

entry.summary: Introduces CytoCRF, adapting conditional random field refinement of zero-shot VLM predictions from histopathology to cytology, where stains and cell morphology differ substantially, by targeting chromatin and cytology-specific staining in pairwise terms and combining multiple backbones to enrich neighborhoods. Outperforms baselines across ten cytology datasets. Extends annotation-free VLM classification to a clinically important modality.

entry.title: Preserve-and-Compose Training for Composed Image Retrieval

author.name: Sehyun Kwon

entry.summary: Proposes Preserve-and-Compose Training for zero-shot composed image retrieval, learning from image-text-text triplets without target images by aligning composed queries with target captions while preserving source-image evidence through visual supervision, since target captions often omit details that should be retained. Also introduces Chord scoring. Addresses a real supervision-gap problem in CIR.

entry.title: Realizability Is Not Enough: Encoding, Liveness, and Auditing of Synthesized Robot Supervisors

author.name: David C. Conner, Joshua Luzier, William J. Doyle, Emma R. Faith, Aubrie B. Kooiker, Andrew J. Farney, Sebastian Fox, Evangelina Grimes, Ian G. Conner, Kyle Bloom

entry.summary: This paper argues that proving a GR(1) specification realizable is insufficient for deploying reactive-synthesis-based robot supervisors; designers must also encode failure-prone capabilities, choose liveness assumptions matching retry intent, and audit strategies. The authors present an open-source ROS 2 FlexBE pipeline that generates capability-based GR(1) specifications, analyzes assumptions before synthesis, audits strategies, reduces states with behavior-preservation proofs, and emits executable supervisors.

entry.title: A Second Torque Port for Series Elastic Actuators: Parallel-Integrated Design and Time-Scale Torque Allocation

author.name: Donghao Jia, Xiubo Xia, Junhang Liu, Zeyu Zhu, Xiaoyu Geng, Jian Sun

entry.summary: Pi-SEA opens a second torque port on the load side of a series elastic actuator by adding a direct-drive micro motor in parallel with the spring, allocating torque between channels by time scale, and reading torque from spring deflection and motor current without extra sensors. This fixes the classic SEA weakness of torque amplitude collapsing at high command frequencies and commands lost below breakaway friction. It is a thoughtful actuator architecture contribution.

entry.title: CognitiveReality: Robot-Agnostic Semantic Gaussian Mapping with an LLM Agent for Immersive Collaborative VR Teleoperation

author.name: Timofei Kozlov, Dmitrii Maliukov, Andrey Marchenko, Dmitrii Plotnikov, Miguel Altamirano Cabrera, Dzmitry Tsetserukou

entry.summary: CognitiveReality builds a live, semantically indexed Gaussian-TSDF map from a robot RGB-D stream shared between a VR teleoperator and a tool-using LLM agent, with open-vocabulary instance identities, per-object observation quality at 2 Hz, and robustness to localization outages via a shadow tracker. Speech and controller rays are grounded against persistent scene elements. It unifies immersive teleoperation and language-agent reasoning over one spatial representation.

entry.title: Rank-Reliable Teacher-Guided Fitness Approximation for Expensive Evolutionary Optimization: A TinyML Architecture Search Study

author.name: Soumen Garai, Suman Samui

entry.summary: Proposes TGL-NSGA-II, a low-fidelity framework for TinyML neural architecture search in which a pretrained teacher stratifies samples by difficulty and class, candidates receive short knowledge-distillation scoring, and a Gaussian-process surrogate fuses the score for full-evaluation selection. The key insight is that expensive optimization often needs reliable rankings rather than exact fitness values.

entry.title: HasMem: Hard-Origin Adaptively Softened Memory for Long-Term LLM Agents

author.name: Zihong He, Junxiao Shen, Chen Liang, Hai-Ning Liang

entry.summary: Proposes HasMem, a memory architecture for long-term LLM agents where frozen hard-prompt embeddings provide a verifiable initial state, and a controller adaptively adjusts memory widths with a Writer re-encoding resized entries and Reader/Global modules for readout adaptation. On a reconstruction probe over 535 Multi-Session Chat questions it reaches lexical F1 of 95.3 while using about 93.6 percent of the hard reference's framed memory positions. Addresses the coupling between memory capacity allocation and readout in context compression.

entry.title: Governed Deduction: Policy-Grounded Premise Authorization Beyond Relevance

author.name: Wesley Shu, Hsi-Ching Lin

entry.summary: This paper formalizes Governed Deduction, a distinction between premise relevance and premise authorization in reasoning systems, via a transition-local admission predicate. Using an RBAC-augmented Spider benchmark with 4,461 matched permitted/denied pairs, the authors find a joint controller reaches 99.19 percent accuracy but a transition-only control reaches 100 percent, exposing a role-name shortcut. It highlights both the promise and brittleness of policy-grounded inference controls.

entry.title: Neural State Prediction: Obstructing Shortcut Learning in EEG Foundation Models

author.name: Kieren Yu, Ziyang Liu, Chang Huang, Jintai Chen, Kaishun Wu

entry.summary: The paper identifies that masked prediction objectives for EEG foundation models can be satisfied via stable positional cues and local correlations without integrating distributed neural context. It introduces Neural State Prediction, a latent-predictive framework using an EMA-updated target encoder and identity residualization to strip channel-identity and timing cues from supervision. This improves transferable neural representations for EEG foundation models.

entry.title: G2MAF: Test-Time Gradient Guidance for Multi-Agent Flow Policies

author.name: Guowei Zou, Haitao Wang, Guoxin Wang, Zhiquan Chen, Beiwen Zhang, Guojie Wang, Hejun Wu

entry.summary: G2MAF is a test-time refinement framework for offline multi-agent RL in which a frozen policy's one-shot joint action is improved using a globally normalized, projected critic gradient to coordinate all agents' corrections while keeping actions feasible and near the behavior data. It addresses suboptimal deployment commitments in offline MARL. Together with MA-WAM it signals a broader test-time-compute trend in multi-agent RL.

entry.title: Segment-Level Agentic Topic Modeling for Improved Data Exploration and Resource Efficiency

author.name: Myeongjun Erik Jang, Antonios Georgiadis, Sae Young Moon, Fran Silavong

entry.summary: This paper tackles drawbacks of LLM-based topic modeling, including the inability to produce document-level topic distributions, overly broad or narrow topics, and high resource consumption that scales with document count and length. It introduces a segment-level agentic approach for topic modeling aimed at better data exploration and improved resource efficiency. The work is relevant to industry text-mining pipelines where cost is a key constraint.

entry.title: SignTrace: Describe a Sign, Find the Word

author.name: Zengji Tu, Xingye Zhu, Ningjing Wang, Tingyi Huang, Yangjunfeng Zhu, Dai Wan

entry.summary: SignTrace solves the reverse-lookup problem in sign language learning, where a learner remembers a sign's movement but not its meaning or feature codes, via natural-language access to a Chinese sign-language dictionary. It combines LLM-based dictionary enrichment, action extraction, seven-channel retrieval, and candidate reranking over 6,699 entries, achieving 94.0 percent Hit@1 on a 500-query benchmark, with reranking raising Hit@1 from 71.8 to 94.0 percent. It is deployed for user trials with positive feedback.

entry.title: A Unified Account of Concepts and Chunks

author.name: Karthik Singaravadivelan, Pat Langley

entry.summary: The paper bridges two nearly disjoint literatures in cognitive psychology — concept formation and chunking — by extending the Cobweb computational account of categorization to incorporate chunks and their acquisition. The authors present TRELLIS, an implementation, and demonstrate it by learning context-free grammars, with a modality-agnostic theory applicable to structured experience.

entry.title: A Framework for Identifying, Categorizing, and Explaining Bias in AI-Generated Code

author.name: Manaal Basha, Aimee M. Ribeiro, Gema Rodriguez-Perez

entry.summary: The authors build a taxonomy-driven framework for identifying and explaining bias in AI-generated code, extending an existing dataset of biased Python snippets with manual annotations and human-authored justifications as ground truth. They then evaluate proprietary and open-source LLMs as automated bias detectors using this dataset. This addresses an under-studied fairness issue as LLMs enter software development workflows.

entry.title: Werracle: Sub-Cent Intra-Block AI Reflex Oracles and Flash-Loan Circuit Breakers for EVM Smart Contracts

author.name: Volkan Da\u{g}l{\i}, Zerrin Da\u{g}l{\i}, Da\u{g}han Da\u{g}l{\i}

entry.summary: Werracle proposes sub-cent AI oracles that run inference inside EVM blocks to combat atomic DeFi exploits like flash-loan attacks and sandwich MEV, sidestepping the memory/latency wall of on-chain inference and the proving latency of ZK-ML. It introduces intra-block reflex oracles and flash-loan circuit breakers. This bridges applied AI with blockchain security infrastructure.

entry.title: PORL: Pretrained Offline Reinforcement Learning for the Job Shop Scheduling Problem

author.name: Mateo Toro Diz, Jonathan Hoss, Noah Klarmann

entry.summary: PORL is a hybrid reinforcement learning approach for the Job Shop Scheduling Problem combining simulation-based online pretraining with offline fine-tuning on production-specific historical data. It leverages broad strategy exploration in simulation while closing the sim-to-reality gap using real offline datasets. This targets practical industrial deployment where both simulation and historical logs are available.

entry.title: From Shortcut Learning to Discrete Neural Insertion Sort

author.name: Konstantinos Mylonas, Thrasyvoulos Spyropoulos

entry.summary: Studying neural algorithmic reasoning on insertion sort, the authors show the CLRS30 baseline weakly optimizes hint objectives and decodes sorted outputs early, indicating shortcut learning rather than faithful algorithm execution. They propose Discrete Neural Insertion Sort, which represents intermediate steps discretely to enforce alignment with the intended algorithm.

entry.title: SPADE: Escaping the Popularity-Similarity Frontier to Measure Serendipitous Recommendations

author.name: Tobias Vente, Maarten Peirsman, Noah Dani\"els, Hannu Toivonen, Bart Goethals

entry.summary: SPADE is a new offline evaluation metric for serendipity in recommender systems that jointly considers similarity, popularity, and user relevance by mapping items into a 2D space and computing distances from a user-specific Pareto frontier of maximally popular and historically similar items, scored only on correctly recommended items.

entry.title: Intent2Tc: Automated Intent-to-Traffic Control Translation with Language Models

author.name: Andrea Masini, Sudipta Acharya, Paolo Bellavista, Luca Foschini, Burak Kantarci

entry.summary: Intent2Tc is a closed-loop, language-model-driven framework that translates business-level traffic-shaping intents into declarative sub-intents and validated Linux tc configurations, supported by an AQM-based digital twin for semantic validation. It targets reliable, automated QoS enforcement in intent-based networking.

entry.title: Offline Policy Evaluation as a decision support tool for designing Adaptive Experiments

author.name: Jo\~ao Victor Ferreira Alves, Eduardo Rocha Laurentino, Gustavo de Oliveira Kanno, Thiago Costa Rizuti da Rocha

entry.summary: The paper combines off-policy evaluation with warm-start simulation to determine whether adaptive experiments (contextual bandits) would have outperformed fixed A/B tests on logged historical data. This provides practitioners a principled decision tool before committing to adaptive designs. It matters because adaptive experimentation is increasingly used in industry but poorly understood relative to standard A/B testing.

entry.title: Fake News Theories: Harnessing Disciplinary Insights for Computational Modeling, Detection, and Explanation

author.name: Zhaoyang Cao, Miriam Metzger, Reza Zafarani

entry.summary: This paper builds a theory-informed computational framework for fake-news detection and explanation by systematically reviewing cross-disciplinary theories of persuasion, credibility, and human judgment from social sciences, psychology, and economics, and translating them into measurable features used with statistical techniques and LLMs. It aims to close the gap between accurate but opaque detectors and established theory. The structured theory-to-feature mapping is its main contribution.

entry.title: LUMO (Lightweight Unified Multilingual Orchestrator): A Privacy Preserving Offline Voice Assistant

author.name: Md. Mehedi Hasan Naeem, Mst. Kamrunnahar Ruma, Nafiza Anjum, Shakila Sultana, Md. Sujan Ali

entry.summary: LUMO is a fully offline voice assistant pipeline for edge hardware (Raspberry Pi 5, 8 GB RAM) integrating local ASR, a locally deployed quantized LLM, and TTS synthesis. It targets environments with limited internet connectivity and strong privacy needs, where cloud-dependent assistants introduce latency and privacy vulnerabilities. The work demonstrates practical multilingual voice interaction under strict resource constraints.

entry.title: Learning Provable Neural Network Observer for Uncertain Dynamical Systems

author.name: Zhangyi Wang, Jiaxu Liu, Chen Song, Chao Xu, Shengze Cai

entry.summary: This work introduces a two-stage framework for training neural network observers of uncertain dynamical systems that come with certified Lyapunov stability: a point-guided pre-training phase achieves accuracy and local stability, then an LMI fine-tuning phase reduces the large SDP scalability bottleneck. This enables provably stable learning-based state estimation for safety-critical control.

entry.title: Bayesian Tensor Autoencoder with Physics-informed Predictive Prior for Multi-dimensional Time Series Anomaly Detection

author.name: Jianan Liu, Chunguang Li

entry.summary: The paper introduces a Bayesian tensor autoencoder for anomaly detection in multi-dimensional (tensorial) time series, avoiding reshaping operations that break intrinsic correlations. It combines reconstruction-based and prediction-based autoencoding with a physics-informed predictive prior.

entry.title: Decodable In-Context State and Model Output Across Training

author.name: Manas Venkata Sai Ravulapalli, Samrath Singh Chadha

entry.summary: The study tracks probe accuracy, model output, and steering response for in-context binding across Pythia pretraining and post-training checkpoints, showing probe accuracy rises during pretraining and steering benefit grows with scale. It also examines whether saved scores can separate probe-correct errors with distinct model probabilities.

entry.title: Scaffold-Constrained Subset Dynamic Programming for Exact SSE Clustering

author.name: Yordan P. Raykov, Max A. Little

entry.summary: The paper develops an exact dynamic program for Euclidean K-means (sum-of-squared-errors) clustering that uses data-derived geometric graphs to precondition the search, admitting only connected vertex subsets as clusters while preserving the unrestricted optimum. A remaining-set recurrence with bottleneck thresholds analyzes how much computational support can be removed while retaining exact solutions.

entry.title: Parameter Estimation for Unnormalized Discrete Models via Empirically Localized Deformed Bregman Divergence

author.name: Takashi Takenouchi

entry.summary: Proposes combining empirical localization with deformed Bregman divergences to estimate parameters of discrete probabilistic models without computing intractable normalization constants. The approach drastically reduces computational cost while allowing the choice of divergence deformation to endow the estimator with desirable statistical properties.

entry.title: AFA-Net: A Differential Attention Approach for Auditory Attention Detection

author.name: Philip H. Lee, Shreeram Suresh Chandra, Karan Thakkar, John H. L. Hansen

entry.summary: Applies a differential attention mechanism to auditory attention detection from EEG in multi-speaker environments, replacing vanilla attention to better focus on task-relevant neural activity amid noisy signals. AFA-Net reaches 96.8% accuracy at a 2-second decision window with substantially fewer parameters than most existing methods.

entry.title: Retail Product Search: A Practical Approach at Target

author.name: Darshan Sonagara, Qujiaheng Zhang, Ankit Singh, Alex Li

entry.summary: This industry paper describes Target's hybrid retail product search system combining lexical and vector search to handle intents from exact matching to open-ended discovery while balancing relevance, revenue, and latency. It documents practical design tradeoffs that keyword-only or vector-only systems struggle with. It is valuable as a production case study rather than a research advance.

entry.title: Effects of Transcript Compression on LLM-based Medical Misinformation Detection in Japanese YouTube Videos

author.name: Yuya Wake, Sho Tsugawa, Toshiyuki Amagasa

entry.summary: This study examines how different transcript input designs (full transcripts, LLM summaries, RAPTOR-based RAG, and sentence screening) affect LLM classification of Japanese medical YouTube videos as real or fake across 74 long-form videos. It finds that transcript compression choices materially impact misinformation detection performance. The work matters for practical LLM-based health content moderation in non-English settings.

entry.title: Asymmetric Classifier-Free Guidance for Target-Speaker ASR

author.name: Yiwen Guan, Jacob Whitehill

entry.summary: The paper introduces asymmetric classifier-free guidance for target-speaker ASR built on Whisper, where a speaker-conditioned branch predicts the target transcript and an unconditioned branch predicts serialized multi-speaker transcripts, with a guidance scale calibrated at inference time. A lightweight encoder-based predictor adjusts conditioning to changing overlap and noise. This improves robustness of speaker-targeted transcription in real acoustic conditions.

entry.title: CSCWD: Cross-Scale Channel-wise Knowledge Distillation for Lightweight Tiny Object Detection on Edge Devices

author.name: Amir Zamani, Zeinab Ghasemi-Naraghi

entry.summary: CSCWD is a training-time knowledge distillation framework that transfers high-resolution spatial features from a YOLO11m-P2 teacher to a compact YOLO11n student for tiny object detection in aerial imagery, using cross-scale channel-wise alignment from teacher P2 to student P3. The student architecture is unchanged at inference, preserving edge deployability, and it reaches 50.17% mAP under a unified Drone-vs-Bird validation protocol. The work targets real-time detection on resource-constrained devices.

entry.title: Exploiting Spatial Structure for Transductive Few-Shot Classification of Whole-Slide Images

author.name: Tiffanie Godelaine, Manon Dausort, Karim El Khoury, Beno\^it G\'erin, Beno\^it Macq, Christophe De Vleeschouwer

entry.summary: Proposes SlideTIM, an adaptation of the transductive LC-TIM approach to whole-slide image classification, adding a combined spatial-latent regularizer and a prior on patch classification confidence to jointly refine noisy zero-shot VLM predictions. Targets annotation-free cancer diagnosis support to reduce pathologist workload while improving fine-grained accuracy. Same research group as the CytoCRF paper, forming a coherent research line.

entry.title: Vision-Based 6-DoF Grasp Pose Estimation for Robot Cloth Unfolding

author.name: Domen Tabernik, Peter Nimac, Jan Jeri\'cevi\'c, Danijel Sko\v{c}aj, Andrej Gams

entry.summary: This work addresses deformable-object manipulation by tackling cloth unfolding with a regrasping-in-the-air strategy where one manipulator holds the cloth while another grasps at an optimal point. The proposed CeDiRNet-6DoF jointly predicts grasp points and full 6-DoF grasp poses using dense 3D grasp regression, segmentation, and sine-cosine-encoded Euler angles. This handles occlusion-heavy, high-dimensional perceptual challenges typical of cloth.

entry.title: ST-pRRTC: Parallel Space-Time RRT-C with Adaptive Goal-Time Forests

author.name: Duo Zhang, Jintong Li, Junshan Huang, Jingjin Yu

entry.summary: ST-pRRTC is a GPU-parallel space-time RRT-Connect motion planner for problems with known obstacle trajectories and unspecified arrival times. It builds a shared forward tree plus an adaptive forest of backward goal-time trees, with an interval-root formulation that continuously samples arrival times and guarantees probabilistic completeness and asymptotic arrival-time optimality. A practical root-recycling policy adapts a fixed number of backward trees, trading formal guarantees for efficiency.

entry.title: Can a Robot Read Braille? - Learning to Adapt Contact via Imitation Learning for Tactile Braille Recognition

author.name: Xi Chen, Yunlong Shan, Sihan Chen, Jun Hu, Zhongxuan Li, Shiyao Zhang, Sichao Liu, Zhong Zhao, Kosta Jovanovic, Peng Zhou

entry.summary: This work presents an adaptive-contact framework for robotic tactile Braille reading that assesses contact quality and physically corrects poor contact before recognition, trained via multi-head policy learning on expert-guided adjustment demonstrations. It fills a neglected gap: most robotic Braille readers only handle recognition after contact. The accessibility application and the active contact-establishment framing are both novel.

entry.title: From Visual Search to Movement Control: A Priority Field for Artificial Agents

author.name: Han Zhang, Zhong Cao

entry.summary: The authors extend cognitive-science notions of a priority map from visual search to movement control, first fitting a lightweight saccade model trained on human eye movements, then equipping an agent with a priority field for a reach-avoid navigation task. Priority-field agents trained more efficiently and performed better than alternative architectures. The cross-disciplinary link between human attention models and robot control is the key contribution.

entry.title: Quadruped Obstacle Avoidance and Footstep Planning with Distributed Low-cost Time-of-Flight Sensors

author.name: Giammarco Caroleo, Timoth\'ee Mahamoodally, Matteo Manzardo, Jin Jin, Marco Pontin, Matias Mattamala, Renato Vidoni, Perla Maiolino, Maurice Fallon

entry.summary: This work designs a distributed time-of-flight sensing architecture for the ANYmal quadruped as a low-cost, low-power alternative to depth cameras and LiDAR for near-field terrain mapping, footstep planning, and obstacle avoidance, eliminating blind spots of frontal sensors. Benchmarking shows the approach supports terrain reconstruction and locomotion. A practical perception-hardware contribution for legged robots.

entry.title: dRVG: Quadtree-Guided, Resolution-Complete Online Motion Planning for Polygonal Robots in Unknown Environments

author.name: Duo Zhang, Hechen Zhang, Junshan Huang, Jingjin Yu

entry.summary: dRVG is an online motion planner for polygonal robots in unknown static environments that merges local rotation-stacked visibility graph roadmaps across observations and uses a spatial quadtree to schedule sensing goals, avoiding uniform grids. Under stated assumptions it is resolution-complete relative to full-map RVG, and experiments solve all 140 cases across 20 difficult maps. A rigorous theoretical addition to online geometric planning.

entry.title: Sector: de-slopping AI-driven research

author.name: Taras Kutsyk

entry.summary: A LessWrong post by an AI safety researcher presenting Sector, an open workflow repository for making LLM-driven research less low-quality and more verifiable. The workflow instructs agents not just to execute prompts but to make their work easy to understand, easy to verify, and engaging enough to keep the human in the driver's seat, synthesizing two years of daily LLM research practice into reusable principles.

entry.title: Thinking Less to Simulate Better: Intuitive Prompting Improves LLM Agents Simulating Individual Social Media Reactions, Including Unfamiliar Content

author.name: Ljubisa Bojic, Tijana Stanic, Joerg Matthes, Agariadne Dwinggo Samala, Bojana Dinic, Jue Wang

entry.summary: Validates LLM agents simulating individual social media users by profiling eight Serbian participants and asking four language models to predict their reactions to 68 posts under five prompting conditions. Attitudinal profile content improved prediction over demographic backstories, and lighter, intuitive prompting outperformed heavier reasoning-style instructions.

entry.title: The Right Information Extraction Pipeline Depends on the Document: Accuracy-Energy Trade-offs for Small, Local Models

author.name: Christoph Walser, Mauricio Fadel Argerich, Jonathan F\"urst

entry.summary: This benchmarking study compares on-premise information extraction pipelines for privacy-sensitive documents using small (at most 8B parameter) text-only and vision-language models, evaluating accuracy and energy across input representation, model family, and inference configuration. Key findings include that batching cuts energy per page by 38-85 percent at no accuracy cost, FP8 quantization saves 27-32 percent, and whether to process page images versus parsed text flips across the document layout spectrum. It offers practical, sustainability-oriented guidance for local document AI.

entry.title: A Survey on Fake Review Detection: From Pre-trained Language Models to Large Language Models

author.name: Fanji Yang (Guizhou University of Finance and Economics), Huiyao Chen (Harbin Institute of Technology), Xi Yu (Guizhou University of Finance and Economics), Meishan Zhang (Harbin Institute of Technology), Xiaohong Xiao (Guizhou University of Commerce), Mingsen Deng (Guizhou University of Finance and Economics)

entry.summary: This survey reviews 211 studies on fake review detection from 2018 to early 2026, organized from an information fusion perspective covering review text, sentiment, rating behavior, and other evidence sources and fusion levels. It covers the shift from pre-trained language models to LLMs, noting LLMs both generate more convincing fake reviews and provide stronger semantic representations for detection. The survey maps the landscape for future work in this dual-use area.

entry.title: FedHisto-PAST: Parameter-Efficient Stain-Aware Federated Learning for Cross-Site Lung Histopathology Classification

author.name: Muhammad Muhtasim Shahriar, M. M. Golam Hafiz, Saad Aloteibi, Mohammad Ali Moni

entry.summary: FedHisto-PAST v2 combines a frozen HIBOU-B pathology foundation model with parameter-efficient adaptation, stain-conditioned paired-view consistency, reliability-aware prototype learning, and adaptive federated aggregation for cross-site lung histopathology classification. It is evaluated in a five-client, non-IID simulation with ablations and communication accounting.

entry.title: LipSSM: Structurally Lipschitz-Bounded Cascaded State-Space Model via Metric Transfer between Consecutive SSM Layers

author.name: Natsuki Yoshino, Ren Uchida, Kazuki Matsumoto, Kohei Yatabe

entry.summary: LipSSM extends the LipKernel approach to cascaded state-space models, transferring metric information between consecutive SSM layers to obtain a tighter bound on the overall Lipschitz constant than layer-wise enforcement, improving the robustness-expressivity tradeoff. This yields certifiably robust sequence models with less conservative restrictions.

entry.title: Differential Attention Unlocks Complementary EEG and Speech Fusion for Emotion Recognition

author.name: Philip H. Lee, Shreeram Suresh Chandra, John H. L. Hansen

entry.summary: EmoSpeechBrain fuses EEG and speech for multimodal emotion recognition, using differential attention—subtracting two attention maps—to cancel shared EEG noise before fusion, plus an attention-based gating adapter for modality weighting. It addresses the common failure where naive fusion underperforms the stronger single modality.

entry.title: DiffusionShadow: Diffusion-based Shadow Caching for Neural Volume Rendering

author.name: Kai-Chen Tung, Qi Wu, David Bauer, Mengjiao Han, Silvio Rizzi, Kwan-Liu Ma

entry.summary: DiffusionShadow compresses a large set of precomputed shadow implicit neural representations for direct volume rendering into a single diffusion model, avoiding both expensive per-frame shadow ray marching and prohibitive storage of many lighting directions. This enables real-time neural volume rendering with advanced illumination effects for scientific visualization applications.

entry.title: From Mono to Stereo: Accelerating Binocular Gaussian Splatting via Reprojection and Selective Patching

author.name: Hongfei Zhu, Ling Zhou

entry.summary: The authors accelerate binocular 2D Gaussian Splatting rendering by fully rendering only a dominant-eye RGB image plus an alpha-weighted depth proxy, then reprojecting to the second eye and repairing disocclusions via selective ROI re-rendering. The depth proxy reuses alpha-blending weights from the dominant-eye rasterization, avoiding a separate depth pass. This substantially reduces redundant visibility and shading work in stereo rendering.

entry.title: IDM-Net: A Lightweight Illumination-Decoupled Modulation Network for Low-Light Image Enhancement

author.name: Cheng-Yen Hsiao, Jing-Ming Guo

entry.summary: Proposes a lightweight dual-encoder network for low-light image enhancement that separates luminance and chrominance and uses illumination as an explicit guidance prior during feature reconstruction rather than merely as an enhancement target. Targets the difficulty of jointly optimizing illumination restoration and color fidelity in the RGB space under computational constraints. Useful for edge deployment of enhancement pipelines.

entry.title: MoTop: Motion-Topological Model For Micro AU Detection

author.name: Huai-Qian Khor, Mengting Wei, Yante Li, Chu Kiong Loo, Guoying Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes MoTop, a motion-topological model for detecting facial action units in micro-expressions, modeling fine-scale facial movement to mitigate AU ambiguity arising from constrictive activation regions. Positions micro AU detection as a crucial upstream task for facial analysis and downstream emotion recognition in high-stakes environments. Specialized affective computing contribution.

entry.title: mHolmes improves cross anatomical cadaveric microbiome forecasting for postmortem interval estimation

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: A Nature Communications paper (per the URL) presenting mHolmes, a machine learning model that improves microbiome-based forecasting of postmortem interval across different anatomical sampling sites on cadavers. Cross-anatomical generalization is a known obstacle for forensic microbiome models, so an approach that improves robustness across body sites could advance forensic time-of-death estimation.

entry.title: Semantic Navigation for Issue Localization in Code Repository

author.name: Yunxiang Wei, Zhenyu Lei, Jundong Li

entry.summary: SemNav is a framework for repository-level issue localization that combines deterministic retrieval to seed a broad candidate set with an LLM agent that iteratively inspects code and refines candidates. It addresses limitations of current agent environments, which force agents to search unresolved relation targets and revise judgments without evidential basis. This is relevant to autonomous software engineering workflows.

entry.title: Do LLMs Understand Context? A Knowledge Graph-Based Evaluation Framework

author.name: Subavarshana Arumugam, Mamta Nallaretnam, Kithuni Wickramasinghe, Chamath Gunapala, Pragatheeswaran Vipulanandan, Kamal Premaratne, Uthayasanker Thayasivam

entry.summary: Proposes a knowledge graph-based evaluation framework to test whether LLMs genuinely comprehend context rather than performing surface pattern matching, moving beyond BLEU and perplexity metrics. The framework targets question answering where responses must be contextually grounded and factually consistent.

entry.title: Evaluating Real-Time Voice Agents: From Component Quality to Grounded Outcomes

author.name: Shivam Negi, Arpit Rawat, Rashi Jain

entry.summary: A survey-style analysis of real-time voice agent evaluation, organizing 38 primary sources into a six-category application-centric taxonomy spanning speech foundation modeling, turn-taking psycholinguistics, and agentic evaluation. It argues these communities rarely cite one another, so no single metric captures deployed agent quality, and presents three evidence-based claims including that architecture choice is a deployment constraint rather than a settled verdict. Useful for unifying voice agent evaluation practice.

entry.title: OmouAI: Argumentative Human-AI Policy Deliberation with Simulated Personas

author.name: Stylianos Loukas Vasileiou, Antonio Rago, William Yeoh, Georgina Curto

entry.summary: OmouAI is an interactive deliberation system combining LLMs with computational argumentation to let a human deliberate policy claims with simulated personas such as stakeholders, experts, and devil's advocates. It targets known problems with LLM debate in high-stakes settings, including sycophancy and unfaithful explanations. The system is relevant to inclusive, human-centered AI-assisted public policy deliberation.

entry.title: ENAS: An Efficient Hardware-Aware Neural Architecture Search Framework for TinyML on Resource-Constrained Microcontrollers

author.name: Mohd Moin Khan, Naman Srivastava, Pandarasamy Arjunan

entry.summary: ENAS is a hardware-aware neural architecture search framework for TinyML that combines static feasibility checks, a cell-based search space, a three-stage hybrid search strategy with cross-run caching, and notably operates without GPU acceleration. It is evaluated on Visual Wake Words and Melanoma Cancer benchmarks across eight microcontrollers with 20 KB to 1 MB SRAM footprints. The work targets NAS in constrained development environments where GPU-based NAS is infeasible.

entry.title: MedTokenBudget: Lesion-Preserving Token Routing for Dermoscopic Image Classification

author.name: Zhexiang Li

entry.summary: MedTokenBudget is a supervised post-backbone token routing framework for Vision Transformer dermoscopy classifiers that keeps tokens concentrated in lesion regions under a compute budget. Its Lesion-Aware Token Scoring module fuses attention entropy, feature norm, and local contrast, trained with budget curriculum learning. This improves efficiency while preserving diagnostic evidence in medical imaging.

entry.title: Quantum Diffusion Models for Medical Image Analysis

author.name: Francesco Aldo Venturelli, Stefano Martina, Marco Parigi, Filippo Caruso, Alba Cervera-Lierta, Miguel A. Gonz\'alez Ballester

entry.summary: The authors present a hybrid quantum diffusion model that uses a discrete-time quantum walk on a real quantum device for the forward diffusion dynamics and a classical network for the backward denoising step, evaluated on medical image analysis. The work aims to overcome the scalability limits of prior quantum machine learning attempts in imaging.

entry.title: Different Corruptions, Different Signals: Uncertainty and Loss in Federated Data Quality

author.name: Bradley Scott, Zeqi Luo, Edmond S. L. Ho

entry.summary: The paper compares input-conditional uncertainty (aleatoric variance, MC dropout, entropy) versus prediction-label loss as signals for detecting two corruption modes in federated learning: additive input noise and persistent label flips. Experiments on ResNet-20 with CIFAR-10 and SVHN under non-IID Dirichlet partitions show the signals behave differently per corruption type.

entry.title: When the Preconditioning Exponent Turns Negative: Learning-Rate Coupling and Cross-Environment Generalization

author.name: Gongyue Zhang, Honghai Liu

entry.summary: This controlled study examines how the preconditioning exponent in adaptive optimizers interacts with the learning rate to affect cross-environment generalization, using a four-environment classification setup with spurious sparse features. It finds the optimal exponent shifts with learning rate, including into negative values, challenging the standard practice of fixing exponents between momentum and Adam's square root.

entry.title: Improving Molecular-Morphology Contrastive Pretraining using Deep-Learning-based Morphology Profiles

author.name: Jie Li, Kathryn E. Kirchoff, Dante A. Pertusi, Zhizhuo Zhang

entry.summary: The paper extends MoCoP, a contrastive pretraining strategy aligning small-molecule embeddings with cell morphology fingerprints, by replacing CellProfiler-derived features with richer deep-learning-based cell image encodings. The resulting molecular representations show transferable performance on QSAR prediction tasks. This advances image-based molecular representation learning for drug discovery workflows.

entry.title: Adaptive Interaction Graphs for Particle Simulation

author.name: Aiden Zhou

entry.summary: The paper makes the interaction graph of learned GNN particle simulators adaptive: a per-particle variance head trained with heteroscedastic NLL drives expansion of neighborhoods for high-uncertainty particles, at minimal inference cost by reusing the previous step's uncertainty. Notably, the variance head learns a meaningful uncertainty signal rather than merely fitting noise.

entry.title: Deterministic Regime Switching and Feasibility Inversion in Dynamic Tensor Rematerialization

author.name: Mahesh Reddy Pagadala

entry.summary: This paper reports fine-grained deterministic instabilities in Dynamic Tensor Rematerialization (DTR), a memory-constrained training eviction policy, showing that budget changes of 0.10% can switch execution regimes with overheads differing by up to 7.3x due to repeated re-evictions. A budget sweep on ResNet-32 reveals a deterministic feasibility inversion.

entry.title: Manifold Projection and Iterative Autoencoder Refinement for Masked Language Modeling

author.name: Narges Mokhtari, Farzan Haddadi, Ebrahim Rezaii

entry.summary: This paper replaces attention in masked language models with stacks of low-rank bottleneck autoencoder mixing modules operating over local neighborhoods, the full sequence, and across heads. Masked positions are refined via manifold projection and iterative autoencoder reconstruction, offering a content-dependent, computationally simpler alternative to attention-free MLP mixers.

entry.title: Skill Profiling with Attributable Reasoning (SPAR): A Wearable Analysis System for Boxing

author.name: Nibraas Khan, Hanchen David Wang, Enya Bullard, Ritam Ghosh, Ruj Haan, Aarav Agrawal, Meiyi Ma, Nilanjan Sarkar

entry.summary: Presents SPAR, an eight-IMU garment with pressure insoles that classifies boxing punches as expert or novice and produces tiered, actionable explanations of the prediction (per-joint attribution, kinematic counterfactuals) as coaching feedback. The system goes beyond punch-type classification to skill quality assessment with human-interpretable reasoning.

entry.title: THA: Weighted Finite-State Text Normalization and Inverse Text Normalization for Khmer

author.name: Seanghay Yath
